Assume all participants read at the same level
Incorporate varied instructional strategies (visuals, demonstrations, discussion, plain-language text)
Remove all text and rely only on pictures
Varied methods reach visual, auditory, reading/writing, and kinesthetic learners and different literacy levels. Removing all text is an overcorrection.
Why is it important to assess the literacy levels of participants before a training session?
To tailor the training content and delivery methods to the group’s needs
To exclude those who do not meet the minimum literacy requirements
To create a competitive environment among participants
Only to gather data without influencing training design
Knowing literacy levels lets the trainer tailor vocabulary, visuals and delivery methods to the audience; it is a needs-analysis input, not a screening tool to exclude workers.
Which is a type of sprinkler system used in freezer warehouses.
Dry-pipe systems hold pressurized air in the piping and admit water only after a head opens, so pipes in unheated or freezer areas do not freeze; wet systems would freeze.

Flammable storage rooms inside must be provided with:
Ref: 1910.106(d)(4)(v)
Self closing fire doors with 6 hour fire rating
OSHA 1910.106(d)(4)(v) requires at least one clear aisle 3 feet (36 in) wide in inside storage rooms; the sill requirement is 4 in, and ventilation is six air changes per hour.
Which is a characteristic of Category 3 flammable liquids?
Flash point is below 73°F; boiling point is at or above 100°F.
Flash point is below 73°F; boiling point is below 100°F.
Flash point is at or above 73°F, but below 100°F.
Flash point is at or above 200°F

Under GHS/HCS, Category 3 is flash point at or above 73.4 F and at or below 140 F; option C is the only choice in that band (A/B are Cat 2/1 style, D is not flammable). Note: GHS Category 3 upper limit is 140 F (option C reflects older 100 F limit); key is still the best choice.
Sodium Hydroxide has a Ph of 13. Which is true?
It is more acidic than Sulfuric Acid
It is more caustic than water
pH 13 is strongly basic (caustic); water is neutral at pH 7, so NaOH is far more caustic than water and is not acidic.
At constant pressure, a gas occupies 8.57 L at 273 K. What will its volume be at 355 K?
Charles's law at constant pressure: V2 = V1 x T2/T1 = 8.57 x 355/273 = 11.1 L. Temperatures must be absolute (K).
Which of the following is a noble gas?
Argon is a Group 18 noble gas (inert, full valence shell); oxygen, chlorine and hydrogen are reactive. Inert gases still pose asphyxiation hazards in confined spaces.
Personal fall arrest systems (PFAS), when stopping a fall, shall be rigged such that:
The PFAS has a maximum arresting force of 5000 pounds or five times the potential impact energy of an employee
An employee cannot free fall more than 6 feet or contact any lower level
The PFAS has a separate anchorage point for each employee
An employee can use a self-retracting lanyard or lifeline
OSHA 1910.140(d)(1) requires a PFAS be rigged so an employee cannot free fall more than 6 ft or contact any lower level; maximum arresting force is 1,800 lb with a body harness, not 5,000.
The attachment point of the body harness for a 6 foot fall arrest shall be located?
In the center of the wearer's back near shoulder level
In the center of the wearer’s lower back.
In the center of the wearer's chest.
In the center of the wearer's front abdomen.
OSHA 1910.140(d)(1)(iii) and 1926.502(d)(17) require the harness attachment point to be at the center of the back near shoulder level (dorsal D-ring) for fall arrest.
Travel restraint lines must be capable of sustaining a tensile load of ________ pounds? Ref: 1910.140(c)(14)
1910.140(c)(14) requires travel restraint lines to sustain a tensile load of at least 5,000 lb (22.2 kN), matching lanyard/lifeline strength.
Since nearly all worksite fatalities, injuries, and illnesses are preventable, OSHA suggests using the term ________________ investigation. Ref: https://www.osha.gov/incident-investigation
OSHA recommends 'incident' investigation because 'accident' implies an unpreventable event; nearly all incidents are preventable with root causes that can be corrected.
One way to conduct an effective incident investigation include:
Search through the company database for clues to previous incidents of similar nature.
Delegate the supervisor to lead the investigation, with an initial report due in 24 hours.
Conduct individual interviews of witnesses, take multiple photos, and create a timeline of the incident.
Hire an outside expert within 72 hours to conduct the investigation and determine causation factors.
Effective investigations gather evidence promptly: separate witness interviews, photographs and a timeline of events, which support root cause analysis.
When should the investigation be conducted following an injury?
Based on the evidence only because witness statements are usually biased or hearsay.
Immediately, with all witnesses simultaneously to get the most accurate statements.
The next working day after emotions have settled down.
Individually, with all direct and indirect witnesses as soon as possible.
Interview witnesses individually and as soon as possible, while memories are fresh and before accounts are influenced by others. Group interviews contaminate testimony.

Apex fork truck driver Jose had been working in the same warehouse for 45 years. During his most recent work shift, Jose bumped an overhead steam pipe with the mast of his truck. While there was no damage to the pipe, the insulation was damaged, some of which fell to the floor. The safety manager observed the incident and when Jose returned with a broom and dustpan, the manager stopped Jose from sweeping up the mess. Why?
The janitor was supposed to clean up the mess.
The fallen material could contain asbestos.
It was probably too hot to safely handle.
The insulation material could damage Jose’s hands if he tried to handle it.
Older pipe insulation may be asbestos-containing material; damaged (friable) insulation must be treated as presumed ACM and not dry-swept, per OSHA 1910.1001/1926.1101 work practices.
Teratogens cause developmental malformations (birth defects) in an embryo or fetus; carcinogens cause cancer and mutagens damage DNA.
Skin is usually soft, small red blisters.
Frostbite begins with prickling, tingling and numbness, then hard, pale or waxy skin; hot dry skin indicates heat stroke and cool moist skin indicates heat exhaustion.

Given an automobile model where the chance of windshield wipers failing after 40,000 miles is 0.5, and the likelihood of brake pads requiring replacement at the same mileage is 0.3,
What is the probability that the windshield wipers and the brake pads will both have issues simultaneously after 40,000 miles?
Please select the correct probability:
For independent events P(A and B) = P(A) x P(B) = 0.5 x 0.3 = 0.15. Adding (0.8) would be the OR rule without the overlap correction.

A safety professional is assessing the risk level of a particular activity. The risk level is calculated using the formula: Risk = Probability of Occurrence x Severity of Outcome. If the probability of occurrence is rated as 4 (on a scale of 1 to 5) and the severity of outcome is rated as 3 (on a scale of 1 to 5), what is the calculated risk level?
Risk = probability x severity = 4 x 3 = 12 on a 25-point matrix; adding the ratings (7) is the common trap.

The Total Recordable Incident Rate (TRIR) is a key safety metric calculated per 100 full-time workers. If a workplace has reported 10 incidents in a year, and the total hours worked by all employees is 200,000 hours, what is the TRIR? (Note: TRIR = (Number of Incidents x 200,000) / Total Hours Worked)
TRIR = (10 x 200,000) / 200,000 hours = 10 recordable cases per 100 full-time workers.
What is the primary purpose of conducting a needs assessment in organizational training programs?
To determine the profitability of the company
To assess the job performance data of the highest-ranking officials only
To identify gaps between current and desired performance levels
To evaluate the effectiveness of the marketing strategies
A training needs assessment identifies the gap between current and desired performance and whether training (vs. another fix) can close it.
Which method is most effective for assessing job knowledge and understanding specific tasks within a job role?
Direct observation and job shadowing show how tasks are actually performed and what knowledge is needed, the basis of task analysis.
When analyzing job performance data for training needs, what type of information is crucial to gather?
Only the highest and lowest performance scores
Specific areas where employees are underperforming
Needs analysis targets specific performance deficiencies so training addresses real gaps; extremes or unrelated data do not define training content.
What should be included in property insurance coverage, which protects physical items and assets like buildings and non-mobile equipment?
Materials and equipment in transit to or from your facility.
Pay for costs to property not owned by your company.
Cover the costs of injuries to your employees.
Reflect the replacement cost of the property.
Property coverage should reflect replacement cost so a loss can be fully restored; transit goods are inland marine, others' property is liability, and employee injury is workers' compensation.

When evaluating the effectiveness of safety protocols and controls aimed at preventing hand injuries, which method would be effective?
Ref: The Risk Management and Insurance Guidebook for Industry; MacWilliam, K. (2001)
Comparing incident and injury data before and after implementing the controls.
Conducting a perception survey among all employees about hand safety controls.
Monitoring the correct usage of personal protective equipment (PPE).
Comparing incident and injury data before and after controls directly measures outcome effectiveness; audits, PPE monitoring and surveys measure activity or perception, not results.
Which category of business risk is associated with changes in government regulations and tax laws?
Regulatory (compliance) risk is exposure to changes in laws, regulations and tax rules imposed by government.
One of the risks of nano products is?
It will cause leukemia due to the fine particles.
The cosmic rays of the nano products will become mutagenic in the body.
The ionizing radiation will destroy DNA.
The nanoparticles distribute themselves in ultrafine quantities and accumulate in various organs
Nanoparticles are small enough to penetrate deep in the lungs, cross membranes and translocate to and accumulate in organs (liver, brain); they are not inherently radioactive.
Using the hierarchy of control, which is the best method to reduce the inhalation hazard from abrasive blasting?
Schedule blasting when the least amount of workers are on site.
Provide wash stations so workers can wash routinely.
Use abrasive agent that can be delivered with water.
Provide supplied air respirators for the workers.
Wet abrasive blasting is an engineering/substitution control that suppresses dust at the source; respirators (PPE) and scheduling/hygiene (administrative) rank lower in the hierarchy.
In the event of a fire emergency, which of the following is the correct sequence of actions according to the "RACE" protocol?

RACE is Rescue, Alarm (Alert), Confine (Contain), Extinguish (or Evacuate); option C matches the standard sequence of these steps. Note: RACE versions use Extinguish or Evacuate as the last step; D could also be argued.
What is an example of cyberbullying?
Telling a consultant that you will underbid them in the next contract.
Creating an embarrassing picture of your coworker and forwarding it to your friend's email addresses
Telling a forklift driver to wear a seat belt and the first is a verbal warning.
Accepting a gift card for not writing up some issues on a safety audit.
Cyberbullying is using electronic communication to harass, humiliate or intimidate; circulating an embarrassing image of a coworker by email fits that definition.
The safety program book is a legal document that does what?
Describes how businesses should deal with an accident
Records of how an establishment is protecting (or plans to protect) employees overall for a safety or health hazard
Records the details of an accident in the workplace
Lists the first aid requirements of the workplace
A written safety program documents how the employer protects, or plans to protect, employees from hazards, and can be used as evidence in OSHA or legal proceedings.
You notice the forklift driver driving erratically. He tells you that he is on new medication, and it is affecting him. What do you think your next course of action should be?
Have him get off the forklift and have the worker go and report the issue to the Medical Clinic.
Counsel the worker to drive slower and be careful.
Conduct an impairment test and discipline the worker if they fail an impairment test.
Send the worker to the Medical Clinic for urinalysis.
Remove the impaired operator from the truck immediately (stop the hazard), then refer him to medical; drug testing or discipline is not the first priority for a disclosed prescription effect.

Which category represents the largest group of victims in nonfatal workplace assaults? Ref:
https://www.cdc.gov/mmwr/volumes/69/wr/mm6912a2.htm
The CDC MMWR (2020) analysis of nonfatal workplace violence found law enforcement and security workers had the highest victimization, far above retail and teaching.
Which four basic security concepts should be included in a facility security program?
Layered security aims to deter attempts, detect intrusions, delay the intruder long enough for a response, and respond.
x= 2a - 3b + ab, then solve for x if 3=a and 4=b.
A right angle in a triangle represents?
A right angle measures exactly 90 degrees; the three angles of any triangle sum to 180 degrees.
The Circumference of a tire that has a radius of 18 inches is ___________ inches
C = 2 x pi x r = 2 x 3.1416 x 18 in = 113.1 in, about 113 in. Using pi x r (56.5) is the usual error.

The contents of the first aid kit shall be placed in a weatherproof container with individual sealed packages for each type of item and shall be checked by the employer before being sent out on each job and at least _____________ on each job to ensure that the expended items are replaced.
KEY CORRECTED by trainer review: 1926.50(d)(2): first-aid kit contents are checked before being sent out and at least WEEKLY on each job.

A HAZMAT team member enters an area to retrieve soil samples wearing safety glasses, steel-toe boots, coveralls, gloves, and a hard hat, with no respiratory protection. What EPA protection level is this?
Level D is a work uniform with no respiratory protection and minimal skin protection. Level C adds an air-purifying respirator; B adds SCBA; A is fully encapsulating.

The five steps in emergency preparedness are prevention,
Mitigation, preparedness, response, and recovery. The
Installation of a new fire alarm system is best described by
Which step?

Installing alarm and warning systems is a preparedness activity: it readies the organization to detect and respond to a fire, while mitigation reduces the hazard or its consequences. Note: Some sources classify warning-system installation as mitigation; preparedness is defensible.
What are the six levels of Bloom's Taxonomy, in order from lowest to highest cognitive skill?
Understand, Remember, Apply, Analyze, Evaluate, Create
Remember, Understand, Apply, Analyze, Evaluate, Create
Analyze, Evaluate, Create, Understand, Remember, Apply
Create, Evaluate, Analyze, Apply, Understand, Remember
Revised Bloom's Taxonomy (Anderson and Krathwohl, 2001) runs from lowest to highest: Remember, Understand, Apply, Analyze, Evaluate, Create.
Which description best captures the essence of the 'Apply' level in Bloom's Taxonomy?
Apply means using learned information or procedures in a new or concrete situation, such as performing a lockout on a different machine.
Analyzing involves breaking information into parts to explore understandings and relationships. Which of the following activities best demonstrates the analysis level of Bloom's Taxonomy?
Summarizing the plot of a novel
Creating a poster that categorizes types of animals
Comparing theories requires breaking ideas into parts and examining relationships, the Analyze level; memorizing is Remember and summarizing is Understand.
A machine operator who is not allowed to clear a jam or service the machine is an ______________ employee.
Under 1910.147(b) an affected employee operates or works in the area of equipment being serviced but does not perform the servicing; authorized employees perform lockout.
What is the purpose of a lockout/tagout procedure?
To prevent the unexpected start-up or energization of machines and equipment during service or maintenance
To ensure the machine is running efficiently
To verify the identity of workers
To secure the building at the end of a workday
1910.147 controls hazardous energy to prevent unexpected energization, start-up or release of stored energy during servicing and maintenance.
Why is it important to verify the absence of energy after performing a lockout?
To confirm that the lockout device is attached
To ensure that the equipment is still operational
To make certain there is no residual energy that could pose a danger when performing maintenance
To check the jog function of the machine
Verification (try-out) confirms isolation is effective and stored or residual energy (capacitors, springs, hydraulics, gravity) is released before work begins, per 1910.147(d)(6).

"_____________________ person" means one who is capable of identifying existing and predictable hazards in the surroundings, or working conditions which are unsanitary, hazardous, or dangerous to employees, and who has authorization to take prompt corrective measures to eliminate them.
OSHA 1926.32(f) defines a competent person as one able to identify existing and predictable hazards and authorized to take prompt corrective measures to eliminate them.
Trenches _____ feet deep or greater require a protective system unless the excavation is made entirely in stable rock.
1926.652(a)(1) requires protective systems in excavations 5 ft or deeper unless entirely in stable rock; under 5 ft, a competent person may decide.

The contractor wishes to use ladders are necessary to establish a means of entry and egress from his trench, at what depth do ladders, ramps and stairways become mandatory according to the OSHA standard?
1926.651(c)(2) requires a stairway, ladder, ramp or other egress in trenches 4 ft or deeper, within 25 ft of lateral travel.
In order to foster worker involvement in an effective safety management program, which element is crucial to cultivating their commitment?
A positive safety culture of shared values and management commitment drives genuine worker involvement; incentives and discipline influence behavior short term but do not build commitment.
Corrective actions related to safe work practices are MOST effective when they are:
Related to an occurrence, a behavior, and a consequence.
Behavior-based corrective action links an antecedent occurrence, the specific behavior and a consequence (ABC model), which makes it understood and effective.
Forklifts are different from cars because?
Forklifts steer from the rear and always weigh less than cars.
Forklifts are easier to stop than cars.
Forklifts are more maneuverable than cars.
Forklifts steer from the rear, while cars steer from the front.
Most forklifts steer with the rear wheels, so the rear swings wide when turning; they are heavier and harder to stop than cars.
What factors should be considered when designing and selecting machine guards?
Guards must be made of durable material, strong enough to withstand normal use, and allow visibility of the operation (OSHA 1910.212 and ANSI B11.19 guard design criteria).
Which of the following should be a KEY consideration when selecting and installing machine guards?
The availability of the guard to match the machine.
The ease with which the guard can be removed.
Ensuring the guard does not introduce additional hazards.
Making sure the guard can be seen from a distance.
OSHA guarding principles require that a guard not create new hazards (shear points, sharp edges) or interfere with work; guards should not be easy to remove.
If a conveyor belt needs to be cleaned, what is the best practice?
Clean it while the conveyor is moving to ensure all debris is removed
Use compressed air to blow debris off the conveyor belt
Stop the conveyor and follow lockout/tagout procedures before cleaning
Spray the conveyor with water while it's running to clean it
Cleaning a conveyor is servicing; 1910.147 requires stopping it and applying lockout/tagout to prevent caught-in injuries at nip points.
What is the primary purpose of a pilot course in training development?
To test the course’s effectiveness and gather feedback
To market the course to potential learners
A pilot course is a trial run with a representative audience to test effectiveness, timing and materials and collect feedback for revision before rollout.
When developing a new training course, what is a critical first step?
Learning objectives define what learners must be able to do and drive content, methods and evaluation (ANSI/ASSP Z490.1); media and venue follow.
How often should feedback be collected and analyzed during a pilot course?
Only at the end of the course
At scheduled intervals throughout the course
Collecting feedback at scheduled intervals during a pilot captures reactions to each module while fresh, rather than relying only on an end-of-course survey.
What action should be taken if a crane operator comes into contact with a 7200 volt power line and the crane is not on fire?
Continue operating to complete the task quickly
Immediately shut down the crane, have the area evacuated and stay in the cab.
Try to remove the power line from the crane using a dry wooden stick and rubber gloves. .
Ask bystanders to pull the crane away from the power line.
If the crane contacts a power line and no fire exists, the operator should stay in the cab, stop operation and keep everyone clear, since stepping off can complete a path to ground.

According to 1926.1431(d)(1), when using suspended personnel platforms, the total load (including the platform, hook, load line, and rigging) must not exceed what percent of the rated capacity for the radius and configuration of the equipment, except during proof testing?
1926.1431(d)(1) limits the total hoisted load for a personnel platform to 50% of rated capacity for the radius and configuration, except during proof testing.
Which does not affect the which of the following factors do not affect the load capacity of the crane?
Use of an anti-two block device.
Load charts vary with boom length, boom angle (radius) and outrigger setup; an anti-two-block device prevents hook-block contact but does not change rated capacity.
Most training experts recommend a second_______________ after 6 months to obtain valid student reaction to the training.
A follow-up evaluation about six months later shows whether learners still value and use the training on the job (Kirkpatrick levels 1-3 over time).
Which document is used to standardize a presentation so that different instructors deliver the same content and no critical material is omitted?
A lesson plan lays out objectives, content sequence, methods, timing, and assessments so delivery is consistent across instructors and sessions.
Trainer should arrive ____________ minutes before the start of training to get set up, check the learning environment, verify materials are in order, and greet participants as they arrive.
Common trainer practice is to arrive about 30 minutes early to set up equipment, check the room and materials, and greet participants.
A right triangle has one leg 40 feet high and the other leg 100 feet wide. What is the area?
Area of a right triangle = 1/2 x base x height = 0.5 x 100 ft x 40 ft = 2,000 sq ft.
Question: How many sides does a hexagon have?
KEY CORRECTED by trainer review: A hexagon has 6 sides.
What is the significance of the Pythagorean theorem (a² + b² = c²) in construction safety?
It is used to calculate the safe distance from a point of operation.
It helps determine the proper length of ladders when leaned against a wall.
It is used to calculate the volume of safety helmets.
It assists in the aesthetic design of safety signs
A ladder against a wall forms a right triangle, so a^2 + b^2 = c^2 gives the required ladder length; the 4:1 setback rule is applied with it.

The periodic inspection of authorized employees must be conducted every _____. 
Ref:1910.147(C)(6)
1910.147(c)(6) requires periodic inspection of each energy control procedure at least annually by an authorized employee other than the one using it.
Who is authorized to perform a lockout/tagout procedure?
Any employee with a key to the lockout device
Only the owner of the company
Only authorized employees, trained under 1910.147(c)(7), may apply lockout/tagout devices and service equipment.
Which of the following is an essential step before starting lockout/tagout procedures?
Notifying all affected employees that a lockout/tagout procedure will be performed
Making sure the machine is operating correctly
1910.147(d)(1) and (f)(2) require notifying affected employees before lockout devices are applied and before equipment is restarted.
Engineering fire controls for a warehouse include.
Proving the use of flame retardant clothing.
A sprinkler system is an engineering control built into the facility; housekeeping and training are administrative controls, and flame-resistant clothing is PPE.
Which of the following is an example of an engineering control?
Machine guards physically separate workers from the hazard, making them engineering controls; training and inspections are administrative, goggles are PPE.
Using two people to lift a pipe weighing 80 pounds is an example of:
A team lift changes how the work is done, not the equipment, so it is an administrative (work practice) control; a hoist or vacuum lifter would be engineering.
Toxic Substances Control Act gives EPA specific authority to move against chemical hazards such as PCBs and ________________.
TSCA (1976) authorizes EPA to regulate existing chemical substances, explicitly PCBs (Title I) and asbestos (Title II, AHERA); food, drugs and pesticides fall under FDA and FIFRA.
Your company makes reinforced plastic fuel tanks. You install the fuel tanks at gas stations. Which of the following regulatory agencies would be concerned with your operation?
OSHA governs worker safety during fabrication and installation, and EPA regulates underground storage tanks for petroleum (40 CFR 280); CERCLA, RCRA and HAZWOPER are laws/standards, not agencies.
For A Large Quantity Generator Of Hazardous Waste, How Long Must You Retain Copies Of Annual Training Provided To Those Workers Who Are Currently Employed By The Company?
Three years from the date of training
Fifteen years from the date of training
40 CFR 262.17(a)(7)(v): training records for current personnel are kept until facility closure; for former employees, at least 3 years from the last date worked.
What is the primary purpose of maintaining test security in a training program?**
To ensure that all participants pass the exams
To increase the length of the training program
To make the test harder for participants
To minimize the risk of cheating and content theft
Test security protects validity of results by preventing cheating and theft of items, so scores reflect real competence.
When evaluating the results of a training program, it is essential to ensure that the evaluation is:
Based solely on the highest scores achieved
Conducted in a manner that is consistent and fair for all participants
Available to the public for transparency
Influenced by the participants' personal opinions about the course
Evaluations must be applied consistently and fairly to all participants so results are valid, reliable and defensible.
What should be the primary consideration when updating course materials for a training program?
The cost of printing new materials
The popularity of the course topics
Compliance with the latest industry standards and regulations
The color scheme of the materials for aesthetic appeal
Training content must reflect current standards and regulations; outdated material can teach noncompliant practices and create liability.
Two approaches to material handling are:
Lifting limits are set with biomechanical (spinal load), physiological and psychophysical (acceptable weights) approaches, e.g. Snook tables and the NIOSH lifting equation.
What is the most important factor to check before operating an indoor crane?
The weather conditions inside the facility
Before use, confirm the load is within rated capacity and the crane is stable and functioning, per 1910.179 inspection and loading requirements.
If you discover a mechanical problem with an indoor crane, what should be your first course of action?
Continue using the crane but with lighter loads
Report the issue to a supervisor or maintenance personnel immediately
Try to fix the problem yourself without stopping operations
Ignore the problem if the crane can still lift some weight
Defects affecting safe operation must be reported and the crane removed from service until repaired (1910.179(j)); operating with a defect risks failure.
Organizational culture greatly affects implementation of a safety program, and each organization has its own culture. What is one way to measure safety culture improvement?
Regular safety perception surveys of all workers
Implementation of OSHA safety and health guidelines
Implement a formal Pareto Perception Analysis For All

Perception surveys of all workers, repeated over time, directly measure shared beliefs and attitudes, i.e., culture. Citation counts and guideline adoption are compliance measures, not culture measures.
Under 29 CFR 1910.1020, employee exposure records must be retained for:
29 CFR 1910.1020: exposure records are kept at least 30 years; medical records for duration of employment plus 30 years.
The best suggestion for enhancing an employer’s Safety and Health Management Programs is:
Adding more disciplinary steps for workers not following safety rules
Placing more emphasis on the reporting of near-misses
Instituting a management team responsible for safety at a company
OSHA's Recommended Practices emphasize worker participation; involving employees in JSAs uses their task knowledge and builds ownership of hazard control.
What is the primary purpose of Energy Trace and Barrier Analysis (ETBA)?
To measure the energy consumption of a facility
To determine the most cost-effective energy sources for a project
To identify energy sources and evaluate the barriers protecting against hazardous events
ETBA identifies energy sources in a system and evaluates the adequacy of barriers between those energies and people or property.
Deming popularized the Plan-Do-Check-Act (PDCA) cycle (from Shewhart), the basis of continual improvement in ISO 45001, ISO 14001 and ANSI Z10.
What does the term 'Fail Active' refer to in safety-critical systems?
A system that stops functioning when a failure is detected.
A system that remains operational in a safe mode when a component fails.
A system that requires manual intervention when a failure occurs.
A system that increases risk when a failure is detected.
A fail-active (fail-operational) design keeps functioning in a safe mode after a component failure, unlike fail-passive designs that simply shut down.
Ohm's Law states that the current in a circuit is directly proportional to the:**
Resistance and inversely proportional to the voltage
Voltage and inversely proportional to the resistance
Power and directly proportional to the resistance
Voltage and directly proportional to the power
Ohm's law I = V/R: current rises directly with voltage and falls inversely with resistance.
Electric panel boxes must have _____ feet of clear space. Ref: 1910.303
1910.303(g)(1) requires minimum working clearance of 3 ft in front of electrical equipment operating at 0-150 V to ground (deeper for higher voltages and conditions).
What is the primary purpose of NFPA 70E standards?**
To provide guidelines for petrochemical plant operations
To detail the financial responsibilities of electrical contractors
To outline safety procedures for working with electrical systems and equipment
To establish the color codes for wiring in residential buildings
NFPA 70E is the Standard for Electrical Safety in the Workplace: safe work practices, arc flash and shock risk assessment, and PPE for energized work.
Ionizing radiation occurs as a result of particles or electromagnetic waves having enough energy to detach what from atoms or molecules?
Ionizing radiation carries enough energy to remove electrons from atoms or molecules, creating ions that can damage DNA.
What is the primary protective measure against excessive exposure to radiation?
Radiation protection uses time, distance and shielding; minimizing exposure time directly reduces dose. Sunscreen, water and exercise give no protection.
What is the unit used to measure the biological radiation dose absorbed by a person?
The sievert (Sv) is the SI unit of equivalent/effective dose reflecting biological effect; the gray measures absorbed energy, and 1 Sv = 100 rem.
Which of the following is a common leading indicator in safety?
Near-miss reporting rate is a proactive, leading measure; LTIR, TRIR and first-aid rates count injuries that already happened (lagging).
One of the company's metrics they measure is “percent of personnel that had completed all the required OSHA training”. This indicator is an example of:
Training completion measures a preventive activity before injuries occur, so it is a leading indicator.
What is a lagging indicator in safety management?
A predictive measure that helps prevent future incidents.
A measure based on safety training completion rates.
A metric derived from recorded injuries and incidents.
An indicator used to measure employee engagement.
Lagging indicators measure past outcomes such as recordable injuries, lost-time cases and incidents.
What is the primary purpose of selecting an appropriate evaluation instrument in training programs?
To ensure that the training is entertaining
To measure the effectiveness of the training accurately
To extend the duration of the training
To reduce the cost of the training
An appropriate evaluation instrument must validly and reliably measure whether objectives were achieved, i.e., training effectiveness.
When collecting data from an evaluation instrument, what is most crucial to ensure its validity and reliability?
Collecting as little data as possible to simplify analysis
Ensuring that data collection methods are consistent
Changing data collection methods frequently to maintain interest
Using different types of data collection methods for each participant
Consistent, standardized data collection is essential to reliability, which is a prerequisite for valid conclusions.
In the context of analyzing data collected from training evaluation, which method is typically used to determine if training objectives were met?
Asking participants if they enjoyed the training
Estimating the cost-effectiveness of the training
Evaluating the aesthetics of the training materials
Pre-test vs. post-test comparison measures learning gains against objectives (Kirkpatrick Level 2); enjoyment is only reaction (Level 1).
What is the purpose of a tagline in rigging operations?
To keep workers clear of the load
To secure the load to the rigging equipment
To prevent the load from swinging
A tagline (tag line) lets a worker control rotation and swing of a suspended load from a safe distance; it is not a lifting or securing device.
Which of the following does not affect the capacity of a wire rope sling?
Sling capacity is reduced by low D/d ratio, smaller sling angle and damage like kinks; thimbles protect the eye and do not reduce rated capacity.
A 500-lb pipe is lifted by a two-leg bridle sling with the load centered. Each leg makes a 60-degree angle with the horizontal. What is the tension in each leg?
Tension per leg = (W/2) / sin(angle) = 250 / 0.866 = 289 lb. 250 lb ignores the angle; 354 lb uses 45 degrees.
Which of the following is NOT a safe practice when working with power tools?
Keeping hoses and cords away from oil, heat, and sharp edges
Pulling the cord at the tool end to disconnect it from the receptacle
Securing work with a clamp, keeping both hands free to use the tool
Inspecting the tool cord daily for defects
OSHA 1926.302 / 1910 hand-tool rules prohibit yanking the cord to disconnect; pull the plug itself. The other options are required safe practices.
Before using any power tool, what is the most important safety step?
Ensuring the tool is plugged in
Making sure the tool is the right color
Checking the tool for any damage or defects
Telling everyone in the area you are about to use the tool
Inspect tools before use and remove damaged ones from service (1926.300(a), 1910.242(a)); a damaged cord, guard or switch can cause shock or injury.
Which piece of personal protective equipment (PPE) is essential when operating loud power tools?
Loud power tools can exceed 85-90 dBA, so hearing protection is required under 1910.95 when engineering controls do not reduce noise.
1926.1052(c)(6) requires stair handrail height not more than 37 in nor less than 30 in, measured from the tread surface in line with the riser face.
Ladders shall have nonconductive ________________ if they are used where the employee or the ladder could contact exposed energized electrical equipment 1926.1053(b)(12)
1926.1053(b)(12) requires nonconductive siderails on ladders used where employees or the ladder could contact exposed energized equipment.
A structural defect on a ladder would be? 1926.1053(b)(16)
Corroded components are a structural defect requiring the ladder to be tagged and removed from service (1926.1053(b)(16)); dirt, paint or a missing sticker are not structural.
Your company drove 57,553,441 miles last year and had 42 collisions. Using Fleet incident rate = (incidents x 1,000,000) / miles driven, what is the rate?
42 x 1,000,000 / 57,553,441 = 0.73 collisions per million miles. 1.37 is the inverse (miles/incidents scaled); 0.42 and 0.57 simply misread the inputs.

What is the maximum number of hours a truck driver can drive in a day according to DOT regulations?
Ref https://www.fmcsa.dot.gov/.../summary-hours-service...
FMCSA hours-of-service: property-carrying drivers may drive 11 hours after 10 consecutive hours off, within a 14-hour on-duty window.

If a vehicle is stopped on a highway or shoulder for a reason other than a necessary traffic stop, the driver must use
Ref: FMCSA.dot.gov 6.3.6
FMCSA 49 CFR 392.22 requires hazard flashers and placement of warning devices (triangles) when a commercial vehicle is stopped on the roadway or shoulder.
Ototoxins (toluene, styrene, lead, carbon monoxide) damage the inner ear and hearing, often synergistically with noise.
The three bones of the ear are the incus, malleus and
The middle-ear ossicles are the malleus (hammer), incus (anvil) and stapes (stirrup); the cochlea is inner ear.
What is the primary function of the alveoli in the respiratory system?
Alveoli are the gas-exchange sacs where oxygen diffuses into and CO2 out of the blood; particles under about 4 um reach this region.

The scaffold has a capacity of 350 pounds per plank. The contractor will use a base of 5 planks wide to hold the concrete blocks. Each concrete weighs 32 pounds. How many concrete blocks can be put on the scaffold planks in total?
Capacity = 5 planks x 350 lb = 1,750 lb; 1,750 / 32 lb = 54.7, so a maximum of 54 blocks (round down to stay under capacity).
What is the primary purpose of calculating storage capacity for safety?
To ensure efficient use of space.
To prevent overload and potential hazards.
Storage capacity calculations prevent overloading floors, racks and containers that could collapse and keep storage within fire code limits.
If a storage area is filled beyond its calculated safe storage capacity, what safety concerns arise?
The items may be easier to find.
Risk of structural failures, fire hazards, and restricted access for emergency response.
The storage area may appear more organized.
There might be more light reflecting due to closely packed items.
Overfilling risks rack or floor structural failure, increased fire load, blocked sprinklers (18 in clearance) and obstructed egress for responders.
What is the first step in effectively facilitating a safety training session?
Distribute materials at the end of the session.
Start with a detailed discussion of company policies.
Establish clear objectives for the session.
Conclude the session with a safety demonstration.
Facilitation starts with clear objectives so learners know the purpose and expected outcomes; everything else is built around them.
When facilitating a discussion on safety, it’s important to”
Focus solely on the negatives and past accidents.
Allow one or two participants to dominate the discussion.
Stick strictly to a script without allowing questions.
Good facilitation draws participation from all attendees, which improves engagement and retention; letting a few dominate limits learning.
How should a facilitator handle a situation where a participant shares incorrect information about safety practices?
Ignore the incorrect information to avoid embarrassment.
Correct the information politely and provide the correct details.
Allow other participants to correct the mistake without intervening.
Dismiss the participant’s contribution and move on.
The facilitator must correct misinformation tactfully and give accurate information so unsafe practices are not reinforced.
The employer shall select a _____________________-certified respirator for protection against air contaminants. Ref 1910.134(d)(1)(ii)
1910.134(d)(1)(ii) requires the employer to select a NIOSH-certified respirator used within its certification conditions.
A quantitative fit factor (QNFF) is defined as the:
Factor applied to qualitative fit testing (QLFT) results to calculate the equivalent results required from quantitative fit testing (QNFT)
Maximum level of exposure to a contaminant allowed for the specific respirator being tested
Minimum expected level of respiratory protection provided by a properly fitted and functioning respirator
Quantitative measure of the fit of a particular respirator facepiece to a particular individual
1910.134(b) defines fit factor as a quantitative estimate of the fit of a particular respirator to a specific individual (ambient / in-mask concentration).

Ralph is assigned to sweep a dusty floor and asks for a filtering facepiece respirator (dust mask). Dust levels are well below regulatory limits. The supervisor refuses because Ralph has not been fit tested. Was the supervisor correct?
Yes, anyone wearing a tight-fitting respirator must be medically evaluated and fit tested prior to wearing one.
Yes, Ralph should not have asked for the respirator due to budget constraints.
No, fit testing is not required in this specific case.
No, the safety supervisor should have performed a fit test and issued the respirator.
Voluntary use of a filtering facepiece where exposures are below limits falls under 1910.134 Appendix D: give the user Appendix D information; fit testing and medical evaluation are not required.
What is the recommended best practice for injury prevention when handling materials?
Always bend at the knees, not at the waist.
Always maintain straight legs and lift with your back.
Always bend at the waist, not at the knee.
Always bend both at the waist and the knee
Bend at the knees and hips, keep the back straight and the load close so the leg muscles do the work and lumbar moment is minimized.
What is the primary goal of ergonomics in a workplace?
To increase the aesthetic appeal of the office
To enhance employee productivity by improving working conditions
To promote rapid performance regardless of working conditions
To enforce strict compliance with industry standards
Ergonomics fits the task to the worker, reducing MSD risk and fatigue while improving productivity and comfort.
Ordered data 3, 3, 5, 9, 11: the middle (3rd of 5) value is 5. The mean would be 31/5 = 6.2 and the mode 3.
A measure of the amount of variation or dispersion of a set of values
A measure of the correlation between two variables
A measure of the shape of a distribution
Standard deviation measures dispersion around the mean (square root of the variance).
What does the 'range' in statistics refer to?
The average value of a data set
The difference between the highest and lowest values in a data set
The value that occurs most frequently in a data set
The midpoint value of a data set
Range = highest value - lowest value, the simplest measure of spread.
Class D fire extinguishers are designed to extinguish which type of fire?
Class D fires involve combustible metals (magnesium, sodium, titanium) and need dry-powder agents; Class C is electrical and Class K is cooking oils.
Which of the following resources would the Logistics Section be LEAST likely to provide?
Food and water for incident personnel

Under ICS, intelligence and information analysis is handled by Planning (or a separate Intelligence/Investigations function); Logistics provides supplies, food, communications and medical support for responders.
In the context of ICS, what does the term "Unified Command" mean?
A single commander making decisions for all agencies
Multiple agencies sharing information but working independently
A combination of facilities, equipment, and personnel integrated into a common organizational structure
Different agencies working together under a shared set of objectives and strategies without losing agency authority
Unified Command lets agencies with jurisdiction jointly set one set of objectives and strategies without giving up their own authority or accountability (NIMS).
Which hazard may not be apparent to workers?
Carbon monoxide is colorless, odorless and tasteless, so workers get no sensory warning; H2S and odorized LPG are detectable by smell at low levels.

Lead is commonly present in various building materials, paints, and industrial coatings, and exposure to lead can be hazardous due to its negative health impacts. Which description most accurately identifies the controls for lead hazards?
Proper respirator use, maintaining good personal hygiene, and disposing of potentially contaminated clothing are necessary.
The sole control to prevent lung exposure to lead dust is using a self-contained breathing apparatus.
Wearing rubber gloves, utilizing a full-face shield, and using an N95 dust mask are required.
Since lead is a naturally occurring element, venting airborne lead dust outdoors poses no risk.
OSHA lead standards (1910.1025/1926.62) rely on respirators, hygiene (washing, no eating in work areas) and handling contaminated clothing to prevent inhalation and take-home exposure.
What is the primary reason for securing a safety training test?
To ensure that the training is only accessible to management
To prevent unauthorized access and maintain the integrity of the test
To make the test easier for trainees
To limit the number of trainees who pass the test
Securing tests prevents unauthorized access and keeps scores a valid measure of competence.
When delivering a safety training exam, it is crucial to:
Change the exam content frequently to keep it interesting
Ensure that all trainees receive different exam questions
Deliver the exam in a standardized manner to all trainees
Focus solely on theoretical knowledge, ignoring practical skills
Standardized administration (same instructions, time, conditions) makes results fair, comparable and defensible.
Consistency in evaluation across trainees can be achieved by:
Having a different evaluator for each trainee
Using a clear and detailed scoring rubric
Allowing trainees to evaluate each other
Adjusting the passing score based on the group's overall performance
A detailed scoring rubric defines criteria so different evaluators score consistently (inter-rater reliability).
Which of the following actions aligns with the ALARA principle?
Increasing the time individuals spend exposed to radiation sources
Using shielding materials to reduce exposure
Keeping distance from radiation sources as minimal as possible
Using older, less efficient radiation technology to save on costs
ALARA uses time, distance and shielding; adding shielding reduces dose. Increasing time or decreasing distance raises exposure.
What is the primary purpose of using lead shielding in environments where radiation is present?
To absorb and reduce the amount of radiation that reaches workers and patients.
To reflect radiation back to its source.
To increase the intensity of radiation for effective treatment.
To visually indicate areas where radiation is used.
Lead, a dense high-Z material, absorbs and attenuates X- and gamma rays, reducing dose to workers and patients.
What is the primary goal of the ALARA principle in radiation safety?
To keep radiation exposure as low as reasonably achievable
To use as much radiation as possible in medical treatments
To maximize the cost-effectiveness of radiation use
ALARA keeps radiation doses as low as reasonably achievable, accounting for economic and social factors, below regulatory limits; zero exposure is not the goal.
A dust is considered to be combustible if the Kst value (defined as the speed of pressure rise) is:
NFPA 652/68 classify dusts with any Kst > 0 as explosible (St 1: 0-200, St 2: 201-300, St 3: >300 bar-m/s); St 0 means no explosion.
As a safety profession using the hierarchy of controls, which of the following methods could you suggest to control dust hazards?
Infrared thermographic imaging and inspection controls
Layers of physical and operational control
Substituting a less dusty product and using local exhaust ventilation are higher-order controls (substitution and engineering) per the hierarchy.
Which of the following industries is NOT typically at risk for combustible dust incidents?
Woodworking, textiles and grain create organic combustible dusts; lead smelting fume and dust is a toxic, not typical combustible dust, hazard.
A 10-kg rubber block slides on a concrete floor (mu = 0.65). What is the friction force? (F = mu N; g = 9.8 m/s2)
Friction F = mu x N = 0.65 x (10 kg x 9.8 m/s2) = 0.65 x 98 N = 63.7 N.
What is the force that attracts two objects toward each other due to their mass?
Gravitational force attracts masses toward each other (F = Gm1m2/r^2); weight is gravity acting on mass.
What is the unit of force in the International System of Units (SI)
The newton (N = kg x m/s^2) is the SI unit of force; joule is energy, watt is power and pascal is pressure.
Which of the following is a key principle of ISO 45001?
Implementing a zero-waste policy for all organizations
Ensuring that all employees receive a minimum wage
Continual improvement of occupational health and safety performance
Mandating a specific ratio of managers to employees for better supervision
ISO 45001 is built on PDCA and requires continual improvement of OH&S performance (clause 10.3).
What is one of the primary benefits of implementing an ISO 14001 environmental management system?
Guaranteed financial savings on energy costs
Instant recognition as an environmentally friendly company
Enhanced legal compliance and reduced risk of penalties
Mandatory certification for all employees in environmental awareness
ISO 14001 requires identifying and evaluating compliance obligations, so it improves legal compliance and reduces penalty risk; savings and recognition are not guaranteed.
What does ISO 45001 emphasize the importance of, in terms of management approach?
ISO 45001 clause 5 places responsibility on top management leadership and commitment, including worker consultation and participation.
The chance of loss or the perils including retained (uninsured) losses and related loss adjustment expenses, risk control costs, transfer costs, and administrative costs

This describes the total cost of risk: retained losses, adjustment expenses, risk control, transfer (insurance) and administrative costs; 'Risk' is the only option fitting that concept. Note: Stem defines 'cost of risk'; 'Risk' is the closest option.
In terms of safety investment, what is a significant consideration for financial decision-makers?
The cost of safety training materials
The potential for reducing accident-related costs
The price of personal protective equipment
Decision-makers weigh safety spending against reduced accident costs (direct and indirect), which drives ROI and cost-benefit outcomes.
Method for resolving direct vs. Indirect costs of injuries/illnesses
Process which is ideally suited for use with a risk matrix
Technique which shifts financial risk from one party to another
Safety principle involving worker rotation to reduce chemical exposures.
Risk transfer shifts the financial consequences of a loss to another party, via insurance, contracts, indemnity or hold-harmless agreements.
Which of the following would not normally be identified in the risk identification process?

Risk identification inventories specific exposures (property, liability, human resource, external); 'pure risk' is a classification of risk type, not an exposure identified in that step. Note: Pure risk is a classification rather than an identified exposure; wording is awkward.
Which of the following is true about pure risks?
They are risks that are beyond human control and result in a loss or no loss with no possibility of financial gain
They are completely unrelated to hazard risks.
Are only recently being considered by risk managers.
Consist of Property and associated Human Resource risk only.
Pure risks have only loss or no-loss outcomes with no chance of gain (fire, injury), unlike speculative risks such as investments.
Scaffolds shall be erected, moved, dismantled, or altered only under the supervision and direction of a___________________ person qualified in scaffold erection. 1926.451
1926.451(f)(7) requires scaffold erection, moving, dismantling or alteration under the supervision of a competent person qualified in scaffold erection.
Crossbracing is acceptable in place of a Midrail when the crossing point of two braces is between ________ inches and__________________ inches. 1926.451(g)(4)(xv)
1926.451(g)(4)(xv) allows crossbracing as a midrail when the crossing point is 20 to 30 in above the work platform.
Scaffolds with a height to base ratio of more than ____:1 must be restrained from tipping. 1926.451(c)
1926.451(c)(1) requires supported scaffolds with a height-to-base width ratio greater than 4:1 to be restrained by guying, tying or bracing.
Which of the following tools is most appropriate for conducting a virtual training session?
Video conferencing supports live audio, video, screen sharing and interaction, which a virtual instructor-led session needs.
How can technology improve audience engagement during a presentation?
By allowing presenters to read scripts verbatim
By using multimedia elements like videos and animations
By avoiding the use of any visual aids
By limiting questions until the end of the session
Multimedia (video, animation, polls) engages multiple senses and learning styles, improving attention and retention.
In the context of training, what does the term 'asynchronous communication' refer to?
Communications that do not require immediate responses
Asynchronous communication does not occur in real time; learners respond on their own schedule (forums, e-learning, email).
Hazardous atmosphere" is Atmospheric oxygen concentration below ___________percent or above 23.5 percent;
OSHA 1910.146(b) defines a hazardous atmosphere as oxygen below 19.5% or above 23.5% (plus flammables >10% LFL and toxics above PEL).
The smell of rotten eggs, an indication of the presence of deadly _______________ ________________ gas.
Hydrogen sulfide has a rotten-egg odor at low ppm, but olfactory fatigue occurs around 100 ppm, so smell is not a reliable warning.

The LEL meter reads 3% of the LEL for Methane. The LEL of Methane is 5.3%.
How many ppm of methane is in the air.
Concentration = 0.03 x 5.3% = 0.159% by volume; 0.159% x 10,000 ppm per % = 1,590 ppm methane.
Which of the following is NOT a primary goal of safety management?
Safety management aims to prevent injuries, reduce loss costs and improve morale; raising production quotas is an operational goal, not a safety goal.

What is the MOST important element of a safety program?
Ref: https://www.osha.gov/safety-management
Proper use of personal protective equipment (PPE)
An open communication system regarding safety hazard
OSHA's Recommended Practices stress open communication so workers can report hazards without fear, which enables hazard identification and worker participation.
When conducting a risk assessment, what two factors are considered to determine the level of risk?
Severity of potential harm and likelihood of occurrence
Employee experience and cost of repairs
Time of day and location of work
Risk is the combination of severity of harm and likelihood of occurrence (ANSI/ASSP Z590.3, ISO 31000 risk matrix approach).
Your company is installing a new process that uses a chemical rinse that was not previously used in the company. What should your first action be to evaluate the health hazards.
Make sure the room has 6 air changes and hour
Order PPE before the work starts.
The SDS is the first source of hazard information (Sections 2, 8, 11) and guides exposure assessment, controls and PPE choice; sampling comes later.
Two police officers enter your hard hat only site on a non-emergency basis. What would you do?
Have security escort them out of the site.
Ask them to wear the visitor hard hats and sign in at the general contractor trailer for site meeting.
Tell them to return to their police station and get hard hats.
All visitors, including police on non-emergency business, must follow site rules: sign in and wear required PPE such as hard hats.
Safety footwear must meet standards set by ANSI and…:
American Society for Testing and Materials (ASTM)
OSHA 1910.136 accepts protective footwear meeting ASTM F2412/F2413 (formerly ANSI Z41).
Under GHS, which elements are required on a shipped container label?
Chemical formula, warnings, and pictograms only
pH, boiling point, flash point, and pictograms
Product identifier, pictogram, signal word, hazard statement, precautionary statement, and supplier information
SDS number, pictograms, and training date
HazCom 1910.1200(f) requires product identifier, signal word, hazard statements, pictograms, precautionary statements, and the supplier's name, address and phone.
What is the Globally Harmonized System (GHS)?
A system for classifying and labeling chemicals
A set of international trade regulations
A global positioning system for shipping hazardous materials
A database of chemical safety data sheets
The GHS is a UN system for classifying chemical hazards and communicating them through standardized labels and 16-section SDSs.
Which one of the following is not represented by a GHS pictogram?
The nine GHS pictograms include flame, health hazard and gas cylinder; eyewash station is an ANSI Z535/ISO 7010 safety sign, not a GHS pictogram.
Which statement is correct regarding hand and power tools?
It is the employer’s responsibility to ensure that only well-maintained and operable hand and power tools are utilized on the job site.
Regular maintenance logs must be kept on all hand and power tools and submitted to the safety manager monthly.
Only supervisors are allowed to make repairs to hand and power tools.
It is the supervisor’s responsibility to ensure that all hand and power tools on the job site are well-maintained and operable.
1926.300(a) and 1910.242(a) place responsibility on the employer for the safe condition of all tools, including employee-owned tools.
What is the MAIN purpose of a Job Hazard Analysis (JHA) in construction?
To identify potential hazards associated with each job task
To determine the required personal protective equipment (PPE)
To train the worker in required site safety rules.
A JHA breaks the job into steps and identifies hazards for each step so controls can be developed; PPE selection is a product of that.
Which of the following is a common method used for hazard assessment in construction?
Job Safety Analysis (JSA/JHA) is the common task-based hazard assessment method in construction; Ishikawa is a cause analysis tool and RACI is a responsibility matrix.
Clean Air Mercury Rule of 2005 was specifically targeted at regulating and reducing mercury emissions in what industry?
EPA's 2005 Clean Air Mercury Rule targeted mercury from coal-fired power plants through a cap-and-trade program (vacated in 2008).

Greater Bulk Cartage has three 1,000 gallon above-ground storage tanks (AST). Two have about 500 gallons of diesel each. The other is nearly empty, containing only a few gallons of gasoline.
In a recent inspection of their fuel storage, the inspector cited them for not having an SPCC plan. The EHS manager complained, stating that they never have more than 1000 gallons of diesel at any time, and the gasoline tank is no longer in use. Did the citation stand?
Yes, because the inspector has a lot of leeway when interpreting the rules.
Yes, because the requirement for an SPCC plan is based on capacity.
No, because the amount on hand at any one time is less than 1,320 gallons.
No, because fuel is exempt from the rule.
40 CFR 112 SPCC applies when aggregate aboveground oil storage capacity exceeds 1,320 gal (containers 55 gal or larger); 3 x 1,000 gal = 3,000 gal of capacity, regardless of actual contents.
Leadership in Environmental Excellence and Development
Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design
LEED is Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design, the USGBC green building rating system.
What is the primary purpose of conducting a Training Needs Assessment (TNA)?
To evaluate the effectiveness of past training programs
To identify specific training needs based on current competencies and desired performance levels
To assess the financial resources available for training
To finalize the training schedule for the year
A TNA identifies the gap between current and required performance so training targets real needs. Evaluating past training is effectiveness evaluation, not needs assessment.
In a Task Matrix, what does the intersection of a specific task and a role typically indicate?
The cost associated with that task
The relevance of the task to the specific role
The timeline for completing the task
The location where the task is performed
In a task (training) matrix, the intersection shows whether a task applies to a role, which defines required training for that role.
Which of the following is a key benefit of using a Task Matrix during the Training Needs Assessment process?
It helps in identifying which tasks are outdated or obsolete.
It assists in determining the financial budget for each department.
It facilitates the alignment of specific tasks with the appropriate roles and identifies training gaps.
It provides a social platform for employees to communicate.
A task matrix maps tasks to roles and current qualifications, revealing who needs which training (the gap).
As an organization's culture transitions towards a safety-centric approach, which indicators should stakeholders expect to observe?
Increased safety audits, revised disciplinary program, and mandatory performance goals.
Reduction in injury reports, fewer regulatory citations, and higher profits.
Additional safety professionals, more formal training, and monetary incentives
Management support, open communication, and company-wide participation.
A culture shift shows up as management support, open communication and company-wide participation. Fewer injuries and citations are lagging results, and more audits or incentives are inputs.
What considerations should be made to effectively communicate the company's risk management plan to all employees?
Distribute a printed version and require a signature to confirm receipt.
Understand your audience's level of understanding, education, and knowledge.
Email the entire plan as an attachment to ensure all employees receive every detail.
Summarize the key elements of the plan to avoid confusion.
Effective risk communication is tailored to the audience's knowledge, education and language; dumping the full plan or a signature does not ensure understanding.
What financial impact can effective safety programs have on a company?
They increase the cost of training significantly
They can lead to higher insurance premiums
They can reduce costs associated with accidents and legal fees
Effective programs reduce direct and indirect accident costs (workers' compensation, legal fees, lost productivity) and can lower EMR and premiums.
Which one of these statements is true?
It’s best to use multi-factor authentication to access areas of the business network with sensitive information.
You should use the same password for key business devices to guarantee that high-level employees can access them in an emergency.
The best way to protect business data is to make sure no one loses any device.
You shouldn’t limit login attempts on key business devices, because getting locked out for having too many incorrect attempts would leave you unable to access your accounts.
Multi-factor authentication adds a second factor so a stolen password alone cannot access sensitive systems (NIST/CISA guidance).
Using deception to manipulate you into revealing confidential or personal information that may be used for fraudulent purposes called:
Social engineering manipulates people (phishing, pretexting) into revealing confidential information or granting access.
What should an employee do if they witness violent behavior in the workplace?
Ignore the situation and hope it goes away
Report the behavior to a supervisor or human resources immediately
Attempt to physically subdue the individual
Workers should report violent behavior immediately to supervision, HR or security and not confront or physically intervene.
The lower flammable limit of a flammable gas or vapor is the:
Lowest concentration of the gas or vapor in air, expressed as a percentage, that can be ignited
Highest concentration of the gas or vapor in air, expressed as a percentage, that can be ignited
Amount, in grams or kilograms, that can be ignited
Amount that is equivalent to the limiting oxygen percentage that can be ignited
The LFL (LEL) is the minimum concentration of a gas or vapor in air, in volume percent, that can propagate a flame when ignited.
OSHA requires _____________ air changes an hour in a flammable liquid storage room. Ref 1910.106
1910.106(d)(4)(iv) requires inside storage room ventilation capable of at least six complete air changes per hour.
Which of the following is considered to be the most important source of fire standards in the industry today?
NFPA publishes the consensus codes (NFPA 1, 13, 70, 101, etc.) that are most widely adopted and referenced by OSHA and local jurisdictions.
The lower flammable limit of a flammable gas or vapor of a flammable liquid (expressed at a specified temperature and pressure) is the:
Lowest concentration of the gas or vapor in air, expressed as a percentage, that can be ignited
Highest concentration of the gas or vapor in air, expressed as a percentage, that can be ignited
Amount, in grams or kilograms, that can be ignited
Amount that is equivalent to the limiting oxygen percentage that can be ignited
The LFL is the lowest volume percent of gas or vapor in air that can be ignited and propagate a flame at specified temperature and pressure.
What is the atomic number of carbon?
Carbon has 6 protons, so its atomic number is 6 (atomic mass about 12).
What is the atomic number of an element determined by?
The number of protons in the nucleus
The number of neutrons in the nucleus
The total number of protons and neutrons in the nucleus
The number of electrons surrounding the nucleus
Atomic number equals the number of protons in the nucleus; protons plus neutrons give the mass number.
According to 1926.502(b)(1), the top rail of a guardrail system must be a height of ____ inches +/- 3 inches above the walking/working level.
1926.502(b)(1) requires the top rail at 42 in +/- 3 in (39-45 in) above the walking/working surface.
From what do the majority of fatal falls occur?

BLS data show roofs, then ladders and scaffolds, account for most fatal falls in construction; roofs and scaffolds is the best option given. Note: BLS ranks roofs then ladders; scaffolds not second, but A is still best option.
According to OSHA, fall protection must be provided at elevations of how many feet or more in general industry workplaces?
1910.28(b)(1) requires fall protection at 4 ft in general industry (5 ft shipyards, 6 ft construction, 8 ft longshoring).
What Theory says - Accident results from a completed sequence of factors; ignores system weaknesses.
Heinrich's domino theory treats an accident as the last in a linear sequence of factors and is criticized for ignoring management and system weaknesses.

After a situation, an incident management team will analyze the situation through a series of stages. Once the incident is reported and the investigation begins, the team will secure and document the scene and interview witnesses. Which of the following should occur after witnesses are interviewed?
An event root cause analysis is conducted
A conduct behavior discipline analysis is established
After evidence and witness information are collected, the team analyzes it to determine root causes; corrective recommendations and the report follow.
The process of investigating incidents or injuries employs a causal factor analysis to identify elements that played a direct role in the event. This method is commonly known as a:
Root cause analysis identifies causal factors and the underlying system causes that, if corrected, prevent recurrence.
What is the first step in designing an effective training course?
Analysis comes first (ADDIE): assessing the audience's baseline knowledge defines the gap from which objectives are written.
When designing a training course, why is it important to assess the target audience’s baseline knowledge level?
To ensure the content is neither too easy nor too difficult for the participants
To determine the budget for training materials
Knowing baseline knowledge sets the right level of content and avoids boring experienced learners or overwhelming novices.
Which method is effective for determining the baseline knowledge of your target audience before designing a training course?
Using the same material for all sessions regardless of the audience
Pre-training surveys or pre-tests measure what the audience already knows before design begins.

Asbestos fibers cause scarring of the alveoli, thus preventing effective oxygenation of the blood. The MOST effective control method to prevent asbestos fibers from entering the respiratory system is:
Provide full containment and negative air pressure for any work with asbestos.
Wear an N95 two-strap dust mask.
Cover mouth and nose with a clean 100% cotton cloth.
Asbestos becomes hazardous when friable fibers are released; keeping ACM intact (managing in place, encapsulation) prevents fiber release at the source, ahead of containment or respirators.

The manganese level sampled for the welders are 13 times over the 0.02 mg/m³ TLV.
What should your initial response be?
Stop the welding and subcontract it out.
Require the welders to have PAPR until the ventilation expense can proceed through the management team.
Require N95 respirators to be worn.
Provide fans to dilute the welding fume.
At 13x the TLV, interim protection is needed immediately; a PAPR (APF 25-1,000) covers 13x, while an N95 (APF 10) does not, and fans spread fume. Ventilation remains the permanent fix.
An investment of $20,000 earns an annual interest rate of 2.5%, compounded annually. Using F = P(1 + i)^n, what is the approximate future value after 3.5 years?
F = 20,000 x 1.025^3.5 = 20,000 x 1.0903 = about $21,805. Trap: using simple interest or rounding n to 4 or more.
What does a 95% confidence interval for a population mean indicate?
The population mean is 95% larger than the sample mean
95% of the sample data fall within the interval
Any single interval has exactly 95% of the population values
If sampling were repeated many times, about 95% of the intervals built this way would contain the true mean
Confidence describes the method's long-run capture rate of the true mean, not the spread of individual data points.
Pareto Analysis is particularly useful for which of the following?
Determining the financial stability of a company.
Identifying the causes of problems to prioritize solutions that will have the greatest impact.
Estimating the exact financial loss due to various business activities.
Assigning tasks to employees in an organization
Pareto analysis (80/20 rule) ranks causes by frequency or cost so effort goes to the vital few with the greatest impact.

Ensuring the well-being and safety of workers involves managing their physical health and mental well-being. What is the term used for a program that offers assistance to employees dealing with personal, physical, or stress-related issues through a network of professional services and trained providers?
An Employee Assistance Program provides confidential counseling and referral for personal, health, stress and substance issues.
Which element represents a risk management function important for the overall success of a safety management program?
Hazard and risk identification and assessment is the core risk management function; injury reports and EMR are lagging outcomes.
An organization has many activities, in which each of these activities may create hazards. The range, nature, distribution, and significance of the hazards is called_______? DY p.594 2ndEd
Per Yates, the range, nature, distribution and significance of hazards created by an organization's activities is its hazard burden.
Air carriers that generate Foreign Object Debris are found frequently in what location.
Foreign object debris is a hazard on the airport apron, ramps and taxiways where aircraft operate and debris can be ingested by engines.

Compressed air should be used to clean your clothes at what pressure?
Ref: [https://www.osha.gov/.../standardinterpretations/1994-01-14](https://www.osha.gov/.../standardinterpretations/1994-01-14)
OSHA interpretation: using compressed air to clean clothing worn by a person is prohibited at any pressure because air can enter the skin or eyes; 30 psi in 1910.242(b) applies to cleaning surfaces.
Which is a correct statement regarding completion of the daily job/task hazard analysis (JHA)?
The JHA must be completed by the project manager.
The JHA form must be completed and documented in English.
The JHA form should be developed with contributions from all employees involved in the documented task(s).
The JHA is only required to be completed on the first day of the project
A JHA should be developed with the workers who perform the task, since they know the steps and hazards best (OSHA 3071).
A single term algebraic expression is called?
A monomial is a single-term algebraic expression (e.g., 3x^2); binomials have two terms and trinomials three.
If a triangle has a sum of internal angles of 180 degrees, What is the sum of internal angles OF A SQUARE?
Interior angle sum = (n - 2) x 180 = (4 - 2) x 180 = 360 degrees for a square.
What is the weight of a cylinder of water that is 5 feet high and 1 feet in radius? Water weighs 62.4 lbs/cuft
V = pi x r^2 x h = 3.1416 x 1^2 x 5 = 15.71 ft^3; weight = 15.71 x 62.4 lb/ft^3 = 980 lb, about 979 lb.

Where the eyes or body of any person may be exposed to injurious ________________ materials, suitable facilities for quick drenching or flushing of the eyes and body shall be provided within the work area for immediate emergency use. 1910.151c
1910.151(c) requires quick-drench or eye-flush facilities where employees may be exposed to injurious corrosive materials (ANSI Z358.1 gives 10-second access).
Smoke management is for the benefit of occupants and firefighters. What are the three principles that are necessary?
Smoke management relies on controlling air flow, using buoyancy of hot smoke (stack effect, venting) and compartmentation to limit spread (NFPA 92).
A warehouse has a spill of a chemical, where would the BEST place to quickly find the emergency cleanup information?
The SDS (Section 6, accidental release measures) is the readily available source of spill cleanup information required at the workplace.
What is the primary purpose of conducting a pilot class during course development?
To give the primary instructors a break
To test the course materials and delivery methods before full rollout
To finalize the annual training schedule
A pilot is a trial run with a representative audience so content, timing, materials, and methods can be corrected before the course is delivered widely.
What is a representative training sample in the context of a pilot class?
A small group of participants that accurately reflects the larger audience's characteristics
Any group that is available at the time of the pilot
Only new employees who need the most training
A representative pilot sample mirrors the target audience's experience and characteristics so feedback reflects real learners.
What should be evaluated during a pilot class to improve the final course?
The quantity of the training materials needed
The effectiveness of the training environment, materials, and instructor methods
The personal style of the participants
The time it takes for the instructor to travel to the training location
Pilot evaluation examines materials, environment and instructional methods to revise the course before full delivery.
Who can perform emergency medical response and rescue in a confined space?
Anyone who can respond inside the recommended four-minute window
The company confined space rescue and response team
Either an onsite or offsite trained rescue team with immediate availability
1910.146(k) allows onsite or offsite rescue services if they are evaluated, trained, equipped and able to respond in a timely manner for the hazards.
What should be included in the structure of COMMAND responsibilities in an emergency response scenario?
Directing all emergency activities, ensuring outside emergency services are notified, and directing shutdown or evacuation of the affected facility.
Safety of property, materials, and the public.
Trained hazardous materials responder, personal protective equipment, and self-contained breathing apparatus certified.
Authority to issue orders to employees, first aid trained, multi-lingual, and be a certified first responder.
Command (incident commander) directs all response activities, notifies outside agencies and orders shutdown or evacuation, per 1910.120(q) and ICS.
Which elements should be included as common components in an emergency response plan?
A written plan, an identified chain of command, emergency response team, training, medical assistance provision, and personal protective equipment
