A public relations spokesperson, company officer, emergency transportation vehicles, and legal representation
Fire-fighting equipment, chemical spill clean-up kit, trained medical professionals, dedicated communication equipment, and evacuation equipment
Food, water, extra clothing, and accommodations for evacuees
Common ERP components include a written plan, chain of command, response team, training, medical assistance and PPE (1910.38/1910.120).
Which is the correct order for lockout.
Energy isolation, Shutdown machine or equipment, Isolate equipment, Notify employees
Notify employees, Prepare for shutdown, Lockout, Verify Isolation,
Application of control, Lockout tagout, Isolate equipment, Shutdown machine or equipment
Lockout, Isolate equipment, Shutdown machine or equipment, Notify employees
1910.147(d) sequence: prepare and notify, shut down, isolate, apply lockout devices, release stored energy, then verify isolation; option B follows that order.
What is a lockout device used for?
To sound an alarm if someone tries to restart a locked out machine
To physically lock the control switch, valve, or energy source in an inoperative position
To track which employees have locked out which machines
To provide lighting for working on locked out equipment
A lockout device uses a positive means (lock) to hold an energy-isolating device in the safe, off position (1910.147(b)).
Which of the following is a necessary component of an effective lockout/tagout program?
Training only new employees on the procedures
Using a universal lock that fits all types of machinery
Implementing the procedures only for electrical equipment
1910.147(c)(4) requires documented, equipment-specific energy control procedures stating steps for shutdown, isolation, securing and verification.

At least one copy of the ________________________data, which identifies the registered professional engineer who approved the data, shall be maintained at the jobsite during construction of the protective system.
1926.652(c)(3)(iv) requires a copy of the tabulated data, identifying the approving registered professional engineer, to be kept at the jobsite.
Trench boxes must be within ____ feet of the bottom of the trench.
1926.652(g)(2) permits excavation up to 2 ft below the bottom of a shield if it is designed for the full depth and there is no indication of soil loss.

The contractor’s excavation undermines a buildings foundation. If he is not going to support or underpin the building, whose approval must he obtain before sending employees into an excavation according to the OSHA standard? Ref: 1926.651 (i)
1926.651(i)(2) allows excavation below a foundation without support or underpinning only if a registered professional engineer approves that the structure is not endangered.
Safety management systems require several basic elements to be successful. Which is one of those elements?
Hazard identification, analysis and prevention/control is a core SMS element (OSHA Recommended Practices, ANSI Z10); EMR, injury rates and premiums are outcomes.
Which is the PRIMARY constituent of galvanized steel that causes metal fume fever in welders?

Galvanized steel is coated with zinc; welding or cutting it volatilizes zinc oxide fume, the classic cause of metal fume fever (flu-like chills, fever). Iron oxide causes siderosis and manganese causes neurological effects, not typical metal fume fever.
What is the primary purpose of wearing a welding helmet during welding operations?
To protect the eyes and face from ultraviolet and infrared rays emitted during welding
To keep the hair and head clean

Welding arcs emit intense UV and IR radiation plus spatter; a helmet with the correct ANSI Z87.1 filter shade protects the eyes and face from arc flash (photokeratitis) and burns. It does not improve visibility or protect hearing.
Why is it important to work in a well-ventilated area while welding?
To reduce the risk of fire
To avoid inhaling harmful fumes and gases
To prevent others from walking into the work area

Welding generates metal fumes and gases (ozone, NOx, CO, shielding gas displacement); ventilation per OSHA 1910.252 / ANSI Z49.1 keeps concentrations below exposure limits so workers avoid inhaling them.

The management of change process covers four primary concepts, regardless of the type of change. Three of these are:
Identification of hazards associated with the change
Assessment of the risks associated with the change
Consideration of the hazards and risks prior to the change
Which is the fourth primary concept?
Implementation of controls needed to address hazards and risks associated with the change
Performance of a "what if" analysis to identify expected risks
Hiring of additional management personnel to oversee and direct organizational change
Compliance with all applicable regulatory guidelines regarding changes in an occupational health and safety management program
The fourth element is implementing controls to address the hazards and risks identified for the change; identification and assessment are useless without control.
The organization tasked with developing and updating standards for explosion prevention and combustible dust safety is:

NFPA develops consensus codes on combustible dust and explosion prevention (e.g., NFPA 652, 654, 68, 69). OSHA enforces regulations, the CSB investigates incidents, and EPA addresses environmental releases.
What is a common cause of secondary combustible dust explosions?
Ignition of accumulated dust layers within the facility
Ignition of a small amount of dust in a confined space

A primary explosion or disturbance lofts accumulated dust from beams, ledges and floors into a cloud that then ignites, producing a larger secondary explosion. Housekeeping to remove dust layers is the key prevention.
What is a primary method for controlling combustible dust hazards?
Keeping the workplace temperature below freezing
Regular cleaning to minimize dust accumulation
Only operating machinery during daylight hours
Banning all electronic devices in the area

Controlling dust accumulation through housekeeping (NFPA 652/654), along with dust collection and ignition source control, removes the fuel needed for primary and secondary explosions. The other options do nothing to control fuel.
Which strategy is MOST effective in reducing risks to employees?

Elimination is the top of the hierarchy of controls (ANSI/ASSP Z10) because it removes the hazard entirely. Risk assessment, documentation and training identify or manage risk but do not physically remove it.

Conveyors create in-running nip points where a belt or chain meets a pulley, sprocket or roller, a major caught-in hazard requiring guarding (OSHA 1910.212, ASME B20.1). Reciprocating motion and shear points are more typical of presses and cutters.
These devices use a series of cables attached to the operator's hands, wrists, and/or arms that withdraw the operators hands from the point of operation.

Pullback devices use cables attached to the operator's hands or wrists that physically withdraw the hands as the press ram descends (OSHA 1910.217). Restraint devices hold hands back at all times rather than pulling them away.
What is the MOST important thing to do before performing maintenance on a conveyor system?

Before maintenance, hazardous energy must be isolated and locked out/tagged out per OSHA 1910.147 so the conveyor cannot start unexpectedly. Notifying a supervisor and PPE are secondary to energy control.
What is a common indicator that a trainee might be confused during a training session?
The trainee asks many relevant questions
The trainee has frequent eye contact with the trainer
The trainee avoids asking questions even when prompted
A confused trainee often withdraws and avoids asking questions even when prompted, fearing embarrassment. Relevant questions, detailed notes and eye contact are signs of engagement, not confusion.
If a trainee is browsing the internet during training, what is this most likely an indicator of?**
High engagement in the training material
Browsing the internet during instruction is an off-task behavior signaling disengagement; the trainer should re-engage the learner with interaction or activities.
Which of the following body language cues may indicate that a trainee is disengaged or confused?
Making direct eye contact with the instructor
Fidgeting or doodling are common nonverbal cues of boredom, disengagement or confusion. Leaning forward, nodding, relaxed posture and eye contact usually indicate attention.
Crane Operator training. The employer must provide each operator-in-training with sufficient training, through a: Reference 1926.1427
Session of handons use of the crane.
Combination of formal and practical instruction,
Verification the operator has a driver’s license

OSHA 1926.1427 requires that operators-in-training receive sufficient training through a combination of formal and practical instruction to operate the equipment safely. Lectures or hands-on use alone are insufficient, and a driver's license is irrelevant.

To make an eye in a wire rope, How many clips are required?
Ref. 1926.251(c)(5)
One with the u-bolt on the dead end.
Two with the u-bolts on the live end.
Three with the u-bolts on the dead end.
Four with the u-bolts on the live end.

Per OSHA 1926.251(c)(5)(i) Table H-20, U-bolt clips on an eye splice must have the U-bolt on the dead (short) end and saddle on the live end; minimum for small common rope sizes is three clips. Remember: never saddle a dead horse.
Which of the following is the MOST important factor in ensuring crane safety on a construction site?
Using the newest and most advanced crane model
Proper training and certification of crane operators
Painting the hand signals on the crane.
Having the crane inspected once a year

Most crane incidents involve human error, so trained and certified operators (OSHA 1926.1427) are the most important safety factor. A new model or annual-only inspection does not address operator competence, and frequent inspections are also required.

An example of good training preparation is one where the organization has a provided a __________to the trainer with identification of the gaps in employees’ knowledge and skills before these gaps start creating real issues that can affect the organization.
Past test scores of the students.

A training needs analysis identifies gaps between required and current knowledge/skills before they cause problems, so the trainer can target content. Curricula and past scores do not by themselves define current gaps.
What is the primary goal of brainstorming?
To critically evaluate each idea as it is suggested
To generate as many ideas as possible in a short period
To identify the best idea quickly
Brainstorming aims to generate as many ideas as possible quickly while deferring judgment; evaluation and selection come afterward. Critiquing ideas during generation suppresses creativity.
What technique can be used to expand on ideas generated during a brainstorming session?
Voting on each idea to determine the best one immediately
Ignoring less popular ideas to focus on the most liked ones
Building on others’ ideas through open discussion and collaboration
Limiting discussion time strictly to 10 minutes per idea

Brainstorming expands ideas by building on others' contributions (piggybacking) through open, nonjudgmental discussion. Immediate voting, discarding unpopular ideas and rigid time limits stifle idea development.
The perimeter of a lot that is 100 ft long and 60 ft is ________ feet.
Perimeter = 2(L + W) = 2(100 ft + 60 ft) = 320 ft. 6,000 is the area in square feet and 160 is only L + W.
What is the formula for the area of a rectangle?
Area of a rectangle = Length x Width, giving square units. 2(Length + Width) is the perimeter.
When considering the geometry of a workspace, which shape is typically considered the most stable for scaffolding?

The triangle is the most rigid, stable geometric shape because it cannot deform without changing a side length; scaffolds and trusses gain stability through triangulation (diagonal cross-bracing). An unbraced square frame can rack into a parallelogram.

When a tag is attached to an energy isolating means, it is not to be removed without authorization of the ____________ person responsible for it, and it is never to be bypassed, ignored, or otherwise defeated.
KEY CORRECTED by trainer review: 1910.147: a tag is not removed without authorization of the AUTHORIZED person responsible for it.
What does a lockout device do?
It identifies the operator of the machine
It physically prevents the energization or start-up of a machine or equipment

Per OSHA 1910.147, a lockout device uses a positive means such as a lock to hold an energy-isolating device in a safe position, physically preventing energization or start-up. A tag only warns; it does not physically prevent operation.
When can a lockout/tagout device be removed and by whom?
By any worker when the job is perceived as finished
By the maintenance team at the end of the shift
Only by the authorized employee who applied it, after ensuring the work is completed and the area is safe
By the site manager at any time

OSHA 1910.147(e)(3) requires each lockout/tagout device to be removed by the authorized employee who applied it, after verifying work is complete, tools removed and employees clear. Removal by others is allowed only under the strict exception procedure.
What the MOST important element listed of a comprehensive safety management system?

Incident investigation and reporting is a core SMS element (ANSI Z10, ISO 45001 clause 10.2) because it identifies root causes and drives corrective action and continual improvement. Incentives, budgets and productivity programs support but are not core safety elements.
How can safety professionals promote a strong safety culture within an organization?
Ignoring safety non-compliance to avoid conflicts
Leading by example and demonstrating a commitment to safety
Limiting communication about safety to top management only
Providing minimal safety training to reduce costs

Visible leadership commitment and leading by example are foundational to a strong safety culture (ANSI Z10, ISO 45001 clause 5.1). Ignoring noncompliance, restricting communication and minimizing training erode culture.
What is the MOST common challenge faced by safety professionals in the field?
Ensuring 100% employee engagement at all times
Balancing productivity and safety without compromise
Compliance with regulations is unnecessary for safety professionals
Unlimited resources for safety program management
Safety professionals commonly must balance production pressure with safety requirements, integrating safety into operations without compromise. The other options are unrealistic or false statements.
Why Is PPE Typically Considered the Last Resort For Controlling Hazards?
Workers do not fit in many PPE. Front-line workers are involved in the PPE selection process.
PPE needs to be constantly replaced.
PPE doesn’t eliminate hazards, and sometimes introduces them.
Workers do not want to wear it because it’s uncomfortable.

PPE is the least effective control because it does not eliminate or reduce the hazard at its source; it relies on correct fit, use and maintenance, and can introduce hazards such as heat stress or reduced visibility.
Which control measure focuses on changing work practices and procedures?

Administrative controls change how people work (procedures, scheduling, rotation, training, signage). Elimination and substitution remove or replace the hazard, and PPE places a barrier on the worker.
What is the purpose of the hierarchy of controls?
To prioritize control measures based on their effectiveness in reducing or eliminating hazards
To minimize the use of personal protective equipment
To save costs by implementing the cheapest controls first

The hierarchy of controls ranks control measures from most effective (elimination) to least effective (PPE) so the most protective feasible option is chosen first. Compliance and cost are not its purpose.
What is the primary goal of remediation in a training program?
To discipline trainees who did not meet the standard
To provide additional instruction and support so trainees can meet the learning objectives
To evaluate a trainee's future potential in the organization
To reduce the training time allocated to each trainee
Remediation closes individual learning gaps with targeted re-instruction and practice, then reassesses. It is corrective, not punitive.
Which of the following is an effective method for remediating trainees who are struggling to understand the material?
Increasing the complexity of the information

One-on-one coaching provides individualized explanation, practice and feedback targeted to the trainee's specific difficulty, which is an effective remediation method. Increasing complexity, reducing interaction or blaming hinder learning.
What should be considered when designing a training program to ensure it accommodates the need for remediation?
Including a variety of learning materials and methods to cater to different learning styles
Making the content as difficult as possible to challenge trainees
Limiting access to remedial resources to motivate independent learning
Focusing solely on theoretical knowledge without practical application

Providing varied materials and methods (visual, auditory, reading, hands-on) accommodates different learning styles and gives struggling trainees alternative paths for remediation, consistent with adult learning principles.
What is the maximum speed at which a forklift should be driven in a workplace where pedestrians are present ?
There is no maximum speed set by OSHA.

OSHA 1910.178 does not specify a numeric forklift speed limit; it requires safe speed for conditions, slowing at cross aisles and obstructed views, and yielding to pedestrians. Employers often set site limits (e.g., 5 mph), but OSHA does not.
Which of the following should NOT be present in the crane operating area?

Unauthorized personnel must be kept out of the crane swing radius and fall zone (OSHA 1926.1424 work area control and 1926.1425 keeping clear of the load). Signage, manuals and emergency stops are expected safety features.

Wire rope shall not be used if, in any length of eight diameters, the total number of visible broken wires exceeds ______ percent of the total number of wires, or if the rope shows other signs of excessive wear, corrosion, or defect.
Ref: 1926.251(c)(4)(iv)
OSHA 1926.251(c)(4)(iv) prohibits using wire rope when visible broken wires exceed 10 percent of total wires in any length of eight diameters, or when it shows excessive wear, corrosion or defects.
Which is an example of plagiarism?
Reading a paragraph online and retyping it in your own words.
Copying and pasting someone else's work into your paper using quotation marks and citing the author
Typing a paper in your own words
Copying and pasting a sentence from the Internet into your paper.

Pasting another's sentence into your paper without quotation marks or citation presents their words as your own, which is plagiarism. Quoted and cited material, and your own words, are not plagiarism.
The legal responsibilities of an employer with regards to health and safety include what?
Charging employees for replacing damaged or lost PPE
Taking out additional insurances for dangerous work
Providing safe place of work for all employees
Ensuring that only one member of staff works on a dangerous job

Under the OSH Act General Duty Clause (Section 5(a)(1)), employers must provide a workplace free from recognized serious hazards. OSHA generally requires employers to pay for required PPE, so charging employees is not a duty.
What is a universal aspect of professional ethics in the safety, health, and environmental profession, irrespective of the specific field of expertise?

Practicing only within one's area of individual professional competence is universal to ethics codes (BCSP Code of Ethics, ASSP), regardless of specialty. Certification, hazmat management and compliance are field-specific or not universal ethical tenets.
What is the primary cause of groundwater contamination?
Leaching of contaminants from the soil

Groundwater is mainly contaminated when pollutants from spills, landfills, septic systems, USTs or agriculture leach downward through soil into aquifers. Air pollution and activated carbon filtering are not primary pathways.
What is a common indicator of groundwater contamination?**
Change in water taste, odor, or color
Contamination often shows as a change in water taste, odor or color (e.g., petroleum odor, metallic taste, discoloration), though many contaminants are undetectable and require lab testing.
Which method is commonly used to remediate contaminated groundwater?

Pump-and-treat extracts contaminated groundwater through wells and treats it above ground (air stripping, carbon adsorption), the most common groundwater remediation method. Thermal desorption and composting treat soils, not groundwater.
What is the most important safety measure when storing oxidizers?
Storing them near heat sources to maintain stability
Keeping them in a damp environment
Separating them from fuels and other combustibles

Oxidizers supply oxygen that intensifies combustion, so NFPA 400 and OSHA require segregating them from fuels, flammables and combustibles, away from heat. Heat, dampness and cloth coverings increase fire risk.
What should you do in the event of an oxidizer spill in the workplace?
Ignore the spill if it is small
Quickly wash the spill away with lots of water
Evacuate the area and follow the emergency response plan
Use a standard broom to sweep the spill up

Oxidizer spills can ignite combustibles or react violently, so personnel should evacuate and follow the emergency response plan (OSHA 1910.38/1910.120) with trained responders. A broom introduces combustible material and water can spread the spill.
A lithium-ion battery fire in a fully charged electric vehicle could be which two classes for fire?

In an EV lithium-ion battery fire, the electrolyte is a flammable liquid (Class B) and the battery is an energized electrical source (Class C). It is not a combustible metal (Class D) fire because lithium-ion cells contain little metallic lithium. Note: Vehicle interior also burns as Class A; B and C is the best fit among options.
What is the Safety Case Approach?
An incident investigation technique required in the United Kingdom Health and Safety Executive.
Regulatory system where a company presents it’s case that a facility is safe to operate.
A systematic method of assessing and prioritizing hazards in an industrial facility
A contested OSHA inspection which has become a litigation case

The safety case is a regulatory approach (used in the UK, Australia, offshore) in which the operator presents a documented, evidence-based argument that a facility is acceptably safe to operate. It is not an investigation technique or litigation.
Match the person with the work - Acquired Needs Theory

David McClelland developed Acquired Needs Theory: needs for achievement, affiliation and power are learned through experience. McGregor proposed Theory X/Y, Likert the management systems, and Argyris the maturity-immaturity theory.
Failure Modes and Effects Analysis (FMEA) is a step-by-step approach for identifying all possible __________ in a design or process.
FMEA systematically identifies all possible failure modes of each component or process step, then evaluates their effects and causes and prioritizes them (RPN = severity x occurrence x detection).
A________________ diagram helps team members visually diagram a problem or condition's root causes, allowing them to truly diagnose the problem rather than focusing on symptoms.

A fishbone (Ishikawa or cause-and-effect) diagram organizes potential root causes into categories (people, methods, machines, materials, environment, measurement) to diagnose the problem rather than its symptoms.
The three basic steps of the behavior based safety processes are:
Interview the worker, write an action plan, and recommend corrective acts.
Identify critical behaviors, conduct measurement through observations, and give performance feedback.
Choose a data recording method, divide the work in small categories and, record a video.
Behavior-based safety follows an ABC-based process: identify critical safe/at-risk behaviors, measure them through observation, and provide performance feedback to reinforce safe behavior.
When faced with disagreements during consensus-building in training, the trainer should:
Ignore the disagreements and move on
Encourage participants to explore the reasons behind their differing views
Side with the majority opinion without further discussion
Dismiss participants who disagree with the trainer's perspective

Consensus-building requires exploring the reasons behind differing views so underlying concerns surface and a shared understanding can form. Ignoring, siding with the majority or dismissing dissent undermines buy-in.
When is the best time to build consensus during a training session?
At the beginning of the session, before introducing any new material.
Throughout the session, as new topics or concepts are introduced.
Only during designated group activities or discussions.
At the end of the session, after all material has been covered.
Consensus is best built continuously as each new topic or concept is introduced, checking understanding and agreement before moving on rather than only at the start or end.
How should a trainer handle a situation where two groups in a training session have conflicting opinions?
Choose the side that aligns most closely with the trainer's own views.
Ignore the conflict and proceed with the training agenda as planned.
Ask each group to identify common ground and build a solution from there

Asking conflicting groups to identify common ground and build a solution from it is a collaborative approach that produces true consensus. Voting creates winners and losers, and siding or ignoring conflict reduces engagement.
Equipment and associated wiring approved as _________________ safe is permitted in any hazardous (classified) location for which it is approved. Ref 1910.307(c)(1)

OSHA 1910.307(c)(1) permits intrinsically safe equipment and associated wiring in any hazardous (classified) location for which it is approved, because it cannot release enough energy to ignite the atmosphere.
What is the primary function of a Ground Fault Circuit Interrupter (GFCI)?**
To prevent electrical fires by detecting temperature increases
To protect circuits from overload by breaking the circuit
To prevent electrical shock by interrupting faulty circuits
To reduce energy consumption in household appliances

A GFCI detects a current imbalance between hot and neutral (about 4-6 mA) and trips quickly to prevent electrocution. Overload protection is a circuit breaker's role and fire prevention from arcs is an AFCI's role.
The NFPA code to protect workers from shock and arc flashes is NFPA ________________
NFPA 70E, Standard for Electrical Safety in the Workplace, addresses shock and arc flash protection. NFPA 30 covers flammable liquids, NFPA 101 is the Life Safety Code, and NFPA 70 is the NEC.

Leading indicators measure proactive activities and conditions (inspections, training, near-miss reports) that predict future performance before harm occurs. Lagging indicators are reactive, measuring outcomes after the fact.
Why are lagging indicators important in safety management?
They help identify potential future risks and safety needs.
They provide data on past incidents to guide safety improvements.
They are solely used for regulatory compliance.
They indicate the level of proactive safety measures taken.

Lagging indicators (injury rates, DART, lost workdays) measure past outcomes, providing data to evaluate results and guide improvements. Predicting future risk and measuring proactive activity describe leading indicators.
Which of the following is an example of a lagging indicator?
Number of safety meetings held per month.
Total number of workdays lost due to injuries.
Lost workdays due to injury is an outcome measure after harm has occurred, so it is lagging. Safety meetings, perception surveys and new protocols are leading, activity-based measures.
A two-piece block and tackle with 4 part of rope to lift a weight of 2,000 lbs. requires how much force for lift (no friction)? ___________________ lbs.? [See image below]
Ideal mechanical advantage equals the number of rope parts supporting the load: F = W / n = 2,000 lb / 4 = 500 lb, ignoring friction.
The rigger must know the load weight and the _________ before lifting an odd shaped load off a trailer with slings.

Riggers must know the load weight and its center of gravity so slings can be placed and the hook positioned directly above the CG; otherwise the load tilts, shifts or overloads a sling leg. Truck weight and manufacturer are irrelevant.

Special custom design grabs, hooks, clamps, or other lifting accessories, for such units as modular panels, prefabricated structures and similar materials, shall be marked to indicate the safe working loads and shall be proof-tested prior to use to____ percent of them rated load.
Ref: 1926.251(a)(4)
OSHA 1926.251(a)(4) requires special custom lifting accessories to be marked with safe working loads and proof-tested to 125 percent of their rated load before use.

All damaged tools must be removed from service and:
Ref https://www.osha.gov/.../files/publications/osha3080.pdf
Stored in a damaged tool area
Damage them to the point that no one else can use them
OSHA's Hand and Power Tools guidance (OSHA 3080) states damaged tools must be removed from service and tagged 'Do Not Use' so no one uses them until repaired or replaced.
If a power tool has a frayed cord or damaged plug, what should you do?**
Use it quickly and then put it away
Report it and ensure it is not used until it is repaired by a qualified person
Ignore it if it still turns on

A frayed cord or damaged plug creates shock and fire hazards; the tool must be removed from service, reported, and repaired by a qualified person before use (OSHA 1926.302/1910.242 and 1910.334). Tape repairs are not acceptable.
All HAND and power tools shall be:
Kept in an approved storage container

OSHA 1926.300(a) (and 1910.242(a)) requires all hand and power tools, whether employer- or employee-furnished, to be maintained in a safe condition. Not every tool requires a guard or monthly testing.
Which chemical has the lowest atomic weight?
Hydrogen has the lowest atomic weight of any element, about 1.008 g/mol. Helium is about 4, nitrogen 14 and oxygen 16.
Give the ratio in which hydrogen and oxygen are present in water by volume.
Water (H2O) forms from 2 volumes of hydrogen gas and 1 volume of oxygen gas (Gay-Lussac's law of combining volumes), so 2:1 by volume. By mass the ratio is 1:8.
Balance atoms: P4O6 needs 4 P and 6 O; 6 O atoms = 3 O2 molecules. So 4P + 3O2 -> P4O6, coefficients 4:3.
A ladder (or stairway) must be provided at all work points of access where there is a break in elevation of __________________ inches. 1926.1051

OSHA 1926.1051(a) requires a stairway or ladder at all personnel points of access where there is a break in elevation of 19 inches (48 cm) or more, unless a ramp, runway, embankment or personnel hoist is provided.
What angle should an extension ladder be placed at for safe use?
An extension ladder should be set at about 75.5 degrees, the 4:1 rule: base 1 ft out for every 4 ft of working length (OSHA 1926.1053(b)(5)(i)).

Portable ladders used for access to an upper landing surface, such as a roof, shall have
side rails that extend at least ________________ above the upper landing surface to which the
ladder is used to gain access.
OSHA 1926.1053(b)(1) and 1910.23(d)(4) require side rails to extend at least 3 feet (0.9 m) above the upper landing surface, or another secure grasping device provided.
What is an effective way to maintain the integrity of a safety training exam during delivery?
Allowing trainees to take the exam home
Monitoring the exam session to prevent cheating
Conducting all exams orally without written documentation
Proctoring or monitoring the exam session prevents cheating and preserves validity of results. Take-home, open-book-only or undocumented oral exams weaken integrity and records.
Ensuring that safety training exams are consistent and fair involves:
Providing different instructions to each trainee based on their prior knowledge
Using standardized materials and procedures for all trainees
Focusing on subjective questions that can be interpreted in various ways
Allowing trainees to discuss questions during the exam
Using standardized materials, instructions and procedures for all trainees ensures reliability and fairness so scores reflect knowledge, not differences in administration.
In the context of training ethics, what does the term "confidentiality" refer to?
Respecting the privacy of training participants
Using personal information for marketing purposes
Selling training programs to unauthorized individuals

Confidentiality means protecting participants' personal information, test results and disclosures and using them only for legitimate purposes. Sharing or selling materials or using data for marketing violates ethics.
A chemical that causes a negative neurological effect will affect the ___________?
Neurotoxins affect the nervous system, whose central organ is the brain (e.g., solvents, lead, mercury). The liver is the target of hepatotoxins and the heart of cardiotoxins.
Approximately ___________ of the recordable encountered in workplace are Ergonomics hazards.

OSHA and BLS data indicate work-related musculoskeletal disorders account for roughly one-third (about 30 percent) of recordable injuries and illnesses involving days away from work. Note: Figure varies by source (about 29-33 percent).
The long bone in the upper arm is called the:
The humerus is the long bone of the upper arm from shoulder to elbow. The radius and ulna are in the forearm, and the scapula is the shoulder blade.
When changing lanes, in addition to using your turn signal, you should:
Check your mirrors and blind spots.

Defensive driving requires checking mirrors and turning the head to check blind spots before changing lanes, in addition to signaling. Honking, flashing lights or speeding up do not confirm the lane is clear.
A truck transporting compressed gas would display which DOT hazard class placard?
DOT Class 2 = gases (2.1 flammable, 2.2 non-flammable, 2.3 toxic). Class 1 = explosives, Class 3 = flammable liquids, Class 8 = corrosives.

The employer shall ensure that employees using a tight-fitting facepiece respirator pass an appropriate _________________ or quantitative fit test (QNFT) as stated in this paragraph.
Ref:1910.134(f)(1)

OSHA 1910.134(f)(1) requires tight-fitting facepiece respirator users to pass a qualitative fit test (QLFT) or quantitative fit test (QNFT) before use, whenever a different facepiece is used, and at least annually.
Of the following, which one uses a container with a filter, sorbent, catalyst, or combination of these to remove specific contaminants from the air passed through the container? A/An:
Type C SAR or airline respirator

OSHA 1910.134(b) defines a canister or cartridge as a container with a filter, sorbent or catalyst that removes specific contaminants from air passing through it, used on air-purifying respirators. SCBA and airline respirators supply air instead.
What does the phrase “Assigned Protection Factor (APF)” refer to?
The level of protection that a respirator or a class of respirator is expected to offer
The level of protection that engineering controls and work practices offer against respiratory hazards
The point at which a respirator stops offering any protection to the wearer
The employee to whom a respirator is assigned

OSHA 1910.134(b) defines APF as the workplace level of respiratory protection a respirator or class of respirators is expected to provide when a continuing, effective respiratory protection program is implemented (e.g., half-mask APR = 10).
Which tools are considered the highest risk for vibration?

Hand-arm vibration risk is greatest for high-amplitude vibration at low frequencies (roughly 8-16 Hz, the peak of the ISO 5349 frequency weighting), as from percussive tools like breakers and rock drills. Note: Depends on frequency-weighting interpretation; key is defensible.
Which of the following is a very common sign of poor ergonomic practices?
Lower energy levels throughout the workday
Persistent discomfort or pain during work

Persistent discomfort or pain during work is an early warning sign of ergonomic risk factors (awkward postures, force, repetition) and possible developing MSDs. The other options do not indicate ergonomic problems.
What is an effective way to maintain the integrity of a safety training exam during delivery?
Allowing trainees use their phone in the exam.
Monitoring the exam session to prevent cheating
Conducting all exams orally without written documentation
Monitoring or proctoring the exam prevents cheating, including phone use, and keeps results valid. Allowing phones, open-book-only and undocumented oral exams compromise integrity.
What is a trainer's ethical obligation when they observe participants engaging in discriminatory behavior during the training?
Encourage other participants to address it
Address and correct the behavior immediately, promoting a respectful environment
Wait until the end of the training to mention it in general terms

Trainers have an ethical duty to promptly address discriminatory behavior and restore a respectful, inclusive learning environment. Ignoring it, delegating it to participants or delaying it tacitly condones it.
A lot of 100 items contains 3% defectives. If a sample of 4 items is drawn without replacement, what is the probability that none is defective?
P = (97/100)(96/99)(95/98)(94/97) = 0.884. Using 0.97^4 gives 88.5%, about the same; 96% wrongly subtracts 4 x 1%.
In statistics, what is the term for a measure of the spread or dispersion of a dataset?
Standard deviation measures how spread out data are around the mean. Mean, median and mode are measures of central tendency.
Why is the range considered a measure of variability?
Because it identifies the typical value in a data set
Because it shows how data points are concentrated
Because it indicates how spread out the data points are from each other
Because it determines the skewness of the data set
Range = maximum - minimum, showing how far apart the data extremes are, so it is a simple measure of variability. It does not identify a typical value or skewness.
Which elements should be included as common components in an emergency response plan?
A written plan, identified chain of command, emergency response team, training, medical assistance provision, and personal protective equipment
A public relations spokesperson, company officer, emergency transportation vehicles, and legal representation
Fire-fighting equipment, chemical spill clean-up kit, trained medical professionals, dedicated communication equipment, and evacuation equipment
Food, water, extra clothing, and accommodations for evacuees

Core ERP components (OSHA 1910.38 and 1910.120(q)) include a written plan, chain of command, trained emergency response team, training, medical assistance and PPE. The other options list supporting items, not core plan elements.
What are the 5 C’s of safety? Commitment, Culture and?
In the source's model the 5 C's of safety are Commitment, Culture, Champions, Cost and Compliance. Note: Non-standard model; '5 Cs' lists vary by source.
Which role in the Incident Command System is directly responsible for managing tactical operations at an incident?

In ICS (NIMS), the Operations Section Chief directs all tactical operations to carry out the Incident Action Plan. The Incident Commander has overall responsibility, and the PIO and Safety Officer are command staff.
What role does personal protective equipment (PPE) play in supporting the ALARA principle?
PPE is unnecessary if the radiation levels are already low
PPE should be worn at all times, regardless of radiation levels
PPE is used to further reduce exposure when other controls are in place
PPE can increase radiation exposure if not used properly

Under ALARA, time, distance and shielding (engineering controls) are primary; PPE such as lead aprons, gloves and respirators adds a further layer to reduce exposure or contamination when other controls are in place.
What is the principle of ALARA in radiation safety?
ALARA means As Low As Reasonably Achievable: radiation doses are kept as far below limits as practical using time, distance and shielding (10 CFR 20).

A radiography machine emits X-rays with an intensity of 500 mGy per minute at a distance of 1 meter from the source. What will be the intensity of X-rays at a distance of 2 meters from the source?
I₂ = I₁ * (d₁/d₂)²
Inverse square law: I2 = I1 (d1/d2)^2 = 500 mGy/min x (1 m / 2 m)^2 = 500 x 0.25 = 125 mGy/min. Doubling distance cuts intensity to one-quarter, not one-half.
What are the PRIMARY risks that workers are likely to encounter in confined spaces?
Cardiac arrest, lead poisoning, and chemical burns.
Musculoskeletal disorder, repetitive motion syndrome, and hearing loss.
Confined space fatalities are dominated by atmospheric hazards (asphyxiation from oxygen deficiency or toxic gases), engulfment, and hazardous energy such as electrocution (OSHA 1910.146).
Which conditions commonly indicate long-term noise-related injuries?
Ringing in the ear and difficulty in hearing normal conversation.

Tinnitus (ringing) and difficulty understanding normal conversation are typical signs of chronic noise-induced hearing loss. Bleeding from the ear indicates acute trauma, and disorientation suggests vestibular problems.
Machinery and equipment often pose risks of caught-in and struck-by injuries. Which of the following should be considered a hazardous condition?
A modified pulley guard that allows adjustments during operation.
A punch press equipped with a two-hand operator control.
A backup alarm on earth-moving equipment.
A single strobe beacon mounted on the roll-over protection of a forklift.

A modified guard allowing adjustments during operation defeats protection and exposes workers to caught-in hazards (OSHA 1910.212, 1910.219). Two-hand controls, backup alarms and strobes are safeguards.

A man walks 7 km in 2 hours and 2 km in 1 hour in the same direction. 
 What is the man's average speed for the whole journey?
Average speed = total distance / total time = (7 km + 2 km) / (2 h + 1 h) = 9 km / 3 h = 3 km/h.

What Law states that the acceleration of an object as produced by a net force is directly proportional to the magnitude of the net force, in the same direction as the net force, and inversely proportional to the object’s mass.

Newton's Second Law, F = ma (a = F/m): acceleration is proportional to net force, in its direction, and inversely proportional to mass. Boyle's and Charles' laws relate gas pressure, volume and temperature.
Which of the following energy forms is associated with an object in motion?
Kinetic energy is the energy of motion, KE = 1/2 mv^2. Potential energy is stored energy due to position or condition.
Which principle is crucial for effective adult learning in safety training programs?

Adult learning theory (Knowles' andragogy) holds that adults learn best with practical, relevant, problem-centered experiences tied to their work. Testing without feedback, rigidity and pure theory reduce effectiveness.
What is the primary advantage of using multimedia elements in safety training for adult learners?
It simplifies complex safety concepts for easier comprehension
It reduces the overall time required for training completion
It accommodates diverse learning preferences and improves knowledge retention
It increases the cost-effectiveness of the training program
Multimedia combines visual, auditory and interactive elements, accommodating diverse learning preferences and improving engagement and retention. It may or may not reduce time or cost.
How does incorporating self-directed learning elements enhance the effectiveness of adult safety training programs?
It reduces the trainer's workload and responsibility
It increases the organization's control over the learning process
It promotes learner independence and intrinsic motivation
It accelerates the completion of mandatory training requirements

Self-directed learning matches the andragogy principle that adults are self-directed, fostering independence, ownership and intrinsic motivation. Reducing trainer workload or speeding completion are not the main benefit.
ISO 45001 is the international standard for occupational health and safety management systems. ISO 14001 covers environmental management, ISO 31000 risk management, and ISO 9001 quality.
What does the "Plan-Do-Check-Act" (PDCA) cycle in ISO 9001 aim to achieve?
PDCA (Deming cycle), the structure of ISO 9001, 14001 and 45001, drives continual improvement of processes and the management system.
What is the primary goal of business continuity planning?
To ensure the uninterrupted operation of a business during and after a disruption or crisis
To increase profits and market share
To implement employee training and development programs
To develop a comprehensive marketing strategy

Business continuity planning (ISO 22301, NFPA 1600) aims to maintain or quickly resume critical business functions during and after a disruption. Profit, training and marketing are not its primary goal.
The Life Cycle Costs are all costs that the owner or producer of the ____________ will incur over its lifespan.
Life cycle cost is the total cost of owning an asset over its life: acquisition, installation, operation, maintenance and disposal. It is used in economic analysis of safety investments.

The average cost Of a recordable back strain injury moving 55 gallon drums is $44,000. The company has four back strains a year from moving the drum from a conveyor to a pallet. The company wants to buy a lifting robot that costs $20,000. What is the payback period?
Annual loss = 4 x $44,000 = $176,000/yr = $14,667/month. Payback = $20,000 / $14,667 per month = 1.36, about 1.4 months.
Why is budget allocation crucial in safety management?
It allows for increased spending on non-essential items.
It enables procurement of necessary safety equipment and training.
It is only relevant during financial audits.
It focuses primarily on maximizing employee bonuses.
Budget allocation provides the resources to procure safety equipment, training, controls and staffing; ISO 45001 clause 7.1 requires resources for the OH&S system.
What is the difference between insurance and a bond?
Insurance protects a specific person and project while bonds protect a person, business, or company.
A bond protects a contractor who hires someone for a specific project while insurance protects people or businesses from a covered loss

A surety bond protects the owner who hires a contractor, guaranteeing performance or payment, while insurance protects the insured against covered losses. The bond is a three-party agreement; insurance is two-party. Note: Option D wording imprecise but is the best answer.
Which of the following is true about pure risks?
The risk/return tradeoff is applicable to pure risks.
A firm cannot profit from its exposure to pure risk.
Risk managers must be tolerant of negative outcomes related to pure risks.
Pure risk is not a source of great concern for risk managers.
Pure risk offers only loss or no loss (fire, injury), so a firm cannot profit from it. Speculative risk involves possible gain, so the risk/return tradeoff applies to speculative, not pure, risk.
Which of the following is not a tort?
A tort is a civil wrong outside contract, such as battery, assault and negligence. Breaking a contract is a breach of contract, handled under contract law, not tort law.

Scaffold components manufactured by different manufacturers shall not be ___?
Ref: 1926.451 B 10
Used without the express written consent of both manufacturers.

OSHA 1926.451(b)(10) states components from different manufacturers shall not be intermixed unless they fit together without force and the scaffold's structural integrity is maintained; any modification must be approved by a competent person.

Scaffold casters and wheels shall be locked to prevent movement of the scaffold while the scaffold is used in a ________________________________ manner.
Ref: 1926.452 W 2
OSHA 1926.452(w)(2) requires scaffold casters and wheels to be locked with positive wheel and/or swivel locks to prevent movement while the mobile scaffold is used in a stationary manner.

When hook-on and attachable ladders are used on a supported scaffold more than 35 feet (10.7 m) high, they shall have rest platforms at _________foot maximum vertical intervals.
Ref: 1926.451(e)
OSHA 1926.451(e)(2) requires hook-on and attachable ladders on supported scaffolds over 35 feet (10.7 m) high to have rest platforms at 35-foot maximum vertical intervals.
Oxygen enriched atmosphere" means an atmosphere containing more than ___________ percent oxygen by volume.
OSHA 1910.146(b) defines an oxygen-enriched atmosphere as more than 23.5 percent oxygen by volume; below 19.5 percent is oxygen-deficient. Enrichment greatly increases flammability.

Three requirements of a Permit-Required Confined Space are that the space must have limited access and egress, be large enough to enter, and not be designed for human habitancy.
Which is an additional requirement?

Under OSHA 1910.146(b), a permit-required confined space is a confined space that also has a serious hazard: a hazardous or potentially hazardous atmosphere, engulfment potential, an inwardly converging or sloping configuration, or any other serious safety or health hazard.
Which is True about Confined space training? 1910.146(g)
The trainees must be given a test to verify understanding of the training.
The training certification shall contain each employee's name, trainers’ names, location of training, training matrix, and the dates and time of training.
Rescue personnel, attendant, entrant, and entry supervisor must be all trained before the employee is assigned these duties.

OSHA 1910.146(g)(2) requires training before the employee is first assigned duties as entrant, attendant or entry supervisor, and 1910.146(k) requires rescue personnel to be trained. OSHA does not mandate a test or annual retraining, and the certification lists name, trainer signatures/initials and dates.
You are starting at a new company. Last year, eye injuries and foot injuries were the highest cause of recordable incidents. As a new safety professional what action should you perform first?
Survey the facility and operations to determine the cause of the injuries.
Hold the safety meeting discussing the need to be more careful.
Require everybody to wear safety glasses and safety toe shoes.
Put up safety posters reminding workers to wear their protective equipment all the time.

A new safety professional should first survey the facility and operations to determine the root causes of the eye and foot injuries. Blanket PPE rules, meetings or posters before analysis may miss causes and higher-order controls.
If police officers are observed walking on your construction site without wearing hard hats, what is the correct course of action?
Allow them to continue as they are on official duty.
Politely inform them about the site safety rules and direct them to the trailer to obtain visitor hard hats.
Ignore the situation since they are not regular site workers.
Report them to their superior for not following site safety protocols.

Site safety rules apply to all visitors, including officials; politely informing them of the rules and providing visitor hard hats (OSHA 1926.100) protects them without obstructing their duty. Ignoring the hazard or escalating is inappropriate.
When must PPE be used according to safety regulations?
Whenever there are risks that cannot be adequately controlled by other means
At the discretion of the site manager

PPE is required when hazards cannot be adequately eliminated or controlled by engineering or administrative controls (OSHA 1910.132(a), hierarchy of controls). It is not limited to inspections, worker requests or manager discretion.
What is the primary goal of a training needs assessment?**
To evaluate the effectiveness of current training programs
To identify gaps in skills and knowledge among employees
To determine the budget for the next fiscal year
To assess the performance of management
A training needs assessment identifies gaps between required and current knowledge, skills and abilities so training targets real needs. Evaluating existing training effectiveness is a separate step.
Which of the following is NOT typically a method used in conducting a training needs assessment?
Needs assessments use systematic data sources: surveys, interviews, observation, performance appraisals, incident and job analysis. Randomly assigning topics is not an assessment method.
In a training needs assessment, what does the term "KSA" stand for?
KSA stands for Knowledge, Skills and Abilities, the competencies a needs assessment compares between job requirements and current employee capability.

The SDS’s have ____ information sections that conform to the requirements of
the GHS of Classification and Labeling of Chemical Standard.
OSHA HazCom 2012 (1910.1200(g) and Appendix D), aligned with GHS, requires a standardized 16-section SDS format, from identification (section 1) to other information (section 16).
What is the primary purpose of the Hazard Communication Standard (HCS)?
To ensure chemical manufacturers provide detailed financial reports
To ensure that all chemicals are banned from the workplace
To ensure that the hazards of all chemicals produced or imported are classified and that information concerning the classified hazards is communicated to employers and employees
To monitor the import and export of chemicals

OSHA 1910.1200(a)(1) states the HCS purpose is to ensure hazards of all chemicals produced or imported are classified and that information is transmitted to employers and employees via labels, SDSs and training.
Which of the following is a required element on a Safety Data Sheet (SDS)?
Fire-fighting measures are SDS Section 5 under OSHA 1910.1200 Appendix D (extinguishing media, specific hazards, protective equipment). CEO contacts, pricing and marketing are not SDS elements.

Information security protects information and the media that store it, such as flash drives, from loss, theft or unauthorized access. Fire doors and badges are physical security, and trademarks are intellectual property.
The technique used by hackers to forge a phone number so that it looks like it comes from a legitimate source is called:
Caller ID spoofing falsifies the displayed phone number so a call appears to come from a trusted source, a common social engineering technique (vishing). The other terms are not standard.
Name potential warning signs of potential violence?
Violating company rules and complaining about work being hard.
Bragging about how many guns they have and getting a ticket for Driving under the Influence.
Constantly talking about violence and vandalizing company property.
Worker has no sense of humor and is by themselves at lunch

Persistent talk of violence and destroying company property are recognized warning signs of potential workplace violence (OSHA, FBI guidance). Complaining, a DUI or being quiet at lunch are not specific predictors.
Who has the responsibility for controlling the crane during a lifting operation?
Any employee with a clear line of sight to the load

The crane operator controls the crane and has authority to stop and refuse unsafe lifts (OSHA 1926.1417, ASME B30.5). Signal persons communicate, but only the operator controls the crane; anyone may signal an emergency stop.

When selecting proper gloves for chemical materials handling, it is important to understand the chemical breakthrough rating for the type of chemical that the employee may come into contact with. The chemical ratings are E, G, F, and P.
What is the meaning of the "P" chemical breakthrough rating? Please select one of the following options:
Poly-coated, highly recommended (breakthrough times greater than 8 hours)
Perforated, not designed for chemical exposure (breakthrough times less than 1 hour)
Performance, highly recommended (breakthrough times greater than 8 hours)
Poor, not recommended (breakthrough times less than 1 hour)
In glove chemical-resistance charts, ratings are Excellent, Good, Fair and Poor; P (Poor) means not recommended, with rapid breakthrough (typically under 1 hour).
What is the primary goal of hazard assessment in construction?
To identify and mitigate potential risks.
Hazard assessment (e.g., JHA, OSHA 1926.20(b)) identifies hazards and potential risks so controls can be implemented before work begins, preventing injuries.
What is the primary purpose of the BCSP Code of Ethics?
To ensure industry-wide recognition of qualifications
To advocate for stricter regulations to address workplace safety
To establish professional standards for integrity, honor, and prestige in the safety profession
To require certification holders to share knowledge for compensation

The BCSP Code of Ethics establishes standards of professional conduct so certificants uphold integrity, honor and prestige of the safety profession, including protecting people, property and the environment.
How does a Safety Manager's input in the development of a corporate business plan influence safety management and performance goals?
It ensures the allocation of resources to achieve a zero-injury target.
It identifies areas for improvement and sets specific, measurable safety objectives.
It integrates safety goals into the overall business strategy and resource allocation.
It determines the company's financial projections and resource allocation, with no direct impact on safety goals.
Safety input to the business plan integrates safety goals into the overall strategy and resource allocation, so safety is resourced like any other business objective.
How does a Safety Manager's input into the business plan impact resource allocation?
It ensures that safety initiatives are funded as needed
It allocates a fixed percentage of the budget to safety initiatives
It prioritizes resource allocation based on business objectives, including safety
It has no impact on resource allocation

When the safety manager contributes to the business plan, safety is integrated with business objectives, so resources are prioritized and allocated alongside other strategic goals, not automatically funded or fixed.
What differentiates the four Categories of a flammable liquid?
Under OSHA 1910.106 and GHS, flammable liquid Categories 1-4 are defined by flashpoint and initial boiling point (e.g., Category 1: FP < 73.4 F and BP <= 95 F).
If two chemicals combined have synergistic effects, when the chemicals are combined, the effects of this combination will:
mimic that of the chemical with the strongest effects.
become toxic because each chemical enhances the other.
be less than the effects of the chemicals on their own.
be greater than the effects of the chemicals on their own.

Synergism means the combined effect is greater than the sum of the individual effects (2 + 2 = 6), e.g., asbestos and smoking. Additive is equal to the sum, antagonism is less, and potentiation is a non-toxic agent increasing another's toxicity.
A warehouse is 1,000,000 sq.ft. but only 800,000 of that is usable storage space. The clear height of the building is 25 ft. What is the warehouse storage capacity in cubic feet?
Storage capacity = usable area x clear height = 800,000 ft^2 x 25 ft = 20,000,000 ft^3. Using total area gives 25,000,000, not an option.
What is the result of not considering floor load capacity when determining storage capacity?
Risk of floor collapse or damage.

Exceeding the rated floor load capacity can cause structural damage or collapse; OSHA 1910.22(b) requires walking-working surfaces not exceed maximum intended load, and floor load limits must be posted where required.
Which of the following factors should be considered when calculating safe storage capacity?
The color of the storage bins.
The historical value of stored items.
The weight, size, and nature of items, along with the design and material of the storage solution.

Safe storage capacity depends on item weight, size and nature (stability, hazards) plus the rated capacity and design of shelving, racks and floors (e.g., ANSI MH16.1 rack loads). Color, brand and value do not matter.
When mechanical equipment is being used perpendicular to the roof edge, the warning lines cannot be closer than _______ feet. 1926.502(F)(1)(ii)

OSHA 1926.502(f)(1)(ii) requires warning lines at least 6 feet from the roof edge parallel to mechanical equipment travel and at least 10 feet from the edge perpendicular to the direction of equipment operation.
Which represents the formula used to calculate free fall distance (FF) when the anchor point is above the attachment point?
FF = Lanyard x Distance between attachment and anchor point
FF = Lanyard - Distance between attachment and anchor point
FF = Lanyard + Distance between attachment and anchor point

With the anchor above the harness D-ring, free fall equals lanyard length minus the distance the anchor is above the attachment point; e.g., 6 ft lanyard with anchor 2 ft above D-ring gives 4 ft free fall.

What is the minimum height at which OSHA requires fall protection for construction workers working on a walking/working surface with an unprotected edge?
Ref: OSHA's 29 CFR 1926.501(b)(1)
OSHA 1926.501(b)(1) requires fall protection for construction workers on walking/working surfaces with an unprotected edge 6 feet or more above a lower level. General industry is 4 feet (1910.28).
What is a method to decrease forceful exertion, a frequent ergonomic risk?
Providing handles or handholds for lifting or carrying
Supplying back and knee braces to employees
Enhancing climate control in the work area
Requiring higher fitness standards during hiring

Adding handles or handholds improves grip and coupling, reducing required force (a better coupling factor in the NIOSH lifting equation). Braces are not proven controls and fitness hiring screens are not ergonomic controls.
What is the primary purpose of an Occupational Exposure Assessment?
To measure the effectiveness of workplace communication
To identify and evaluate potential hazards in the workplace
To assess the productivity of employees
To evaluate the aesthetic of the workplace
Occupational exposure assessment identifies and evaluates workplace hazards and worker exposures (AIHA exposure assessment strategy) and compares them to OELs to decide whether controls are needed.
What is 'additive effect' in the context of toxicology?
The cumulative effect of two substances equals the sum of their individual effects.
The effect of a substance being completely nullified by another substance.
The unexpected increase in toxicity when two substances are mixed.
The process of a toxin building up in the body over time.

An additive effect means the combined effect equals the sum of individual effects (2 + 3 = 5), e.g., two organophosphate pesticides. A greater-than-sum effect is synergism, and nullification is antagonism.
What is a key consideration when designing a training course?**
Selecting a time that is only convenient for the trainers
Using only one type of teaching method for all content
Ensuring the content aligns with the learners' needs and learning outcomes
Focusing solely on theoretical knowledge without practical application

Instructional design (ADDIE, ANSI/ASSP Z490.1) requires content aligned with learners' needs and measurable learning outcomes. Trainer convenience, a single method and pure theory reduce effectiveness.
How should resources be allocated to maximize the effectiveness of a training program?
Allocate resources based solely on what is least expensive
Distribute resources equally among all possible tools regardless of effectiveness
Invest in resources only after the training is complete to assess needs
Target resources to areas that directly support the learning objectives and methods
Resources should target materials, tools and methods that directly support the learning objectives and chosen delivery methods. Cheapest, equal or after-the-fact allocation ignores effectiveness.
What is an effective way to manage training resources in a budget-constrained environment?
Cut corners on essential materials to save costs
Prioritize resources that have multiple uses and high impact on learning
Ignore digital tools to focus exclusively on traditional methods
Reduce the number of training sessions to lower costs

With a tight budget, prioritize versatile, high-impact resources (reusable props, simulations, e-learning modules) that best support learning. Cutting essential materials or sessions harms training effectiveness.

The ___________ diagram or [Ishikawa](http://www.skymark.com/resources/leaders/ishikawa.asp) diagram is a cause-and-effect diagram that helps managers to track down the reasons for imperfections, variations, defects, or failures.
The fishbone (Ishikawa) cause-and-effect diagram groups possible causes of a defect or failure into categories along branches of a fish skeleton. Lean 5S is a workplace organization method.
When conducting a systematic cause analysis technique (SCAT), officials must first identify which of the following?
Loss associated with the event being investigated
Control factors that failed, causing an event to occur
Identification of the event that has caused a loss
Recognition of causes of an unanticipated, negative event

The Systematic Cause Analysis Technique (DNV/ILCI loss causation model) begins by identifying the event (type of contact) that resulted in the loss, then works back through immediate causes, basic causes and lack of control. Note: SCAT chart starts with incident description; options overlap.
Which is a tool that enables a team to identify, explore, and graphically display the possible causes of an incident or hazardous conditions?

An Ishikawa (fishbone) diagram lets a team brainstorm and graphically display possible causes of an incident or condition by category. Gantt and PERT charts are scheduling tools and Venn diagrams show set overlap.
Employees working with which of these tools are advised to wear head and face protection in addition to the required eye protection?
OSHA 1910.266 and chainsaw guidance call for head protection (hard hat) and face protection (mesh face screen) in addition to eye protection, due to kickback, flying chips and falling limbs.
Which tools require an equipment grounding conductor?
Circular saws with a metal housing made in 1980.

A tool with exposed metal housing that is not double insulated must have an equipment grounding conductor (3-prong plug) per OSHA 1910.334 and 1926.404/302. Double-insulated, cordless and battery tools do not.
Silica is commonly found in many construction materials. What is the main hazard it poses to workers on a construction site, and what is the MOST effective method to manage this hazard?
Inhalation of crystalline silica leads to silicosis (a lung disease). To manage this, use water to suppress dust formation.
Silica is abrasive, damaging the eyes, skin, and teeth. The recommended control measure is a full-face supplied air mask.
Exposure to silica dust irritates the mouth and throat. A single strap dust mask is sufficient for protection.
The primary issue with naturally occurring silica is that it obscures vision by dirtying safety eyewear. Regularly wipe eyewear with a clean cotton cloth to mitigate this.
Respirable crystalline silica causes silicosis, lung cancer and COPD; OSHA 1926.1153 Table 1 favors engineering controls such as wet methods (water suppression) and local exhaust before respirators.

What three readings are taken outdoors to calculate the heat index?
Wet bulb temperature, Dry bulb temperature and?

The WBGT index uses natural wet bulb, globe and dry bulb temperatures: outdoors WBGT = 0.7 NWB + 0.2 GT + 0.1 DB (ACGIH). The globe thermometer measures radiant heat. Note: Stem says heat index but describes WBGT.
What formula should be used to calculate the free fall distance (FF) when the anchor point is positioned above the harness attachment point?
FF = Lanyard x Distance between attachment and anchor point
FF = Lanyard - Distance between attachment and anchor point
FF = Lanyard + Distance between attachment and anchor point

When the anchor is above the D-ring, free fall distance = lanyard length - distance of the anchor above the attachment point. For example, 6 ft lanyard with anchor 3 ft above D-ring gives 3 ft free fall.
An SDS lists the density of petroleum diesel as 6.943 lb/gal. What is the weight of diesel in a full 100,000-gallon tank?
Mass = volume x density = 100,000 gal x 6.943 lb/gal = 694,300 lb. This matters for foundation, floor loading and containment design.
What are the essential components of a "what if" hazard analysis?
Aimed at facilitating root cause analysis
Requires minimal time, few resources, and little preparation
Meets regulatory requirements for pre-task planning
Cost-effective, utilizes a multi-skilled team, and employs a qualitative approach

What-if analysis is a qualitative, brainstorming-based hazard analysis by an experienced multi-disciplinary team asking 'what if' questions; it is relatively cost-effective and flexible (CCPS, OSHA 1910.119 PHA method).
What is an effective approach to enhancing workers' attitudes towards safe work practices?
Implementing a three-step discipline program for unsafe behavior.
Offering higher wages to all employees.
Identifying and communicating the desired behavior.

Behavior-based approaches (ABC model) improve attitudes by clearly defining and communicating desired safe behaviors and reinforcing them. Discipline, wages or more staff alone do not shape safe behavior.
What is risk mitigation in project management?
The process of transferring all project risks to another party to handle.
The act of ignoring minor risks until they become significant.
The process of taking proactive steps to reduce the likelihood or impact of potential project risks.
The practice of insuring against all possible risks to ensure no financial loss
Risk mitigation proactively reduces the probability and/or impact of identified risks (PMI PMBOK). Transfer and insurance shift risk to another party, and ignoring risks is passive acceptance.
Why does the occurrence of Foreign Object Debris cause concern for an aviation company?
FOD can cause significant damage to aircraft, leading to costly repairs and safety risks.
FOD can increase the aesthetic appeal of an aircraft, attracting more customers.
FOD increases the efficiency of airport operations by streamlining maintenance checks.
FOD helps in improving the fuel efficiency of aircraft by modifying aerodynamics.

Foreign object debris can be ingested by engines, damage tires, airframes and controls, causing costly repairs and potential catastrophic failure. FAA AC 150/5210-24 addresses FOD prevention programs.
Which of the following is NOT an essential component of a comprehensive lesson plan?
Detailed marketing strategy for the course
Trainee materials such as handouts and job aids
Lesson plans contain objectives, content, methods, materials, and assessment. Marketing is not part of instructional design. Watch for the NOT.
What type of training delivery platform is best suited for participants who are geographically dispersed?
Strictly mobile learning with no interactions

Instructor-led online (virtual) training reaches geographically dispersed learners while maintaining real-time interaction, questions and feedback. Classroom requires travel, and no-interaction or paper-only formats reduce engagement.
What should be considered when validating a training course's content?
The popularity of the course topics
Adherence to relevant regulations and consensus standards
The personal preferences of the course developer

Content validation verifies that material is accurate and consistent with applicable regulations (OSHA) and consensus standards (ANSI/ASSP Z490.1) and job requirements. Popularity, volume and preference do not validate content.
Only employers with _____ or fewer employees may communicate an Emergency Action Plan orally to employees. 1910.38a
OSHA 1910.38(b) allows an employer with 10 or fewer employees to communicate the emergency action plan orally instead of in writing. The same applies to fire prevention plans (1910.39(b)).
Under incident command, the command staff positions include:
Public Information Officer, Chief Executive Officer, Safety Officer
Safety Officer, Public Information Officer, And Liaison Officer,
Operations Section Chief, Logistics Section Chief, Planning Section Chief, And Finance Section Chief

ICS command staff are the Public Information Officer, Safety Officer and Liaison Officer, reporting to the Incident Commander. Operations, Planning, Logistics and Finance/Administration are general staff section chiefs.
What is typically the primary focus of vulnerability assessments?

Security vulnerability assessments (e.g., DHS CFATS, API/CCPS SVA) primarily evaluate susceptibility to intentional acts such as terrorism and sabotage. Natural hazards are evaluated in hazard vulnerability analyses. Note: Vulnerability assessment can be all-hazards; key reflects security sense.
What is the primary purpose of lockout/tagout procedures?
To increase productivity during equipment maintenance
To prevent the accidental startup of machinery during maintenance
To track the usage of equipment
To assess the financial value of the machinery
OSHA 1910.147 lockout/tagout prevents unexpected energization, start-up or release of stored energy that could injure workers during servicing and maintenance.
When can a lockout device be removed and who can remove it?
The device can be removed by any worker at the end of the shift
The device can be removed by a supervisor when the work is deemed complete
The device can only be removed by the person who applied it after the work is complete
The device can be removed by maintenance personnel before equipment inspection

OSHA 1910.147(e)(3) requires each lockout device to be removed by the authorized employee who applied it, after work is complete, tools removed and employees safely positioned. Supervisor removal is allowed only under the 1910.147(e)(3) exception procedure.
Employees shall not work in excavations in which there is accumulated?

OSHA 1926.651(h)(1) prohibits work in excavations with accumulated water or where water is accumulating unless adequate precautions (protective systems, water removal monitored by a competent person, harness and lifeline) are taken. 78% nitrogen and 20.9% oxygen are normal air.
Trenches over ____ feet must be designed by a professional engineer.

OSHA 1926.652(b)/(c) requires protective systems for excavations deeper than 20 feet to be designed by a registered professional engineer; sloping per Appendix B and tabulated data cover shallower depths.

According to the OSHA standard, an employer must check an excavation for HAZARDOUS ATMOSPHERE if he suspects one might be present when the depth of the excavation is _______ feet or greater.
Ref: 1926.651(g)(1)(i)

OSHA 1926.651(g)(1)(i) requires atmospheric testing before employees enter excavations greater than 4 feet deep where an oxygen-deficient or hazardous atmosphere exists or could reasonably be expected (e.g., near landfills or hazardous substance storage).
What is a KEY consideration for a safety manager aiming to get an effective job safety analysis?
Thoroughly identify all past occurrences associated with the task.
Utilize a consistent form and numbered work tasks to enhance usability across all analyses.
Ensure the analysis is signed by every team member involved.
Empower the work team to collaborate in compiling and discussing the analysis at the work location

An effective JSA involves the workers who do the job, developing and discussing it at the work location where actual steps and hazards can be observed (OSHA 3071). Worker participation improves accuracy and buy-in more than forms or signatures.
Safety training records, certifications earned, and total hours trained are:
A valid reason for promotion or a raise in a worker's wage.
Confirmation of a positive return on investment.

Training records document that required training occurred and can be subpoenaed and admitted as evidence in litigation or OSHA proceedings to show due diligence or its absence. Not every agency requires them and they do not prove ROI.
Which system, comprising tools, processes, and procedures, significantly lowers the risk of accidental releases of highly hazardous chemicals when correctly implemented and adhered to?

Process Safety Management (OSHA 1910.119) is a system of 14 elements (PHA, MOC, mechanical integrity, operating procedures, etc.) that prevents or minimizes catastrophic releases of highly hazardous chemicals. HazCom, SDSs and GHS communicate hazards only.
During arc welding, the welder is exposed O3 (ozone) which is a pulmonary gas due to lack of ventilation. These are gases that:
Replace the oxygen in human blood.
Lead to obstructive diseases in the lungs.

Ozone is a pulmonary irritant that damages lung tissue, causing airway inflammation, edema and with chronic exposure obstructive lung disease. Gases that displace oxygen in blood are chemical asphyxiants like CO.
When is it appropriate to remove your welding gloves?
Only when welding is completely finished, and equipment is cool
As soon as the welding stops
After each weld to check the quality
Gloves should stay on until welding is complete and the workpiece and equipment have cooled, to protect against burns from hot metal and electric shock (ANSI Z49.1, OSHA 1910.252).
Which equipment is involved in the most dust explosions

Dust collectors are the equipment most frequently involved in combustible dust explosions because they concentrate fine dust in a confined vessel (NFPA 652 data, CSB). Silos, conveyors and mixers follow.
The spread of a flame in a combustible environment outward from the point at which the combustion started.
An area of pressure expanding supersonically outward from an explosive core.
Combustion which propagates through a gas or across the surface of an explosive at subsonic speeds, driven by the transfer of heat.
Combustion which propagates through a gas or across the surface of an explosive at supersonic speeds, driven by the transfer of heat.
NFPA 68 defines deflagration as combustion propagating at subsonic velocity through the unburned material by heat transfer. Supersonic, shock-driven propagation is a detonation.
What role does proper ventilation play in managing combustible dust?
It reduces the oxygen level in the air to prevent combustion
It cools down the machinery to prevent overheating
It helps disperse dust particles to reduce their concentration in the air
It adds moisture to the air to make the dust heavier and less likely to become airborne
