Ventilation and dust collection capture and remove dust and dilute airborne concentrations below the minimum explosible concentration, reducing fuel for a dust cloud. Ventilation does not reduce oxygen or add moisture.
How does proper lighting in a learning environment affect students?
It increases the risk of headaches and eye strain.
It has no significant effect on learning or comfort.
It enhances concentration and reduces eye strain.
It decreases students' ability to concentrate on visual tasks.
Adequate, glare-free lighting (IES recommendations, about 300-500 lux for classrooms) improves visual comfort and concentration and reduces eye strain and fatigue.
What is the recommended noise level for a learning environment?
Classroom background noise should be low, around 35-50 dBA (ANSI/ASA S12.60 sets 35 dBA unoccupied), so speech is clearly intelligible. 50-60 dB is speech level, not background.
What type of lighting is most effective for learning environments?
Natural daylight improves alertness, mood and visual comfort and is associated with better learning performance. Dim red lighting impairs visual tasks and fluorescent flicker can cause fatigue.
All machines consist of three fundamental areas, including __.
Flywheels, connecting rods, and transverse moving parts
Point of operation, power transmission device, and operating controls
Reciprocating parts, rotating parts, and on/off switch
Feed mechanisms, auxiliary machine parts, and nip points

OSHA 3170 (Safeguarding Equipment) states all machines have three fundamental areas: the point of operation, the power transmission apparatus, and other moving parts/operating controls. Hazardous motions occur in each.
Unguarded circular saw blades are a common causal factor for a:

An unguarded rotating circular blade can catch clothing, gloves or hands and draw them in, causing caught-in injuries such as amputations (OSHA 1910.213 requires blade guards). Note: Laceration not offered; caught-in is intended.
When should guards be used on a conveyor system?
Only when the conveyor is in operation
At all times to protect against accidental contact
Only when local regulations require them

Conveyor guards must be in place at all times during operation to prevent accidental contact with nip points and moving parts (OSHA 1910.212, ASME B20.1); during maintenance the conveyor is locked out and guards are replaced before restart.
Which statement reflects Malcolm Knowles' view of adult learners?
Adults are motivated to learn when they see the value of the information to their personal and professional lives
Adults will avoid training whenever possible
Adults need to know why they are learning something; showing job relevance and benefit increases motivation.
In the ADDIE Instructional Design Model, which phase involves identifying the learning needs and the overall goals of the instructional program?
In ADDIE (Analysis, Design, Development, Implementation, Evaluation), the Analysis phase identifies learner needs, performance gaps and overall instructional goals before design begins.
Gen Z (born about 1997-2012) are digital natives who grew up with smartphones and the internet; they tend to value diversity and want immediate feedback and relevant content.
A right triangle has one leg 40 feet high and the other leg 100 feet wide. What is the hypotenuse?
Pythagorean theorem: c = sqrt(a^2 + b^2) = sqrt(40^2 + 100^2) = sqrt(1,600 + 10,000) = sqrt(11,600) = 107.7, about 107 ft. 4,000 is a simple product, not the hypotenuse.
In a circle, what is the line called that passes through the center and connects two points on the circle?
The diameter is a chord through the center, equal to twice the radius. The radius runs from center to edge and the circumference is the distance around.
In terms of safety, how does understanding the area of a floor space contribute to workplace safety?
It helps calculate the amount of paint needed for the floor.
It determines the maximum number of people that can safely occupy the space.
It is useful for determining where to place decorations.
It assists in calculating the speed of walking across the floor.
Floor area is used to calculate occupant load (area / occupant load factor, NFPA 101 Table 7.3.1.2), which determines the maximum safe number of occupants and required egress capacity.

What is the main purpose of the overhead guard on a forklift?
Ref: https://www.osha.gov/.../types.../parts/overhead-guard....
To protect the operator if falling items such as boxes dropped from heights
To stop the operator from being crushed in an event of a truck tipping over
To protect the operator if a forklift from a sliding load on a forklift
To protect the operator from Birds and bats.

OSHA 1910.178(m)(11) and ANSI/ITSDF B56.1 state the overhead guard protects the operator from falling objects such as small packages and boxes; it is not intended to withstand a capacity load or protect in a tip-over.
Where should the load be carried while operating a forklift?
As low as possible and tilted back
At the top of the mast

Carry the load as low as possible (typically 4-6 inches off the floor) with the mast tilted back to keep the combined center of gravity within the stability triangle (OSHA 1910.178(o)). Raised loads increase tip-over risk and block vision.
Forklift modifications and additions which affect capacity and safe operation shall not be performed by user without ____ ? Ref. 1910.178(a)(4)

OSHA 1910.178(a)(4) prohibits modifications and additions that affect capacity and safe operation without the manufacturer's prior written approval; capacity, operation and maintenance plates must then be changed.
You are short 0.2 CEU for the recertification cycle. What should the safety profession do?
Write BCSP and ask for an extension.
Add 0.4 CEUs and make it up later.
Write BCSP and ask for an exemption

BCSP recertification requires meeting point requirements by the cycle end; a certificant who is short should contact BCSP in writing and request an extension rather than misreporting credits. Exemptions are not provided for shortfalls. Note: BCSP policy may change; verify current recertification rules.
In disability terminology, what is a stigmatizing term which places an individual in a passive role as an object of pity?
Disability etiquette guidance discourages 'victim' because it frames the person as a passive object of pity; person-first language (person with a disability) is preferred.
What is the ethical priority of a safety professional?
The health and safety of employees
Ending the spread of communicable disease through employee hygiene
The BCSP Code of Ethics places protection of people's health and safety (and property and environment) as the paramount priority over business interests such as profit.

Your facility is a Large Quantity Generator(LQG) of hazardous waste. Employees involved in the management of your hazardous waste complete annual refresher training as required by Resource Conservation & Recovery Act (RCRA). How much training must be completed each year to comply with RCRA’s training requirements?

RCRA (40 CFR 262.17(a)(7) and 265.16) requires LQG personnel to complete initial training and take part in an annual review of it, but specifies no minimum number of hours. The 8-hour annual refresher is a HAZWOPER (1910.120) requirement.
EPA uses these principles for environmental sustainability.
EPA's waste management hierarchy for sustainability emphasizes Reduce, Reuse, Recycle, with source reduction most preferred. Plan-Do-Act is a management cycle, not a sustainability principle.
What is a primary objective of conducting trainee evaluations?
To determine the effectiveness of the training program.
To decide the compensation of the trainers.
Trainee evaluations (Kirkpatrick levels 1-4) measure whether learners met objectives and thereby determine the training program's effectiveness and where it needs improvement.
Which method is effective for documenting trainee behavior changes?
Using a standardized form to record specific observations.
Ignoring minor behavior changes to focus on major ones.

A standardized observation form records specific, objective behaviors consistently over time, allowing valid comparison and documentation (Kirkpatrick level 3). Verbal-only feedback and annual reviews without notes lack evidence.
How should behavioral changes be reported to ensure effective communication?
By waiting until a pattern is clearly established before reporting.
Through informal conversations without any written documentation.
Immediately in an ad-hoc manner as they occur.
Regularly and systematically using formal reports.

Behavioral changes should be reported regularly and systematically in formal reports so trends are documented and communicated consistently. Ad hoc, informal or delayed reporting loses data and accountability.
Which is generally the best location for the air intake of a large office building?
Halfway up the building, near the street.
On the ground level, in the inner courtyard.
On the ground level, next to the loading dock.
On the rooftop, near the building’s center.

Outdoor air intakes should be away from contaminant sources such as street traffic, loading docks and vehicle exhaust (ASHRAE 62.1 separation distances); a rooftop location near the center, away from exhausts, generally gives the cleanest air.

According to the generally accepted hierarchy of controls, personal protective equipment (PPE) is typically considered as the last resort for controlling hazards. However, under which circumstances might it be justified to prioritize PPE as the FIRST control to be used?
Convenience and comfort of the worker
Severity and duration of risk exposure

PPE may be used first when risk severity and exposure duration demand immediate protection while higher-level controls are being implemented, or for short-duration, emergency or non-routine tasks where other controls are infeasible. Budget, schedule or comfort are not valid justifications.
What is the correct order of the ANSI Z10 Hierarchy of Control, from most effective to least effective?
Elimination, Substitution, Engineering Controls, Warning Administrative Controls, PPE
PPE, Administrative Controls, Warning, Engineering Controls, Substitution, Elimination
Engineering Controls, Administrative Controls, PPE, Warning Substitution, Elimination
Administrative Controls, PPE, Engineering Controls, Warning, Substitution, Elimination
ANSI/ASSP Z10 hierarchy, most to least effective: Elimination, Substitution, Engineering controls, Warnings, Administrative controls, PPE. Option B is the reverse order.

Disaster recovery planning (NFPA 1600, FEMA) should include contacts and coordination with local emergency management officials and responders. Respirator records and benchmarking are not recovery plan elements and 'disaster competent person' is not a recognized certification.
Form of injury/illness measurement used by large corporations
Process to develop an annual safety and health budget
Process to compare company safety program to industry peers
Benchmarking is the process of comparing your safety program and performance to industry peers or recognized leaders.
Which of the following statements best describes the concept of a safety and health management program?
Increases value-added work by eliminating waste and reducing incidental work
Is an operational strategy oriented toward achieving the shortest possible cycle time by eliminating waste
Provides a framework to ensure occupational health and safety compliance with OSHA and consensus standards
Provides an effective tool for continual improvement of a company’s occupational health and safety performance

A safety and health management program (OSHA Recommended Practices, ANSI Z10, ISO 45001) is a PDCA-based tool for continual improvement of OH&S performance, going beyond mere compliance. Options A and B describe Lean.
Systemic Cause Analysis Technique (SCAT) looks at five categories of loss events, starting with the loss and working backward to the event. Some of the five events are:
Loss, Event, Lack of Control Factor

SCAT, based on the ILCI loss causation model, works backward from the Loss to the Event (type of contact), immediate causes, basic causes and Lack of Control factors. Man-machine-method are fishbone categories.
Dr. Roger Bauer said the most effective method to fix accountability for losses is to:
Coach the root causes with the team.
Praise every for one minute a day.
Charge the loss to the supervisor cost center

Charging losses to the responsible supervisor's cost center fixes accountability by making losses affect the supervisor's own budget and performance measures, a classic loss-control accountability technique. Note: Attribution to a specific author not verified.
What does "fail operational" mean in the context of safety and system design?
A system or component that fails in a way that causes harm to people or the environment
A system or component that continues to function safely and effectively even in the event of a failure
A system or component that shuts down or becomes inoperable in the event of a failure
A system or component that requires manual intervention to prevent harm in the event of a failure

Fail-operational means a system continues to perform its function safely after a failure, typically via redundancy (e.g., aircraft flight controls). Shutting down on failure is fail-safe or fail-passive.
One __________________ is defined as energy consumption of one joule per electric charge of one coulomb. (Electromotive force)
One volt equals one joule of energy per coulomb of charge (V = J/C), the unit of electromotive force. Ampere is coulomb per second, ohm is volt per ampere, and watt is joule per second.
At a shock of current at 50-200 mA, you could have ventricular fibrillation or _____________ arrest

Currents of about 50-200 mA through the chest can cause ventricular fibrillation and cardiac arrest, often fatal without defibrillation (OSHA electrical effects table). Above about 200 mA, burns and clamping of the heart occur.
What is the primary purpose of the grounding conductor in a receptacle that has hot, neutral, and grounding conductors?
To provide a path for electrical current to flow to the device being powered
To provide a safe path to ground for fault currents and protect against electrical shock
To increase the voltage rating of the receptacle
To reduce the number of wires needed for the receptacle

The equipment grounding conductor provides a low-impedance path for fault current back to the source so the overcurrent device trips and exposed metal does not become energized (NEC 250, OSHA 1910.304). Normal current flows on hot and neutral.
What is the main purpose of using leading indicators in safety?
TO measure the success Of safety programs
To determine the root cause of safety incidents
To provide early warning signs of potential safety issues
To evaluate the overall effectiveness of safety programs

Leading indicators are proactive, predictive measures that provide early warning of potential safety problems so they can be corrected before incidents occur (ANSI Z16.10). Measuring outcomes is the role of lagging indicators.
Your company wants to get to an annual incident rate of 0.5 recordable injuries. This indicator is a:
A target incident rate is still an outcome measure based on injuries that already occurred: a lagging indicator.
Which of the following is an example of a leading indicator in a safety management system?
Number of days since the last recordable injury
Number of safety training sessions conducted per quarter
Percentage of employees who report hazards or near misses
Total workers' compensation costs per year

Percentage of employees reporting hazards or near misses measures proactive engagement and identifies precursors before injury, a strong leading indicator. Days since last recordable and workers' comp costs are lagging. Note: Training sessions conducted is also leading; C is the stronger performance-based measure.
45 degrees angle sling has approximately ____________ more tension from the horizontal.

Sling tension = load per leg / sin(angle from horizontal). At 45 degrees, 1/sin 45 = 1.414, about 41 percent more tension than a vertical sling; 45 percent is the nearest option. Note: Exact value is 41 percent.
A fiber core wire rope has _____ breaking strength than a wire rope with an independent wire rope core of the same size.

A fiber core (FC) wire rope has lower breaking strength (about 7.5 percent less) and less crush resistance than an independent wire rope core (IWRC) rope of the same size, because the steel core carries load.
What is the primary purpose of a sling load chart in rigging operations?
To determine the weight of the load being lifted
To calculate the angle of the sling or rigging equipment
To ensure the crane or hoist is properly configured for the lift
To verify the capacity of the rigging equipment and prevent overload
A sling load chart gives rated capacity by sling type, size, hitch and angle, allowing the rigger to verify the rigging can handle the load and avoid overload (OSHA 1910.184, ASME B30.9).
What is the primary purpose of assessing on-the-job performance after training?
To determine if the training should be made more difficult.
To identify who should be promoted.
To evaluate if the training objectives have been met.
To determine the pay scale for employees.
On-the-job performance assessment (Kirkpatrick level 3, behavior) evaluates whether trainees transfer learning and meet training objectives in the workplace. Promotion and pay are not its purpose.
Which method is most effective for assessing practical skills after a training session?
Practical skills are best verified by directly observing the trainee perform the task (performance-based assessment); written tests and surveys measure knowledge or reaction, not demonstrated skill.
What should be done if an assessment reveals that employees are not applying what they learned in training?
Ignore the findings, as the training is only a formality.
Provide additional training focused on application.

A transfer gap (Kirkpatrick Level 3, behavior) calls for targeted remedial training on application plus reinforcement on the job; ignoring, cutting funding or terminating does not correct the root cause.
A worker must climb a 30 foot fixed ladder. Which provides the best protection?
A ladder cage that extends from the ground to 33 feet.
A body harness with a 12 foot lanyard.
Ladder climbing system with a body harness and 9 inch lanyard.

A ladder safety (climbing) system with harness and short connector arrests a fall within inches; OSHA 1910.28 is phasing out cages, and a 12 ft lanyard allows excessive free fall. Training alone gives no physical protection.
What is the recommended angle for setting up a ladder against a wall or other vertical surface?
Non-self-supporting ladders are set at about 75 degrees, the 4:1 rule (base 1 ft out for every 4 ft of working length), per OSHA 1926.1053(b)(5)(i) and ANSI A14.
What is the maximum distance allowed to get to a ladder when in a trench?
OSHA 1926.651(c)(2): trenches 4 ft or deeper need a stairway, ladder, ramp or other egress so that no more than 25 ft of lateral travel is required.
The longest bone in the body is the
The femur (thigh bone) is the longest and strongest bone in the human body; the radius and ulna are forearm bones and the skull is not a long bone.
De quervain’s Tenosynovitis occurs in the ____________ area.

De Quervain's tenosynovitis is inflammation of the tendon sheaths of the abductor pollicis longus and extensor pollicis brevis at the thumb side of the wrist, often from repetitive pinching or gripping.
Which organ is responsible for filtering waste products from the blood and producing urine?
The kidneys filter blood in the nephrons, removing wastes such as urea and producing urine; the liver metabolizes and detoxifies but does not produce urine.
In the context of occupational exposure, what does TLV stand for?
TLV is the ACGIH Threshold Limit Value, the airborne concentration to which nearly all workers may be repeatedly exposed day after day without adverse effect (TLV-TWA, STEL, Ceiling).
What role does air monitoring play in Occupational Exposure Assessment?
It provides data on the financial health of the company
It determines the training needs of employees
It helps to establish exposure control measures
It assists in marketing strategy development
Air monitoring quantifies worker exposure against OELs (PEL, TLV), which determines whether and which engineering, administrative or PPE controls are needed and verifies their effectiveness.
Which method is commonly used to assess airborne contaminants in a workplace?

Direct-reading instruments (e.g., PIDs, multi-gas meters, aerosol monitors) give real-time airborne concentrations; integrated sampling with lab analysis is the other standard method. Self-reporting is not a measurement.
Assigned Protection Factors for full face is __________
OSHA 1910.134 Table 1 assigns an APF of 50 to a full-facepiece air-purifying respirator (half-mask APR = 10; PAPR/supplied air can be 1,000).
The PPE that provides the greatest level of skin and respiratory protection during an emergency response is:
EPA/OSHA HAZWOPER Level A is a fully encapsulating vapor-tight suit with SCBA, giving the highest skin and respiratory protection; Level B gives full respiratory but less skin protection.
There are two major classes of respirators; one is air-purifying, the other is…

Respirators are either air-purifying (filter or cartridge cleans ambient air) or atmosphere-supplying (SCBA, supplied-air) that provide breathing air from a separate source, required for IDLH or oxygen-deficient atmospheres.

Which BEST describes lifting frequency? 
REf:Yates, W. D. (2015). Safety Professional's Reference & Study Guide (2nd ed.). Boca Raton, FL: Taylor & Francis Group, LLC. -- p.496
Average number of lifts in a 15-minute period
Average number of lifts in a 25-minute period
Average number of lifts in a 20-minute period
Average number of lifts in a 5-minute period

In the NIOSH Lifting Equation, frequency (F) is the average number of lifts per minute measured over a 15-minute sampling period. Note: Options omit 'per minute'; frequency is lifts/min averaged over 15 minutes.
What ergonomic adjustment can help reduce the risk of carpal tunnel syndrome for someone who works at a computer?
Increasing the brightness of the computer screen
Lowering the chair so the feet dangle
Keeping the wrists straight and flat using a wrist rest
Using a chair without any back support

Carpal tunnel risk rises with flexed or extended wrists that compress the median nerve; keeping wrists neutral (straight) with proper support reduces that pressure. Dangling feet and no back support worsen posture.
What is the primary purpose of a workplace drug policy?
To discipline employees who use drugs
To provide treatment and support for employees with substance abuse issues
To prevent workplace accidents and ensure a safe working environment
To comply with federal regulations and avoid lawsuits

A workplace drug and alcohol policy exists primarily to prevent impairment-related incidents and keep the workplace safe; discipline, EAP treatment and compliance are supporting elements, not the primary purpose.
What should a manager do if they suspect an employee is struggling with alcohol abuse?
Ignore the situation as it is a personal matter
Refer the employee to the workplace Employee Assistance Program (EAP)
Discuss the issue openly with all team members to find a solution

Managers should document performance concerns and refer the employee to the EAP for confidential assessment and help; immediate termination or discussing it with the team violates fairness and privacy.
How can alcohol abuse in the workplace affect overall team performance?
It can lower teamwork and morale
It has no impact on team performance
It can lead to lower safety risks and lower productivity
It promotes a culture of tolerance
Alcohol abuse reduces reliability and trust, lowering teamwork and morale and increasing absenteeism and incidents. Option C is wrong because safety risk rises, not falls.
What is the primary purpose of copyright law?
To protect the rights of creators by giving them exclusive rights to their works.
To prevent anyone from using digital media.
To regulate the prices of copyrighted works.

Copyright law grants creators exclusive rights to reproduce, distribute and adapt original works; promoting creativity is the broader policy goal, but the legal mechanism is protecting creators' rights.
Which of the following is an example of a trademark?
A trademark is a word, symbol or logo identifying the source of goods or services; novels, scripts and musical compositions are protected by copyright.
What is the LARGEST risk of not complying with copyright and trademark laws in corporate training materials?
The students know that you did not create the material
None, as educational use is always exempt

Using copyrighted or trademarked content without permission in training materials exposes the company to infringement suits, statutory damages and penalties; educational fair use is limited and not a blanket exemption.
What does the flashpoint of a substance indicate?
The temperature at which it melts
The temperature at which it can suddenly explode
The lowest temperature at which it can vaporize to form an ignitable mixture in air
The temperature at which it freezes
Flash point is the lowest temperature at which a liquid gives off enough vapor to form an ignitable mixture with air near its surface (NFPA 30); it is not the autoignition or explosion temperature.
When nearby combustible materials cannot be removed or guarded during welding, a fire watch must be maintained for at least how long after the work is completed?
OSHA 1910.252(a)(2)(iii) requires the fire watch for at least 30 minutes after hot work ends to detect smoldering fires. NFPA 51B (2019+) extends this to 60 minutes, so read what the question cites.
Per NFPA 850, Recommended Practice for Fire Protection for Electric Generating Plants and High Voltage Direct Current Converter Station, fire protection and water supply mains:
Must be installed before construction starts on the power plant.
Must be installed as major construction progresses.
Not required, as long as a smoke detection system and employee alarms are in place
NFPA 850 recommends that fire protection water supply and mains be installed and placed in service as construction progresses, so protection is available before significant combustibles accumulate.
One standard deviation from the mean encompasses what percentage of data in a normal distribution?
In a normal distribution, about 68.2% of values fall within plus or minus 1 standard deviation of the mean (95.4% within 2 SD, 99.7% within 3 SD). 34.1% is only one side.
What is the formula for calculating the mean (average) of a set of numbers?
Sum of all values / number of values
Product of all values / number of values
Sum of all values * number of values
Square root of the sum of all values
The arithmetic mean = sum of all values divided by the number of values (x-bar = sum x / n).
ISO/IEC 27001 is the information security management system standard; ISO 20000 covers IT service management, ISO 22301 business continuity, ISO 9001 quality.
According to ISO 45001, which of the following is a requirement for an effective occupational health and safety management system?
Mandatory overtime for all employees to ensure production targets are met
Engagement and participation of workers and their representatives in safety management
Outsourcing all high-risk tasks to external contractors
Implementation of a strict zero-tolerance policy towards workplace accidents

ISO 45001 clause 5.4 requires consultation and participation of workers (and their representatives) at all levels; zero-tolerance policies, mandatory overtime or outsourcing risk are not requirements.
What is the primary focus of ISO 45003?
Improving physical health in the workplace
Managing psychosocial risks in the work environment
ISO 45003 gives guidance on managing psychosocial risks (stress, workload, harassment, burnout) within an ISO 45001 OH&S management system.
If a radioactive element decays to 1/8th of its original quantity in 15 years, how long is its half-life?
1/8 = (1/2)^3, so three half-lives elapsed. Half-life = 15 years / 3 = 5 years.
Which of the following is an effective practice for minimizing radiation exposure to personnel?
Increasing the distance between the source of radiation and the individual.
Using higher doses of radiation for shorter times.
Conducting all operations manually to maintain control.
Keeping doors open to radiation areas to improve ventilation.
Radiation protection uses time, distance and shielding; dose rate from a point source falls with the inverse square of distance, so increasing distance is highly effective.
What should be done immediately if a radiation spill occurs?
Evacuate the area and notify the designated radiation safety officer.
Clean up the spill with regular cleaning equipment.
Continue working but avoid the contaminated area.
Seal the area with tape and continue working around it.
For a radioactive spill, stop work, evacuate and secure the area to limit spread and exposure, and notify the Radiation Safety Officer, who directs decontamination with proper equipment.
How many official OSHA crane hand signals are there? Ref App. A 1926 Subpart CC

Appendix A to 1926 Subpart CC references the standard crane hand signal chart, which the source counts as 19 signals (hoist, lower, swing, stop, emergency stop, boom and travel signals, etc.). Note: Count depends on chart version; key accepted per source.
What is the primary purpose of the anti-two block device in crane operations?
To increase the lifting capacity of the crane
To prevent the hook from colliding with the boom tip
To stabilize the crane during high winds
To enhance the speed of the crane operations
An anti-two-block device prevents the hook block or load from contacting the boom tip (two-blocking), which can part the hoist line and drop the load; required by 1926.1416(d)(3).

A crane will work near a power line whose voltage has not been confirmed by the utility. Under OSHA 1926.1408(a)(2), with the line assumed to be up to 350 kV, no part of the crane, load line or load may come closer to the line than:

1926.1408 sets a 20-ft minimum approach distance for lines up to 350 kV unless the utility confirms the voltage, in which case Table A applies (for example 10 ft up to 50 kV). Over 350 kV the distance is 50 ft.
According to the ANSI Z-10 hierarchy of controls, which is the MOST effective method to control a fall risk to a lower level in your facility?
Signage warning of a fall hazard
Safety net to prevent striking the surface below
Barriers to prevent access to the fall hazard

Barriers that prevent access remove exposure to the fall hazard, ranking as engineering control above nets (fall arrest), harnesses (PPE) and signage (administrative/warning) in the ANSI Z10/ISO 45001 hierarchy.
What factors are commonly linked to the occurrence of workplace violence?
Alcohol and drug abuse are widely recognized risk factors linked to workplace violence (OSHA, NIOSH); cameras and background checks are prevention measures, not causes.
What have worker job satisfaction, morale, and stress levels been shown to impact?

Research links low job satisfaction, poor morale and high stress to increased work-related injuries and incidents through distraction, fatigue and risk-taking; lower productivity is a consequence but not the safety-focused answer.
Why is it important to consider cultural diversity when designing communication training for a diverse group?
To ensure all training materials are in English
To promote a single cultural perspective
To cater training to match different communication styles and norms
Effective training adapts to cultural differences in communication styles, norms and language so all learners understand and engage; forcing one perspective or language reduces effectiveness.
A trainee with a visual impairment is attending a training session. What is the most effective way to accommodate their needs?
Provide a written transcript of the training material
Use large print handouts and provide a magnifying glass
Offer one-on-one assistance from a trainer or assistant
Provide audio descriptions of visual aids and offer braille materials

Audio description of visual content plus braille materials provide equivalent access for blind or low-vision learners (ADA effective communication); large print only helps partial sight and transcripts still rely on reading print.
What is the term for the differences in values, attitudes, and behaviors between different age groups, such as Millennials and Baby Boomers?
Generational diversity describes differences in values, attitudes and work behaviors among age cohorts such as Baby Boomers, Gen X, Millennials and Gen Z.
Calculate the momentum of a 1200kg car with a velocity of 25m/s. M=mv
Momentum p = m x v = 1,200 kg x 25 m/s = 30,000 kg.m/s.
What is the unit of electric potential difference?
Electric potential difference is measured in volts (1 V = 1 J/C); joule is energy, watt is power, ohm is resistance.
Which of the following is NOT a type of energy?
Potential, kinetic and magnetic energy are recognized forms of energy; 'yellow energy' is not a physical energy type.
A company incurred $800,000 in losses over the last 3 years. Assuming the same loss rate and no inflation, what are the expected losses over the next 10 years?
Annual rate = 800,000 / 3 = $266,667; x 10 years = $2,666,667. Trap: 2.4 million multiplies by 3.
A company invests $10,000 in exoskeletons for workers who install overhead bolts. The exoskeletons save $15,000 in injury costs in the first year. What is the first-year ROI?
ROI = (benefit - cost)/cost x 100 = (15,000 - 10,000)/10,000 = 50%. Trap: 150% is benefit/cost, not net return.
What is the impact of cutting safety budgets in terms of long-term financial outcomes for a company?
It increases overall profitability by reducing expenses.
It has no impact on the company’s financial health.
It can lead to higher costs from accidents and insurance claims.
It enhances the company’s reputation in the industry.
Cutting safety budgets may lower short-term costs but typically increases incidents, workers' compensation, insurance premiums (EMR), and indirect costs, producing higher long-term costs.
Risk can be referred to as:
The chances of having an unexpected or negative outcome
A calculated output from analysis of all inputs
The movement of uncertainty in the decision-making process.
Risk is the chance (likelihood) of an unexpected or adverse outcome combined with its consequence; it is uncertain, not a certain loss.
Which of the following is true about the relationship between direct and indirect losses?
The impact of indirect losses can be much bigger than the original direct loss.
Direct losses are the result of an indirect loss due to business interruption.
Indirect losses are irrelevant compared to direct losses.
Indirect (uninsured) costs such as downtime, investigation, retraining and lost business often exceed direct costs several times over (iceberg model; Heinrich's 4:1 ratio).
Which one of the following lists presents the three major categories of "legal liability" for a business?
Reputational liability, res ipsa loquitur torts, gross neglience
Criminal wrongs, product liability, intentional interference
Knowing liability, breach of contracts, liability without fault
Business legal liability is commonly grouped into contractual liability, tort liability (negligence, strict liability, intentional torts) and criminal liability.

Fall protection for scaffolds starts at ____________________ feet.
1926.451g
OSHA 1926.451(g)(1) requires fall protection for each employee on a scaffold more than 10 ft above a lower level (vs. 6 ft for general construction under Subpart M).

What should not be used on scaffolds to increase the working level height of employees?
1926.451 f 14

1926.451(f)(14)-(15): makeshift devices such as boxes and barrels, and ladders, shall not be used on scaffold platforms to increase working height (except limited large-area scaffold ladder conditions).

What is the maximum distance the front edge of a scaffold platform can be from the face of the carpentry work, unless guardrail systems or personal fall arrest systems are used?
1926.451 b 3
1926.451(b)(3): the front edge of platforms shall not be more than 14 inches from the work face unless guardrails or PFAS are used (18 inches for plastering and lathing).
Confined Space is not designed for continuous _________________________ occupancy.
OSHA 1910.146 defines a confined space as large enough to enter, with limited entry/exit, and not designed for continuous employee occupancy.
The individual serving as entry ____________________ shall sign and date each confined space permit
1910.146(f)(6): the entry supervisor signs the permit authorizing entry; entry supervisor duties include verifying conditions and terminating entry.

Confined spaces excavations in landfills pose what hazards?
Choose the BEST answer.
Landfill excavations generate methane and hydrogen sulfide (asphyxiation, toxicity and fire/explosion) and pose cave-in risk from unstable fill, making B the most complete set.
Eye and face protection equipment used to protect against hazards shall meet the requirements specified in:
OSHA 1910.133(b) and 1926.102 require eye and face protection to meet ANSI/ISEA Z87.1; Z89.1 covers head protection, Z41 footwear, and Z244.1 lockout.

When selecting proper gloves for chemical materials handling, it is essential to understand the chemical breakthrough rating for the type of chemical the employee may contact. The chemical ratings are E, G, F, and P.
What is the meaning of the "P" chemical breakthrough rating? Please select one of the following options:
Poly-coated, highly recommended (breakthrough times greater than 8 hours)
Perforated, not designed for chemical exposure (breakthrough times less than 1 hour)
Poor, not recommended (breakthrough times less than 1 hour)
Performance, highly recommended (breakthrough times greater than 8 hours)
In glove chemical resistance charts, E = excellent, G = good, F = fair and P = poor (not recommended, short breakthrough time), so P gloves should not be selected for that chemical.
According to OSHA regulations, which of the following is **true** about eye protection in the workplace?
Safety glasses are only required for tasks involving flying objects
Eye protection should only be worn when working with chemicals
All employees must wear safety goggles, even if no visible hazards are present
Eye protection must be provided when there is potential exposure to chemical, environmental, or mechanical hazards

OSHA 1910.133(a)(1) requires appropriate eye or face protection when employees are exposed to hazards from flying particles, molten metal, liquid chemicals, acids or caustics, gases or vapors, or radiation.
When determining which safety courses are needed for employees as a new safety director, what is the first step in the analysis process?
Assessing the cost of the training
Conducting a hazard assessment to identify risks
Training needs start with a hazard/risk assessment (and needs analysis) to identify what workers must know; cost, vendor and scheduling decisions follow once needs are defined.
Which of the following is a key factor in a cost-benefit analysis for safety training?
The number of training materials purchased
The total hours of training required
The potential reduction in accidents and injuries post-training
Cost-benefit analysis compares training costs against benefits, chiefly the avoided injury and incident costs from reduced accidents after training.
What is one advantage of online delivery strategies for safety training?
It allows for greater flexibility in scheduling
It eliminates the need for trainers
Online delivery lets learners train asynchronously at convenient times and locations, giving scheduling flexibility; it still costs money, needs designers, and does not provide hands-on practice.
Training in the hazards of the chemical is ____________ and when a new chemical is introduced.
HazCom 1910.1200(h)(1) requires training at the time of initial assignment and whenever a new chemical hazard is introduced into the work area; annual retraining is not mandated.
The Red in the NFPA diamond is for?
In the NFPA 704 diamond, red indicates flammability (fire), blue health, yellow instability/reactivity, and white special hazards.
Which organization publishes annually the Threshold Limit Values from chemicals every year.
ACGIH publishes its TLVs and BEIs booklet annually; OSHA sets PELs and NIOSH publishes RELs.
Which of the following will BEST help secure a facility from unauthorized access?
Armed guards, Warning signs, and wire-embedded windows.
Fencing, Bright Lights, and Security Cameras
Attack Dogs, Robots, and Light Curtains
Perimeter fencing, lighting and CCTV are core CPTED/physical security layers that deter, detect and delay unauthorized access; attack dogs and drones are not standard best practice.
A site has a URL. This URL stands for:
URL stands for Uniform Resource Locator, the address used to locate a resource on the internet.
In the event of an immediate threat of violence, what should employees do?
Engage in physical self-defense and retaliation
Ignore the threat and continue working
Notify appropriate authorities and follow established emergency procedures
Take matters into their own hands to resolve the situation
For imminent violence, employees should follow the emergency action plan (e.g., run-hide-fight guidance, alerting security) and notify authorities rather than confront or retaliate.
Which statement is correct regarding the use of high visibility retro-reflective personal protective equipment garments?
Garments should be inspected to ensure that micro-reflectors have not been worn off and garment retains proper retro-reflection.
Reflective characteristics should be measured by a coefficient of retro-reflection (cd/lx/m4).
Nighttime flaggers in the work zone are required to wear class 2 retro-reflective yellow/orange gloves at all times.
Nighttime work requires that the outer garment be class 6 retro-reflective orange, yellow, white, silver, or strong yellow-green.

ANSI/ISEA 107 garments lose performance as retroreflective material wears or is soiled, so they must be inspected and replaced. Retroreflection is measured in cd/lx/m2, and garment classes are 1-3 plus E, not 6.
Once hazards have been identified during a site safety assessment, what is the next step?
Implement controls to eliminate or mitigate hazards
Document hazards and move on to the next area

After hazards are identified, the next step is to select and implement controls using the hierarchy (eliminate, substitute, engineer, administrative, PPE); training and PPE are parts of that, not the next step.
What is the LEAST effective in the hierarchy of controls for machine guarding?
Installing fixed guards, interlocked guards, or other physical barriers
Redesigning the machine to eliminate pinch points or hazard areas
Adding safety devices like light curtains or pressure-sensitive mats
Warning signs and labels are administrative/awareness measures that rely on human behavior, the least effective level; redesign is elimination, and guards and devices are engineering controls.
How does the experience modification rate (EMR) impact overall profitability?
The EMR directly influences future insurance premium costs for your company.
It is determined by industry associations and measures customer satisfaction.
The EMR ranks your company and its competitors based on experience and tenure in business.
EMR compares a firm's actual losses to expected losses for its industry; it multiplies workers' compensation premiums, so a higher EMR raises costs and can disqualify bids.
Which of the following is an effective initial approach to defusing conflict?
De-escalation begins with empathy, actively listening and acknowledging feelings to lower emotional intensity; reasoning works only after calm, and threats or discipline escalate conflict.
What is a primary business benefit of maintaining a strong safety culture in the workplace?
A strong safety culture reduces incidents, workers' compensation, insurance and downtime costs, lowering operational costs; the other options are negative outcomes.
The area of a circle with a 18 inch radius is _______ sq inches
What is the formula for water?
Water is H2O, two hydrogen atoms bonded to one oxygen atom; HCl is hydrochloric acid, NaCl salt, CO2 carbon dioxide.
What does the pH scale measure?
The concentration of carbon dioxide in a solution
The concentration of hydroxide ions in a solution
The concentration of hydrogen ions in a solution
The radioactive decay rate in a solution
pH = -log[H+], measuring hydrogen ion concentration; pH 7 is neutral, below 7 acidic, above 7 basic.
Which is the best PREVENTION from being struck by falling tools.
Toeboards at the edge of a floor
Warning line six feet away from an elevator shaft.
Tool tethering prevents the tool from falling at the source, a prevention control; toeboards and nets only stop or catch objects already dropping, and training is administrative.
Which of the following is MOST important for reducing electrical hazards when using power tools?
Using a tool with a plastic casing
Double-insulated tools (or grounded tools with GFCI) provide built-in engineering protection against shock per 1926.302/1910.243; rubber gloves are PPE and ventilation is unrelated.
Which of the following design features minimizes the risk of kickback in power saws?
Riving knives keep the kerf open to prevent binding and anti-kickback pawls grip the stock to stop it being thrown back, engineering features required by 1910.213 for table saws.
What is the primary opportunity cost of sending employees to off-site training sessions?
Opportunity cost is the value of the next best alternative forgone; for off-site training it is mainly lost production time while employees are away (plus travel).
Which of the following best represents a conflicting use of resources during a training session?
The training takes place during normal working hours
The conference room used for training is also needed for a client meeting
Training provides new skills to employees
Employees get extra breaks during training
A conflicting resource use occurs when the same resource is needed simultaneously for two purposes, e.g., a conference room booked for both training and a client meeting.
What is a key strategy to minimize opportunity costs related to training?
Extend the duration of training to ensure comprehensive learning
Schedule training during peak business hours to ensure maximum participation
Use in-house resources for training, such as conference rooms and projectors, when they are not in high demand
Require employees to cover their own travel costs for training
Using in-house rooms and equipment during low-demand periods avoids added rental costs and does not displace other productive uses, minimizing opportunity cost.
Regarding bloodborne pathogen programs, which is a universal precaution?
All custodial workers should wear gloves and appropriate PPE while handling waste.
First responders should have access to prophylactic antiviral treatments.
Treat all bodily fluids as if they are potentially infectious with bloodborne pathogens.
Workers who could be at risk of coming into contact with bloodborne pathogens should be trained.
Under OSHA 1910.1030, universal precautions means treating all human blood and certain body fluids as if known to be infectious for HIV, HBV and other bloodborne pathogens.
A chemical that causes a substantial proportion of exposed people or animals to develop an allergic reaction in normal tissue after repeated exposure to the chemical is called?
A sensitizer causes an allergic (immune) reaction in a substantial proportion of exposed people after repeated exposure (1910.1200 Appendix A); ototoxic chemicals damage hearing.
Which infection is associated with milk?
Brucellosis is a zoonotic bacterial disease (Brucella) transmitted through unpasteurized milk and dairy products or contact with infected livestock.
What is the pH of a solution that contains 10^{-2} hydrogen ions per liter?
pH = -log[H+] = -log(10^-2 mol/L) = 2, a strongly acidic solution.
If you have a cylindrical tank with a height of 7 meters and a radius of 2 meters, what is its volume? Use the formula V=π×r2×h.
What is the primary principle behind Pareto Analysis?
80% of problems are caused by 20% of causes.
20% of workers contribute to 80% of results.
50% of problems are caused by 50% of causes.
100% of results come from 100% of efforts.
The Pareto principle states roughly 80% of effects come from 20% of causes, so analysis focuses resources on the vital few causes.
Which set of elements should be incorporated into an effective safety management program?
Plan-Do-Check-Act (Deming cycle) is the continual improvement structure underlying ANSI/ASSP Z10 and ISO 45001 safety management systems.
Which initiative is MOST effective in reducing the potential for serious injury or fatality in a workplace?
Requiring use of personal protective equipment
Having pre-job planning and safety analysis
Pre-job planning and hazard analysis identify and control SIF precursors before work starts, addressing high-energy hazards proactively; PPE is the last line of defense and meetings are general.
What is risk mitigation in the context of business risk management?
Ignoring risks and hoping for the best
Reducing or controlling the impact and likelihood of risks
Transferring all risks to external parties
Accepting all risks without taking any action
KEY CORRECTED by trainer review: Risk mitigation = reducing the likelihood and/or impact of risks.
What is the primary focus of LEED certification?
Sustainable building performance, such as energy efficiency and water conservation
LEED (Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design) rates buildings on energy, water, materials, indoor environmental quality and site sustainability.

Spray booths shall be so installed that all portions are readily accessible for cleaning. A clear space of not less than _______ feet on all sides shall be kept free from storage or combustible construction. 1910.107
OSHA 1910.107(b)(9) requires a clear space of not less than 3 ft on all sides of a spray booth kept free from storage or combustible construction.
Which of the following is the BEST first step when starting a Job Hazard Analysis?
Review the company's annual safety report
Analyze the efficiency of equipment used in production
Break down the job into individual tasks and steps
JHA (OSHA 3071) begins by selecting the job and breaking it into a sequence of basic steps, then identifying hazards for each step and determining controls.
By solving the inequality 4.5a < 18, the answer will be
Divide both sides by 4.5 (positive, so the inequality sign stays): a < 18/4.5 = 4.
The distance from the center of circle to the outer most boundary is called
The radius is the distance from the center to any point on the circle; the diameter is twice the radius and a chord connects two points on the circle.
Micro means 10^-6, so 1 microgram = 0.000001 g (0.001 mg).
Who has overall responsibility in a large emergency such as a hazardous material spill of Vinyl Chloride from several tank cars?
Under NIMS/ICS and HAZWOPER 1910.120(q), the Incident Commander has overall authority and responsibility for managing the emergency response.
A powerline of 7200 volts has fallen across the crane’s outrigger. What is the best course of action for the crane operator?
Use the crane to lift the line out off the outrigger.
Jump out of the cab and shuffle their feet to get away.
Use an insulated hot stick to lift the wire off the outrigger.
Stay in the cab until emergency crews arrive.

With energized line contact, the operator should stay in the cab (unless fire forces exit, then jump clear with feet together and shuffle) until the utility de-energizes the line, avoiding step and touch potential.
Which roles are generally part of the command staff in the Incident Command System (ICS)?
Public Information Officer, Chief Executive Officer, and Safety Officer
Logistics Section Chief, Safety Officer, and Contracting Officer
Liaison Officer, Operations Section Chief, and Finance Section Chief
Safety Officer, Public Information Officer, and Liaison Officer
ICS Command Staff consists of the Public Information Officer, Safety Officer and Liaison Officer; Operations, Planning, Logistics and Finance/Admin chiefs are General Staff.
What is the primary purpose of developing trainee materials in a lesson plan?
To provide background on the instructor's qualifications
To serve as reference materials that support trainee learning and retention
To fill time during the training session
To serve as decorative elements for the training session
Trainee materials (handouts, job aids, workbooks) reinforce lesson content and serve as references after training, improving learning and retention.
Which of the following is a key component of an effective instructor manual?
A list of the personal achievements of the instructor
Step-by-step guidance on how to deliver course content and facilitate discussions
An outline of trainee assessment techniques only
A copy of the company’s yearly report
An instructor manual/guide gives step-by-step delivery guidance: objectives, timing, activities, discussion prompts and assessment notes, so instruction is consistent across trainers.
What is the role of job aids in a training program?
To test trainees' knowledge at the end of the course
To introduce new theories unrelated to the course
To provide feedback to the instructor
To help trainees apply the skills learned to their daily tasks
Job aids (checklists, flowcharts, pocket cards) support correct performance on the job and reduce reliance on memory, especially for infrequent or critical tasks.
What is the primary goal of fleet safety programs?
Fleet safety programs (ANSI/ASSP Z15.1) aim to reduce crash risk, injuries, property damage and associated liability; profitability and morale are secondary benefits.
What is the most common cause of distracted driving?
Using a cell phone while driving
NHTSA identifies cell phone use (talking and especially texting) as the most common and dangerous cause of distracted driving because it combines visual, manual and cognitive distraction.
What is a common indicator of driver fatigue?
Drowsy driving signs include yawning, heavy eyelids, difficulty staying awake, drifting from the lane and missing exits; increased speed and aggression are not typical fatigue indicators.
What is the primary responsibility of managers in ensuring lockout/tagout (LOTO) compliance?
Ensuring all machines have visible warning labels
Verifying that energy control procedures are documented, implemented, and reviewed annually
Overseeing employee attendance during lockout/tagout training sessions

1910.147 requires the employer to establish documented energy control procedures, train employees, and conduct periodic inspections at least annually; managers ensure this program is implemented and reviewed.
How often are managers required to conduct periodic inspections of energy control procedures?
Only when a new machine is installed
1910.147(c)(6) requires periodic inspection of each energy control procedure at least annually by an authorized employee other than those using the procedure.
Which of the following statements about lockout/tagout is FALSE?
Lockout/tagout procedures are only necessary for electrical hazards.
Personal locks should have the individual's name and other identifying information.
A lockout device is used to hold an energy-isolating device in a safe position.
Tagout devices are warning devices affixed to energy-isolating devices and do not provide the physical restraint that a lock does.
Lockout/tagout covers all hazardous energy (electrical, mechanical, hydraulic, pneumatic, chemical, thermal, gravity), so A is false; B, C and D are true per 1910.147.
A ladder shall be within _______ ft for an employee when placed in a trench.
OSHA 1926.651(c)(2) requires a means of egress in trenches 4 ft or deeper within 25 ft of lateral travel for employees.
An excavation is being performed in an old landfill. What should the air be tested for? (xCHST rewritten question, not in book)
Decomposing landfill waste produces methane (flammable/asphyxiant) and hydrogen sulfide (toxic), so atmospheres should be tested for these plus O2 and LEL.
Employees shall not be allowed in trench shields when shields are? Ref: 1926.652(g)(1)(iv)
Being installed, removed, moved vertically or horizontally
Being installed, removed, or moved horizontally
Being installed, removed, or moved vertically.
1926.652(g)(1)(iv): employees shall not be allowed in shields when shields are being installed, removed, or moved vertically.
In the context of effective workplace safety programs, which trio of responsibility categories is deemed essential? (This is from the NSC Supervisor Safety Manual)
Managing/prequalifying subcontractors, training/orienting to site safety, and ensuring facility security/upkeep.
Managing budget/finances, overseeing equipment/tools, and handling emergency response/medical care.
Overseeing administrative/management tasks, handling operational/technical aspects, and promoting cultural/behavioral safety norms.
Enforcing discipline/accountability, facilitating training/development, and conducting safety management/audits.
The NSC Supervisor's Safety Manual groups safety responsibilities as administrative/management, operational/technical, and cultural/behavioral, which together build an effective program.
Safety goals for any organization should possess the following characteristics:
They should be sufficiently broad to ensure their attainment.
They should be established by the executive management of the organization.
They should be based on injury rates.
Effective safety goals must be achievable and measurable (SMART). Broad goals cannot be tracked, and injury rates alone are lagging measures.
What steps should be taken if a facility continuously experiences accidents due to serious hazards not being identified? (Yates 2nd p648)
Educate inspectors to identify different hazards.
Educate employees to recognize different hazards.
If serious hazards are repeatedly missed, the inspection process is failing; per Yates, inspectors must be trained to recognize a broader range of hazards so inspections are effective.
OSHA requires screen protection from ____________ welding rays.
OSHA 1910.252(b)(2)(iii) and 1926.351 require screens or shields to protect nearby workers from arc welding rays (UV/IR radiation).
Always protect ______ from being run over by equipment. Avoid kinks and tangles.
Oxy-fuel and welding hoses must be protected from traffic, kinks and tangles (1910.253, 1926.350) because damage can cause leaks, fire or flashback.
What type of clothing should be worn while welding?
Tight-fitting clothes to avoid catching sparks
Welders should wear flame-resistant, non-synthetic (e.g., wool, heavy cotton) clothing without cuffs; synthetics melt onto skin and loose clothing catches sparks.
Which is a measure to PREVENT a dust explosion?
Installing explosion venting in a dust collector.
Installing an extinguishing system in the dust collector.
Housekeeping removes the accumulated dust fuel, preventing a secondary explosion; venting, suppression and outdoor location mitigate consequences rather than prevent the explosion.
What five conditions are needed for a dust explosion? Oxygen / Dispersion / Ignition Source / Fuel and ?
The dust explosion pentagon adds dispersion and confinement (containment) to the fire triangle of fuel, oxygen and ignition source (NFPA 652).
In the event of a combustible dust explosion, what safety measure is crucial?
Having a water sprinkler system installed
Ensuring all workers are wearing soundproof headphones
Providing escape routes and emergency exits
Turning off all lights in the facility
Clear escape routes and emergency exits allow workers to evacuate quickly after a dust explosion, which often triggers secondary explosions and fires; sprinklers may help but egress protects life.
What is the primary goal of a well-structured classroom layout?
To provide enough seating for students.
To make the classroom visually appealing.
To enhance student interaction and facilitate learning.
To ensure the instructor has a comfortable seat.
A classroom layout should support interaction and learning, matching the arrangement to the instructional method rather than aesthetics or seating count.
Which of these classroom setups is most effective for promoting student collaboration?
Teacher-centered setup with no group tables.
A U-shaped arrangement lets participants see each other and the instructor, encouraging discussion and collaboration; auditorium and rows are lecture-centered.
Which of the following is a benefit of active learning spaces?
Increased engagement and participation from students.
Active learning spaces with flexible furniture and technology increase learner engagement and participation, which improves retention.
These devices use cables or straps that are attached to the operator's hands at a fixed point.
Restraint (holdout) devices attach cables or straps to the operator's hands at a fixed point so hands cannot reach the danger zone; pullback devices move with the ram to pull hands out.
What is the primary purpose of machine guarding in the workplace?
To make the machine run energy efficient
To prevent accidental startup of machines
To protect workers from hazards such as cuts, burns, or crushing injuries
Per 1910.212, machine guarding protects operators and others from point-of-operation, nip point, rotating part and flying chip hazards that cause amputations, cuts and crushing.
What should be considered when installing a machine guard?
The guard should only be installed on new machines.
It must be easily removable for maintenance without the need for special tools.
The guard should only cover electrical hazards.
The guard should allow for normal operation while preventing access to danger zones.
Effective guards prevent contact with hazards while allowing normal operation; they must be secure, not easily removed without tools, and create no new hazards (OSHA 3170).
Which is the best way to convey the safety message on a jobsite.
In-person, face-to-face communication allows two-way dialogue, demonstration and immediate verification of understanding, making it most effective on a jobsite.
Which is the BEST slide type for PowerPoint?
The 6 x 6 rule (about six lines with six words each) keeps slides readable and focused; 150 words and all-capitals reduce readability.
What is the MOST effective way to demonstrate to senior management that the company will benefit from the money invested in safety initiatives?
Provide proven results showing a portion of the safety budget returning to the company.
Present a return on investment (ROI) analysis demonstrating 15% or higher.
Utilize a cost-benefit analysis comparing the cost of training to potential injury/incident costs.
Highlight the regulatory standards mandating safety training for all employees.

A cost-benefit analysis directly compares safety investment costs with avoided incident costs (direct and indirect), showing management the business value; arbitrary ROI thresholds or compliance alone are weaker.
What is the formula for the volume of a cylinder?
Cylinder volume V = pi x r^2 x h (base area times height); V = lwh is a rectangular prism.
Which geometric shape is most effective for maximizing stability in construction and other temporary structures?
Triangles are rigid; their shape cannot change without changing side lengths, so triangulated bracing (as in scaffolds and trusses) maximizes stability.
When considering the angle of a ladder against a wall for safe usage, what is the recommended angle between the ladder and the ground for maximum safety?
OSHA 1926.1053(b)(5)(i) and ANSI A14 call for about 75 degrees, the 1:4 horizontal-to-working-length ratio.

Anchorages used for attachment of personal fall arrest equipment shall be independent of any anchorage being used to support or suspend platforms and capable of supporting at least ____________ pounds per employee attached. 1926.502(d)
1926.502(d)(15): PFAS anchorages must support at least 5,000 lb per employee attached, or be designed with a safety factor of two under a qualified person.
What is prohibited for fall arrest over 5 feet.
Since 1998 OSHA 1926.502(d) prohibits body belts as part of a personal fall arrest system because of injury risk; they are allowed only for positioning.
According to OSHA standards, at what height must fall protection be provided in general industry workplaces? Ref: 1910.28
OSHA 1910.28(b)(1) requires fall protection in general industry at 4 ft or more above a lower level (6 ft in construction).
When traveling with a load on a forklift, what should the operator do to ensure stability and prevent tipping?
Carry the load at a high height
Use the forklift on an uneven surface
Sudden turns, stops or starts shift the combined center of gravity outside the stability triangle; operators should travel at safe speed with the load low and tilted back (1910.178).
When should a forklift operator use the horn?
Only when a pedestrian is nearby
At blind corners, intersections, or when approaching people
Only when they feel like it
1910.178(n)(4) requires operators to slow down and sound the horn at cross aisles and other locations where vision is obstructed, and when approaching pedestrians.
How should a forklift operator travel when carrying a load on an incline?
Always travel downhill with the load in front
Always travel uphill with the load in front
The direction doesn’t matter, as long as the operator is careful
Avoid traveling on inclines with a load
1910.178(n)(7): on grades, loaded trucks are driven with the load upgrade, so going up the load is in front (forward travel) and going down the truck travels in reverse.
What is an important ethical responsibility outlined in the BCSP Code of Ethics?
Being honest, fair, and impartial in all professional actions.
Prioritizing the interests of employers above all else.
Acting in a way that only benefits colleagues and clients.
The BCSP Code of Ethics requires certificants to act with honesty, fairness and impartiality and to hold paramount the safety and health of people.

Sunday, a worker twisted the knee.
He went to the hospital at night since the clinic was closed.
The hospital doctor wrote 2 days off and a prescription anti-inflammatory.
The company doctor was absent on Monday.
Tuesday, the company doctor says the worker is ready to go back to work.
The CEO doesn't want the streak of no injuries broken.
Your response should be:
Provide an OSHA letter of interpretation that says it is recordable.
Tell the CEO that OSHA might be called, and he would go to jail.
Have the company doctor write that the worker was not hurt Sunday, and it is not recordable

Prescription medication and days away (doctor-recommended) make the case recordable under 1904.7 regardless of the company doctor's later opinion; documented OSHA interpretations persuade management ethically.
Regarding the Board of Certified Safety Professionals (BCSP) code of ethics, which statement is MOST accurate?
Adherence to the code is required for individuals who have received present and past certifications from BCSP.
Only government agency employees in the safety field are required to follow the code.
The code must be followed by individuals currently certified by the BCSP.
Every professional with a safety degree must observe the BCSP code of ethics.

Per the source, the BCSP Code of Ethics binds individuals who hold or have held BCSP credentials, as conduct while certified remains subject to the code. Note: BCSP applies the code to certificants and candidates; key accepted per source.
What is the primary purpose of evaluating safety training?
To reduce the cost of future training programs
To determine if the training objectives were met and if it improved workplace safety
To increase the number of training sessions offered
Training evaluation (Kirkpatrick levels) determines whether learning objectives were met and whether behavior and safety results improved.
Which of the following is an example of a method for evaluating the effectiveness of safety training?
Reviewing the company’s annual profit and loss statements
Using surveys or feedback forms to gather employee input on the training
Conducting a site inspection before training starts
Comparing safety training topics with other companies
Surveys and feedback forms measure participant reaction (Kirkpatrick Level 1), a common evaluation method; tests, observations and incident trends measure higher levels.
How can safety training evaluations help improve future training sessions?
By eliminating the need for future training
By reducing the length of training sessions
By determining which employees need to be retrained immediately
By identifying areas where training was ineffective or unclear and adjusting future content accordingly
Evaluation findings show where content, methods or delivery were ineffective so future training can be revised, part of the ADDIE continuous improvement loop.
Running other software on idle computer without the knowledge of the organization is called theft of ____
Using an employer's computer resources for unauthorized purposes is theft of computer time (misuse of resources), an IT ethics concept.
Which strategy is commonly recognized for multinational companies to handle the diversity of statutory laws across different countries?
Lobby to change the laws in each country to make them uniform.
Align all operations with the least restrictive country law.
Conform all operations to the strictest laws of the country where the corporate office is based.
Ensure compliance with the laws of each country where branches are located.
Multinationals must comply with the laws of each host country where they operate, often adopting a corporate baseline that meets or exceeds local law.
Four liability theories can render a defendant liable for Injuries they may have caused. These are intent, recklessness, negligence, and ______________ .
Liability arises from intent, recklessness, negligence, and strict liability, where liability attaches without fault (e.g., abnormally dangerous activities, defective products).
Which pesticide was banned by EPA in 1972.
EPA banned general use of DDT in 1972 due to bioaccumulation and harm to wildlife and potential human health effects.
Under EPCRA Section 302, what is a 'threshold planning quantity' (TPQ)?
The minimum quantity of any chemical that can be stored without reporting
The quantity of an extremely hazardous substance (EHS) on site that triggers emergency planning notification
The maximum amount of any chemical that may be released without consequence
The quantity of waste a company must dispose of yearly to avoid EPA oversight
When an EHS is present at or above its TPQ, the facility must notify the state and local emergency planning bodies and take part in local emergency planning.
Under the CAA (Clean Air Act), the EPA has established six criteria for pollutants. They are Lead, Carbon Monoxide, Sulfur Dioxide, Nitrogen Oxides, Ozone and?
The six NAAQS criteria pollutants are ozone, particulate matter (PM10/PM2.5), carbon monoxide, lead, sulfur dioxide and nitrogen dioxide; VOCs are ozone precursors, not criteria pollutants.
With few exceptions, OSHA requires that PPE used to comply with OSHA standards be paid for by the:
OSHA 1910.132(h) requires employers to pay for required PPE, with limited exceptions such as ordinary safety-toe footwear and prescription eyewear.
What is the most important initial action when arriving at an accident scene?
Secure the area and assess hazards.
Responders must first secure the scene and assess hazards to prevent further injury to themselves and others, then summon help and provide care.
The incident investigation uses a tool to identify factors causing the injury. This is referred to as:
Root cause analysis identifies the underlying system causes (management, design, procedures) that led to the incident, so corrective actions prevent recurrence.
What is the basic provision that workers' compensation insurance is designed to offer?
Ensure employment for the rest of their career.
Cover all medical expenses and a set percentage of their standard wage.
Provide a one-time lump sum settlement, determined by the type of injury.
Cover all medical costs related to a workplace injury.

Workers' compensation is a no-fault system providing medical care plus wage replacement (indemnity), typically about two-thirds of average weekly wage, for work-related injury or illness. D omits wage benefits.
A disciplinary program works more effectively if
Used in a positive manner for reinforcement of safety rules
Disciplinary cases are widely publicized within the department
It’s a one step process done with immediacy
Discipline is most effective when applied fairly and positively to reinforce safety rules and correct behavior, typically as progressive discipline, rather than publicized or harsh.
___________________ is a common element of disaster recovery and business continuity phases of disaster contingency planning
Worker training for new skills needed
ICS/NIMS provides a common, scalable management structure used across response, recovery and continuity phases of disaster contingency planning.
Aside from OSHA's safety and health program guidelines, which consensus standards BEST establish occupational safety and health management system approaches?

ISO 45001 and ANSI/ASSP Z10.0 are the principal consensus standards for occupational health and safety management systems. ISO 9001 is quality, ISO 14001 environmental, ISO 19011 audit guidance, and Lean a production method.
What is the primary purpose of getting employee and management feedback during change management?
To identify and assess the influence of various parties on the change process
To determine the financial implications of the change
To assign blame for past failures
To create a detailed plan for implementing the change
Feedback from employees and managers identifies stakeholders, their influence and concerns, so the change process can address resistance and impacts (MOC stakeholder analysis).
What does a Fault Tree Analysis (FTA) focus on in a system safety assessment?
Visualizing and analyzing potential causes of system failures
FTA is a top-down deductive method starting with an undesired top event and using AND/OR logic gates to trace combinations of failures that cause it.
Which of the following best describes a "fail-passive" system?
When a system fails, it activates a backup system to maintain its operation.
Upon failure, the system might cause a new hazard that wasn't previously present.
If a system encounters a failure, it ceases its operation without creating any adverse effects.
The system continuously monitors and corrects its own failures without human intervention

Fail-passive design: on failure the system goes to its lowest-energy/inoperative state without creating an adverse effect (e.g., a circuit breaker opening). Fail-active/operational designs keep functioning.
When performing a jobsite observation, what is the most effective way to gather accurate safety information?
Relying on memory after leaving the jobsite
Completing a structured observation checklist during the site visit
Asking employees to submit written feedback on their own performance
Focusing only on areas where previous incidents occurred
A structured checklist completed during the observation captures consistent, accurate data in real time; relying on memory or self-reports introduces bias and omissions.
Which is an essential element of a good management observation program?
Ensuring observations are done sporadically and unannounced
Focusing only on worker behavior without reviewing equipment
Providing immediate feedback to workers after observations
Observing only the top-level managers at the site
Immediate, specific feedback after an observation reinforces safe behaviors and corrects at-risk ones (behavior-based safety ABC model).
What is the primary purpose of conducting a course evaluation after workplace safety training?
To critique the instructor's performance only
To gather feedback for improving future training sessions
To determine the wages of participants
To compare the course with other training programs
Post-course evaluations collect participant feedback on content, delivery and relevance to improve future sessions.

Slings used in rigging must be visually inspected by a competent person.
Ref: 1926.251 (a)(6)
1926.251(a)(6): each day before use, slings and fastenings must be inspected by a competent person for damage or defects.
What is the primary purpose of a tagline when rigging a load?
To increase the lifting capacity of the crane
To prevent the load from spinning or swinging
To measure the weight of the load
To protect the load from damage
Taglines let workers control load rotation and swing from a safe distance, keeping them out of the load path.
The weight is 1000 pounds to be lifted. The sling angle from the horizontal is 60 degrees. What is the tension in each sling leg in pounds?
Leg tension = (W / number of legs) / sin(angle) = (1,000 lb / 2) / sin 60 = 500 / 0.866 = 577 lb.
One _________________ is defined as the Current that FLOWS with electric charge of one Coulomb per second.
One ampere is a current of one coulomb of charge passing a point per second (I = Q/t).
Which is true about a Ground Fault Circuit interrupter.
It will interrupt current in 1/40th of a second.
It will tell the impedance in a circuit.
It prevents a voltage spike so that computers are protected.
A Class A GFCI trips at about 5 mA ground fault current within roughly 1/40 second (25 ms), fast enough to prevent electrocution; it detects current imbalance, not voltage.

Cord and plug connected equipment should be checked daily before use if using an assured equipment grounding program. 
Ref: 1926.404(b)(1)(iii)(C).
Only required if equipment shows visible damage
Only required on a weekly basis
Under 1926.404(b)(1)(iii)(C) assured equipment grounding programs, cord sets and cord-and-plug equipment must be visually inspected before each day's use.
Which of the following is an example of a leading indicator in safety?
Number of days without an accident
Leading indicators measure proactive activities (audits, inspections, training, near-miss reports) that predict future performance; days without accidents, TRIR and claims are lagging.
The first indicators that are used in performance appraisals.
The lagging indicators that are critical.
Trends that predict future loss performance
Leading indicators are proactive, predictive measures that signal future safety performance and allow intervention before losses occur.
Which of the following is an example of a lagging indicator in safety?
Number of safety training sessions conducted
TRIR measures injuries that have already occurred, a lagging (outcome) indicator; training, inspections and hazard reports are leading.
