What is the primary purpose of emergency drills and exercises?
To provide an ergonomic-related break from repetitive daily activities
To evaluate the overall effectiveness of emergency response procedures and the emergency action plan
To meet the ISO standard for the required number of drills per week
To enhance employee awareness of worst-case scenarios
Drills test and evaluate the emergency action plan and response procedures, revealing gaps in alarms, evacuation and roles for correction (1910.38, NFPA 1600).
4000 gallons of gasoline was spilled from a tanker truck and flowed into the local river. Which person is responsible for the ongoing emergency response?
Under ICS/NIMS and HAZWOPER 1910.120(q)(3), the Incident Commander directs the ongoing emergency response; the Safety Officer advises the IC.
What is the primary purpose of an emergency preparedness plan?
To ensure rapid response and recovery during emergencies
To limit the number of safety drills
An emergency preparedness plan prepares people and resources so the organization can respond rapidly, protect life and property, and recover from emergencies (NFPA 1600, 1910.38).
What is a factor implicated in many incidents related to violence in the workplace?
The workplace has high stress levels.
The workplace has some workers with a criminal record.
The workplace allows drinking alcohol at lunch.
The workplace requires workers to be in the office four days a week.

High stress levels (workload, layoffs, conflict) are frequently implicated in workplace violence incidents; a criminal record alone is not a reliable predictor. Note: Alcohol at lunch (C) is also a recognized factor; stress is the broader key.

In the progression of the aggression continuum related to workplace incidents of aggressive behavior, violence is seen as the culminating step.
Which step represents the LAST phase before reaching this point?
In the aggression continuum, behavior escalates through anxiety and stress/defensiveness toward intimidation and threats, the last phase before physical violence.
________________ temperature is the temperature at which the vapor of flammable material ignites an air without an ignition source.
Autoignition temperature is the minimum temperature at which a material's vapor-air mixture ignites spontaneously without a spark or flame; flash point requires an ignition source.
A fire evacuation simulation was given at a hospital. The audit observer noted multiple issues made by nurses during the drill. What should the follow-up for the drill be?
Provide training for the nursing staff
Ignore the issues and assume they won't happen again
Conduct a written test on evacuation procedures
Drill deficiencies by a specific group indicate a knowledge or performance gap, so targeted training for the nursing staff should follow, then re-drilling to verify improvement.
Large building under construction for an industrial facility should what kind of protection to prevent fires at the job site.
A daily visit by the fire department to job trailer of the project superintendent.
Fire insurance of 110% the value of the property and material.
An established program of pre-fire plans consisting of daily surveillance and housekeeping.
NFPA 241 (construction fire safety) relies on pre-fire planning, a fire prevention program manager, surveillance and good housekeeping to prevent fires at construction sites.
The maximum opening between vertical members such as balusters on a stair is _______ inches. 1926.1052(c)(4)(iii)
1926.1052(c)(4)(iii): intermediate vertical members (balusters) in stair rail systems shall be spaced not more than 19 inches apart.
The top or ______________ step of a stepladder shall not be used as a step. Ref: 1926.1053(b)(13)
1926.1053(b)(13): the top or top step of a stepladder shall not be used as a step, as it destabilizes the ladder.
When ascending or descending a ladder, the worker should:
Face the ladder and maintain three points of contact.
Carry tools and materials in their hands for efficiency.
Lean away from the ladder to reach objects.
Use the top two steps for better reach.
1926.1053(b)(20)-(22): face the ladder and maintain at least one hand (three points of contact) while climbing, and do not carry objects that could cause loss of balance.
Epoxy sensitization in adhesives would MOST affect the ____________.
Epoxy resins and hardeners are strong skin sensitizers causing allergic contact dermatitis, the most common health effect among epoxy users.
A carpenter that has a sore elbow from hammering nails might be suffering from:
Lateral epicondylitis (tennis elbow) is tendon inflammation at the elbow from repetitive forceful gripping and wrist extension, such as hammering.
What is the primary function of the spinal column in workplace ergonomics?
To facilitate the movement of the upper and lower limbs.
To provide structural support and protect the spinal cord.
To produce blood cells for oxygen transport.
The spinal column provides structural support for the body and protects the spinal cord; ergonomics aims to keep it in neutral posture to avoid disc and muscle injury.
What is the MOST appropriate guideline for safe chemical handling?
Always assume that any unfamiliar chemical substance is hazardous.
Most chemicals are no longer hazardous after their expiration date.
Safety data sheets are not specific to a chemical’s year of production.
PPE should always be utilized as a control for chemical exposure.
Prudent practice is to treat any unknown chemical as hazardous until identified with its SDS; PPE is the last control, not always the primary one.
What is the first step in conducting an occupational exposure assessment?
Exposure assessment (AIHA strategy) begins with basic characterization: identifying hazards, agents and tasks, then evaluating exposures and selecting controls.
Which organization sets widely recognized exposure limits (TLV) for various substances in the workplace?
National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health (NIOSH)
American Conference of Governmental Industrial Hygienists (ACGIH)
ACGIH publishes Threshold Limit Values (TLVs); OSHA sets enforceable PELs and NIOSH publishes RELs.
What is the purpose of an N95 respirator?
To protect against sulfur dioxide pollution
To shield against harmful chemical solvents
An N95 filtering facepiece filters at least 95% of airborne particles (not oil resistant); it offers no protection from gases such as SO2 or solvent vapors and supplies no oxygen.
What injury is when the tendon sheath on the thumb side of wrist is irritated from overuse of the wrist?
De Quervain's tendinitis/tenosynovitis affects tendon sheaths on the thumb side of the wrist from repetitive gripping and wrist deviation; carpal tunnel involves the median nerve.
Which type of injury is the single LARGEST occupational health hazard?
Repetitive-motion and other musculoskeletal disorders account for the largest share of occupational illnesses and lost-time cases (BLS), making them the leading occupational health hazard.
Which of the following is an indicator of potential substance abuse in the workplace?
Enhanced productivity and meticulous attention to detail
Strengthened relationships with coworkers and supervisors
Reduced levels of stress and anxiety
Frequent tardiness, absenteeism, performance decline and behavior changes are common indicators of possible substance abuse; the other options are positive traits.
What should a supervisor do if they suspect an employee is under the influence of a substance at work?
Confront the employee and accuse them of substance abuse
Ignore the behavior and hope it doesn't happen again
Document the behavior and report it to HR or management
Try to cover up the behavior to avoid disciplinary action
Supervisors should document observable behaviors and follow policy by reporting to HR or management for reasonable suspicion procedures; they should not diagnose, accuse or ignore.
Which of the following BEST describes active listening in a conflict resolution conversation?
Restating what was said to confirm understanding
Listening for weaknesses in the other person's argument
Agreeing with everything to avoid further conflict
Taking notes to use against the other person later
Active listening means paraphrasing and checking understanding, which builds trust and surfaces the real issue.
In a training session, if a conflict arises between participants, what is the first step you should take as the facilitator?**
Encourage the participants to continue the discussion until they resolve it on their own
Immediately stop the training and send everyone home
Identify the points of agreement before addressing the differences
Focus on who is to blame for the conflict
Facilitators de-escalate by finding common ground, identifying points of agreement first, then addressing differences constructively; blame or unmanaged debate escalates conflict.
During a safety training session, a participant repeatedly interrupts with irrelevant questions and comments, disrupting the flow of the training. How should the trainer address this behavior?
Publicly reprimand the participant to discourage further disruptions.
Ignore the participant and continue with the training.
Politely ask the participant to hold their questions until a designated Q&A period or offer to address them privately during a break.
Sarcastically thank the participant for their "valuable contributions."
Respectfully redirect the disruptive participant by parking questions for a Q&A or a private discussion, maintaining the learner's dignity and the session flow.
Mode is the most frequent value; 3 appears twice, so mode = 3. Mean = 31/5 = 6.2 and median = 5 are the distractors.
If the scores in a dataset are spread out far from the mean, the dataset will have a:
Standard deviation measures spread about the mean; widely dispersed values produce a high SD. SD can never be negative.
Which set of numbers has the highest average?
Means: A = 10, B = 100/4 = 25, C = 80/4 = 20, D = 120/4 = 30. D has the highest average.
ISO 9001 specifies requirements for a quality management system; ISO 45001 covers OH&S and ISO 31000 risk management.
Which of the following is a key principle of ISO 45001?
ISO 45001 is built on PDCA with continual improvement of OH&S performance as a core principle (clause 10.3).
Which of the following is a requirement for an organization implementing ISO 45001?
The organization must use a specific set of tools for risk management as prescribed by ISO.
The organization must ensure that workers from external providers are trained in the internal safety practices.
The organization must commit to eliminating hazards and minimizing OH&S risks, including the continual improvement of its OH&S management system.
All members of the organization must be certified individually in OH&S practices.
ISO 45001 policy must include commitments to eliminate hazards and reduce OH&S risks and to continual improvement; it does not prescribe specific tools or individual certification.
What is the primary purpose of wearing a dosimeter when working with radiation?
To measure the total amount of radiation exposure received.
To prevent radiation from entering the body.
To shield the body from alpha particles.
To decontaminate the body after radiation exposure.
Personal dosimeters (TLD, OSL, film badge) measure the cumulative dose a worker receives; they provide no shielding or protection.
Which action most effectively minimizes radiation exposure?
Maximizing the distance from the radiation source
Minimizing the time spent near the radiation source
Taking iodine supplements before radiation exposure

Distance is highly effective because dose rate decreases with the inverse square of distance (doubling distance cuts dose to 1/4); time and shielding are the other ALARA tools. Note: Time, distance and shielding are all valid; distance keyed via inverse square law.
What is the meaning of ALARA in radiation safety protocols?
ALARA, As Low As Reasonably Achievable, is the NRC (10 CFR 20) principle of keeping radiation doses below limits as far as practical using time, distance and shielding.
A wireless anemometer is used on a crane to measure?
An anemometer measures wind speed; crane operators use it to stop lifts when wind exceeds manufacturer limits (1926.1417(n)).
According to OSHA standards, what must an employer do when manufacturer's procedures for crane operation are unavailable? Ref. 1926.1441(c)(2)
Discontinue using the crane until manufacturer's procedures are obtained.
Develop and ensure compliance with necessary safe operation procedures, and ensure operational control procedures are developed by a qualified person.
Use common industry practices for crane operations.
Only ensure that the crane's operational controls are regularly inspected

1926.1441(c)(2): when manufacturer procedures are unavailable, the employer must develop and ensure compliance with safe operating procedures, with operational control procedures developed by a qualified person.
To identify areas within your facility that are most susceptible to slip, trip, or fall hazards, which tool would be MOST suitable for your use?
Root cause analysis of previous slip, trip, or fall incidents
Facility floor plan showing locations of related injuries for the past 12 months
Recent Inspection reports indicating potential risk factors for walking and working surfaces
Near miss reports related to unsafe conditions

Recent inspection reports identify current walking-working surface risk factors (1910.22) before injuries occur, the most direct tool for locating susceptible areas; incident data reflects past events only.

If construction workers at your facility are seen carrying 80-pound (36.29 kilograms) bags of material up four flights of stairs, which action should the on-site safety manager take first to mitigate the risk of incidents or injuries?
Ref: Elements of Ergonomic Programs; National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health. (1997).
Assess the work for duration, stress, work rotation, and material handling concerns.
Provide a hoisting device to raise the materials to the 4th floor.
Conduct a safety meeting to discuss proper material handling and body positioning.
NIOSH's Elements of Ergonomics Programs calls for first assessing the job (duration, force, frequency, rotation, handling) to identify risk factors, then selecting controls such as hoists.
In a work setting where temperatures can vary SIGNIFICANTLY and potentially reach extreme levels during a shift, what approach can help employees keep a safe core body temperature?

When temperatures swing to extremes, portable heating/cooling units actively control the microclimate to maintain core temperature; hydration, layers and breaks help but cannot offset extremes alone. Note: Ambiguous; other options are also valid heat/cold strategies.
How much force is needed to accelerate a 66 kg skier at 2 m/sec2? F=ma
F = m x a = 66 kg x 2 m/s^2 = 132 N.
What is the formula for calculating force?
Newton's second law: force = mass x acceleration (F = ma, N = kg.m/s^2); F = mg is weight, a special case, and mv is momentum.
What is the phenomenon in which light bends around the corners of an obstacle or aperture?
Diffraction is the bending of waves around obstacles or through apertures; refraction is bending as light passes between media, reflection is bouncing off surfaces.
What is the primary purpose of a gap analysis in a training needs assessment?
To count the number of employees requiring training
To determine the profitability of training programs
To identify discrepancies between current and desired performance levels
To evaluate the effectiveness of past training programs
Gap analysis compares actual performance (or KSAs) with the required standard; the difference defines what training must close.
What outcome is expected after successfully conducting a gap analysis?
Creation of a detailed training program that addresses specific gaps
Reduction in the workforce to improve efficiency
A gap analysis compares current and desired performance; its output is a plan, such as a targeted training program, to close the specific gaps identified.
When analyzing gaps in a Training Needs Assessment, what should be prioritized?
Gaps that are easiest to address
Gaps that are most critical to organizational goals
Gaps that require the least expensive training solutions
Gaps identified by the most senior employees
Training needs gaps should be prioritized by criticality to organizational goals and risk (safety-critical tasks first), not by ease, cost or seniority.

There were 49 OSHA recordables in 2020
The hours worked was 2,500,000
The incident rate is ?
Incident rate = (recordables x 200,000) / hours worked = (49 x 200,000) / 2,500,000 = 3.92, about 3.9.
Why does OSHA use 200,000 hours in some of its incident rate formulas?
It represents the total number of hours 100 employees would work in one year.
It's the average number of hours a single employee works in a year.
OSHA considers it a lucky number.
It's the average number of hours in a working month.
200,000 hours = 100 full-time employees x 40 hours/week x 50 weeks/year, normalizing rates per 100 workers.
What role does financial analysis play in safety management?
It is used to determine the entertainment budget for corporate events.
It helps justify the cost-effectiveness of safety interventions.
It is irrelevant to the practical aspects of safety management.
It is solely focused on reducing the workforce to save costs
Financial analysis (ROI, cost-benefit, payback) demonstrates that safety interventions are cost-effective, supporting budget approval.
What are the two types of risk transfer?
Risk transfer is either contractual (hold-harmless/indemnity agreements, shifting to contractors) or financial through insurance.
What is the primary goal of risk treatment in safety management?
To assess the likelihood of hazards occurring.
To implement measures to reduce, eliminate, or transfer risk.
To monitor and review the financial impact of hazards.
ISO 31000 risk treatment selects and implements options to avoid, reduce, share/transfer or retain risk; eliminating all hazards is rarely possible.
What role does insurance play in risk treatment?
It eliminates the hazard causing the risk.
It transfers the financial risk associated with a hazard to another party.
It reduces the likelihood of a hazard occurring.
It identifies new hazards in the workplace.
Insurance is financial risk transfer; it shifts the cost of losses to the insurer but does not eliminate the hazard or reduce its likelihood.

Fall protection for scaffolds starts at ____________________ feet.
Ref: 1926.451g
OSHA 1926.451(g)(1) requires fall protection on scaffolds more than 10 ft above a lower level.

Employees handling scaffolding materials at head level and bending and leaning between scaffolding members are at risk of impact-type head injuries. Slips and falls also increase this risk. Why are protective helmets required in this situation?
To enhance visibility on the worksite.
To protect against impact-type head injuries.
1926.100 and 1926.451(h) require hard hats where employees are exposed to impact or falling-object head injury, as when handling materials at head level on scaffolds.
To protect employees from falling objects on a construction site, what safety measures must be implemented when working on scaffolds more than 10 feet above lower levels?
Install bright lighting around the scaffold perimeter.
Erect barricades below the scaffold and restrict access to the hazard area, and install toeboards along the edge of platforms.
Ensure all workers wear high-visibility clothing.
Conduct daily safety briefings for all employees entering the site.
1926.451(h): protect against falling objects with toeboards, screens or debris nets, plus barricading the area below and prohibiting entry, along with hard hats.
"Hazardous atmosphere" is a Flammable gas, vapor, or mist in excess of _________ percent of its lower flammable limit (LFL);
OSHA 1910.146 defines a hazardous atmosphere as including flammable gas, vapor or mist above 10% of its LFL; 19.5% and 23.5% are oxygen limits.
Name a substances or hazards that must be tested for workers going into a live sewer manhole hole, 10 feet deep, to clear a blockage.

Sewers generate methane (and H2S) from decomposing organic matter; methane is flammable (LEL 5%) and displaces oxygen, so atmospheric testing for O2, flammables (LEL) and toxics is required before entry per OSHA 1910.146. Helium and argon are not sewer gases.
What minimum level of oxygen is required if personnel are entering confined space without breathing apparatus?
OSHA 1910.146 defines an oxygen-deficient atmosphere as below 19.5%; entry without supplied air requires 19.5%-23.5% O2. 23.5% is the upper (enriched) limit, not the minimum.
How often should you inspect your PPE to ensure it’s in good condition and functioning properly?

OSHA 1910.132 requires PPE to be maintained in reliable condition; manufacturers and OSHA guidance call for inspection before each use so defects are caught before exposure. Periodic weekly or monthly checks alone could miss damage.
Why is it critical for personal protective equipment (PPE) to be properly fitted to the individual worker? Select the most accurate option:
To enhance the aesthetic appeal and style of the worker
To adhere to organizational dress code policies
To maximize comfort and ease for the worker
To optimize the protective function and reduce the potential for injury or hazard exposure

OSHA 1910.132(d) requires PPE to be selected to fit each affected employee because poorly fitting PPE (e.g., respirators, gloves, harnesses) leaves gaps or is removed, defeating protection. Comfort aids wear but protection is the purpose.
When conducting a PPE hazard assessment, which of the following is NOT typically included?

A PPE hazard assessment (OSHA 1910.132(d)) identifies hazards through walkthrough observation, worker input and injury/illness data review. Workers' compensation premium calculation is a financial/insurance task, not part of hazard identification.
Under GHS labels, what are the signal words?
GHS (and OSHA HazCom 2012) uses only two signal words: Danger for more severe hazards and Warning for less severe. Caution is an ANSI Z535 signal word, not a GHS one.
What is the primary purpose of Threshold Limit Values (TLVs) on a Safety Data Sheet?
To define the legal limits for exposure in the workplace
To provide guidelines for safe exposure levels to chemical substances and physical agents
To determine the economic impact of chemical usage
To specify the required personal protective equipment for each chemical.

ACGIH TLVs are health-based guidelines for airborne levels to which nearly all workers may be repeatedly exposed without adverse effect. They are not legal limits; OSHA PELs are the enforceable values.
Which IARC group indicates that an agent is probably carcinogenic to humans?
IARC classes: Group 1 carcinogenic to humans, Group 2A probably carcinogenic, Group 2B possibly carcinogenic, Group 3 not classifiable. Group 4 was retired in 2019.
What is a crucial first step in implementing a training course in an organization?
Evaluating the performance of the organization

Instructional design (ADDIE, ANSI/ASSP Z490.1) starts with a needs assessment to identify performance gaps and set learning objectives; materials, delivery and evaluation tools are built afterward to meet those objectives.
Which factor is most important when creating a filing and reporting system that is easy to recover?
Color-coding all files according to department
Keeping all files in a single location

Recoverability depends on redundancy: a digital backup system (preferably off-site or cloud) protects records against fire, loss or corruption. Keeping everything in one location or paper only increases the risk of unrecoverable loss.
What is an effective strategy to ensure that a new training program is integrated successfully into existing organizational processes?
Require mandatory attendance for all employees
Align the training with organizational goals and culture
Offer incentives for completing the training

Training integrates and sustains when it supports organizational goals and fits the culture, giving management support and relevance to daily work. Mandatory attendance or incentives may raise participation but do not ensure integration or transfer.
Which control must be specified in a hot work permit?
The required amount of water to be present onsite
The contact details for the nearest two fire stations
The fire insurance policy number of the employer
The designation of a fire watch

OSHA 1910.252 and NFPA 51B require the hot work permit to address fire watch designation (during work and at least 30 minutes after) along with combustible removal and extinguisher availability. Insurance numbers and fire station contacts are not required.
Which safety measure is crucial to prevent siderosis in ironworkers?

Siderosis is a pneumoconiosis caused by inhaling iron oxide dust/fume, so the control is preventing inhalation via ventilation and respiratory protection. Hand washing, goggles and skin care do not address the inhalation route.
What is a primary health concern for construction workers involved in welding and cutting operations?

Welding and cutting steel generate iron oxide and other metal fumes, a primary respiratory health concern (siderosis, metal fume fever) addressed by OSHA 1926 Subpart J ventilation rules. Noise, shock and UV are real but the question targets the health fume hazard. Note: Noise, shock and UV are also genuine welding hazards; key relies on 'health concern' framing.
How should you respond to the Chief Financial Officer's request to justify the expenditure on safety training for all employees in your company?
Develop a cost and benefit analysis.
Create an injury trend analysis covering the past five years.
Compare number of reported injuries before and after the training.
Calculate the return on investment rate.

A cost-benefit analysis compares training costs with expected benefits (reduced injury costs, lost time, insurance) in financial terms a CFO uses to justify expenditure. Trend data or before/after counts show effect but not monetary justification; ROI is one output of the analysis. Note: ROI (D) is also a defensible financial justification.
Your company may be required to communicate safety or risk-related information to the public. It's crucial to manage these communications effectively to ensure the message is:
Clear, concise, and includes only essential information.
In compliance with all regulatory requirements concerning content, timing, and responsibility.
Distributed via all major communication channels.
Assigning blame, explaining the reasons for the incident/injury, or admitting guilt.

Effective risk communication to the public is clear, concise and limited to essential information so the audience understands and acts. Assigning blame or admitting guilt is inappropriate; regulatory compliance matters but does not make the message effective. Note: Option B (regulatory compliance) is also defensible.
How does workers' compensation insurance benefit employers?
It provides full legal immunity from all workplace incidents
It limits financial liabilities related to workplace injuries
It covers all types of damages an employee might claim

Workers' compensation is no-fault insurance and the exclusive remedy for most workplace injuries, which limits employer liability and transfers financial risk to the insurer. It does not give full immunity (e.g., third-party or intentional-act exceptions) or cover all damages.
Pure water at 25 C is neutral with pH 7 because [H+] = [OH-] = 1 x 10^-7 mol/L. Values below 7 are acidic and above 7 are basic.
A container holds 0.55 mol of gas at 105.7 kPa and 300 K. What volume does the gas occupy? (PV = nRT; R = 8.31 L kPa/mol K)
What is the primary purpose of a Material Safety Data Sheet (MSDS)?
To provide financial information about hazardous materials
To guide the safe handling and use of chemicals
To list the manufacturer's contact information only
To serve as a legal document for environmental violations

The MSDS (now SDS under OSHA HazCom 2012, 1910.1200) communicates chemical hazards and safe handling, storage, PPE, first aid and emergency measures. Manufacturer contact is only one section, and it is not a financial or enforcement document.
Hand tools hurt workers when they are:

OSHA notes the greatest hand tool hazards come from misuse and improper maintenance (e.g., mushroomed chisel heads, cracked handles). Age alone is not the hazard; tools must be inspected before use, not merely monthly.
Which of the following should you always do when changing a drill bit or saw blade?
Leave the tool plugged in but switch it off.
Ask a friend to hold the tool while you change the bit.
Unplug the tool or ensure it's disconnected from its power source.
Use a wet cloth to hold the drill bit or blade.

Power tools must be disconnected from their energy source before changing bits, blades or accessories (OSHA 1926.300/1910.242) to prevent accidental start-up. A switched-off but plugged-in tool can still be energized.
What Is The Traditional Risk Management Approach For Industrial Hygiene?
Anticipation, Recognition, Evaluation, Control, and Confirm
Planning, Hazard Identification, Risk Assessment, Risk Control, Monitor and Review
Policy, Organize, Plan and Implement, Measure Performance, Review Performance

The classic industrial hygiene paradigm is Anticipation, Recognition, Evaluation and Control (with confirmation/follow-up). PDCA is a management system model and the other options describe ISO-style risk management and HSG65 frameworks.
OSHA uses a ___________ of 50 ppm for carbon monoxide
The OSHA PEL for carbon monoxide is 50 ppm as an 8-hour TWA (1910.1000 Table Z-1). NIOSH's REL is 35 ppm and ACGIH's TLV is 25 ppm; PELs are the OSHA enforceable limits.
According to OSHA's asbestos standard (1910.1001(k)(7)), which statement about sanding asbestos-containing flooring is correct?
Sanding is allowed if local exhaust ventilation captures fibers above the PEL
Sanding is allowed if the surface is first wetted or enclosed
Sanding is allowed if it is done in a wet state
Sanding of asbestos-containing flooring material is prohibited
OSHA prohibits sanding asbestos-containing flooring outright; floor care must use wet methods and low-abrasion pads at low speeds.

What is the name of a program that provides employees with access to professional services and trained providers to address personal, physical, or stress-related issues that may impact their overall well-being?
KEY CORRECTED by trainer review: An Employee Assistance Program (EAP) provides confidential professional help for personal, physical and stress-related issues.
To ensure a safe and healthy workplace, organizations must understand the basics of indoor air quality (IAQ). Which item(s) would MOST likely compromise IAQ?

EPA and NIOSH identify inadequate ventilation (insufficient outdoor air) as the most common cause of IAQ problems, since it allows contaminants from all sources to accumulate. Cleaning products and humidity are contributors but less common root causes.

A manufacturing plant is assessing risks associated with a new machinery installation. The risk assessment team identifies potential hazards, including:
- Electrical shock
- Crushing injuries
- Fire
A risk matrix categorizes the electrical shock hazard as "High Severity" and "Medium Likelihood." What does this indicate?
The risk is acceptable without controls

On a typical risk matrix, high severity combined with medium likelihood falls in the high-risk zone, which is unacceptable without controls and requires prompt mitigation using the hierarchy of controls. Periodic review fits low or tolerable risks.
What is the MOST effective way to evaluate job performance change following a safety training course?
Compare incident rates before and after training
Observe workers performing their tasks and provide feedback
Administer a written test immediately after training
Direct observation measures actual behavior change. Incident rates are lagging and influenced by many factors; a written test measures learning, not performance.
According to the Kirkpatrick Model, which level evaluates the extent to which learners apply new skills and knowledge on the job?
Kirkpatrick levels: 1 Reaction (satisfaction), 2 Learning (knowledge gained), 3 Behavior (application on the job), 4 Results (organizational outcomes). On-the-job application is Level 3.
What is a key indicator of successful job performance improvement following safety training?
Decrease in workplace incidents and injuries

Safety training aims to change behavior and reduce harm, so a decrease in incidents and injuries indicates improved job performance (Kirkpatrick Level 4 results). Satisfaction, cost and reputation do not measure performance improvement.
Which guidance sets overall safety standards for ships, including those carrying dangerous goods. It mandates requirements for vessel stability, fire protection, and navigation systems.
International Convention for the Safety of Life at Sea (SOLAS)
Merchant Marine Safety for Ships Afloat (MMSSF)
Naval Vessel Flag of Registration requirements (NVFR)

SOLAS, an IMO convention, sets minimum safety standards for ship construction, stability, fire protection, life-saving appliances and navigation; Chapter VII covers carriage of dangerous goods (IMDG Code). The other options are not recognized international instruments.
What is the PRIMARY purpose of ROTE in maritime navigation?
To establish speed limits for vessels.
To regulate the discharge of pollutants.
To ensure the proper loading of cargo.

The Rules of the Road (COLREGs internationally, Inland Rules in the US) govern vessel conduct, lights, sound signals and right-of-way specifically to prevent collisions. Pollution is MARPOL and cargo loading is covered elsewhere. Note: 'ROTE' appears to be a typo for Rules of the Road.
What is the primary purpose of the International Maritime Dangerous Goods (IMDG) Code?
To establish rules for preventing collisions at sea
To regulate the discharge of pollutants from ships
To set standards for ship construction and design
To provide requirements for safely transporting dangerous goods by sea
The IMDG Code (IMO) governs sea transport of dangerous goods; IATA DGR covers air, and 49 CFR covers US ground transport.
_________________ refers to the number of subordinates under a manager’s direct control.
Span of control is the number of subordinates reporting directly to a manager. In ICS the recommended span is 3-7, ideally 5, for effective supervision.
When developing an Emergency Management plan, what is the principle which the strategies and tactics must be met?
Protection of life, property, and the environment

Emergency plan strategies and tactics follow the incident priorities: life safety first, then incident stabilization/property protection, then environmental protection (NFPA 1600/ICS). Command, communication and continuity support these priorities.
Which factor determines the span of control for an Incident Commander (IC)?
The level of experience of the IC
The number of responders available at the scene
The geographical location of the incident

Span of control (3-7, ideally 5, per NIMS/ICS) is set by how many resources/responders the IC must directly supervise; as responders increase, the IC delegates to sections, branches and divisions. Severity influences complexity but the number supervised drives span. Note: Many ICS sources say span depends on incident type/complexity; key is defensible.

A paint storage room requires six air changes per hour to maintain safe air quality by diluting and removing potentially toxic fumes. If the paint storage room has a volume of 240 cubic meters, how much air must be circulated through the room each hour to meet this requirement?
Required airflow Q = ACH x V = 6 /hr x 240 m3 = 1,440 m3/hr.

A dike is being constructed to protect a riverside area. It has a rectangular cross-section with a width of 5 meters and a height of 3 meters. If the dike is to extend for 200 meters, what is the volume of material needed to construct the dike?
Volume of a rectangular prism = width x height x length = 5 m x 3 m x 200 m = 3,000 m3.
The volume of a cylinder with a radius of 2 feet and height of 4 is _____ Cuft.
V = pi r^2 h = 3.1416 x (2 ft)^2 x 4 ft = 3.1416 x 16 = 50.27 ft3, approximately 50.2.

During a safety training session, an employee confides in you about a personal medical condition that may impact their ability to perform certain tasks. The employee asks you to keep this information confidential.
What do you do?
Share the information with the employee's supervisor to ensure their safety.
Keep the information confidential, but inform the employee of their responsibility to disclose the condition.
Document the information and store it in the employee's personnel file.
Ignore the employee's request and share the information with HR.

Medical information is confidential (ADA requires it be kept separate from personnel files), so honor the confidence while advising the employee to disclose job-relevant limitations through proper channels (medical/HR) so accommodations can be made. Sharing without consent breaches ethics.

You're conducting a safety training session on fall protection. A participant mentions that they often skip using their harness when working at heights because it's "too uncomfortable." How do you respond?
Ignore the comment and continue with the training.
Tell the participant that their behavior is unacceptable and could lead to disciplinary action.
Explain the potential consequences of not wearing a harness and emphasize the importance of following safety procedures.
Suggest that the participant find a more comfortable harness.

Coach first: explain the consequences of falls and the purpose of the harness, reinforcing required procedures (OSHA 1926.502). This addresses the behavior constructively; discipline alone or ignoring it fails, and fit/comfort can be addressed as a follow-up. Note: D (better-fitting harness) also addresses root cause; key reflects training-context response.

You are a safety trainer preparing a report on recent incident statistics to present in a training session. You notice that reporting a slightly lower incident rate would make the safety record look significantly better.
Question: What is the most ethical approach to take in this situation?
Adjust the numbers slightly to show improvement and encourage the team.
Report the actual statistics, ensuring that the data reflects the true safety performance.
Exclude some incidents that were minor to improve the overall statistics.
Discuss the idea of altering the data with a supervisor before making a decision.

The BCSP Code of Ethics requires honesty and objectivity; data must be reported accurately. Adjusting, excluding or even contemplating altering data misrepresents performance and undermines trust and decision-making.
What is one of the most effective ways to reduce accidents in a fleet operation?

Most fleet crashes stem from driver behavior, so driver selection, training and education are among the most effective controls (ANSI/ASSP Z15.1). Adding vehicles or cutting maintenance increases risk, and road infrastructure is outside the employer's control.
Which technology has been shown to significantly improve transportation safety by monitoring driver behavior?

Telematics systems combine GPS, accelerometer and engine data to monitor speeding, harsh braking, acceleration and cornering, enabling feedback and coaching that reduce crashes. GPS alone only tracks location; dash cams are one component.
Why is it important to verify the absence of energy after performing a lockout?
To confirm that the lockout device is attached.
To ensure that the equipment is still operational.
To make certain there is no residual energy that could pose a danger when performing maintenance.
To check the machine's jog function

OSHA 1910.147(d)(6) requires verification of isolation (try-out/test) after locks are applied because stored or residual energy (capacitors, springs, pressure, gravity) or a wrong isolation point can still injure workers. Attaching the lock alone does not prove zero energy.
Name two atmospheric tests that must be conducted if entering a broken sewer main in a trench

Sewage decomposition produces hydrogen sulfide (toxic, PEL ceiling 20 ppm) and methane (flammable, oxygen-displacing), so these plus O2 and LEL must be tested before entering a broken sewer main (OSHA 1926.651(g) hazardous atmospheres).
Before starting excavation work, what is the most important step to ensure safety?
Setting up barriers around the excavation site
Securing the necessary tools and equipment
Informing local authorities about the excavation work

Before excavating, a hazard/risk assessment (including utility locates per OSHA 1926.651(b), soil classification and protective system selection by a competent person) drives all other controls. Barriers and equipment follow from that assessment.
Type A soil is sloped at ____________:1
OSHA 1926 Subpart P, Appendix B: maximum allowable slope for Type A soil is 3/4H:1V (53 degrees); Type B is 1:1 (45 degrees) and Type C is 1.5:1 (34 degrees).
What the three parts of effective communication
KEY CORRECTED by trainer review: Effective communication has three parts: sender, message and receiver.
When used alone, lectures can be ineffective because they do not permit active participation between students and the instruction. What does "active participation" typically involve?

Active participation means learners interact and apply content, such as group discussion, questioning, case studies and practice, which improves retention for adult learners. Note-taking, memorizing and passive listening are one-way activities.

The common 6x6 rule (no more than about six lines with six words each) keeps slides readable and focused so the presenter, not the text, carries the message. All-caps text and dense 150-word slides reduce readability.
Which technique is most effective for maintaining learner engagement during a training session?

Attention declines after roughly 15-20 minutes, so frequent short breaks (and interaction) help sustain engagement and retention. Uninterrupted lecture or one-way communication causes fatigue and disengagement.
When introducing a new concept, what is a recommended facilitation technique?
Using technical jargon to sound knowledgeable
Starting with an advanced topic before basics
Connecting the concept to real-world applications
Avoiding questions until the end of the session

Adult learners (Knowles' andragogy) are problem-centered and need relevance, so linking a new concept to real-world job applications aids understanding and transfer. Jargon, starting with advanced material and deferring questions hinder learning.
What role should multimedia play in a training session?
It should be used sparingly to avoid distractions
It should replace all traditional teaching methods
It should be the primary source of information
It should complement the training by reinforcing learning objectives

Multimedia should support, not replace, instruction by reinforcing learning objectives and engaging multiple learning modalities. Used as the primary source or as a replacement it can overload or distract learners.
As a company safety manager, what would be your initial step to address the recent increase in hand and arm lacerations at a manufacturing plant?
Retrain all workers in hand and arm safety.
Buy more personal protective equipment and enforce its use.
Carry out a training needs assessment.

An increasing injury trend should first be investigated through root cause analysis to determine why lacerations are occurring (guarding, tools, procedures, PPE). Retraining or buying PPE before knowing the cause may not fix the real problem.
Safety training and education are typically classified into two categories: formal and informal. In the case of informal training:
It includes on-the-job training and online training
It may necessitate 75% more time compared to formal training covering the same material.
It is not limited to the work environment alone.
It constitutes approximately 90% of adult learning

Research on workplace learning (e.g., the 70-20-10 model and informal learning studies) estimates that the large majority of adult learning, often cited as up to about 90%, occurs informally through experience and interaction. Note: Percentage varies by source (70-90%).
According to William C. Pope, which three factors contribute to the cause of an incident?

William Pope's management-oriented model attributes incidents to three factors: error (human), defect (equipment/material) and oversight (management/system failures). The other combinations are not Pope's classification.
Which of these can be explosive AS A DUST?

Finely divided aluminum is a highly reactive metal dust with a low minimum ignition energy and high Kst, making it a severe combustible dust explosion hazard (NFPA 484). Lead and copper dusts are not significant explosion hazards. Note: Silicon dust is also combustible; aluminum is the classic best answer.
What is the primary reason for conducting a combustible dust hazard analysis (DHA) in industrial settings?
To identify and assess the risks associated with combustible dust.
To comply with local building code.

NFPA 660 (formerly 652) requires a Dust Hazard Analysis to identify fire, flash fire and explosion hazards of combustible dust in processes and to evaluate safeguards. Insurance or building code compliance is secondary.
Which method is most effective for preventing the risk of dust explosions in a facility handling combustible powders?
Regular housekeeping to remove dust accumulations.
Installation of explosion venting in the ventilation system.
Use of water sprinklers in areas where dust is present.
Increasing the humidity levels to above 95% at all times.

Housekeeping removes the fuel, preventing dust layers that can be lofted into a secondary explosion; OSHA's Combustible Dust NEP and NFPA 660 emphasize controlling accumulation (e.g., 1/32 inch layer threshold). Venting mitigates consequences but does not prevent explosions.
Which of the following explains how a fixed guard protects workers?
Stops the machine when a worker enters the danger area
Restrains the worker from entering the danger area
Creates distance to keep the worker from entering the danger area
Provides a barrier to prevent access to the danger area

A fixed guard is a permanent physical barrier that prevents any part of the body from reaching the point of operation or danger zone (OSHA 1910.212). Stopping the machine describes an interlock or presence-sensing device; restraint describes pullback/restraint devices.
The three major types of machine guards are:

OSHA's machine guarding guidance classifies guards as fixed, interlocked, adjustable and self-adjusting; among the listed choices fixed, interlocked and automatic (self-adjusting) best represent the principal guard types. Note: OSHA lists four guard types (fixed, interlocked, adjustable, self-adjusting).
What is the most important thing to do before performing maintenance on a conveyor system?

OSHA 1910.147 requires conveyors to be de-energized and locked out (including gravity and stored energy) before servicing to prevent unexpected start-up. Notifying the supervisor, PPE and manuals are secondary to energy isolation.
At a fitness equipment plant, four back injuries this year involved lifting a 110-lb box from a 36-in-high conveyor to a 4-in-high pallet 36 in away. What is the BEST solution?
Rotate the task so each worker lifts the product only two hours a day
Lower the conveyor to 28 inches and ensure two workers lift the boxes
Provide the worker with safe lifting training and implement a stretching program
Provide a vacuum lift-assist device to lift the box to the pallet
Four injuries and a 110-lb box need an engineering control. A vacuum lift assist removes the manual lift. Rotation and training are administrative controls that leave the hazard in place.
Per Clay Carr, what is an adult learning needs?
Trainers must be an expert in the topic

Adult learning principles (Clay Carr, Knowles) emphasize that adults learn best when training is relevant to their jobs and immediate problems. Adults do want feedback, and short length or trainer expertise alone do not drive learning.
Which are the key elements of an effective safety and health performance management system?
Policy, organizing, planning and implementation, and measuring performance, and discipline
Measuring performance, reviewing performance, and auditing near-misses, training, and enforcement
Education, Planning and organization, policy, reviewing performance and enforcement
Policy, organizing, planning and implementation, measuring performance and reviewing performance

The UK HSE HSG65 model (and similar systems) lists policy; organizing; planning and implementing; measuring performance; and reviewing performance (with audit), forming a continuous improvement loop. Discipline and enforcement are not core system elements.
The area of a lot that is 100 ft long and 60 ft wide is ________ square feet.
Area of a rectangle = length x width = 100 ft x 60 ft = 6,000 ft2.
A circle has a diameter of 10 feet. What is its radius?
A safety zone is marked in the shape of a circle. If the diameter of the circle is 10 meters, what is the approximate area of the safety zone?
A = pi r^2 with r = 10/2 = 5 m: 3.1416 x 25 = 78.5 m2. 314 is the area if diameter were mistakenly used as radius.
What is the title of a person who has the knowledge to design and supervise the installation of fall protection systems on a job site?

OSHA 1926.32(m) defines a qualified person as one who, by degree, certificate or extensive knowledge and experience, can solve problems relating to the work; 1926.502 requires qualified persons to design systems such as lifelines. A competent person identifies hazards and can stop work.
Personal fall arrest systems, when stopping a fall, shall limit maximum arresting force on an employee to __________________ pounds when used with a body harness; 1926.502(d)
OSHA 1926.502(d)(16)(ii) limits maximum arresting force to 1,800 lb with a body harness (900 lb formerly with body belts); deceleration distance is limited to 3.5 ft and free fall to 6 ft.
Which of the following is a potential consequence of orthostatic intolerance during a fall arrest?

Orthostatic intolerance, blood pooling in the legs while suspended motionless in a harness, causes suspension trauma that can lead to fainting and death within minutes, so prompt rescue (OSHA 1926.502(d)(20)) and trauma straps are needed.
Which of the following is a key component of effective instructional leadership?
Focusing solely on standardized test scores.
Limiting teacher autonomy to ensure compliance.
Prioritizing administrative tasks over classroom activities.

Effective instructional leadership develops the capability of instructors through professional development, coaching and support. Focusing only on scores, restricting autonomy or prioritizing administration undermines instructional quality.
Effective communication in educational leadership should primarily aim to:
Convey decisions and policies from top management only.
Discourage teachers from expressing concerns or suggestions.
Encourage a one-way flow of information.
Foster an environment of open dialogue and feedback.
Effective leadership communication is two-way, fostering open dialogue and feedback so concerns surface and engagement increases. One-way, top-down communication suppresses input and trust.
Which of the following best describes the use of interpersonal skills in educational leadership?
Avoiding personal interactions to maintain professional distance.
Building relationships to understand and motivate staff and students.
Ignoring conflicts to maintain peace in the organization.
Using a formal approach in all communications to assert authority.

Interpersonal skills are used to build relationships, understand people's needs and motivate staff, which supports engagement and conflict resolution. Avoiding interaction, ignoring conflict or relying on formal authority weakens leadership.
Sheet metal in stamping are used in a facility. During handling of these materials, a risk of lacerations may exist. Which control is MOST effective in minimizing this risk to workers?
Conduct a job brief to discuss proper handling of sheet metal.
Dull the edges of the sheet metal to make it safer to handle.
Mark the edge with orange tape so workers know where to put hands.
Require the use of properly rated, cut resistant gloves.
KEY CORRECTED by trainer review: Hierarchy of controls: removing/dulling the sharp edge is an engineering control and is more effective than gloves (PPE).
What should you do before using a forklift?
Ensure the forklift is suitable for indoor use only.
Perform a pre-use inspection to check for any potential issues.
Modify the forklift for higher performance.
Use the forklift to push loads instead of lifting them.

OSHA 1910.178(q)(7) requires powered industrial trucks to be examined before being placed in service, at least daily or each shift, and removed from service if defective. Modifications require manufacturer approval (1910.178(a)(4)).
What is the primary purpose of implementing ergonomic principles in material handling?
To reduce the environmental impact of manufacturing processes.
To increase the speed of operations and material flow.
To minimize the risk of injuries through proper design and use of equipment.
To comply with international shipping regulations.

Ergonomics in material handling aims to fit the task to the worker, reducing musculoskeletal disorder risk through proper design (lift assists, workstation height, load size). Productivity gains may follow, but injury reduction is the primary purpose.
Your company has a bar bender that needs guarding. The quote is $5,600. The plant manager says that is too expensive. What should you do?
Report the issue to the insurance company.
Report the issue to OSHA anonymously.
Provide the firm with an ultimatum that you will leave if the issue is not resolved.
Show other injuries with the bar bender at other companies and the approximate average cost of $137,000 per injury.

Management responds to business cases: comparing the $5,600 guard cost to an average $137,000 injury cost (direct plus indirect) shows a strong benefit-to-cost ratio. Ultimatums or going outside the company are not the first professional step.
Which is considered a key principle of the BCSP Code of Ethics?

The BCSP Code of Ethics directs certificants to be honest, fair and impartial and to act with responsibility and integrity. Impartiality is a stated principle; the other options are general traits not specifically named as code principles. Note: Objectivity also appears in BCSP code wording on public statements.
What does the "whole man theory" relate to in the context of workers' compensation?
The assessment of an employee's overall health
The determination of compensation based on the impact of an injury on a worker’s overall capabilities
The legal responsibility of employers to maintain workplace safety

The whole man (whole person) theory rates permanent impairment by the injury's effect on the worker's overall body function and capabilities, often as a percentage of the whole person (AMA Guides), rather than only on lost wages or a specific body part.
Which term refers to the process of identifying problems and their solutions by organizing information into either established or newly invented concepts?

Conceptual thinking is the competency of understanding situations by identifying patterns and connections and organizing information into existing or new concepts to solve problems. Analytical thinking breaks problems into parts step by step.
What is the appropriate response when you suspect an employee's complaint is intended to cause trouble for another employee?
Consider the information bona fide until you have the results of the company investigation.
Assume the information of the complaint is not correct.
Discipline the employee who has filed the complaint.
Do not accept the complaint and share the information with other employers.

All complaints should be treated as valid (bona fide) and investigated objectively until facts prove otherwise; presuming bad faith, disciplining the complainant or disclosing information risks retaliation claims and missed hazards.
The Community Right to know is under EPA ______________

SARA Title III (1986), the Emergency Planning and Community Right-to-Know Act (EPCRA), established LEPCs, Tier II inventory reporting and Toxics Release Inventory reporting. CERCLA covers Superfund cleanup, RCRA waste and TSCA chemical manufacture.
The most common source of wildfires is caused by which type of lightning.
Dry lightning, cloud-to-ground strikes from storms producing little or no rain reaching the ground, ignites dry fuels without wetting them and is the leading natural cause of wildfires.
What is the primary purpose of the REACH regulation?
To reduce the administrative burden on chemical manufacturers
To ensure a high level of protection of human health and the environment from the risks posed by chemicals
To increase the import of chemicals into the EU
To deregulate chemical production within the European Union

EU REACH (EC 1907/2006) aims to ensure a high level of protection of human health and the environment from chemical risks by requiring registration, evaluation, authorization and restriction of chemicals, placing the burden of proof on industry.
Which health control for manganese overexposure would be the MOST desirable for a welder arc welding metal ??
Wear a N95 filtering face piece

The hierarchy of controls ranks substitution (low-manganese electrodes/process) above engineering controls, administrative controls (job rotation) and PPE. General dilution ventilation is not adequate for welding fume; local exhaust would be the engineering choice.
Which is BEST control for workers climbing a 30 foot fixed ladders to the roof to physically inspection skylights condition.
Use trained climbers to access the ladder.
Provide ladder fall arrest system when climbing the ladder.
Provide stairs instead of ladders to access the roof
Reduce the task to once a year.

Replacing a fixed ladder with stairs is a higher-order design control that largely eliminates the fall-from-ladder hazard, versus ladder safety systems (OSHA 1910.28(b)(9) for ladders over 24 ft) which only arrest falls. Training and frequency reduction are administrative.
Several loud machines expose nearby workers to noise above the PEL. Which control would be MOST effective in reducing the risk of noise-induced hearing loss?
Replace the noisy machines with quieter models
Provide earplugs or earmuffs to all workers
Rearrange the workspace to increase distance from the machines
Replacing the source with quieter equipment removes the noise at its origin, the highest control available here. Monitoring is not a control.
Accident/Incident investigations determine how and why ___________ occur.

Investigations determine how and why failures (in systems, equipment, procedures, management controls) occur so that root causes can be corrected. Focusing on errors or mistakes tends toward individual blame rather than system causes.
The incident investigation should be conducted:
At the start of the next day with all the witnesses.
As soon as possible individually with each witness separate
Within one hour. Get the witnesses together and see if the group can put together a timeline of events.
Give each witness an incident form to fill out and return to the safety department the next day.

Interview witnesses as soon as possible, while memory is fresh, and separately so accounts are not influenced by others (group contamination). Delaying or relying only on written forms reduces accuracy.
Which of the following is NOT a typical step in an incident investigation process?
Securing the scene and providing first aid.
Gathering information through interviews and observations.
Disciplining employees involved in the incident.
Analyzing the data and identifying root causes.

Investigations aim at fact-finding and root cause, not blame: secure scene, gather evidence, analyze causes, recommend corrective actions. Discipline is a separate HR process; linking it to investigations discourages reporting.
What is active listening and why is it important in effective communication?
Listening to music while talking to someone to improve mood
Paying full attention to the speaker, understanding their message, responding thoughtfully, and remembering what was said
Repeating exactly what someone has said to confirm the message
Avoiding eye contact to better concentrate on the verbal message

Active listening means giving full attention, understanding the message, responding thoughtfully (paraphrasing, questions) and remembering it, which builds trust and reduces miscommunication. Exact repetition alone is parroting, not active listening.
Which of the following is NOT typically considered an interpersonal skill?
Interpersonal (soft) skills involve interacting with people, such as empathy, negotiation and conflict resolution. Software programming proficiency is a technical (hard) skill.
What does the term 'synchronous learning' refer to in the context of training and development?
Learning that happens in real-time, where all participants engage in the learning activity simultaneously.
Self-paced learning modules that participants complete on their own schedules.
Training that is conducted asynchronously in different time zones.
The documentation and tracking of a learner's progress over time
Synchronous learning occurs in real time with instructor and participants engaged simultaneously (live classroom, webinar). Self-paced modules completed on one's own schedule are asynchronous.
Hazard Identification and assessment is an ongoing process to assess ________________.

Hazard identification and assessment (OSHA Recommended Practices) is an ongoing process to find and evaluate workplace hazards as conditions, equipment and processes change. Workers' comp losses and behavior are inputs, not the object.
An effective risk management program includes risk identification, risk analysis, and risk response. One example of risk identification is:
Building a retainer wall to prevent flooding.
Estimating the likelihood and financial impact of a fire.
Doing research on local weather patterns and geological formations.

Risk identification determines what hazards could affect the organization, such as researching local weather and geology to find flood or seismic exposures. Estimating likelihood and impact is risk analysis; building a wall is risk response.
What are the main principles of successful auditing according to ISO 19001.
Intelligence, Articulation of Issues, and Documentation.
Integrity, Independence and Due Professional Care.
Length, Knowledge, and Identification of Hazards.

ISO 19011 (the question's 19001 is a typo) lists audit principles: integrity, fair presentation, due professional care, confidentiality, independence and evidence-based approach (plus risk-based approach). Note: Standard is ISO 19011, not 19001.

The metal ring weighs 1000 lbs.
The three sling angles are at 45 degrees from horizontal.
What is the tension in each sling leg?
_______________ pounds.
Per-leg tension = (W / n) / sin(angle from horizontal) = (1000 / 3) / sin 45 = 333.3 / 0.7071 = 471 lb.

Which grade of chain is the only acceptable type for use in chain slings?
Ref: 1926.251(b)
OSHA 1926.251(b)(1) and ASME B30.9 require alloy steel chain (Grade 80 or higher) for overhead lifting slings. Proof coil, high test and transport chain are not rated for overhead lifting.
What is the primary purpose of a rigging plan in construction?
To determine the cost of materials and labor for a project.
To ensure that the right type of crane is available on-site.
To outline procedures and safety measures for lifting and moving loads.
To provide training for new construction workers.

A rigging/lift plan defines load weight, center of gravity, equipment and rigging selection, sling angles, crane configuration, communications and exclusion zones so lifts are performed safely (OSHA 1926 Subpart CC, ASME B30). Cost and training are not its purpose.
One ______________ is defined as the energy consumption rate of one joule per second (power)
One watt is the SI unit of power equal to one joule per second (P = E/t, also P = V x I). The ampere measures current, the ohm resistance and the volt potential difference.
Voltage is directly proportional to the square of resistance.
Current is inversely proportional to resistance.
Voltage is directly proportional to current.
Resistance is directly proportional to current.

Ohm's law V = I x R: at constant resistance, voltage is directly proportional to current. Current is also inversely proportional to resistance at constant voltage, but C is the direct statement of the law. Note: B is also true at constant voltage.
A ground loop impedance tester is used to test _________________
The Resistance in the grounding wire.

A ground (earth) loop impedance tester measures the impedance/resistance of the fault return path, including the grounding conductor, to confirm enough fault current will flow to trip the overcurrent device. It does not measure amps, watts or voltage directly. Note: Tester measures whole fault-loop impedance, not only the ground wire.

After discussing it with your workers, you learned that most of the trips and falls were caused by floors cluttered with tools and equipment that workers used to assemble automotive parts, including air hoses used for pneumatic tools. What is a good leading indicator?
Hold slip trip and fall training every month and measure the amount of slip and trip incidences.
Ask employees to report unsafe conditions to you. Measure the number of suggestions.
Measure and keep track of slips and falls.
Create an indicator that measures the frequency of inspecting and clearing the floors, and your goal is once daily.

A leading indicator measures a proactive activity that prevents the hazard, here the frequency of floor inspections and clearing against a daily goal. Counting slips and falls is a lagging indicator, and suggestion counts do not target the identified cause.
When calculating incident or injury rates, which factors are commonly considered, given the variations due to company policies and regulatory demands?
Total hours employees have worked and the overall count of incidents or injuries.
Count of fatal incidents, average employee count, and the sum of all settlement expenses.
Total training hours received by employees, their salaries, and their tenure in the company.
Duration of absence post-incident, accumulated medical expenses, and specific body regions impacted.
Incident rates normalize the number of cases by exposure hours: rate = (number of cases x 200,000) / total hours worked (OSHA 1904). Costs, salaries, tenure and body parts are not inputs to the rate.
How can leading indicators improve workplace safety?
By providing data on past accidents to avoid future legal issues
By encouraging reactive measures after an incident occurs
By guiding proactive safety measures and interventions
By focusing solely on the financial aspects of safety incidents

Leading indicators (inspections, training, hazard reports, corrective action closure) measure proactive activities, allowing intervention before injuries occur. Data on past accidents are lagging indicators and drive reactive measures.

At what minimum voltage level must an employer guarantee that personnel trained in first aid and CPR are present onsite at all times when employees are working on or near exposed electrical equipment and wiring?
OSHA 1910.269(b)(1) and 1926.950/951 require persons trained in first aid and CPR to be available when employees work on or near exposed lines or equipment energized at 50 volts or more.

What are the 5 C’s of safety? Commitment, Culture and?
 Ref: Sheehan’s Building a Strong Safety Culture, The 5 C’s of Workplace Safety.

In the cited Sheehan model, the 5 C's of workplace safety are Commitment, Culture, Champions, Cost and Compliance, combining leadership commitment, safety champions, the cost case and regulatory compliance to build culture. Note: Source-specific model; not a widely standardized list.
What is the primary goal of an Emergency Action Plan (EAP) in the workplace?
To facilitate and organize employer and employee actions during workplace emergencies.
To provide a financial plan for emergency situations.
To comply solely with local government regulations.
To ensure that the business continues without interruption

OSHA 1910.38 states the EAP's purpose is to facilitate and organize employer and employee actions during workplace emergencies, including evacuation, reporting, alarm and accounting procedures. Business continuity and financial planning are separate.
Observation that workers are mainly motivated by personal gain
The theory that greatest efficiency is achieved by management based on scientific analysis of a process
The tendency of employees to work harder when they are participants in an experiment
Inherently unsafe working conditions caused by bureaucratic management

The Hawthorne effect, from the 1920s-30s Western Electric studies (Mayo), is the tendency of people to improve performance because they know they are being observed or studied. Option B describes Taylor's scientific management.
_________________ seeks to reduce the possibility that a loss will occur and reduce the severity of those that do occur.

Loss control combines loss prevention (reducing frequency/probability of loss) and loss reduction (reducing severity of losses that occur). It is a core risk treatment technique alongside avoidance, retention and transfer.
What is the primary goal of benchmarking?
To improve performance by learning from others

Benchmarking compares an organization's processes and performance with recognized leaders or best practices to identify gaps and adopt improvements. It is not primarily about competitor weaknesses, costs or compliance.
When evaluating clarity in communication, which of the following is the MOST important aspect to consider?
The speaker's tone of voice and rate of speech.
The message is easily understood by the intended audience.
The use of complex vocabulary and technical jargon.
The length of the communication (shorter is always better).

Clarity is judged by whether the intended audience easily understands the message; tone, pace and length matter only insofar as they support understanding. Jargon and complex vocabulary reduce clarity.
Which of these scenarios BEST demonstrates effective active listening skills?
Nodding occasionally while thinking about what you will say next.
Interrupting the speaker to share your own similar experiences.
Summarizing the speaker's points to ensure understanding.
Maintaining constant eye contact without any breaks.

Summarizing or paraphrasing the speaker's points confirms understanding and shows engagement, a core active listening technique. Planning your reply, interrupting or staring intensely are barriers to listening.
Empathy in interpersonal communication is BEST described as:
Agreeing with everything the other person says.
Sharing your own personal experiences to build rapport.
The ability to understand and share the feelings of another.
Offering unsolicited advice to help solve the other person's problems.
Empathy is the ability to understand and share another person's feelings and perspective. It does not require agreement, self-disclosure or offering unsolicited advice.

A chain applies a steady force of 1000 N to a cart, causing the cart to move in a straight line and accelerate at a rate of 25 m/s^2.
Given the formula: Force = Mass x Acceleration,
What is the cart's mass?
m = F / a = 1000 N / 25 m/s2 = 40 kg (about 88 lb, using 2.2046 lb/kg). The other options misapply the formula or units. Note: Option B's lb conversion (80.82) is wrong; 40 kg = 88.2 lb.
A sum of money has a present value of $1,000. If it is invested for 5 years at an interest rate of 3% compounded annually, what will its future value be? Formula is FV=PV×(1+r)n
When constructing a confidence interval for a population mean, which factor does not affect the width of the confidence interval?
The standard deviation of the sample
CI width = 2 x z (or t) x s / sqrt(n), so it depends on confidence level, standard deviation and sample size. The sample mean only sets the interval's center, not its width.
What is social engineering as it applies to information security?
A method for controlling the thought process of a group of people
The negative aspect of decision by committee, otherwise known as groupthink.
The use of emotional triggers and other psychological tactics to obtain confidential information

Social engineering is manipulating people through psychological tactics (pretexting, phishing, urgency, trust) to obtain confidential information or access. It targets human behavior rather than technical vulnerabilities.

Two colleagues in your department have been in a heated argument over work responsibilities for several minutes. The argument escalates, and one of them shoves the other forcefully in view of the team. What is the most appropriate action to take?
Try to physically intervene and separate them yourself.
Shout at them to stop and try to grab everyone’s attention to shame them into stopping.
Call for security or the appropriate personnel to intervene immediately.
Record the incident on your phone to provide evidence in case of an investigation.

Once physical violence occurs, summon trained security or appropriate personnel immediately rather than physically intervening, which risks injury to yourself (OSHA workplace violence guidance). Shaming or filming does not stop the threat.
A recently terminated employee is sending hostile, vaguely threatening emails to your team, saying he might do something to 'make everyone understand.' How should the team respond?
Reply to explain the reasons for his termination
Ignore the emails, assuming he will cool down
Forward the emails to coworkers to gather opinions
Report the emails to security and human resources as soon as possible
Veiled threats from a former employee are a recognized risk factor; preserve the emails and report them to security and HR for threat assessment and protective measures.
In construction, Stair landings are required every ___________________feet. Ref: 1926.1052
OSHA 1926.1052(a)(2) requires a landing at least 30 inches deep and 22 inches wide for every 12 feet or less of vertical rise in construction stairways.
What is the recommended angle for setting up an extension ladder against a wall or other vertical surface?
Extension ladders should be set at about 75.5 degrees, the 4-to-1 rule: base 1 ft out for every 4 ft of working height (OSHA 1926.1053(b)(5)(i)).
A Type 1A ladder as a capacity of ______________ pounds.
ANSI A14 duty ratings: Type IAA 375 lb, Type IA 300 lb (extra heavy duty), Type I 250 lb, Type II 225 lb, Type III 200 lb.
Which is most common entry for chemicals into the body.

Inhalation is the most common and significant route of occupational chemical entry because airborne gases, vapors, fumes and dusts are readily absorbed through the large lung surface. That is why most OELs are expressed as airborne concentrations.
A welder cutting galvanized steel develops fever, chills, a metallic taste and muscle aches several hours after the shift. Symptoms resolve within two days. Which fume is the MOST likely cause?
Inhaling freshly formed zinc oxide fume (for example when welding galvanized steel) causes metal fume fever: flu-like fever and chills that resolve within 24-48 h.
What is the function of the skeletal system in the human body?
To produce blood cells and store nutrients.

The skeletal system supports and protects the body, enables movement, produces blood cells in red bone marrow (hematopoiesis) and stores minerals such as calcium and phosphorus. Temperature, digestion and nerve impulses are other systems.
What is the primary purpose of an occupational exposure assessment?
To identify and evaluate potential health hazards in the workplace
To assess the company's financial performance

Occupational exposure assessment (AIHA strategy) identifies and characterizes workplace health hazards and worker exposures, then compares them to OELs to decide on controls. It does not measure productivity, satisfaction or finances.
Which of the following is NOT typically considered when conducting an occupational exposure assessment?

Exposure assessments focus on the agent, its concentration, route, frequency and duration of exposure, and compare results to OELs. Age and gender are personal susceptibility factors not typically part of the exposure characterization.
What is a Time-Weighted Average (TWA) in occupational exposure assessment?
The average time it takes for a worker to complete a task
The average exposure to a hazardous substance over a specific time period, typically 8 hours
The time it takes for a hazardous substance to break down in the environment
The average time between workplace accidents
A TWA is the average airborne concentration over a defined period, usually 8 hours: TWA = sum(Ci x Ti) / 8. It is the basis for OSHA PELs and ACGIH TLV-TWAs.

There are three requirements before using a tight-fitting respirator. Two requirements are a medical evaluation by a LHCP and initial fit testing, either qualitative or quantitative. What is a third requirement?
Real-time demonstration in a hazardous environment

OSHA 1910.134 requires medical evaluation (k), fit testing (f) and training before use and at least annually (k) for tight-fitting respirators. Leak or user seal checks are done each time the respirator is donned but are not the program element asked.
When a respiratory hazard exists or is suspected, the concentration must be measured. Which testing medium is MOST appropriate for this measurement?

Airborne contaminant concentrations are measured with air sampling devices (pumps with sorbent tubes/filters, direct-reading instruments) per 1910.134(d)(1)(iii) exposure evaluation. A dosimeter measures noise; LEL and O2 meters cover only flammability and oxygen.
Employees working in IDLH atmospheres shall be provided a full facepiece pressure demand SCBA certified by NIOSH for a minimum service life of ____ minutes:

OSHA 1910.134(d)(2)(i) requires a full facepiece pressure-demand SCBA certified by NIOSH for a minimum service life of 30 minutes, or a combination supplied-air respirator with auxiliary SCBA, for IDLH atmospheres.
Raynaud’s phenomenon is a problem which causes
Decreased blood flow to the fingers

Raynaud's phenomenon (vibration white finger, hand-arm vibration syndrome) involves vasospasm reducing blood flow to the fingers, causing blanching, numbness and pain, often triggered by cold and vibrating tools.
Designing the machine to fit the individual
Implementation of a work hardening program

Anthropometry is the measurement of human body dimensions (heights, reaches, grip size) used to design workstations and equipment for population percentiles, typically 5th to 95th. Fitting the machine to the person is ergonomics.
