The employer shall retain each canceled entry permit for at least ______ year(s)
1910.146E6
29 CFR 1910.146(e)(6) requires the employer to retain each canceled entry permit for at least 1 year to facilitate the annual review of the permit space program.
Which of the following is a crucial step before starting mechanical ventilation in a confined space?
Ensuring all personnel are trained on emergency procedures
Testing the atmosphere for oxygen sufficiency and toxic substances
Placing warning signs around the work area
1910.146(d)(5) requires initial atmospheric testing for oxygen, flammables and toxics before entry so ventilation needs and hazards are known; testing establishes the baseline.
A SDS of a chemical has a (CAS) Registry Number. What is CAS?
CAS stands for Chemical Abstracts Service, a division of the American Chemical Society that assigns unique registry numbers to chemical substances, listed in SDS Section 1 or 3.

Antwan is planning to clean the lab floor with a caustic 10% sodium hydroxide solution. He doesn’t have gloves or a respirator. The lab manager stops the activity, stating that it is unsafe. What should the company do?
Go to the safety manager to get permission to use the caustic soda.
Find gloves and a respirator and continue using the caustic soda.
Substituting a less hazardous cleaner applies the hierarchy of controls, removing the caustic hazard rather than relying on PPE. Getting permission or finding PPE leaves the hazard in place.
Which of the following is a required measure to prevent encroachment and electrocution under OSHA 1926.1408(b)?
Conduct a planning meeting with operators and workers to review power line locations and safety steps
Use conductive tag lines to help guide loads around power lines
Assume power lines are insulated unless otherwise stated by the employer
Rely on the crane operator to self-monitor the safe approach distance
29 CFR 1926.1408(b)(1) requires a planning meeting with the operator and other workers to review power line location and steps to prevent encroachment/electrocution. Tag lines must be nonconductive.
What is the most important item for the crane operator to lift a load.

The load chart defines rated capacity for the boom length, radius and configuration, so the operator must use it to determine whether a lift is within capacity. Anti-two-block devices are safety aids, not capacity.

The Controlling entity must inform the user of the equipment and the ________________ of the location of known hazards beneath the crane equipment set-up area (such as voids, tanks, utilities). Ref: 1926.1402
29 CFR 1926.1402(e) requires the controlling entity to inform the user and the operator of the location of known hazards beneath the set-up area, such as voids, tanks and utilities.
If a company spends $200,000 to redesign the workplace ergonomically and it saves $20,000 in annual injury costs after expenses, what is the ROI?

A company is considering two safety interventions:
Option A: Costs $50,000 upfront but saves $30,000 per year in injury costs.
Option B: Costs $20,000 upfront but saves only $5,000 per year in injury costs.
Which method should the company choose based on a cost-benefit analysis over five years?
Option A, because it provides greater long-term savings despite a higher initial cost.
Option B, because it requires a lower initial investment.
Either option, as both result in cost savings.
Neither option, as safety investments should not be based on financial return.
Five-year net benefit: A = 5 x $30,000 - $50,000 = $100,000; B = 5 x $5,000 - $20,000 = $5,000. Option A gives far greater net return despite higher upfront cost.
Which of the following best describes the "cost of risk" in workplace safety?
The total amount a company spends on workers’ compensation insurance.
The combination of direct and indirect costs associated with workplace injuries and accidents.
The total cost of safety training programs.
The cost of replacing injured workers with new hires.
Cost of risk includes retained losses, insurance premiums, risk control and administration costs; in a safety context it combines direct and indirect injury and accident costs, not just premiums.
A construction company identifies a high risk of falls from scaffolding. Which of the following is the most effective risk control method based on the hierarchy of controls?
Conducting weekly safety training on proper scaffold use.
Requiring workers to wear fall protection harnesses at all times.
Installing guardrails and improving scaffold design.
Increasing safety inspections and supervisor oversight.
Installing guardrails and improving scaffold design are engineering controls that passively prevent falls, ranking above PPE (harnesses) and administrative measures (training, inspections).

During a confined space entry, atmospheric monitoring detects Oxygen levels at 19.2%, Hydrogen Sulfide at 25 ppm, and Carbon Monoxide at 70 ppm. According to OSHA 1910.146 and 1910.1000, what is the most immediate course of action?
Proceed with entry while using air-purifying respirators.
Ventilate the space and continuously monitor the atmosphere before entry.
Enter with self-contained breathing apparatus (SCBA) and a standby rescue team.
Proceed with entry as the levels are within acceptable limits.

O2 at 19.2% is below the 19.5% minimum, H2S 25 ppm exceeds the 20 ppm ceiling, and CO 70 ppm exceeds the 50 ppm PEL. Ventilate and continuously monitor until acceptable before entry; APRs are prohibited in O2-deficient air.

A manufacturing plant has a 1 in 500 probability of a chemical spill occurring per year, with an expected cleanup cost of $250,000 per incident. If an investment of $1,000 in spill containment reduces the spill probability to 1 in 2500, what is the annual cost savings from implementing the control measure? Spill Containment last 10 years.
Expected loss before = $250,000 / 500 = $500/yr; after = $250,000 / 2,500 = $100/yr; reduction $400/yr minus annualized cost $1,000/10 = $100/yr gives net savings of $300/yr.

A crew is working on a multi-level scaffold system at a construction site. The foreman notices that workers have placed heavy buckets of mortar and bricks on one section of the platform. The scaffold was rated for a maximum load of 1,000 lbs per section. A worker estimates that the materials and workers on that section weigh around 1,200 lbs.
What is the safest course of action?
Continue working but distribute the weight evenly across the platform.
Remove some of the material and verify the scaffold's load rating before continuing work.
Reinforce the scaffold with extra planks and ties to prevent collapse.
Proceed with caution, ensuring workers move slowly to reduce strain on the scaffold.

1926.451(a)(1) prohibits loading scaffolds beyond rated capacity; at 1,200 lb on a 1,000 lb section, remove material to bring the load within rating before work continues. Reinforcing without engineering does not re-rate it.

A new worker is assigned to a project that involves working on a scaffold 12 feet above the ground. He notices that there are no guardrails installed on the open side, and no personal fall arrest system (PFAS) is provided. The site supervisor tells him to "just be careful" because it's only temporary work. The worker brings it up to the safety professional.
What should the safety professional do?
Comply with the supervisor’s instruction and work carefully without fall protection.
Use a nearby rope to tie himself off temporarily.
The worker should be removed from the scaffold until proper safety measures are in place.
Proceed cautiously but limit movement to avoid falling.
1926.451(g)(1) requires fall protection on scaffolds over 10 feet. At 12 feet with no guardrails or PFAS, the worker must be removed until protection is installed; improvised tie-off is unacceptable.

During an inspection, a safety professional notices workers climbing up the side of a scaffold frame instead of using the designated ladder access. When questioned, a worker responds, "The ladder is on the other side, and this way is quicker."
What is the best safety action to take?
Warn the workers but allow them to continue since they are experienced.
Stop work immediately and instruct workers to use the designated access points.
Allow them to climb carefully, as long as they have three points of contact.
Assign an observer to monitor their climbing technique for added safety.

1926.451(e) requires proper access; climbing cross braces is prohibited. Stopping work and redirecting to the designated ladder corrects an imminent fall hazard; three points of contact on a frame is not approved access.

A construction crew is digging a trench that is 8 feet deep to lay underground utility lines. The soil is classified as Type B. The crew is using a trench box, but one worker is observed working outside the protective system. What is the best immediate corrective action?
Stop work and have the worker re-enter the trench inside the trench box.
Allow the worker to finish the task quickly since no cave-ins have occurred.
Assign another worker to monitor the trench while the task is completed.
Add additional shoring to the trench after the worker completes the task.
1926.652(a) requires workers in excavations 5 ft or deeper to be protected by a protective system; a worker outside the trench box at 8 ft is exposed, so stop work and move him inside the box.

During a routine walk-through of a job site, you notice an extension cord running across a high-traffic walkway, with visible damage to its outer insulation. Nearby, a worker is using an electric drill connected to this cord. What is the best course of action?
Instruct the worker to stop using the cord immediately and replace it.
Tape the damaged section of the cord and allow the worker to continue.
Move the cord away from the walkway but continue using it.
Assign a worker to monitor the cord to prevent trips and falls
1926.405(a)(2)(ii)(I) and 1910.334 require damaged cords to be removed from service; taping or relocating does not restore insulation. Stop use and replace the cord.
Which is one of the MOST commonly cited unsafe conditions at a worksite?
Poor housekeeping (debris, clutter, spills) is among the most commonly observed unsafe conditions and contributes to slips, trips, fire and struck-by hazards across most worksites.
Which is an example of a scenario where energized work is acceptable?
Workers being unable to de-energize the system due to production deadlines
A situation in which additional hazards would be created if the system was de-energized
A system where total voltage to ground is less than 100 volts
Workers being equipped with the correct voltage exposure-rated arc flash PPE

NFPA 70E 110.4 / 1910.333(a)(1) permit energized work only when de-energizing introduces additional hazards or increased risk, or is infeasible. Production deadlines and PPE alone do not justify it; the threshold is 50 V, not 100 V. Note: Key reflects NFPA 70E/1910.333 'additional hazards' justification; infeasibility is the other permitted reason.
During a crane lifting operation, which person is responsible for control of the lift?
Any employee with a clear line of sight to the load

Under 1926 Subpart CC the crane operator is responsible for operations under their direct control and has authority to stop and refuse unsafe lifts; signal persons communicate, but the operator controls the lift.
What is the MOST effective control measure to address pinch points when handling 55-gallon drums?
Ensuring employees are trained on proper hand placement
Using gloves rated for the drum's weight to prevent crush injuries
Mandating two-person lifts for all drum-handling tasks
Utilizing specialized dollies exclusively for drum transport
Specialized drum dollies/handlers are engineering controls that remove hands from pinch points, more effective than training, gloves or two-person lifts (administrative/PPE).
Which condition is most likely to alter the hazards associated with an open excavation?
Operation of heavy machinery near the excavation
An employee with less than one year of experience performing the excavation
The presence of both Type A and Type C soil in the excavation
Multiple excavations present on the same job site

Heavy machinery near the edge adds surcharge loads and vibration that increase cave-in risk (1926.651(j), soil classification changes with vibration). Experience and multiple excavations do not change the soil hazard itself.
Who holds the primary responsibility for maintaining walking and working surfaces in a clean, orderly, and sanitary condition in the workplace?
29 CFR 1910.22(a) places the duty on the employer to keep walking-working surfaces clean, orderly and sanitary. Managers and supervisors act on the employer's behalf.
Which statement is correct regarding hand and power tools?
It is the employer’s responsibility to ensure that only well-maintained and operable hand and power tools are utilized on the job site.
Regular maintenance logs must be kept on all hand and power tools and submitted to the safety manager monthly.
Only supervisors are allowed to make repairs to hand and power tools.
It is the supervisor’s responsibility to ensure that all hand and power tools on the jobs site are well maintained and operable.
29 CFR 1926.300(a) and 1910.242(a) make the employer responsible for the safe condition of tools and equipment used by employees, including employee-owned tools.
Which is an example of a passive fall protection system?
Full-body harness with shock absorbing lanyards
Guardrails are passive fall protection: they prevent falls without requiring worker action or equipment donning. Harnesses and lifelines are active (personal) fall arrest components.
Which criteria would necessitate a critical lift plan?
Repetitive lifts conducted multiple times during the workday or job
Any lift performed by a rough terrain crane
Lifts performed without a designated spotter
Lifting in weather conditions that may affect crane or equipment performance

Adverse weather affecting crane performance (wind, ice, visibility) elevates lift risk and is a common critical lift trigger, alongside lifts near capacity, multi-crane picks and lifts over occupied areas.
Which does the “P” chemical breakthrough rating stand for?
Poly-coated, highly recommended (breakthrough times greater than 8hr)
Perforated, not designed for chemical exposure (breakthrough times less than 1hr)
Poor, not recommended (breakthrough times less than 1hr)
Performance, highly recommended (breakthrough times greater than 8hr)
On glove chemical-resistance charts, 'P' means Poor (not recommended), typically with breakthrough under about 1 hour. Excellent/Good ratings indicate long breakthrough times.
Who is typically responsible for conducting hazard assessments on construction sites?
Effective hazard assessment involves both management (responsibility and resources) and workers (task knowledge); ANSI/ASSP Z10 and OSHA SHP guidelines emphasize worker participation.
What is the first step in conducting a hazard assessment on a construction site?

A site walkthrough is the first practical step in a construction hazard assessment, gathering observations from which hazards are then identified and controls selected. Note: 'First step' is debatable; some sources place hazard identification first.
What is the primary purpose of a post-training report?
To document only the employees who failed
To summarize key outcomes, attendance, and effectiveness of the training
To provide legal protection against employee complaints
A post-training report records what was delivered, who attended, and how effective it was; this data drives the next improvement cycle.
Which of the following is NOT typically included in an interim training report?
Completion status of employees in training
Details of an unrelated accident investigation
Adjustments made to content based on participant understanding
Interim reports track progress, feedback, and mid-course adjustments. Unrelated incident details do not belong. Note the NOT.
Which of the following should be included in a post-training evaluation report?
A summary of participant engagement and understanding.
Disciplinary actions taken during the training.
A list of future company training budgets.

A post-training evaluation report should summarize participation, engagement and learning outcomes (Kirkpatrick reaction/learning levels) to judge effectiveness. Opinions, discipline and budgets do not belong.
Which of the following is NOT a factor in determining the appropriate type of Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) for a task?
The physical condition of the worker
The specific hazards associated with the task
The comfort and fit of the PPE

PPE selection under 1910.132(d) is based on hazard assessment, with proper fit and worker factors considered. Cost may influence purchasing but is not a valid selection criterion for protection level.
When must a worker REPLACE their PPE?
When it becomes damaged or worn out
After each use, regardless of condition
Only after one year of use
1910.132(e): defective or damaged PPE shall not be used. PPE is replaced when damaged, worn or no longer protective, not on a fixed calendar or comfort basis.
Which of the following is the primary factor in determining the type of PPE required for a specific task?
The employee’s personal preference for comfort
The specific hazards present in the workplace
The cost of the PPE to the employer
The hazard assessment of specific workplace hazards (1910.132(d)) drives PPE selection. The standard requires the assessment but does not itself choose the PPE; comfort and cost are secondary.
Which of the following is the MOST compelling reason for senior management to invest in workplace safety programs?
Compliance with OSHA regulations to avoid fines
Improved employee morale, productivity, and reduced turnover
Additional expenses that lower overall profit margins
Management responds most to business value: improved morale, productivity and retention show safety as an investment. Compliance/fine avoidance is a weaker, minimum-level argument.
What is a key financial benefit of reducing workplace injuries?
Lower workers' compensation premiums and reduced lost-time costs
Higher employee turnover due to increased safety protocols
More government regulations being enforced on the company
Increased operating costs due to more training requirements
Fewer injuries lower experience modification rates (EMR), workers' compensation premiums and lost-time costs, a direct financial benefit of injury reduction.
Which of the following is an INDIRECT cost of workplace incidents?
Medical expenses for the injured worker
OSHA fines related to safety violations
Lost productivity and the cost of training replacement workers
Costs associated with repairing damaged equipment
Lost productivity and replacement worker training are indirect (hidden/uninsured) costs. Medical expenses are direct insured costs; fines and equipment repair are typically counted as direct.
What role does risk identification play in the risk management process?
To document all possible risks without assessing their impact.
To determine the financial implications of each identified risk.
To identify all potential risks to which a project might be exposed.
To prioritize risks based on their occurrence in previous projects.
Risk identification (ISO 31000) finds, recognizes and describes all risks that could affect objectives; analysis and evaluation of impact and priority follow in later steps.
In the context of risk response, what does 'Risk Avoidance' involve?
Taking actions to transfer the risk to another party
Implementing controls to mitigate the risk
Choosing alternatives that circumvent the risk altogether
Accepting the risk as part of the operational model
Risk avoidance means not undertaking the activity or choosing an alternative that eliminates exposure to the risk. Transfer shifts it to another party; mitigation reduces it; retention accepts it.
Which is a common risk management technique used to handle multiple project risks simultaneously?
Scenario planning examines combinations of multiple risks and their interactions under alternative futures, so several risks are addressed simultaneously rather than one point at a time.
Combustible liquid has a flash point above _____ F.
Under NFPA 30 (and pre-2012 OSHA 1910.106), a combustible liquid has a flash point at or above 100 F (37.8 C); below 100 F it is flammable.

Which of the answer choices completes the balanced equation for the following?
Fe2 O3 + 3CO=
Balance: Fe2O3 + 3CO -> 2Fe + 3CO2. Fe: 2 = 2; C: 3 = 3; O: 3 + 3 = 6 = 3 x 2. Options A, B and D do not conserve atoms.
Which of the following is an example of a chemical change?
Rusting forms a new substance (iron oxide) by oxidation, a chemical change. Boiling, melting and cutting change only physical state or shape.
What does the 'ADDIE' model stand for in instructional design?
ADDIE is the instructional systems design model: Analyze, Design, Develop, Implement, Evaluate, used for systematic training development (consistent with ANSI/ASSP Z490.1).
Which of the following best describes foreign object debris (FOD)?
Materials that enhance the performance of aerospace vehicles
Unintended objects in a designated area that could cause damage
Equipment used for quality control in manufacturing
A type of nanomaterial used in construction
FOD is any foreign object (debris, tools, hardware) present where it should not be, such as runways or aircraft, that can cause damage or injury.
In nanotechnology, what is typically considered a nanoparticle?
A particle size between 1 and 1000 micrometers
A particle size between 1 and 100 nanometers
A particle size larger than 100 nanometers
A particle that is visible to the naked eye
Per NIOSH and ISO/TS 80004, nanoparticles have at least one dimension between about 1 and 100 nanometers; micrometer-sized particles are far larger.
What officer does not report to the incident commander?
ICS Command Staff reporting to the Incident Commander are the Public Information Officer, Liaison Officer and Safety Officer. Environmental specialists normally sit within the Planning Section.
What is the main preparedness measure workplaces should implement when anticipating an imminent chemical, biological, radiological, or nuclear (CBRNE) attack?
Large central personal protective equipment inventory
CBRN releases can arrive with little warning and outdoor air may be contaminated, so shelter-in-place (seal room, shut HVAC) is the primary protective action unless directed to evacuate.

You're assigned to abrasive blast a corroded pipeline inside a containment. Your coworker arrives wearing only safety glasses and a dust mask.
What should you do?
Advise them to get new PPE at break.
Remind them that full face protection and a supplied-air respirator are required for this task.
Let the supervisor handle it later.
Observe the work to assess the risk further.
Abrasive blasting in containment requires a Type CE abrasive-blast supplied-air respirator and face/head protection (1910.94, 1910.134). Glasses and a dust mask are inadequate; correct it now.

You’re monitoring a pour in the foundry when a worker walks into the area with excessive moisture on their gloves.
What is the appropriate response?
Give them a dry towel to wipe off.
Stop them immediately—moisture can cause a steam explosion when in contact with molten metal.
Observe the work to assess the risk further.
Water contacting molten metal flashes to steam, expanding about 1,700 times and causing violent steam explosions. Moist gloves or tools must be stopped immediately before approaching the pour.

You’re about to begin a task covered in a JHA written over a month ago. Since then, the layout and equipment have changed.
What should you do?
Proceed—the JHA is still technically active.
Stop and revise the JHA with the current hazards before starting.
Just process cautiously with each step.
Ask someone else if they think it's okay.
A JHA must be reviewed and revised whenever equipment, layout or procedures change (management of change). Proceeding on an outdated JHA ignores new hazards.
Thermal stress related specifically to heat becomes increasingly dangerous to a worker’s health. Which heat illness is considered the MOST severe and requires immediate medical attention?
Heat stroke is a medical emergency in which thermoregulation fails (core temperature over about 104 F, altered mental status) and can be fatal; call 911 and cool immediately.

Bloodborne pathogen exposures may be effectively controlled through a variety of methods. If workers on a remote construction site must risk an exposure, such as in administering first-aid, which control measures are required to be in place?
Face shield, latex gloves, and a disposable apron
Antiseptic hand soap, disposable paper towels, and a disposal bag
Chlorine-based bleach wipes and a surgical mask that covers the mouth and nose
Eye wash station and a deluge shower
29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(3) requires appropriate PPE such as gloves, face shields and aprons where blood exposure is anticipated, including first aid. Soap, wipes and eyewash are not barrier protection.
What are the primary routes of lead exposure and the most effective control methods to mitigate its hazards?
Enters the body through inhalation or ingestion. Proper respirator selection, good personal hygiene, and isolating/disposing of clothing that may be contaminated.
Enters the body through inhalation. It is a naturally occurring element, therefore using local area exhaust to remove airborne lead dust to the outside atmosphere will eliminate any potential danger.
Enters the body through inhalation. Use of a self-contained breathing apparatus is the only effective control to prevent lead from entering the lungs.
Enters the body through absorption or inhalation. Effective controls include rubber gloves, full face shield, and an N95 dust mask.

Lead enters mainly by inhalation and ingestion (hand-to-mouth). 1910.1025/1926.62 controls include respirators, hygiene facilities and handling of contaminated clothing; N95s and gloves alone are insufficient.
warehouse stores 55-gallon drums of flammable liquids. The maximum allowable quantity per control area is 660 gallons. How many full drums can be safely stored without exceeding this limit?
Drums = 660 gal / 55 gal per drum = 12 full drums exactly; 13 would total 715 gal and exceed the limit.

A safety inspector needs to calculate the incident rate for a facility. The facility had 3 recordable injuries in a year, with 100 employees working 40 hours per week for 50 weeks. What is the OSHA recordable incident rate?
A worker is exposed to 95 dBA for 2 hours, 90 dBA for 4 hours, and 85 dBA for 2 hours. What is the worker's OSHA noise dose?
Allowed times (OSHA 5-dB rule): 95 dBA = 4 h, 90 dBA = 8 h, 85 dBA = 16 h. D = 2/4 + 4/8 + 2/16 = 0.5 + 0.5 + 0.125 = 112.5%, which exceeds the PEL.
Which of the following is NOT a common component of a fleet safety program?
Fleet safety programs cover driver selection and training, vehicle maintenance, ergonomics, policies and telematics. Marketing strategy is unrelated to fleet safety.
f a driver tailgates you, what should you do?
Slam on your brakes to warn them.
Switch lanes or gradually slow down to let them pass.
Tailgate the vehicle in front of you.
Defensive driving: increase following distance from the vehicle ahead, slow gradually, or change lanes so the tailgater can pass. Braking hard or speeding up increases collision risk.
Proper equipment for prompt _____________ of the injured person to a physician or hospital, or a communication system for contacting necessary ambulance service, shall be provided. Ref: 1926.50
29 CFR 1926.50(e) requires proper equipment for prompt transportation of the injured to a physician or hospital, or a communication system for contacting ambulance service.
_________________ refers to the number of subordinates under a manager’s direct control.
Span of control is the number of subordinates a supervisor directly manages; ICS recommends 3 to 7, with 5 optimal.
Who does the Safety Officer report to in a large emergency?
The Safety Officer is Command Staff and reports directly to the Incident Commander, with authority to stop or prevent unsafe acts.
What are the four sections that report to the incident commander.
The four ICS General Staff sections are Operations, Planning, Logistics and Finance/Administration. Safety, PIO and Liaison are Command Staff, not sections.

Rachel is part of the HAZMAT team working to remediate a contaminated site. She has been instructed to enter a contaminated area to retrieve a batch of soil samples that were previously taken. She was instructed to wear safety glasses, safety boots with steel toes and shanks, coveralls, gloves, and a hard hat. What HAZWOPER PPE level would this constitute?
Level D is a work uniform (coveralls, safety boots, glasses, gloves, hard hat) with no respiratory protection, used only where no atmospheric hazard exists.
A spill of 10,000 pounds of benzene from a vessel requires what?

Benzene's CERCLA reportable quantity is 10 lb; a 10,000 lb release must be reported immediately to the National Response Center, the federal EPA/Coast Guard notification point. Note: Report goes to the National Response Center; 'calling EPA' is the closest option.
A powerline of 7200 volts has fallen across the crane’s outrigger. What is the best course of action for the crane operator?
Use the crane to lift the line out off the outrigger.
Jump out of the cab and shuffle feet to get away.
Use an insulated hot stick to lift the wire off the outrigger.
Stay in the cab until emergency crews arrive.
If a crane contacts a live line, the operator should remain in the cab, warn others away and wait for the utility to de-energize, unless fire forces exit by jumping clear with feet together.
An example of an emergency which planning efforts are more focused on mitigation and recovery than on prevention is a
Earthquakes cannot be prevented, so planning focuses on mitigation (seismic design, anchoring) and response/recovery. Spills, dust explosions and fires are largely preventable.
Which threat or hazard is usually the focus of vulnerability assessments?

Security vulnerability assessments focus on intentional threats such as terrorism, evaluating targets, weaknesses and protective measures. Natural hazards are addressed by hazard/risk assessments. Note: Vulnerability assessments can cover any hazard; terrorism focus reflects security vulnerability assessment usage.
Which positions make up the command staff under the Incident Command System (ICS)?
Public Information Officer, Chief Executive Officer, and Safety Officer
Logistics Section Chief, Safety Officer, and Contracting Officer
Liaison Officer, Operations Section Chief, and Finance Section Chief
Safety Officer, Public Information Officer, and Liaison Officer
Command staff report directly to the IC: Safety, Public Information and Liaison Officers. Section chiefs (Operations, Planning, Logistics, Finance/Admin) form the general staff.

Any organization or workplace can encounter emergencies originating from a myriad of sources at any given time.
Which is the MOST effective safety management instrument for reducing incidents at a workplace?
Perform pre-employment screening for potential hires.
Implement a detailed written management plan.
Establish strong ties with emergency response teams.
A detailed written management plan (emergency action plan/SMS) systematically identifies hazards, assigns responsibilities and controls, reducing incidents more broadly than screening or equipment.
What is a crucial aspect of the pre-incident planning process for a fixed facility?
Arranging for training and drill requirements that involve all potential responders
Prioritizing HAZWOPER over all other regulations related to hazardous materials
Conversing about training and drill requirements specifically with the fire department
Concentrating on the training requirements of the facility's employees
Pre-incident planning for a fixed facility should include training and drills with all potential responders (facility ERT, fire, EMS, hazmat, LEPC) to ensure coordinated response.
Which formula is used to determine risks associated with an event?
Risk = probability × severity × estimate of response time
Risk is expressed as the product of probability (likelihood) and severity (consequence): R = P x S, the basis of risk matrices.
Which of the following lists the top three priorities during emergency planning initiatives, in order from highest to lowest priority?
Protecting the environment, Protecting human life, Protecting property
Protecting human life, Protecting the environment, Protecting continuity of community operations
Protecting human life, Protecting property, Protecting the environment
Protecting property, Protecting human life, Protecting the environment

Traditional emergency planning priorities are life safety first, then property protection, then environmental protection, consistent with many CSP references. Note: Some references rank environment above property; key follows life-property-environment ordering.
During an emergency incident, who is in charge on-site?
Under ICS/NIMS the Incident Commander has overall authority and responsibility for on-scene incident management; the Safety Officer reports to the IC.
Emergency contact numbers to report emergencies should be accessible to:
1910.38 emergency action plans require procedures for reporting emergencies to be known by all employees, so contact numbers must be accessible to everyone.
Where can first responders find generic hazard and initial response information for materials regulated in transportation?
The ERG gives generic guidance by UN/NA number and guide page (isolation distances, fire and spill response). The SDS gives product-specific detail.
Where should employees look for detailed emergency information on specific chemical substances used in the workplace?
SDS (1910.1200(g)) provide chemical-specific hazard, first-aid, firefighting, spill and exposure-control information. The ERG is for initial transportation incident response.
Which of the following is the first step in the emergency planning process?
Discuss the different types of possible emergencies
Determine which types of hazards may affect the organization
Protect and secure potable water supplies
Emergency planning begins with hazard identification/vulnerability analysis to determine which hazards could affect the organization; plans and controls follow.

An electrician has locked out the electrical supply but has not tagged it. What risk is
created by skipping the tagging step?
Difficulty identifying who locked out the equipment
Potential for unauthorized re-energizing of the equipment
Increased wear on the lockout device

Without a tag, others may not know why the device is isolated, raising the risk of unauthorized or inadvertent re-energization. 1910.147 requires identifying the authorized employee who applied the lock.

During a shift change, a second team will take over a maintenance operation already
underway. What is the correct procedure regarding lockout/tagout devices?
The new team uses the existing locks
Each incoming worker adds their own lock
Supervisor replaces existing locks with new ones
Original workers take their lock off. The incoming worker verify the energy is not present and put their lock on.

KEY CORRECTED by trainer review: 1910.147(f)(4) requires continuity of protection during shift change: the incoming worker applies a lock BEFORE the outgoing lock is removed. Removing first leaves a gap.
A machine is serviced regularly, and employees find lockout/tagout procedures time-consuming and often skip minor steps. What is the most appropriate corrective action?
Discipline workers after an incident occurs
Simplify and clearly document procedures, then retrain employees
Allow experienced workers to bypass some steps

Repeated shortcuts signal a system problem; simplify and clearly document machine-specific procedures and retrain authorized employees per 1910.147. Allowing shortcuts or waiting for an incident is unacceptable.
Safety leadership is a personal philosophy. Which behavior exemplifies this trait?
Encouraging an elevated risk tolerance among workers when a hazard is identified.
Holding profit, quality, and safety as equally important in the workplace.
Leading by example models expected safety behavior and builds credibility, a core safety leadership trait. Raising risk tolerance and unquestioning obedience undermine safety leadership.
What is a recommended best practice for delivering safety-related material to employees?
Keep yourself centered on the audience and maintain a consistent pace.
Be enthusiastic, use hand gestures, smile, make eye contact, and vary the pace of speech.
Speak very slowly without inflection so everyone can understand you.
Hold all questions until the end of the presentation, if there is time.
Effective delivery uses enthusiasm, eye contact, gestures and varied pace to keep adult learners engaged. Monotone speech and deferring all questions reduce engagement.
What action(s) must your senior leaders take to support the cultural change necessary for creating a positive safety culture and achieving "world-class" safety within your company?
Lead by example, demonstrating expected behavior and actively engaging at a personal level.
Delegate safety responsibility to mid-level managers.
Discipline workers who violate safety rules and require them to attend a safety seminar.
Adhere to regulatory requirements for safety compliance.

Culture change requires visible, felt leadership: senior leaders demonstrating expected behaviors and personally engaging. Delegation, discipline-only or compliance-only approaches do not change culture.

Like all investment strategies, the objective is to see a concrete return on the invested resources. Which of the following goal-setting approaches might be effective in justifying the upfront cost of new or enhanced safety measures?
Specific, measurable, attainable, realistic, and timely criteria
Setting strategic corporate goals, pinpointing improvement areas, and beginning with an ideal scenario.
SMART goals (specific, measurable, attainable, realistic, timely) give quantifiable targets that can show return on safety investment. Lagging metrics alone do not justify upfront costs.

As worksites become larger – both in area and in the number of contractors/employees – so too does the challenge of communicating with all project team members. Which method of communication and team engagement is BEST suited and has proven to be of great benefit in fostering a unified worksite safety culture?
A large and powerful public address system
A project-wide weekly safety meeting every Monday morning
A multi-employer project safety committee brings all contractors together to share hazards and solutions, building a unified site safety culture. PA systems and reports are one-way communication.

A variety of communication tools are available to organizations, for both internal and external information sharing. Which should be included when considering the specific transfer of hazard and hazard control information to internal stakeholders (i.e. management, supervisors, and workers)?
All available technical data, safety data sheets, diagrams, photos, and regulations related to the hazard
Information that is clear, specific to the situation, and the expected outcome
A signature sheet to confirm the information was received
An email containing several links to additional reference information
Hazard communication to internal stakeholders should be clear, specific to the situation and state the expected outcome; data dumps or email links are less effective.
Which of the following is an illustration of an indirect injury cost among the traditional categories of costs associated with incidents/injuries?
Higher insurance costs due to higher claims.

Damaged public and client relations are classic hidden (indirect) costs not paid by insurance. Medical treatment is direct; note that retraining is also often classed as indirect. Note: Retraining cost (A) is also commonly considered an indirect cost.

Delivering safety-related information is a key responsibility of safety professionals. This includes communicating safety performance, injury trends, project safety planning, and conducting training. Which method is the MOST effective for conveying this information?
Use of social media or email.
Communicate benefits, lessons learned, and advocate for participant engagement.
Take charge of the communication, minimizing questions and feedback.
Utilize a structured and qualitative lecture style.
Communicating benefits and lessons learned while encouraging participation engages adult learners and drives buy-in. One-way lectures or minimizing questions reduce effectiveness.
Which of the following is an example of an indirect cost associated with workplace injuries?
Negative public and client relations are indirect (uninsured, hidden) costs. Medical treatment, workers' compensation and prescriptions are direct costs paid through insurance.
How does a strong safety culture impact employee morale?
Increases employees' trust in management and creates higher stress.
Leads to less safety incidents and lower productivity
Improves overall job satisfaction and less team cohesion.
Increases teamwork and cooperation and increases the feeling that their wellbeing is valued.
A strong safety culture builds trust, teamwork and cooperation, and makes employees feel their wellbeing is valued, improving morale. Other options pair a benefit with a negative outcome.

An amputation cost the company $137,000 in direct and indirect costs. A laser scanner guard that would have prevented it costs $4,000. If the company operates on a 5% profit margin, how much additional sales revenue is needed to pay for the accident?
Sales needed = loss / profit margin = 137,000 / 0.05 = $2,740,000. The $4,000 guard cost is a distractor (though it makes a strong business case).
When justifying a safety initiative, which of the following is the MOST effective method?
Conducting a cost-benefit analysis comparing safety costs to injury-related expenses
Presenting a summary of recent safety violations from competitors
Explaining how safety regulations can be difficult to understand
Listing all safety policies in a long report with no financial data
Cost-benefit analysis comparing control costs to avoided injury costs speaks management's financial language and is the strongest justification for a safety initiative.
A company is considering investing in additional safety training. Which metric would BEST demonstrate the return on this investment?
Number of safety training sessions completed
Reduction in injury rates and workers' compensation claims over time
Total hours spent on training per employee
Cost of hiring a safety consultant
ROI on training is best shown by outcome changes, reduced injury rates and workers' compensation claims over time. Sessions and hours are activity measures, not returns.
According to OSHA, trench boxes must extend at least ______ feet above the slope or incline.
1926.652 Appendix B: shields used with sloped or benched upper portions must extend at least 18 inches (1.5 ft) above the top of the vertical side.

A competent person wishes to use appendix A to classify the soil at his excavation site. What are the minimum numbers of analysis (test) he must make? Ref. https://www.osha.gov/.../standardnu.../1926/1926SubpartPAppA
1926 Subpart P Appendix A requires classification based on at least one visual and at least one manual analysis, so a minimum of 2 tests.
According to OSHA 1926.652 Appendix A, soil classification at an excavation site is primarily determined by performing what type of tests?
Appendix A soil classification relies on visual tests (soil type, fissures, water) and manual tests (plasticity, thumb penetration, pocket penetrometer, dry strength).

You manage safety operations at a construction company aiming to reduce workplace incidents by comparing your safety performance WITH industry leaders. What benchmarking procedure would you initially follow?
Internal Benchmarking - Analyze safety performance within your own teams first.
Functional Benchmarking - Examine safety practices in different industries.
Competitive Benchmarking - Directly compare safety incident rates against similar companies.
Generic Benchmarking - Benchmark against unrelated industries to find innovative safety practices.
Comparing incident rates directly against similar companies/industry leaders is competitive benchmarking. Internal compares your own units; functional/generic look at other industries.
As a safety coordinator in a logistics company, you're tasked with improving vehicle incident rates. Which benchmarking approach would provide the MOST practical insights?
Performance Benchmarking - Measuring specific safety processes against industry best practices.
Strategic Benchmarking - Evaluating long-term safety strategies of competitors.
Product Benchmarking - Comparing safety equipment with competitors' offerings.
Financial Benchmarking - Focusing strictly on financial investment in safety.
Performance benchmarking compares specific measurable processes (e.g., vehicle incident rates, driver programs) against best practice, giving the most practical, actionable insight.
An international retail chain aims to benchmark its workplace safety culture. Which international standard should be used to guide their efforts?
ISO 45001 – Occupational Health and Safety standards.
ISO 45001 is the international OH&S management system standard and provides the framework for benchmarking safety performance and culture globally. ISO 31000 is general risk management.
As a safety professional applying the hierarchy of controls, which of the following methods represents the most effective combination for controlling dust hazards?
Infrared thermographic imaging and inspection controls
Layers of physical and operational controls
Substitution with a less dusty product and engineering ventilation (LEV) are the top two applicable hierarchy levels, more effective than procedural or inspection controls.
During a training session on combustible dust safety, an employee asks how to PREVENT dust accumulation in hard-to-reach areas. What is the most appropriate response?
Use compressed air daily to blow dust into collection areas.
Implement a housekeeping program with regular inspections and cleaning schedules.
Allow dust to accumulate in these areas until it becomes visible and then clean it thoroughly.
Apply anti-static coatings to all surfaces to prevent dust from sticking.
NFPA 652/654 require a housekeeping program with scheduled inspection and cleaning, including hidden/elevated areas, to prevent accumulation. Compressed air disperses dust and creates explosion risk.
While conducting an investigation of a dust-related incident, you discover the facility lacks proper ventilation systems. What is the best immediate recommendation?
Shut down the facility until proper ventilation is installed.
Install portable fans to circulate air and prevent dust buildup.
Implement temporary administrative controls, such as limiting high-dust activities.
Advise the facility to install explosion-proof dust collection systems as a priority.
Until engineered dust collection is installed, interim administrative controls such as limiting dust-generating work reduce risk. Portable fans can disperse dust and create an explosible cloud.
Which of these can cause an explosion
Corn starch is an organic combustible dust that explodes when dispersed in air with an ignition source. Vermiculite, silt and clay are noncombustible minerals.
______________ requires that an explosion isolation device be installed on all suction side ducts that transport material with a KST value above zero.

NFPA combustible dust standards (NFPA 652/654, now NFPA 660) require explosion isolation on ductwork connecting dust collectors to process areas for explosible (Kst > 0) dusts. OSHA has no specific dust standard.
Electrical equipment in combustible dust environments should be Class _______?
Per NFPA 70 (NEC) Article 500, Class II locations are hazardous due to combustible dust; Class I is flammable gases/vapors and Class III is ignitable fibers/flyings.
What type of vacuum cleaner should used to vacuum combustible dust.

Vacuums for combustible dust must be approved for the hazardous location (explosion-proof/dust-ignition-proof, grounded) per NFPA 652/654. HEPA describes filtration, not ignition protection. Note: Term should be 'approved for Class II locations' / dust-ignition-proof rather than explosion-proof.
Which matter can ignite combustible dust in a dust collector?
Tramp iron or steel entering a collector can create frictional/impact sparks that ignite dust. Brass and lead are non-sparking metals; silicon is not a typical ignition source.
What five conditions are needed for a dust explosion?
Oxygen, Ignition Source, Fuel, detonation, Particle size of 0.3 microns,
Oxygen, Source, Fuel, Deflagration, Incipient stage fire.
Oxygen, Ignition Source, Fuel, Dust Collector, Poor House keeping
Oxygen, Ignition Source, Fuel, Dispersion, Confinement
The dust explosion pentagon is fuel (combustible dust), oxygen, ignition source, dispersion of the dust cloud and confinement; remove any one and an explosion cannot occur.
The best strategy to prevent dust explosion and deflagration is to prevent the __________ of dust in the workplace.
Preventing dust accumulation (by containment, collection and housekeeping) removes the fuel for secondary explosions, which cause the most damage; OSHA's NEP focuses on accumulation.
What is the primary factor that contributes to the severity of a combustible dust explosion?
Smaller particle size increases surface area, raising Kst (rate of pressure rise) and lowering minimum ignition energy, making explosions more severe. Humidity affects ignitability less.
Dust particles that are resistant to fire
Dust particles that can ignite and cause a fire or explosion
Combustible dust is fine particulate that presents a fire or deflagration (explosion) hazard when suspended in air in a sufficient concentration (NFPA 652).
What is the purpose of a dust hazard analysis (DHA)?
To identify potential sources of dust accumulation
To assess the risk of a combustible dust explosion
To determine the appropriate ventilation system for a facility
To evaluate the effectiveness of personal protective equipment (PPE)
NFPA 652 requires a Dust Hazard Analysis to identify fire, flash fire and explosion hazards of combustible dust processes and assess risk and needed safeguards.
Which action should be avoided to reduce the risk of a combustible dust explosion?
Keeping dust layers thin and spread out.
Using compressed air to clear dust.
Compressed-air cleaning disperses dust into an explosible cloud and is restricted by NFPA 652/654 unless other methods are impractical and areas are de-energized.
You are inspecting a manufacturing facility that processes grain. You notice a fine layer of dust on the beams and equipment in the production area. What is your first course of action?
Instruct the facility to immediately shut down operations and clean all areas with compressed air.
Conduct a risk assessment to evaluate the potential for a combustible dust explosion.
Recommend opening windows and doors to improve ventilation.
Advise workers to wear respiratory protection while continuing operations.
Visible dust on beams indicates accumulation; first evaluate explosion risk (DHA/risk assessment) to decide controls. Compressed air would disperse dust; respirators do not address explosion risk.
Why is proper grounding of equipment crucial in areas with combustible dust?
To prevent the generation of static electricity that could ignite the dust.
Bonding and grounding dissipate static charge that can build on equipment and personnel, preventing static sparks that can ignite a dust cloud (NFPA 77, 652).
Dust that is toxic when inhaled
Any fine material that can catch fire and explode when mixed with air
Dust that is visible in the air during industrial processes
A type of dust that is only produced in chemical factories
Combustible dust is any finely divided solid that can burn or explode when dispersed in air, whether organic, metal or plastic; it is not limited to chemical plants.

A trained maintenance worker is called to clear a jam on a conveyor system. The machine is still powered, but the emergency stop button has been pressed. The worker bypasses the fixed guard to access the jammed area without performing lockout/tagout (LOTO).
What is the most appropriate action the safety professional should take in this situation?
Commend the worker for resolving the issue quickly and minimizing downtime
Provide additional training on emergency stop procedures
Initiate disciplinary action and reinforce the lockout/tagout and guarding policy
Recommend replacing the fixed guard with a light curtain
An E-stop is not energy isolation; bypassing a guard without LOTO violates 1910.147 and 1910.212. Discipline and reinforcement of the policy address a deliberate violation by a trained worker.
A robotic cell has interlocked gates, but workers prop a gate open with a tool so they can make minor adjustments without stopping the robot. What is the BEST corrective measure?
Install cameras to monitor worker behavior
Install tamper-resistant interlocks and investigate why workers feel the need to bypass, retraining as needed
Post signs telling workers not to enter
Defeat-resistant interlocks restore the engineering control. Addressing the production pressure behind the bypass prevents it from recurring.

An operator reports that a point-of-operation guard on a hydraulic press is slowing down production. They request its removal, claiming they are experienced and can operate safely without it.
What should the safety professional do?
Allow the removal of the guard for experienced operators only
Approve guard removal during high-production periods
Evaluate alternative guarding solutions that ensure safety and efficiency
Remind the operator to be more careful when using the machine
1910.212 requires point-of-operation guarding; removal is not permitted. Evaluate alternative guards or devices (light curtains, two-hand controls) that keep protection while improving efficiency.
What is the formula for the area of a triangle? A= Area, B - base length. L - Height
Area of a triangle = 1/2 x base x height. A = bh and A = lw are for parallelograms/rectangles; pi r^2 is for circles.
A rectangular storage area is 40 feet long and 25 feet wide. You need to install a safety barrier along the entire perimeter of this area. How many feet of barrier material will you need?
Perimeter = 2 x (length + width) = 2 x (40 + 25) = 130 feet. 1,000 is the area in sq ft; 130 meters has the wrong unit.

A roofer shoots his thumb with a pneumatic nailer set to contact (bump) actuation. He was holding the trigger down and tapping the nose on the shingles to drive multiple nails. The tool was in good working order. What is the BEST recommendation?
Issue verbal discipline for the injury
Tell the worker to go slower
Switch to nailers with a full sequential trigger
NIOSH found full sequential triggers cut nail gun injury risk roughly in half compared with contact triggers. This is an engineering fix; gloves, pace and discipline are weaker.
What is the most critical factor in ensuring that a power tool with a locking trigger mechanism does not create a safety hazard?
The tool must have a quick-release feature
The trigger should only lock after a continuous press of 5 seconds
The operator must be trained to disable the lock immediately after use
The tool must have an automatic shutoff or dead-man switch
A tool with a lock-on trigger must stop when the operator releases or loses control; a dead-man switch or automatic shutoff prevents runaway operation (1926.300(d)).

A maintenance crew is tasked with replacing overhead lighting fixtures in a large warehouse. The task requires the use of both powered and non-powered hand tools, as well as an aerial lift. During a pre-task safety meeting, several potential hazards are identified.
Which of the following actions demonstrates the most effective proactive approach TO PREVENTING dropped object hazards during this task?
Ensuring all workers wear hard hats.
Using tool lanyards and tethering tools to the aerial lift basket or worker.
Establishing a designated drop zone with warning signage.
Conducting a visual inspection of tools before use.
Tethering tools to the worker or basket prevents objects from falling at the source (ANSI/ISEA 121), more effective than hard hats (PPE) or drop zones (administrative).
Name one effect on the body that a cave-in can cause ________________________________
Cave-ins crush the chest and abdomen, preventing breathing and causing traumatic or compressive asphyxiation, the main cause of trench fatalities.
The competent person examination of soil consists of a
Blows per sauce foot test and compaction test.
1926 Subpart P Appendix A requires the competent person to classify soil using at least one visual and one manual test.
______ soils have a high clay content.
Cohesive soils contain high clay content, giving cohesion that holds vertical walls. Sandy and silty soils are granular; loam is a mix.
An excavation is being performed in an old landfill. What should the air be tested for?
Decomposing landfill waste generates methane (flammable) and hydrogen sulfide (toxic), so 1926.651(g) testing should target oxygen, flammables and these gases.
Type B soil is Sloped at _____ to 1.
1926 Subpart P Appendix B: Type B soil maximum allowable slope is 1H:1V (45 degrees). Type A is 3/4:1 and Type C is 1.5:1.
Spoil piles must be excavated at least ____ feet away.
1926.651(j)(2) requires spoil and equipment to be kept at least 2 feet from the excavation edge, or retained by devices.

A crew is preparing to enter a trench that is 6 feet deep to install a new utility line. The soil is Type B, and a trench box is available but hasn't been placed yet. The supervisor insists the work must start immediately to meet the schedule.
What should the competent person do?
Allow entry since the trench is under 7 feet and the soil seems stable
Proceed with caution and watch for signs of collapse
Stop the work until the trench box is properly installed
Install a ladder and proceed without the box for quick access
1926.652(a)(1) requires a protective system for excavations 5 ft or deeper unless in stable rock; at 6 ft in Type B soil, stop work until the trench box is installed.

During an inspection of an excavation site, you notice water pooling at the bottom of a 5-foot-deep trench. Workers are nearby and planning to enter the trench to complete some tasks.
What is the safest course of action?
Have the workers wear waterproof boots and proceed
Postpone entry and have a pump remove the water first
Ask the crew to dig a small channel to drain the water away
Assign one worker to monitor the trench while the others enter
1926.651(h) prohibits working in excavations with accumulated water unless adequate precautions are taken; removing the water before entry is the safest action.

The safety professional looks at the blueprints and realizes the trench will get to 25 feet at it deepest. The soil is type C.
What should be the next step?
Provide trench shields rated for 25 feet.
Talk to the project manager about the need to open the trench at a 1:1 slope.
Provide the workers safety harness to extract them quickly.
Consult with a register professional engineer about the choice of protective system.
1926.652(b)(4) and (c)(4) require protective systems for excavations deeper than 20 ft to be designed by a registered professional engineer. A 1:1 slope is incorrect for Type C (1.5:1).
According to the OSHA standard for excavations, registered professional engineers must be used in what situation
When the excavation is over 6 feet deep
When the excavation is over 10 feet deep
When the excavation is over 13 feet deep
When the excavation is over 20 feet deep
1926.652 requires sloping and shoring/shielding systems for excavations over 20 feet deep to be designed by a registered professional engineer.

According to the OSHA standard and employer must check an excavation for hazardous atmosphere if he suspects one might be present when the depth of the excavation is _______ feet or greater.
Ref: 1926.651(g)(1)(i)
1926.651(g)(1)(i) requires atmospheric testing before entry into excavations greater than 4 feet deep where a hazardous atmosphere exists or could reasonably be expected.

A subcontractor installs a trench near a busy roadway and places the spoil pile 1 foot from the edge. No protective system is in place, and the trench is 6.5 feet deep.
What is the most immediate safety concern?
Lack of reflective tape for visibility
Distance of the spoil pile from the trench edge
No protective system for trench support
The trench is not fenced off from pedestrians
At 6.5 ft deep, 1926.652(a) requires a protective system; no cave-in protection is the gravest, most immediate hazard. The 1 ft spoil pile also violates the 2 ft rule, but is secondary.
As well that has been previously excavated, is fissured, or subject to vibration cannot be classified as which type of soil?
Appendix A: soil that is fissured, subject to vibration or previously disturbed cannot be classified as Type A; it must be classified B or C.
What is the MOST effective way to stay alert if you feel drowsy while driving?
Slow down and open the windows for fresh air.
Turn on the radio and sing along.
Pull over and stretch outside the vehicle for several minutes.
Pulling over to rest addresses drowsiness by stopping driving; brief stretching (or a short nap) is safer than tricks like pinching, radio or open windows, which do not restore alertness.
Which is the MOST efficient way(s) to minimize workers' exposure to contaminants?
Engineering controls (ventilation, enclosure, isolation) remove or reduce contaminants at the source without relying on worker behavior, more effective than administrative controls or PPE.

A facility plans to replace a key piece of production equipment with a newer model that operates at higher temperatures. What should a safety professional do FIRST as part of the Management of Change process?
Approve the purchase order to avoid project delays.
Update the safety signage to reflect the higher operating temperature.
Conduct a risk assessment to evaluate potential safety and health impacts.
Notify employees of the upcoming change via email.

Before approval, the change must be risk assessed for safety and health impacts (higher temperature, burns, materials, procedures). Purchasing, signs or emails before assessment skip the 'prior' stage of MOC.
The basic communication model requires a sender, a message (via a channel) and a receiver, with feedback closing the loop. Accuracy and brevity are qualities, not components.
Which option lists the key elements of an effective health and safety performance management system?
Measuring performance, reviewing performance, and auditing near-misses
Auditing and review, policy, organizing, planning and implementation, and measuring performance
Policy, organizing, planning and implementation, and measuring performance
Planning and organization, policy, and review performance
The HSG65 model (POPMAR): Policy, Organizing, Planning and implementing, Measuring performance, and Auditing and reviewing. Options missing auditing/review are incomplete.

A dense cloud of anhydrous ammonia has formed and is 8 miles west of a small town. The wind is blowing directly toward the town at 10 miles per hour. Assuming no dispersion or barriers, how long will it take the cloud to reach the outskirts of the town?
Time = distance / speed = 8 mi / 10 mph = 0.8 h x 60 = 48 minutes.

A toxic gas plume is drifting toward a residential area at a steady 10 mph. It takes 15 minutes to mobilize and complete evacuation of the at-risk population. What is the MINIMUM distance the plume must be from the area when the evacuation order is given to ensure safe clearance?
Distance = speed x time = 10 mi/h x (15/60) h = 2.5 miles. Trap: forgetting to convert minutes to hours.

The OHST receives a report that the wind speed has dropped from 10 mph to 5 mph, and the plume is still 8 miles out. He estimates that changes in terrain will likely slow the chemical's movement by an additional 10%. How long does he now have before the plume arrives?
Wind 5 mph reduced 10% for terrain = 4.5 mph. Time = 8 mi / 4.5 mph = 1.78 h, about 1.8 hours.
What is the purpose of a "toolbox talk" in safety training?
To provide a break from the daily work routine
To assign tasks to the workers
To briefly discuss a specific safety issue or topic
A toolbox talk is a short, informal safety meeting focused on one specific topic relevant to the day's work, reinforcing awareness and allowing discussion.
Why are safety drills important in workplace safety training?
They serve as physical exercise for employees
They prepare employees for potential emergency situations
They serve to entertain and engage employees
They allow employees to take a break from work
Drills let employees practice emergency procedures (1910.38 EAP), building familiarity and revealing plan weaknesses so they respond correctly during real emergencies.
What is a key principle of adult learning (andragogy) according to Malcolm Knowles?
Adults learn best when information is abstract.
Adults bring life experiences to the learning process.
Adults prefer learning without application to real-world problems.
Knowles' andragogy holds that adults bring life experience, are self-directed, problem-centered and need relevance; training should draw on that experience and real-world application.
What personal protective equipment (PPE) is essential when handling oxidizers?**
No PPE is necessary if handling quickly
Oxidizers can cause chemical burns and intensify fires; chemical splash goggles and chemical-resistant gloves are required. Cotton and leather are combustible and can react with oxidizers.

Question: Which of the following is the correct classification for a fire involving deep
fat fryer grease?
NFPA 10 classifies cooking oil and fat fires in commercial kitchens as Class K, extinguished with wet chemical agents that saponify the grease.
What is the correct classification for a fire involving an electrical panel?
NFPA 10 Class C fires involve energized electrical equipment requiring non-conductive agents (CO2, dry chemical). Once de-energized, it becomes Class A or B.
It takes 2/3 of a second to become aware they are falling. In that time, they have fallen ___ feet. Ref. Yates Book. D= ½(g*t2) g=32.2 ft/s2
Hazardous conditions found during an inspection should also be reviewed to determine:
How the employer was negligent in allowing the hazard to exist
What failure in the safety and health system permitted the hazard to occur
Who in the company should be assigned responsibility for correcting the hazard
Which employee was not following the safety and health system requirements specified in the company’s safety policy
Inspection findings should be traced to the management-system failure that allowed the hazard, enabling systemic correction rather than blame of individuals.
Aside from the OSHA 1989 SHMP Guidelines, which other consensus standards establish SHMP approaches?
OHSAS 18001, ANSI Z10-2019, and Lean manufacturing
ANSI/ASSP Z10 and ISO 45001 are the consensus OHS management system standards. ISO 14001 is environmental, OHSAS 18001 was withdrawn and replaced by ISO 45001, and Lean is not an SHMS standard.

You're conducting a safety audit at a manufacturing facility where employees routinely handle materials using both manual techniques and powered equipment like forklifts and pallet jacks.
What is the safest method for manually lifting 15 pounds boxes?
Bend at the waist and keep your legs straight
Keep the load away from your body while lifting
Squat down, keep your back straight, and lift with your legs
Twist your body to gain momentum when lifting
Proper lifting technique: squat, keep the back straight and load close, lift with the legs without twisting. Holding the load away or bending at the waist increases spinal loading.
Which of the following is NOT typically covered by workers' compensation?
Medical expenses related to the injury
Workers' compensation is no-fault and pays medical costs, wage replacement and rehabilitation, but in exchange it does not pay for pain and suffering (exclusive remedy).

During a site inspection, you notice that employees are not wearing the required PPE despite repeated reminders. The supervisor claims enforcing the rule might disrupt operations. What is your best course of action?
Allow the employees to work without PPE to maintain operational flow.
Suspend the work until the employees comply with PPE requirements.
Report the supervisor and employees to upper management without further action.
Create a temporary workaround until PPE is available.
Required PPE is mandatory under 1910.132; when repeated reminders fail, suspend the work until compliance. Allowing work without PPE or a workaround leaves workers exposed.
You are conducting a safety audit and discover a contractor's scaffolding does not meet OSHA standards. The contractor argues it has been used safely for years without issues. How should you respond?
Allow the scaffolding to remain in use and document the situation.
Inform OSHA directly and leave the site without further action..
Suggest minor adjustments but allow continued use until the project is complete.
Insist on immediate compliance with OSHA standards and stop the work until corrections are made
Noncompliant scaffolding (1926.451) is a serious hazard regardless of past history; stop work until corrections are made. Past incident-free use is a normalization-of-deviance argument.
A worker in a loud factory reports hearing loss in one ear over time. Which part of the ear is most likely damaged due to prolonged noise exposure?

Noise-induced hearing loss is sensorineural: prolonged loud noise destroys the hair cells of the cochlea in the inner ear. The eardrum is damaged mainly by sudden impulse or pressure, not chronic exposure.
A painter working on a scaffold collapses from heat exhaustion. As a safety officer, you check for signs of thermoregulation failure. Which part of the body regulates body temperature?

The hypothalamus is the body's thermostat, triggering sweating and vasodilation to shed heat; heat illness reflects these mechanisms being overwhelmed. The thyroid affects metabolic rate, not moment-to-moment temperature control.
A construction worker receives a deep cut to the thigh and experiences heavy bleeding. You apply pressure above the wound to slow the bleeding. What major vessel are you likely trying to compress?
The femoral artery runs through the thigh, and pressure at the groin pressure point compresses it to control leg bleeding. The brachial artery is in the upper arm.
How should safety professionals always endeavor to lead their company?
Exercising the authority granted to them by the company
Enforcing strict discipline and policy adherence
Leading by example builds credibility and models the safety behavior expected of everyone; authority and discipline alone produce compliance, not commitment or a strong safety culture.
In regards to the BCSP Code of Ethics, the word "integrity" is BEST understood by which definition?
Adherence to moral and ethical principles; soundness of moral character
The state of being whole, entire, or undiminished
The state, condition, or quality of being fair or free from bias or injustice
A sound, unimpaired, or perfect condition

In the BCSP Code of Ethics context, integrity means adherence to moral and ethical principles and honesty of character. The other choices are literal or physical meanings (wholeness, fairness, unimpaired condition).
How can safety professionals proactively contribute to community well-being?
By limiting their services to the workplace only.
By volunteering to speak at schools about safety practices.
By keeping their safety knowledge to themselves to ensure job security.
By avoiding involvement in community safety programs to prevent liability.

The BCSP Code of Ethics encourages professionals to serve the public and community; volunteering to teach safety at schools extends prevention beyond the workplace. The other options restrict or withhold service.
What is the primary purpose of the hierarchy of controls?
To increase productivity in the workplace
To implement safety measures based on their level of effectiveness
To determine the financial impact of safety measures

The hierarchy of controls (ANSI/ASSP Z10, NIOSH) ranks controls from most to least effective - elimination, substitution, engineering, administrative, PPE - so the most reliable feasible control is chosen first.
If a hazardous chemical cannot be eliminated or substituted, which control measure should be implemented next according to the hierarchy?
Provide workers with respirators and protective clothing
Develop safe work procedures and train employees
Install ventilation systems or enclose the process
Rotate workers to limit exposure times

After elimination and substitution, engineering controls such as local exhaust ventilation or enclosure come next because they remove the hazard at the source without relying on worker behavior. Procedures, rotation and PPE rank lower.
A worker is regularly exposed to a loud machine that exceeds 90 dB. What is the most effective hazard control according to the hierarchy?
Replace the machine with a quieter model
Add warning signs about noise levels
Schedule shorter shifts to reduce exposure time
Replacing the machine with a quieter model is substitution/elimination of the noise source, the highest-ranked option offered. Earplugs (PPE) and shorter shifts (administrative) are less effective.
Which components must be included in organizational programs designed to effectively manage an incident/injury involving a worker?
Medical case management and human resources oversight
Implementation of a return-to-work program and restricted duty protocol
Investigation, root cause analysis, and elimination of the causal factor
Fault tree analysis and accountability discipline

Effective incident management requires investigation, root cause analysis and correction of causal factors so the event does not recur. Case management, RTW and discipline are supporting elements, not the core prevention program.
What is the recommended course of action for removing debris, equipment, tools, and other related items following an accident?
Shall be preserved in place for 24 hours after the incident.
Will eliminate any hazards created by the accident.
Must be delayed until an accurate and comprehensive investigation has been performed.
Should be done immediately as other workers do not want to be reminded of the accident.

Except to rescue people or prevent further harm, the scene should be preserved until investigators have documented evidence; disturbing it destroys facts needed for root cause analysis. No fixed 24-hour rule applies.
What is the primary objective of all incident/injury investigations?
Engage management in every step of the investigation.
Understand the cause and learn how to prevent a recurrence.
Investigations exist to find causes and prevent recurrence, not to assign blame or build a legal defense. Focusing on fault discourages reporting and hides systemic causes.
A pipe weighing 500 pounds is lifted by two slings. The sling angle from the horizontal is 60 degrees. What is the tension on the right sling?
Each sling carries half the load divided by the sine of the horizontal angle: T = (500/2)/sin60 = 250/0.866 = about 288 lb. 250 lb ignores the angle effect.
What is the significance of the load capacity in rigging operations?
It determines the speed at which a load can be moved.
It specifies the maximum weight that lifting equipment can handle safely.
It indicates the number of personnel needed to operate the rigging equipment.
It measures the height to which a load can be lifted.
Rated load capacity (working load limit) is the maximum load the equipment can safely lift under specified conditions per ASME B30 and OSHA 1926.251; exceeding it risks failure.
During a lift, a rigger notices that the synthetic sling is slightly frayed but decides to proceed since the load is under the sling’s rated capacity. What is the best course of action?
Proceed with the lift since the sling is still within capacity
Tag the sling as "do not use" and replace it before lifting
Tape the frayed area and continue the lift
Notify the crane operator but proceed carefully
OSHA 1910.184 and ASME B30.9 require damaged slings (cuts, fraying) to be removed from service immediately; damage reduces strength unpredictably, so being under rated capacity does not make it safe.

The safety professional was inspecting the electrical that controlled all operating equipment in the plant. She noticed that the manually operated Emergency Power shutoff switch was blocked by a pallet of servers. Why is this a hazard?
Servers are required to be stored outside.
Emergency Power shut off for the electrical cannot be reached.
The switch was not painted red.
The power switch was not labeled.
OSHA 1910.303(g) requires clear working space and ready access to electrical disconnects; a blocked emergency shutoff cannot be reached to de-energize equipment quickly in an emergency.

You discover the electrical cord on a drill has been damaged and some of the cord’s
insulation is missing. You should?
wrap tape around the damaged spot to prevent electrical shocks.
check to see if the drill still works.
tag the drill out of service and notify the department responsible for equipment maintenance.
make sure that the cord does not come in contact with the floor.
OSHA 1910.334 requires damaged cord-and-plug equipment to be removed from service until repaired. Taping over missing insulation is not an acceptable repair and leaves a shock hazard.
Prevent deadly shock by quickly shutting off power to the circuit if the electricity flowing into the circuit differs by even a slight amount from that returning.
It is designed to allow current through the circuit, but in the event that the current exceeds some maximum value it will open, severing the circuit.
Offers an additional path for the electrical circuit to flow into the earth so as to not endanger anyone working with the electricity nearby in the event of a short circuit.
Are so named because they have the ability to measure a multiple of variables: voltage, current, and resistance.

A GFCI compares current in the hot and neutral conductors and trips (about 4-6 mA imbalance) within milliseconds, preventing fatal shock. Option B describes a fuse/breaker, C equipment grounding, D a multimeter.
During a routine inspection, you discover a hazardous chemical spill in the storage area of a manufacturing plant. What immediate action should you take to ensure safety and proper containment?
Evacuate the area and alert the emergency response team.
Identify the chemical using Safety Data Sheets (SDS) and assess the spill size.
Don appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE) and attempt to contain the spill.
Ventilate the area to disperse potential vapors and prevent inhalation hazards.
