Manager, because the (CO2) would both cool the grease and displace oxygen, thus extinguishing the fire.
Thomas, because there would not be enough (CO2) in a single fire extinguisher to completely extinguish the fire.
Neither, because a Class A extinguisher should always be used.

NFPA 10 requires Class K extinguishers for cooking-oil fires; CO2 can scatter burning grease and does not cool it enough to prevent reignition, so Thomas is right. Note: Option A overstates CO2 as 'explosive'; real issue is splatter and reflash.
While inspecting a small facility, you find several containers labeled 'corrosive waste' in the central accumulation area with no dates. What is your BEST course of action?
Notify the facility manager that the containers are noncompliant and must be marked with the accumulation start date
Remove the containers immediately without telling anyone
Have workers put on PPE and move the waste elsewhere
Call the fire department to dispose of the waste
Generators must mark containers 'Hazardous Waste', indicate the hazards, and record the accumulation start date to track time limits (40 CFR 262.16/262.17).
A worker is rinsing containers that once held hazardous waste and pouring the rinse water into a floor drain. What is the safety professional's best action?
Report it as a wastewater violation and initiate containment procedures.
Assume it's acceptable as long as the water is clear.
Install filters to catch the contaminants.
Rinsate from hazardous waste containers is itself regulated hazardous waste (RCRA) and must not be discharged to floor drains without authorization under the Clean Water Act; stop and contain it.

You are tasked with training employees on hazardous waste labeling. Which of the following is a required element on a hazardous waste container in a central accumulation area?
Ref:40 CFR §262.16(b)(6)(i)(C)
The name of the employee who generated it
A red dot sticker for visibility
The words “Hazardous Waste” and accumulation start date
A chemical formula of the contents

Under 40 CFR 262.17 (LQG central accumulation) and 262.16 (SQG), containers must be marked 'Hazardous Waste', indicate the hazards, and show the accumulation start date. Generator names and formulas are not required.

During an audit of a manufacturing facility, the auditor noted that the site’s safety management plan was missing a component related to worker participation. Which of the following is a required component that should be added to meet regulatory and best practice standards?
An automated software system for PPE inventory
A procedure to involve employees in hazard identification and control measures
A mandatory wellness program offering biometric screening
A digital attendance tracking system for safety meetings

ISO 45001 clause 5.4 and ANSI/ASSP Z10 require worker consultation and participation, including involvement in hazard identification and controls. Software, wellness and attendance tracking are not required elements.

A logistics company is implementing a new health and safety program. During review, a consultant advises that one of the following is essential for regulatory compliance and workforce engagement. What is the consultant MOST likely referring to?
A procedure for employees to report hazards without fear of retaliation
A monthly newsletter summarizing productivity statistics
A wearable device pilot program to track worker movements
An optional suggestion box for non-safety ideas
A non-retaliatory hazard reporting process is essential: OSHA Section 11(c) protects reporters, and OSHA's recommended practices rely on workers reporting concerns freely.

While reviewing a corporate safety policy, the regional director identifies a missing
component that could compromise legal defensibility and leadership accountability. Which of
the following should be included in the policy?
A written commitment from top management affirming the company's dedication to safety and health
A rotating schedule for team-building exercises among departments
A training calendar with optional safety workshops for interested employees
A suggestion to include safety data sheets in the employee handbook
A safety and health policy must include a written commitment from top management; it establishes leadership accountability and supports legal defensibility.
Which is true in regards to the Board of Certified Safety Professionals’ (BCSP) code of ethics?
It must be observed by holders of documents of certification conferred by BCSP.
It must be observed by only professionals working for a government agency in the field of safety.
It must be observed by holders of documents of certification conferred by ABSA.
It must be observed by all professionals holding a degree in the field of safety.
The BCSP Code of Ethics applies to holders of BCSP-conferred certifications (CSP, ASP, OHST, CHST, etc.) and candidates, not to all safety professionals or degree holders.
According to the BCSP Code of Ethics, what should be the top priority for a safety professional?
Maintaining the professional image and reputation of the safety expert
Improving the company's insurance safety score
Protecting people, the environment, and property from harm
Ensuring the company looks good to clients and the public
The BCSP Code of Ethics first requires holders to hold paramount the safety and health of people and protection of the environment and property. Image, scores and appearance are secondary.
During the design phase of a new manufacturing line, the engineer decides to automate a task that previously required workers to handle sharp tools. What type of control is being used?
Automating a hazardous manual task physically removes workers from the hazard through design, an engineering control (or near-elimination under Prevention through Design, ANSI/ASSP Z590.3).
A company identifies a chemical hazard. Until a safer alternative is found, it provides special training, updates work procedures and posts hazard signs. Which control levels are being applied?
Training and procedures are administrative controls; signs are warnings. None change the hazard itself.

A manufacturing plant has identified excessive noise levels in a specific work area, potentially causing hearing damage to employees. Following the hierarchy of controls, what should be the best step taken to address this hazard?
Implement a mandatory hearing conservation program with annual audiometric testing.
Engineer out the noise source by modifying or replacing the noisy equipment.
Rotate employees in and out of the area to limit exposure time.

Engineering the noise out at the source by modifying or replacing equipment is the highest-ranked feasible control offered; earplugs (PPE), hearing conservation and rotation (administrative) rank lower.

A sling is lifting 1000 pounds.
The sling angle is 45 degrees from the horizontal.
The approximate stress on each leg is?
Leg tension = (load / number of legs) / sin(angle) = (1000/2) / sin45 = 500 / 0.707 = about 707 lb per leg.
Which of the following is NOT a type of rigging equipment?
Shackles, slings and wire ropes are rigging hardware used to attach and lift loads (OSHA 1926.251, ASME B30). Scaffolding is an elevated work platform, not rigging.

During maintenance on an electrical panel in a manufacturing plant, a safety professional reminds the supervisor that employees must not work on live circuits unless certain conditions are met. According to OSHA 1910.333, what must be done to the circuits before employees work on or near them—unless the employer can prove that doing so would create a greater hazard or is infeasible?

OSHA 1910.333(a)(1) requires live parts to be de-energized before employees work on or near them unless de-energizing creates greater hazards or is infeasible; LOTO is the method used to keep them de-energized.

An electrician is assigned to troubleshoot a live control panel because shutting it down would halt critical hospital equipment. To reduce the risk of injury, what type of personal protective equipment should the worker use to protect their hands while testing live circuits?
Latex gloves to prevent moisture exposure

Energized work requires rubber insulating gloves rated for the voltage (ASTM D120, OSHA 1910.137) with leather protectors, per NFPA 70E. Leather, cut-resistant and latex gloves offer no rated insulation.

A maintenance worker uses a voltage detector to check whether an extension cord is energized before plugging in a grinder. The detector lights up near the cord but hasn't made contact with any exposed wire. What does this indicate?
The detector is sensing the electrostatic field of an energized extension cord
The detector is malfunctioning due to RF interference
The cord must be defective and leaking current
The detector cannot sense voltage unless the cord is cut open

Non-contact voltage detectors sense the electric field around an energized conductor through insulation, so a light without contact indicates the cord is live. Verify with a contact tester before relying on it.
What is the safety professional’s primary role in an incident investigation?
Advisor, ensuring the investigation follows best practices and regulatory requirements
Solely responsible for leading and completing the entire investigation
Assigning blame to the individuals involved in the incident
Documenting disciplinary actions taken against employees

The safety professional typically serves as an advisor or facilitator, ensuring sound methodology, root cause analysis and regulatory compliance, while line management owns the investigation and corrective actions. Blame and discipline are not the goal.

During an incident investigation, the safety manager interviews an employee who witnessed a near miss. The employee says, “I didn’t report it because nobody got hurt.” What should the safety manager emphasize in response?
Reporting is only necessary if there is property damage or injury.
Near misses are important to report because they help prevent future incidents.
The employee should be disciplined for failing to report.
It's better not to document minor events to avoid liability.
Near misses share the same causes as injury incidents (Heinrich/Bird triangle); reporting them allows causes to be corrected before someone is hurt. Discipline discourages reporting.
After a worker falls from a ladder, the investigation reveals the ladder had worn, uneven steps. What type of cause does this represent?
Worn, uneven ladder steps are the unsafe condition that directly produced the fall (direct/immediate cause). The root cause would be why the ladder was not inspected or removed from service.
What is the firststep in the Job Hazard Analysis (JHA) process?
Select the job or task to be analyzed
OSHA 3071 JHA begins by selecting (prioritizing) the job to analyze, then breaking it into steps, identifying hazards and developing controls.
Which of the following hazard analysis techniques uses an inductive approach, starting with specific failures to determine their potential impacts on system safety?
FMEA is inductive (bottom-up): it starts with individual component failure modes and determines their effects on the system. FTA is the deductive opposite.
A chemical processing plant stores large quantities of flammable liquids under pressure. Which of the following best describes the primary objective of a Process Hazard Analysis (PHA)?
To identify, evaluate, and control hazards associated with highly hazardous processes
To document safety performance indicators for quarterly OSHA reporting
To determine the financial impact of loss-of-containment scenarios
To verify the competency of emergency response contractors
A PHA under PSM (1910.119(e)) systematically identifies, evaluates and controls hazards of highly hazardous chemical processes.
A facility with anhydrous ammonia systems lacks up-to-date piping diagrams. Which PSM element is being violated?

OSHA 1910.119(d) Process Safety Information requires up-to-date technology and equipment information, including piping and instrument diagrams (P&IDs). Mechanical integrity covers inspection and testing.
After a near-miss explosion due to a blocked relief valve, an investigation is conducted. What is the Key aspect the facility must do as a result of effective PSM program?
Hold a job brief discussing the incident.
Conduct a safety stand down for 48 hours.
Request OSHA to conduct the investigation
Develop and promptly implement corrective actions
OSHA 1910.119(m) requires incident investigation findings to be addressed and resolved promptly, with corrective actions documented. Briefings and stand-downs do not fix the cause.
During a monthly safety review, a supervisor presents data showing a drop in near-miss reports compared to the previous quarter. What type of indicator is this, and how should it be interpreted?
Leading indicator; it shows workers are becoming less engaged in hazard reporting
Lagging indicator; it confirms fewer injuries occurred
Leading indicator; it may reflect underreporting or lack of hazard awareness
Lagging indicator; it demonstrates completed corrective actions
Near-miss reporting is a leading indicator; a drop may mean underreporting or lower hazard awareness rather than a safer workplace, so investigate before celebrating.

A manufacturing plant implements a new safety initiative requiring supervisors to conduct and document weekly safety observations on employee behaviors around pinch point hazards. After three months, the plant sees a reduction in hand injuries.
Which of the following best describes the weekly safety observations?
A leading indicator, because it measures proactive actions taken to prevent injuries
A lagging indicator, because it tracks injury outcomes
A lagging indicator, because the observations occur after the work is done
Not an indicator, since they are informal and voluntary
Weekly observations are proactive activities that measure prevention efforts before injury, so they are leading indicators. The injury reduction they produced is the lagging outcome.

A company safety manager prepares the quarterly report and notes there were 3 recordable injuries, 1 lost-time incident, and 2 near misses. The report is used to evaluate whether the company met its annual safety performance goals.
Which type of safety indicator is this report primarily based on?
Leading indicators, because it uses behavioral data
Lagging indicators, because it reflects past incident data
Predictive indicators, because it forecasts injury potential
Compliance indicators, because it’s based on OSHA inspections

Recordables and lost-time cases are outcome measures of past events, making the report primarily lagging. Near misses are sometimes treated as leading, but the report evaluates results already achieved.
Which is a requirement of retrieval systems for confined space rescue in a 8 feet deep manhole? 1910.146(k)(3)(i)
Each authorized entrant shall use a chest or full body harness
Wristlets must be used to pull the entrant out.
The entrant must have a body belt to facilitate rescue.
The entrant must use a quick release lifeline.

OSHA 1910.146(k)(3)(i) requires each authorized entrant to use a chest or full body harness with the retrieval line attached at the center of the back or above the head; wristlets only when a harness is infeasible. At 5 ft+ depth a mechanical device is required.
Which of the following is a critical component of an emergency preparedness plan?
Implementation of employee engagement initiatives to promote morale during crises
Strategic allocation of financial resources for long-term business continuity
Post-incident customer communication protocols to preserve brand reputation

Hazard identification and risk assessment is the foundation of emergency preparedness (NFPA 1600, ISO 22301), determining which emergencies the plan must address. The other options are secondary considerations.
Which of the following best describes the role of business continuity planning in occupational safety and health?
Developing marketing strategies for emergency product launches
Managing payroll operations during financial audits and inspections
Increasing sales volume during seasonal business cycles
Ensuring worker safety systems are integrated into recovery plans following a disruption
Business continuity planning (NFPA 1600, ISO 22301) restores critical operations after a disruption; from an OSH view, it must integrate worker safety systems so recovery work is done safely.

A construction site records a noise level of 98 dB at 3 feet from a jackhammer. The safety officer wants to estimate the noise level at 12 feet using the inverse square law.
Question: What will be the approximate noise level at 12 feet?
Drop = 20 log(d2/d1) = 20 log(12/3) = 20 x 0.602 = 12 dB; 98 - 12 = 86 dB. Each doubling of distance (3 to 6 to 12 ft) loses 6 dB.

A worker is using a 6-foot lanyard attached to a harness. The anchor point is located 3 feet above the D-ring on their back. To calculate the total free fall distance, what formula should the competent person apply?
I corrected the answers. Thanks for the catch.
Free Fall = Lanyard − Distance from D-ring to Anchor
Free Fall = Lanyard + Distance from D-ring to Anchor
Free fall = lanyard length - anchor height above D-ring: 6 ft - 3 ft = 3 ft. An anchor above the D-ring reduces free fall; one below the D-ring would add to it.

Before entering a confined space, a gas detector measures the oxygen level at 18%. OSHA’s minimum safe oxygen level for confined space entry is 19.5%.
Question: What action should the safety officer take?
Proceed with entry since 18% is close to the limit.
Enter with a self-contained breathing apparatus (SCBA) without ventilation.
Assess the atmosphere to determine what is in there that is displacing the oxygen.

18% O2 is oxygen deficient (OSHA 1910.146 minimum 19.5%); determine what is displacing oxygen, since the displacing gas may be toxic or flammable and ventilation alone may not be adequate. Note: Ventilation (B) is also defensible; key emphasizes identifying the displacing agent first.

During a BBS observation, a safety professional notices a worker climbing onto a pallet to reach a part on a shelf, even though a step ladder is available nearby. What is the most effective BBS-based response?
Write up the employee for violating safety rules
Publicly correct the employee to discourage others
Wait and document the behavior later to avoid confrontation
Engage the employee in a positive discussion to understand why and suggest safer alternatives

Behavior-based safety relies on positive, non-punitive conversation to understand why the at-risk behavior occurred (barriers, convenience) and coach the safe alternative. Public correction or discipline undermines trust.
A safety team notices that workers consistently bypass a machine guard to clear jams, even after reminders. Which BBS-based strategy should be prioritized to improve safe behavior?
Increase the number of disciplinary actions for non-compliance
Replace supervisors who fail to enforce the rule
Investigate workflow and equipment design to remove barriers to safe behavior
Post more signs and distribute reminder emails weekly
Repeated guard bypassing despite reminders points to a system barrier (jam frequency, design, workflow). Remove the reason for the at-risk behavior; discipline and signs do not address the cause.
Which of the following conditions would require the use of a P100 filtering facepiece? An employee:
Is temporarily working in an area containing organic vapors. The employee only requires a single-use respirator
Performs daily work in an area containing oil particles with a diameter less than 0.3 micrometers. The employee requires a respirator that can be reused for more than one work shift
Requires immediate access to a respirator in an emergency situation that causes an oxygen-deficient atmosphere
Works in an area containing both organic vapors and liquid aerosol particles, as well as eye irritants. The employee requires a respirator that can be reused for more than one work shift

NIOSH 42 CFR 84: P-series filters are oil-proof with 99.97% efficiency (P100) and may be used beyond one shift, suiting reusable protection against oil aerosols. Organic vapors need cartridges and O2 deficiency needs SCBA/SAR.

Which of the following respirators is most appropriate when an air-purifying respirator (APR) does not provide sufficient protection for the anticipated level of contaminants and the employee will be working in the area for two-four hours?
Closed circuit self-contained breathing apparatus (SCBA) with full face mask
Full facepiece respirator equipped with a cartridge designed for multiple contaminants
Half mask respirator equipped with an R99 filter and organic vapor cartridge
Type C supplied air respirator (SAR) connected to a source of respirable breathing air
When APRs are insufficient but the atmosphere is not IDLH, a Type C supplied-air respirator provides an APF of up to 1000 and unlimited air for multi-hour work. SCBA has limited air duration.

An employee will be working in area that has an oxygen-deficient atmosphere. The work that the employee must complete will cause eye irritation. The employee will only need to be in the work area for a maximum of 60 minutes. Under these circumstances, the employee should use a:
Full-facepiece combination respirator with an integrated filter and cartridge
Powered-air purifying respirator (PAPR) with an integrated hood
Type C supplied-air respirator (SAR) combined with an air purifying respirator (APR)

Oxygen-deficient atmospheres require atmosphere-supplying respirators; a full-facepiece SCBA supplies air and protects the eyes from irritants (OSHA 1910.134(d)(2)). Air-purifying respirators and PAPRs cannot supply oxygen.
What is the primary purpose of implementing a lockout/tagout procedure?
To prevent the unintentional energization or start-up of machinery during maintenance or repair activities
To improve overall machine efficiency and operational longevity
To verify the identity and credentials of authorized personnel on-site
To ensure the security of the facility after working hours by controlling access
OSHA 1910.147 lockout/tagout prevents unexpected energization, start-up or release of stored energy that could injure employees during servicing and maintenance.
What best describes a lockout device?
A device used solely to secure keys and prevent unauthorized access to locks
A mechanical or electronic device that secures an energy-isolating device in a safe position through positive means, such as a lock or tag
A system designed to monitor and record the activity of maintenance personnel during equipment servicing
A device that automates the process of energizing or de-energizing machinery to prevent manual errors

OSHA 1910.147(b) defines a lockout device as one using positive means, such as a key or combination lock, to hold an energy-isolating device in the safe position and prevent energizing. Note: Option includes 'tag'; a tag is a tagout device, not a lockout device.
Who is authorized to perform a lockout/tagout procedure?
Any employee who has received basic safety training
Only personnel who are specifically trained, authorized, and capable of understanding the lockout/tagout process
Employees with access to the lockout/tagout keys, regardless of training
Supervisors or managers, but only during designated maintenance windows
OSHA 1910.147(b) defines an authorized employee as one who locks or tags out machines to perform servicing, and (c)(7) requires them to be trained in hazardous energy recognition and control methods.
When conducting personal air sampling to assess worker exposure to a dust hazard, which of the following actions best ensures the data is representative?
Place the sampler near the doorway of the room
Sample during the lowest activity periods
Attach the sampler within the worker’s breathing zone
Collect samples for only 5 minutes and extrapolate
Personal exposure samples must be collected in the breathing zone (within about a 10 in. radius of the nose and mouth) during representative activity, per NIOSH/OSHA sampling methods.
Which situation would MOST likely trigger the need for immediate exposure assessment and real-time monitoring?
A shipment of updated personal protective equipment arrives, pending routine inspection by warehouse staff.
A sudden release of an unidentified vapor occurs during maintenance in a sealed mechanical room with limited ventilation.
Administrative personnel begin an ergonomic workspace adjustment involving non-hazardous materials.
The EHS team conducts a regularly scheduled briefing on safety protocols and incident trends.
An unidentified vapor release in a sealed, poorly ventilated room creates an unknown and possibly IDLH atmosphere requiring immediate assessment and direct-reading monitoring before anyone enters.
Raynaud’s phenomenon is a problem which causes (corrected the 2024 question)
Decreased blood flow to the fingers
Raynaud's phenomenon is vasospasm that reduces blood flow to the fingers, causing blanching and numbness; hand-arm vibration and cold are occupational triggers.

You are a safety manager at a manufacturing facility. During a routine walkthrough, you observe a forklift operator behaving erratically—his speech is slurred, he’s sweating heavily despite cool temperatures, and he nearly collides with a storage rack. When approached, he becomes defensive and claims he's just tired. You recall that he returned from lunch 30 minutes ago.
What is the MOST appropriate course of action?
Immediately remove the operator from duty and initiate a reasonable suspicion drug and alcohol test per company policy
Ignore the behavior for now, but continue observing him throughout the day for more conclusive signs
Send the operator home for the day and remind him to rest before returning to work tomorrow
Document the behavior in your personal notes, but take no immediate action to avoid potential conflict

Slurred speech, sweating and a near collision while operating a forklift are observable signs of impairment; remove him from safety-sensitive duty immediately and follow the reasonable suspicion testing policy. Sending him home unescorted or waiting is unsafe.
What is the main objective of the Globally Harmonized System (GHS)?
Providing a standardized set of criteria for end users of chemicals or hazardous materials.
Establishing a classification system for health, physical, and environmental hazards, safety data sheets, and labels.
Ensuring appropriate packaging, handling, transportation, and use of hazardous chemicals.
Guiding procedures for hazardous spill cleanup, medical protocols, and remediation of accidental discharges.
GHS establishes harmonized criteria to classify health, physical and environmental hazards and communicate them through standardized labels and SDSs; OSHA adopted it in the 2012 HCS.

In a facility, workers are tasked with extracting gypsum wallboard and structural framing from a basement office. What key safety topics should the onsite safety expert emphasize during training for these workers?
Understanding confined spaces, methods of evacuation, and risks of asphyxiation.
Procedures for detecting low-oxygen environments and ensuring proper air circulation.
Identifying risks associated with dust, mold and allergens, monitoring techniques, and protective measures.

Removing gypsum board and framing from a basement generates dust, and damp basements often hide mold and allergens; training should cover these hazards, monitoring and respiratory/protective controls.

Several employees working on an assembly line report experiencing hand numbness after
completing their 8-hour shifts. Their primary task involves manually installing nuts and bolts.
As the company's safety manager, what should be your first step in addressing this issue?
Implement job rotation to alternate physical demands among workers.
Observe the assembly process to identify possible causes of the numbness.
Refer affected employees for medical evaluations to determine the source of symptoms.
Redesign the work area to reduce repetitive motion tasks.

The first step is to observe the task and gather data to identify the actual ergonomic risk factors (force, repetition, posture, vibration) before choosing controls; medical referral addresses symptoms, not cause.
While conducting interviews, a coworker hesitates and seems nervous about sharing what they saw. What is the MOST appropriate action?
Reassure the worker that the goal is to improve safety, not assign blame
End the interview and submit a report without their input
Tell the worker that non-cooperation may be noted
Ask their supervisor to sit in during the interview
Witnesses share information more freely when assured the investigation's purpose is prevention, not blame. Threats or a supervisor sitting in increase fear and reduce candor.
An investigation team determines that an overhead hoist failed due to a worn brake. Maintenance records show it hadn’t been inspected in over a year. What type of cause is this?

The worn brake is the direct cause; the lapsed inspection program is a systemic, management-system contributing cause that allowed the condition to go undetected. Note: Many models would also call the inspection lapse a root cause.
After concluding an incident investigation, what is the MOST effective way to prevent recurrence?
Implement corrective actions and track them for completion
Send a warning email to all employees about the incident
Conduct refresher training only for those involved
Ask supervisors to monitor employees more closely

Prevention depends on implementing corrective actions that address root causes and tracking them to verified completion. Warning emails, narrow retraining and more monitoring do not fix system causes.
The two types of high-energy electromagnetic radiation are?
X-rays and gamma rays are high-energy (ionizing) electromagnetic radiation. Alpha and beta are particulate radiation, and infrared is non-ionizing.
What should be done immediately if a radiation spill of liquid occurs?
Evacuate the area and notify the designated radiation safety officer.
Clean up the spill with regular cleaning equipment.
Continue working but avoid the contaminated area.
Seal the area with tape and continue working around it.
For a radioactive liquid spill, stop work, warn others, evacuate/isolate the area and notify the Radiation Safety Officer (NRC licensee procedures). Untrained cleanup spreads contamination.
Which of the following is NOT a source of ionizing radiation?
Radio waves are low-energy non-ionizing electromagnetic radiation. X-rays, gamma rays and alpha particles have enough energy to ionize atoms.

Waste from a common industrial practice or manufacturing process would be listed on which of the following choices?
Answer Choices:
KEY CORRECTED by trainer review: F-list = wastes from non-specific sources (common industrial processes, e.g., spent solvents). K-list = specific industries.
You must enter a permit required confined space pit with stairs to repair a leaking water pipe. What is required for safety?
Life vest, Safety harness, atmospheric testing.
Atmospheric testing, rescue planning, entry permit, and an attendant.
Waterproof radios, attendant, lockout, air line respirator

OSHA 1910.146 permit-required entry requires an entry permit, atmospheric testing, an attendant and a rescue plan. SCBA, life vests and air lines are selected only if the hazard evaluation calls for them.
An attendant outside a permit-required confined space sees that the entrant has stopped moving and is not responding. What should the attendant do FIRST?
Summon rescue and emergency services and begin non-entry retrieval if equipped
Enter the space to help the entrant
Leave to find a supervisor with rescue equipment
Attendants must not enter (1910.146(i)). They call rescue, attempt non-entry retrieval and stay at their post. Untrained would-be rescuers account for many confined space deaths.
During a confined space entry, the ventilation system fails. The atmosphere is still within safe limits, but the task involves welding. What is the best course of action?
Continue working quickly before levels change
Pause work and manually ventilate with fans
Stop all hot work and exit until ventilation is restored
Ask the gas monitor reader to stay closer

Welding generates fumes and gases that quickly accumulate in a confined space; with ventilation lost, stop hot work and exit until ventilation is restored (OSHA 1910.252(c)(4), 1910.146). Current readings do not reflect upcoming fume buildup.
The GHS classification system categorizes chemicals based on their:
Hazards to human health and environment
GHS classifies chemicals by their physical, health and environmental hazards, not origin or composition alone.
An SDS for a parts-cleaning solvent lists: 'Keep away from heat/sparks/open flame. Use explosion-proof equipment.' In which SDS section are these precautionary statements found?
Precautionary statements are label elements and are listed in Section 2 along with signal word, hazard statements and pictograms. Section 7 gives detailed handling practices.

During a post-incident review, it’s discovered that an employee developed dizziness and headaches after prolonged exposure to cleaning agents stored in unsealed secondary containers. Which GHS element would have best mitigated the risk by providing immediate hazard awareness and protective guidance at the point of use?
The SDS Section 8 outlining permissible exposure limits and PPE requirements
A supplier label including hazard pictograms and precautionary statements
A chemical inventory log showing the last inspection date and stock rotation
The product's CAS number and molecular formula as listed on the SDS

Labels provide point-of-use hazard information - pictograms, signal word, hazard and precautionary statements (OSHA 1910.1200(f)); secondary containers must also be labeled. SDS Section 8 is not at the workstation.

After implementing a new patient intake process, a surgical clinic recorded the number of hours each of the next 7 patients waited from registration to receiving pre-op lab results:
6, 8, 7, 5, 9, 10, 5
What was the mean wait time for these patients?
Mean = (6 + 8 + 7 + 5 + 9 + 10 + 5) / 7 = 50 / 7 = 7.14, about 7.1 hours. 7 hours is the median.
A safety analyst finds a strong positive correlation between overtime hours and incident rates. What does this likely indicate?
More overtime may be contributing to higher incidents
A strong positive correlation means incidents rise as overtime rises, suggesting overtime may contribute (e.g., fatigue), but correlation alone does not prove causation.

A pre-surgery clinic is analyzing patient wait times for lab test results. Five patients undergoing scheduled operations received their blood test results in the following number of hours after sample collection:
8, 10, 12, 9, 11
What is the mean (average) wait time for the blood test results?
Which option among the following represents an administrative control?
Imposing a ban on unauthorized weapons within a facility
Utilizing bright lighting to enhance visibility in high-risk areas
Offering height markers on exit doors
Supplying locked drop safes to reduce the amount of accessible cash
A ban on weapons is a policy or rule governing behavior, an administrative control. Lighting, height markers and drop safes are physical/engineering measures (CPTED).
Before starting crane operations at a job site, which document should be completed and reviewed with the crane crew to identify and control potential hazards?
A Job Hazard Analysis reviewed with the crew identifies task-specific hazards and controls before crane work begins. Site prep plans, ERPs and power-line procedures address specific aspects only.

What procedure is required when operating a personnel platform with a hydraulic crane?
Ref: 1926.1431
Conduct a trial lift with a test weight of 125% of the platform capacity before placing personnel on the platform.
Ensure personnel are secured to a point above the headache ball.
Perform a trial lift by raising the workers a few inches to check that the platform is secured and properly balanced.
Have a qualified engineer visually inspect the rigging before placing personnel on the platform.

Before hoisting personnel, OSHA 1926.1431 requires the platform and rigging to be proof tested to 125% of the platform's rated capacity, plus a trial lift of the unoccupied platform. Workers are never used for the trial lift. Note: Option conflates proof test (125%) with trial lift (anticipated load).
During a risk assessment for a new warehouse conveyor, the team determines that a mechanical failure could cause packages to fall and strike workers. Which step does this represent?
Recognizing what could go wrong and who could be hurt is identification; no likelihood or ranking has been done yet.
A safety professional uses a risk matrix that considers both the probability of an event and the severity of its consequences. What is this method primarily used for?
A risk matrix combines likelihood and severity to rank risks so the highest are addressed first (ANSI/ASSP Z690, ISO 31010). It does not inventory hazards or establish compliance.
A facility safety engineer uses a Fault Tree Analysis to trace the potential root causes of a possible ammonia gas leak. Which best describes this method?
Fault Tree Analysis starts with an undesired top event and works downward through AND/OR gates to identify causes - a deductive, top-down method. FMEA is bottom-up.
What is the speed of a rocket that travels 8,000 m in 13 seconds?
Speed = distance / time = 8,000 m / 13 s = 615 m/s.
A 10-lb wrench slips from a platform 20 ft above a worker who is wearing a hard hat. Which physical principle BEST explains why the wrench still poses a serious injury risk?
Gravitational potential energy converting to kinetic energy
The 10-lb wrench's potential energy (mgh) at 20 ft becomes kinetic energy as it falls and can exceed what a hard hat is designed to absorb. Prevent drops with tool tethers, toe boards and barricades.
A 10-kg toolbox falls from a scaffold platform 2 m high. Ignoring air resistance, what is its approximate velocity just before it hits the ground? (v = sqrt(2gh), g = 9.8 m/s2)
v = sqrt(2gh) = sqrt(2 x 9.8 x 2) = sqrt(39.2) = 6.3 m/s. Mass does not affect free-fall velocity (it does affect impact energy).
A contractor will weld near a combustible wood-framed wall. According to NFPA 51B, what is the BEST course of action before starting hot work?
Cover the wall with a plastic tarp to prevent damage
Keep a fire extinguisher nearby and start welding immediately
Move combustibles at least 35 feet away or protect them with approved fire-resistant shields or blankets
Post a 'Caution: Hot Work in Progress' sign and proceed
NFPA 51B and OSHA 1910.252 require removal of combustibles within 35 ft or protection with fire-resistant guards, plus a permit and fire watch. Plastic tarps are combustible.
A maintenance worker needs to use a torch on piping in a designated hot work area. What is not required if the area is already approved?
A new hot work permit must be issued
Fire extinguishing equipment must be present
The area must be inspected and maintained fire-safe
The worker must be trained in hot work hazards

NFPA 51B and OSHA 1910.252(a)(2)(iv) allow designated (permanent) hot work areas that are already approved, so a new permit is not required each time; fire protection, maintained conditions and training still apply.

A maintenance manager uses a risk matrix to evaluate the installation of a new conveyor belt. The hazard is "caught-in machinery," and the probability is "likely" with "major" consequences. According to most standard risk matrices, what is the correct classification of this risk?
Likely probability combined with major consequences falls in the high-risk zone of standard 5x5 risk matrices, requiring priority control before operation.
A company decides to implement machine guarding and two-hand controls after identifying a serious pinch point hazard. This is an example of:
Guarding and two-hand controls reduce the likelihood or severity of harm, which is risk mitigation (reduction). Avoidance would eliminate the activity; transfer and sharing shift losses.
An employee refuses to use a scissor lift because they "just feel it's unsafe," even though inspections and certifications are current. This reflects:
Refusal based on a feeling despite current inspections reflects individual risk perception, which is subjective and influenced by familiarity, control and dread rather than objective data.

While preparing for a multi-story restoration project, a construction foreman reviews the training logs of new employees assigned to work on suspended scaffolds. He notices that one employee was not trained on the weight limitations of the scaffolding system being used.
What specific scaffold safety training requirement is missing, according to 29 CFR 1926.454(a)(4)?
Training on maximum intended load and load-carrying capacities of the scaffold
Training on personal fall arrest systems only
Training on how to operate forklifts near scaffolds
Training on the manufacturer’s warranty of scaffold components

29 CFR 1926.454(a)(4) requires scaffold users to be trained on the maximum intended load and load-carrying capacities of the scaffold; fall arrest is a separate element and forklifts or warranties are not training requirements.

During a routine inspection of a suspended scaffold system, a safety manager notices that a wire rope used for hoisting shows signs of damage. Upon closer inspection, he identifies six broken wires randomly scattered in one lay of the rope.
Based on OSHA 1926.451(d), what should the safety manager do?
Use the rope only for material hoisting, not for workers
Continue using the rope, but mark it for future replacement
Wrap the damaged section in tape and allow continued use
Remove the wire rope from service immediately

OSHA 1926.451(d)(10) requires removal of suspension wire rope with six randomly distributed broken wires in one lay (or three in one strand). Damaged rope cannot be downgraded to material hoisting or taped and reused.

During a site walk, you observe a crew preparing to erect steel columns near an existing overhead power line. The line appears to be energized and is approximately 12 feet away from the intended work area. What should be your first action as the safety professional?
Allow work to continue since the distance exceeds 10 feet and seems safe
Require the crew to wear rubber gloves and proceed with caution
Pause the activity and coordinate with the site engineer and erection crew to assess voltage and determine the minimum safe clearance
Contact the utility company after the lift is complete to report the proximity

Clearance depends on voltage: OSHA 1926 Subpart CC requires at least 20 ft for lines up to 350 kV unless voltage is confirmed, so 12 ft may be unsafe. Stop work and determine voltage and minimum approach distance before proceeding.

You are working in a lab transferring hydrochloric acid from one container to another. The safety data sheet (SDS) specifies that the acid is corrosive and can burn skin on contact. What type of glove provides the most appropriate protection in this situation?

Neoprene and butyl rubber offer good resistance to concentrated mineral acids such as HCl. Thin disposable nitrile is for incidental splash only, and cotton or leather absorb corrosives and give no chemical protection.

A healthcare worker is drawing blood from a patient and preparing samples for testing. To protect against potential exposure to bloodborne pathogens like hepatitis B or HIV, which glove type should be worn?

OSHA 1910.1030 requires gloves impermeable to blood and OPIM; latex or nitrile exam gloves provide a fluid barrier while preserving dexterity. Cotton and leather are permeable, and butyl is unnecessary for blood.
During a walkthrough you observe employees grinding metal parts with sparks and loud noise. What is the FIRST step in conducting a proper PPE hazard assessment?
Assess and document the specific hazards of the task
Select PPE based on what nearby workers wear
Review injury records and order ANSI-rated PPE
Distribute earplugs and face shields to all workers
OSHA 1910.132(d) requires assessing the hazards first and certifying the assessment in writing; selection follows.
A task with medium likelihood and major severity is rated High Risk on the company's 4x4 risk matrix. What should be the next step?
Eliminate the hazard or substitute the task
Accept the risk and monitor the activity
Proceed with caution and add signage
Document the risk and assign it to a supervisor
A High rating means the risk is not tolerable; treatment should start at the top of the hierarchy of controls, not with signage or acceptance.
A machine produces significant noise and exposes workers to potential hearing loss. Which control option best aligns with risk reduction principles in the hierarchy of controls?
Require workers to double up on hearing protection
Install acoustic shielding around the equipment
Provide training on safe noise exposure levels

Acoustic shielding/enclosure is an engineering control that reduces noise at the source or path, ranking above administrative controls (training, audiometry) and PPE (double hearing protection) in the hierarchy of controls.

You conduct a hazard review and identify a medium-level ergonomic risk in the shipping department. Workers are skeptical about the issue because there haven’t been any recent injuries. What’s the most effective risk communication method in this situation?
Post statistics about national ergonomic injuries on a bulletin board
Wait until an injury occurs before addressing the risk
Tell them not to worry as the risk is only "medium"
Share a real case study of a similar injury from another site

Risk communication is most persuasive when it is concrete and relevant; a real case from a similar operation makes the hazard credible. Generic national statistics are abstract, and waiting or dismissing the risk is unacceptable.
A warehouse has 150,000 ft2 total area, of which 30,000 ft2 is not usable (offices, equipment, aisles). If the maximum allowable stack height is 30 ft, what is the usable storage volume?

Usable area = 150,000 - 30,000 = 120,000 ft2; x 30 ft = 3,600,000 ft3. Using the gross area gives 4,500,000 ft3, which is the trap. Actual loading must still be checked against floor-load ratings and sprinkler clearance.

A facility stores 55-gallon drums of flammable liquid in a designated flammable liquid storage room. The room is equipped with fire-rated walls and mechanical ventilation. During a safety audit, it is discovered that the room holds 90 drums. What should be the primary concern for the safety professional?
The number of drums exceeds the allowable maximum per NFPA and OSHA standards for a single storage room
The fire-rated walls are only required if more than 100 drums are stored
The presence of ventilation means there is no storage capacity limit
As long as the drums are labeled correctly, the quantity stored is not regulated

NFPA 30 and OSHA 1910.106 cap the quantity of flammable liquid allowed in an inside storage room (gallons per square foot by fire rating and protection), so an excessive inventory is the primary concern. Ventilation or labels do not remove limits. Note: Limits are expressed in gal/sq ft, not a fixed drum count; key defensible.

A warehouse manager decides to store additional corrosive chemicals in a metal cabinet already used for acids. The cabinet is not vented and is nearing full capacity. As the safety professional, what is your best course of action?
Approve the storage since the cabinet is labeled for corrosives
Advise installing ventilation to the cabinet to increase capacity
Require a review of chemical compatibility and storage limits before approving
Recommend storing remaining containers on top of the cabinet temporarily

Before adding chemicals to any cabinet, verify compatibility (e.g., oxidizing vs. organic acids, acids vs. bases) and capacity limits. A corrosives label does not ensure compatibility, and storing on top of the cabinet violates storage practice.

Following ISO 19011 guidelines. During the preparation the week before, you notice that the client has not clearly defined the audit objectives, scope, and criteria, and the audit team is unsure about which standard requirements apply to the facility being audited.
According to ISO 19011, what should you do next?
Contact the auditee immediately to obtain and confirm the missing information before finalizing the audit plan.
Proceed with drafting the audit schedule using assumptions based on past audits and update it during the opening meeting.
Wait until the on-site audit begins, then clarify scope and objectives during the opening meeting with the client.
Cancel the audit and submit a report stating that the organization is not audit-ready per ISO 19011 clause 6.3.2.
ISO 19011 requires audit objectives, scope and criteria to be determined before the audit plan is finalized; contact the auditee/client to confirm them. Assuming or waiting compromises the audit.
After identifying a hazard, what is the subsequent step in developing a strategy for reducing or eliminating the risk?
Providing training to workers affected by the hazard.
Determining the severity of the hazard.

In the risk management process, after hazard identification the risk is defined/characterized (consequence, exposure, likelihood) before assessing severity and selecting controls; training and fault trees come later as possible tools.

A safety coordinator at a packaging facility observes that forklifts frequently reverse near a pedestrian walkway. No accidents have occurred yet, but there are frequent close calls.
According to standard risk management steps, what should the coordinator do immediately after identifying this hazard?
Install physical barriers between the forklift path and pedestrian zone
Define the risk by detailing the potential consequences and exposure scenario
Report the hazard to upper management and close the case
Begin training workers on forklift safety without further analysis

The step after hazard identification is to define the risk: describe who is exposed, how, and the potential consequences. Barriers and training are controls chosen after the risk is analyzed; closing the case is never appropriate.

During a risk assessment at a metal fabrication shop, the team identifies flying sparks from grinders as a hazard. After defining and analyzing the risk, the team determines that the risk is unacceptable due to the frequency and potential for eye injuries.
What is the next appropriate stepin the risk management process?
Develop and implement control measures using the hierarchy of controls
Accept the risk as part of the work environment
Skip directly to a final review since the risk was already defined
File an OSHA report and move on to other tasks Jensens Risk management steps is in next post if you need to review.

Once a risk is judged unacceptable, the next step is to select and implement controls using the hierarchy (e.g., guards, shields, then PPE), followed by monitoring. Accepting the risk contradicts the evaluation.
A worker is exposed to a chemical mixture with known OSHA PELs. The combined exposure is calculated using the additive formula. When is the exposure acceptable?
If each chemical is below its individual PEL
If the sum of the ratios is less than or equal to 1
For additive mixtures (OSHA 1910.1000(d)(2)), Em = C1/L1 + C2/L2 + ... must not exceed 1. Each component can be below its own PEL while the sum still exceeds 1.
A chemical has a TLV of 1% but the detector reads 10%. How many ppm is this?
A warehouse employee reports being threatened by a co-worker. What is the company’s top priority?
Place the worker on temporary leave
Protect the worker from retaliation and investigate
Transfer the threatening worker without documentation

Workplace violence response priorities are to protect the threatened employee (including from retaliation) and promptly investigate. Mandatory mediation or undocumented transfers can escalate risk and undermine due process.

A research facility uses several Class 3B lasers for precision cutting tasks. In accordance with ANSI Z136.1 and best practices, which control strategy is most appropriate to reduce both beam and non-beam hazards?
Implementing beam enclosures, restricted access controls, and PPE for operators
Supplying laser safety goggles to employees without further controls
Relying on hazard warning signs and training only
Installing HEPA-filtered smoke extractors near the beam path

ANSI Z136.1 favors engineering controls (beam enclosures, interlocks), administrative access control to the laser controlled area, and PPE together for Class 3B. Goggles or signs alone are insufficient; smoke extraction addresses only one non-beam hazard.

SOLAS Compliance Requirements
Which of the following is a fundamental requirement established by the International Convention for the Safety of Life at Sea (SOLAS) to enhance maritime safety?
Structural design standards and mandatory emergency systems for ships
Harmonized labeling protocols for hazardous chemical cargo
International packaging codes for marine pollutant materials
Standardized spill response plans for onboard hazardous materials

SOLAS sets minimum standards for ship construction, stability, fire protection, life-saving appliances, and emergency systems. Dangerous goods packaging and marine pollution are mainly addressed by the IMDG Code and MARPOL.
A safety manager is reviewing a Gantt chart. What is this chart used for?
A Gantt chart shows tasks as bars against a calendar, including durations, overlaps and dependencies.

A manufacturing plant is considering purchasing a $25,000 automated palletizing machine to reduce manual lifting injuries.
· Investment:$25,000
· Annual Savings: $40,000 (reduced injury claims and improved productivity)
ROI = (Annual Savings ÷ Investment) × 100% Note: This formula is not given on some questions.
If the company buys the palletizing machine and saves $40,000 annually, what is the ROI as a percentage?
A supplier's SDS for a new solvent shows a flame pictogram and the hazard statement 'Flammable liquid, Category 2.' What is your FIRST action before allowing the material on site?
Verify that proper flammable storage and ventilation controls are available
Require the supplier to train all employees in SDS reading
Approve the purchase since the supplier provided an SDS
Have employees store it in the nearest open area
Pre-purchase review should confirm that storage (cabinets, quantity limits), ventilation and ignition controls exist before the material arrives.
During an inspection, you find a drum of acid cleaner (corrosive pictogram) stored next to a pallet of bleach. What is your MOST urgent concern?
The chemicals could react to release toxic chlorine gas
The drum label is missing the manufacturer's phone number
The bleach lacks a transport placard
Acids mixed with sodium hypochlorite liberate chlorine gas; incompatible materials must be segregated in storage (SDS Sections 7 and 10).
A new employee sees the exclamation mark pictogram on a chemical label and asks what it means. How should you explain it under GHS?
“It means the chemical is only dangerous if it catches fire.”
“It means the chemical is safe for short-term exposure.”
“It’s used for chemicals that are explosive.”
“It means the chemical may cause skin irritation or respiratory issues.”

The GHS exclamation mark indicates irritant (skin/eye), skin sensitizer, acute toxicity (harmful), narcotic effects, respiratory tract irritation, or ozone layer hazard. Explosives use the exploding bomb pictogram.
Ménière disease affects which body part.
Meniere disease is a disorder of the inner ear causing vertigo, tinnitus, fluctuating hearing loss, and aural fullness, relevant to noise and balance evaluations.
During an emergency incident with many agencies, who is in charge on-site?
Under ICS/NIMS, the Incident Commander (or Unified Command with multiple agencies) has overall authority for on-scene operations; the Safety Officer is a command staff position reporting to the IC.

A worker in a workshop accidentally drops a wrench from the top of a 3-meter-high ladder. Another worker is standing nearby.
From a basic physics perspective, what is the main safety concern?
The wrench could hit the floor and bounce back up due to air resistance.
The wrench could gain speed as it falls, increasing the risk of injury if it hits someone.
The wrench will float slowly down.
The wrench will stop falling halfway because of magnetic pull from the floor.
A falling object accelerates at about 9.8 m/s2, so its velocity and kinetic energy increase with drop height (v = sqrt(2gh), about 7.7 m/s from 3 m), creating a struck-by hazard.

Two machines in a shop are running side-by-side, producing a combined noise level of 85 dBA measured 6 feet away. A worker moves to 3 feet away from the machines without hearing protection.
Question:
Approximately what noise level will the worker be exposed to?
For a point source, halving distance raises level by about 6 dB (inverse square law: 20 log(6/3) = 6 dB), so 85 + 6 = 91 dBA.
A crew uses a 150 gpm pump to dewater a flooded trench 16 ft long and 3 ft wide, holding 3 ft of water. Using 7.48 gal per cubic foot and assuming no inflow, about how long will pumping take?
A logistics company's telematics show that a driver's lane-departure warnings and harsh-braking events rise sharply after 9 hours on shift. What is the MOST effective immediate action?
Disable the lane-departure warnings to reduce distraction
Move the driver to night routes when traffic is lighter
Assign an online fatigue-awareness module after the shift
Require an immediate rest break and review shift scheduling practices
The data show fatigue in progress. Stopping the exposure now and fixing the scheduling (the root cause) is best. Night routes make circadian fatigue worse.
During scheduled maintenance on a hybrid delivery van, a technician smells fuel vapor near the rear tank. The van also has a high-voltage battery system. What is the safest procedure?
Continue working and finish the battery inspection first
Apply sealant to the suspected leak before shutting down power
Disconnect only the 12-V battery and proceed
Ventilate the area, isolate both the fuel system and the high-voltage system, and follow the manufacturer's hybrid lockout procedure

Hybrids combine a flammable fuel hazard with a high-voltage electrical ignition source. Both energy sources must be controlled per the OEM procedure; the 12-V battery alone does not de-energize the HV system.

A skid steer is stolen overnight from a construction site. The machine's telematics show it was moved off-site at 2:15 a.m., and the security cameras on the south fence were offline. What should be the FIRST preventive improvement?
Provide reliable/redundant power to the cameras and set geofence alerts that trigger when equipment moves after hours
Have operators take equipment home after each shift
Leave all keys in the cab at night
Remove GPS units so thieves cannot tamper with them
Combining surveillance with telematics geofencing gives real-time detection. The other options remove protection or increase the risk of theft.
Which of the following best represents the core components of an effective health and safety performance management system?
Policy, organizing, planning and implementation, performance measurement, and auditing and review
Performance measurement, reviewing results, and tracking near-miss incidents
Policy, organizing, planning and implementation, and performance measurement
Planning and organization, safety policy, and performance review

The HSG65-style safety management model includes policy, organizing, planning and implementing, measuring performance, and auditing and review. The other options omit auditing/review or other elements needed for continual improvement.
Which factor most contributes to the success of safety training programs?
Active support from top management and clearly defined learning objectives
Allowing employees to participate on a random or voluntary basis
Requiring weekly testing regardless of content relevance
Relying exclusively on external consultants for training delivery

Visible management commitment and clear, measurable learning objectives (per ANSI/ASSP Z490.1) drive training success. Voluntary random attendance, irrelevant testing, and full reliance on outsiders weaken programs.

A maintenance team is preparing to replace a defective motor on a conveyor system. The main electrical disconnect is locked out, but hydraulic pressure in the lift section of the conveyor remains stored. The maintenance supervisor insists that locking out the electrical supply is sufficient because “the hydraulics aren’t energized right now.”
What is the correct next step before beginning work?
Proceed with work since the hydraulic system is not actively running
Release and verify the removal of hydraulic energy before starting work
Tag the hydraulic controls with a warning tag but do not lock them
Keep the hydraulic pressure in place to avoid delays when restarting the system

OSHA 1910.147(d)(5) requires stored or residual energy, including hydraulic pressure, to be relieved, disconnected, or restrained and verified before work. Electrical lockout alone does not control hydraulic energy.

An electrician is repairing a control panel that powers three different machines. He applies his personal lock to the main breaker that feeds the panel. While he is working, another employee, unaware of the lockout, attempts to energize one of the machines by using its local start button. The machine does not start, but the control panel still becomes energized through a separate feed from another circuit that wasn’t locked out.
What should have been done to prevent this situation?
Place a tag on the machine’s start button warning others not to use it
Apply lockout devices to all energy sources feeding the control panel
Disconnect only the breaker for the machine being worked on
Have a spotter watch for unauthorized attempts to operate the machine
OSHA 1910.147 requires all energy sources feeding the equipment to be identified and isolated with locks. A second feed left unlocked defeated the lockout; tags or spotters are not substitutes.
During an investigation, a safety team uses a Fishbone (Ishikawa) diagram. What is the primary purpose of this tool?
To calculate the financial loss of the incident
To categorize possible root causes into structured branches
To visualize the sequence of events in a timeline

A fishbone (Ishikawa) diagram organizes possible causes into categories such as people, methods, machines, materials, measurement, and environment. Timelines are shown by sequence/events charts, not fishbones.
In the Swiss Cheese Model, accidents occur when:
All slices of cheese are strong and without holes
Hazards are eliminated entirely before they reach the worker
The holes (weaknesses) in multiple layers of defense align
One single failure in the system happens

Reason's Swiss Cheese Model holds that accidents happen when weaknesses (active failures and latent conditions) in several layers of defense line up, allowing a hazard to pass through, not from one single failure.
The Bowtie method in incident investigation is best described as:
A brainstorming technique to list every possible hazard
A timeline that shows human errors in sequence
A method to calculate injury severity after incidents
A model that links threats, preventive barriers, the top event, and consequences
A bowtie links threats, preventive barriers, the top event, mitigative barriers and consequences in one diagram.

A large manufacturing facility experiences a sudden regional power outage during peak production hours. The facility’s emergency generators are working, but IT systems and supply chain connections remain offline. As the safety professional on the continuity planning team, what is your priority action to maintain business continuity?
Suspend all operations until city power is restored.
Activate the business continuity plan and shift critical operations to alternate facilities.
Contact vendors immediately to renegotiate delivery contracts.
Instruct staff to use manual processes for all tasks until systems return.

Business continuity (ISO 22301, NFPA 1600) calls for activating the BCP and moving critical functions to alternate sites or processes per pre-planned recovery strategies. Shutting down or improvising manual work is not the planned response.

A chemical spill occurs in the warehouse after hours, triggering local media coverage and community concern. Senior management asks you to advise during the crisis meeting. What step is most critical in the crisis communication plan?
Delay communication until a full internal investigation is complete.
Issue a public statement acknowledging the incident, safety measures taken, and expected timeline for resolution.
Restrict all communication to legal counsel only.
Focus solely on internal employee notifications and avoid external communication.

Effective crisis communication is prompt, transparent, and consistent: acknowledge the event, describe protective actions, and give a timeline. Delay or silence erodes trust and lets rumors fill the gap.
A hurricane destroys a regional data center that stores critical safety inspection records and training files. As part of the disaster recovery team, what is the BEST immediate course of action?
Rebuild the data center at the same location as quickly as possible
Implement the disaster recovery plan by restoring records from off-site or cloud backups to an alternate site
Manually recreate records from employee memory and paper notes
Wait until insurance claims are processed before attempting recovery
Contingency planning pre-arranges backups and alternate sites so critical records can be restored quickly; rebuilding or waiting delays recovery.

After a recent incident, a logistics company considers implementing a behavior-based safety (BBS) program. A senior executive is skeptical. As the safety professional, how should you respond to strengthen the business case?
This will help us meet OSHA requirements.
Employees will appreciate the training experience.
Reducing incidents through BBS improves morale and reduces turnover.
It’s the most expensive program available, so it must be good.

Executives respond to business outcomes; linking BBS to fewer incidents, better morale, and lower turnover ties safety to cost and productivity. Compliance alone is weak since OSHA does not require BBS, and cost is not a quality measure.

A construction firm suffered multiple fall-related incidents last year. The safety manager proposes a $15,000 annual fall protection training program. The CEO asks, “What do we get for that money?” What is the best response?
It will make us look better in the community.
We can avoid lawsuits, fines, and lost time incidents.
It’s the same program everyone else is using.
The business case should quantify avoided costs: fewer lost-time injuries, workers' compensation claims, fines, and litigation. Image alone is weak and guarantees of zero incidents are not credible.

A warehouse reports frequent near-miss incidents involving forklifts and pedestrian workers. Management is skeptical about spending money on redesigning traffic flow and adding protective barriers. You are asked to justify the investment from a business perspective.
Which argument provides the strongest business case for implementing the safety improvements?
The redesign reduces the likelihood of costly injuries, lawsuits, and OSHA fines, which directly protects company profits.
Safety investments are required only for compliance and will not affect business performance.
Improvements in safety will likely slow down operations due to additional barriers and procedures.
Installing safety upgrades only improves employee morale but has no financial return.

The strongest business case links the control to avoided direct and indirect costs (injuries, claims, lawsuits, fines, downtime) that protect profit. The other options deny or ignore the financial return.

A construction company is about to begin work on a high-rise project in a hurricane-prone area. Management is concerned about potential financial losses if a major storm damages equipment or delays the project. As the safety professional advising leadership, what is the most appropriate risk sharing strategy?
Stop the project completely until hurricane season ends.
Purchase an insurance policy that covers storm-related damages and delays.
Relocate all operations to a non-hurricane region.
Invest in multiple smaller projects across several states
Risk sharing/transfer shifts the financial consequences to another party, typically through insurance. Stopping or relocating is avoidance, and spreading projects is diversification.

A logistics company relies on a single supplier for specialized safety gloves. During a supply chain disruption, deliveries stop, leaving workers exposed. As the safety professional advising procurement, what action best demonstrates risk diversification?
Stockpile a one-year supply of gloves from the same vendor.
Work with two or three suppliers in different regions to reduce reliance on one.
Eliminate glove use entirely and switch to bare-hand operations.
Negotiate a penalty clause in the contract with the current vendor.

Diversification spreads exposure across multiple independent sources so one disruption cannot stop supply. Stockpiling from the same vendor keeps single-source dependence, and penalty clauses do not restore supply.

A warehouse supervisor identifies that employees are climbing storage racks to retrieve boxes instead of using proper ladders. The behavior creates a high fall hazard. As the safety professional, which decision best demonstrates risk avoidance?
Provide fall arrest harnesses for employees who climb the racks.
Train employees to climb more carefully and enforce 100% tie-off.
Ban climbing racks entirely and require use of ladders or mechanical lifts.
Buy additional insurance to cover injuries from potential falls.

Risk avoidance eliminates the exposure-causing activity altogether; banning rack climbing and requiring proper ladders or lifts removes the hazard. Harnesses and training reduce risk, and insurance transfers it.

A manufacturing plant uses a sanding system that produces fine wood dust. The system vents directly into a standard dumpster outside.
Which safety concern should the professional address first regarding this dust management practice?
The dumpster might overflow and create trip hazards
The dust could attract insects or rodents
Fine dust accumulating in the dumpster may create an explosion hazard if ignited
The location of the dumpster violates zoning regulations

Fine wood dust is a combustible dust (NFPA 660/664); venting it into a dumpster allows accumulation and dust clouds that can ignite or explode. This life-safety hazard outranks housekeeping, pests, or zoning.

A safety audit at a powdered metal facility finds multiple dust collectors are installed indoors without explosion vents or suppression systems.

What critical control measure is missing in this combustible dust environment?
Local exhaust ventilation to capture fumes
Explosion protection for dust collection systems per NFPA 660

NFPA 660 (formerly 652/654/484) requires indoor dust collectors handling combustible metal dust to have explosion protection such as venting to a safe location, suppression, or isolation. The other options address unrelated hazards.

During a routine inspection of a warehouse handling grain products, you observe fine dust accumulation on elevated surfaces, ducts, and equipment. Workers are using compressed air to clean machinery at the end of each shift. Which of the following represents the greatest safety concern in this situation?
The compressed air could spread dust into the air and create a combustible dust cloud.
The dust accumulation may clog HVAC filters and reduce system efficiency.
The elevated surfaces may require fall protection for cleaning access.
The compressed air could create noise exposure above 85 dBA.

Compressed air disperses accumulated dust into a cloud, completing the dust explosion pentagon; OSHA's Grain Handling standard and NFPA 61/660 restrict blow-down. Vacuuming with approved equipment is preferred.

An electrician drills, cuts, and sands in a confined space with corded tools.
Choose the best safety action:
Use drain cleaner to clear dust, and ignore cord damage if the tool still runs.
Check cords/tools for damage, use GFCI, clamp workpiece, and disconnect power before changing blades.
Hold the material with one hand while cutting with the other to save time.
Run tools at full speed in a damp area to test moisture resistance

OSHA 1910.242/1910.334 and Subpart S require inspecting cords and tools, GFCI protection in damp or conductive locations, securing the workpiece so both hands control the tool, and disconnecting power before changing accessories.

A technician must inspect roof edge on a windy day. The ladder is a 28-ft extension ladder, spread on soft soil with a toolbox slung over the shoulder. The ground is sloped, there are overhead power lines nearby, and the worker needs to access a point about 6 feet above the roof edge. The ladder is not tied off yet, and the worker is considering how to proceed safely.
 Choose the best safety action:
Place the ladder on the softest spot available, extend it fully, climb without tying off since the task is short, and keep the toolbox in hand to avoid dropping it.

Set the ladder at the correct angle (about 4:1), use ladder levelers or other stabilization, secure the base, tie off the top if possible, maintain three points of contact, and avoid working near power lines.
Stand on the top two rungs to reach the roof edge more easily and carry the toolbox in one hand, leaving the base loose to adjust height as needed.
Move the ladder to a new location every time you need to reach a different spot, without checking the ground stability, and bypass the use of a spotter to save time

Per OSHA 1926.1053, set extension ladders at a 4:1 angle on firm level footing, secure top and base, extend 3 ft above the landing, keep three points of contact, hoist tools separately, and keep at least 10 ft from power lines.

Servicing a collaborative robot (cobot) arm in a production cell
A technician is performing maintenance on a cobot that handles lightweight parts. The robot is still powered from its teach pendant, but the maintenance task requires removing a guard and accessing a coupling near the end effector. The cell includes conveyors, an emergency stop button nearby, and a hydraulic clamp that can cycle unexpectedly if the system is not properly isolated.
 Choose the best safety action:
Remove the guard and proceed with the maintenance while the robot is in auto mode to verify the task is complete faster.
Lock out the main power, then bypass interlocks to test the system while wearing PPE to maintain dexterity.
Rely on a single person to monitor the robot and keep their hands near the emergency stop button in case the robot starts.

Isolate and lockout both electrical and hydraulic energy, disable the robot via the teach pendant, verify zero energy state, use a documented maintenance procedure, and only then begin work with appropriate PPE and barriers.

OSHA 1910.147 and ANSI/RIA R15.06 require isolating all energy sources (electrical and hydraulic), verifying a zero-energy state, and following a documented procedure. Bypassing interlocks or relying on an e-stop is not energy control.

A conveyor system has a pinch point where rollers rotate and a guard is present but includes a permanent gap that a hand could fit into if an operator inserts a hand while clearing a jam. 
Which action best aligns with standard guarding principles?
Installing a presence-sensing device in addition to the existing guard
Replacing the guard with a larger opening for easier access
Removing the guard to improve workflow if the device is added
Relying on training alone to prevent access to the pinch point

A guard with an opening that allows reach into the hazard does not meet OSHA 1910.212; adding a presence-sensing device provides supplementary protection that stops motion if a hand enters. Bigger openings, removing guards, or training alone increase risk.

A CNC milling machine has automatic tool change with a fully enclosed guarding, with the door interlock. There is an emergency stop button. The maintenance technician opens the interlock door while the machine is in cycle to adjust a fixture after pressing the emergency stop button.
Which corrective action is best for servicing and maintenance?
Replace the door interlock with a fail-safe Interlock.
Add signage reminding technicians to keep clear of the guard
Provide the lockout to facilitate servicing of the equipment.
Rely on operator discipline to prevent entry during cycles

An e-stop and interlock are operational safeguards, not energy-isolating devices; OSHA 1910.147 requires lockout for servicing and maintenance such as fixture adjustment. Signs or discipline are weaker administrative controls.

A packaging line uses multiple machines with different guards. One machine uses a fixed guard with a hinged access panel that has a standard latch, while another uses a perimeter fence with a separate gate and an interlock on the gate. Operators report near-miss events where a hand briefly enters the danger area during line adjustments.
What combination of safeguarding measures would best address the near-miss trends?
Upgrade the fixed guard to include a non-removable cover and install a proper interlock on all access points; ensure gate interlocks are hard-wired and tested
Remove interlocks and rely on operator training to avoid reaching into danger zones
Add more visible warning labels and rely on PPE
Keep current guards but add a maintenance procedure that allows entry during operation

Near misses at access points show the latched panel and gate can be defeated; interlocking every access point with tested, hard-wired (control-reliable) interlocks follows ANSI B11.19. Labels, PPE, or entry during operation are weaker or unsafe.

During an incident investigation, you are interviewing a machine operator who looks nervous and reluctant to share details. You notice he is giving short “yes/no” answers.

What is the best next step for the investigator?
Start by asking direct “yes/no” questions to get facts quickly.
Reassure the worker that the purpose of the interview is prevention, not punishment.
Remind the worker that refusal to cooperate may result in discipline.
Skip the interview and rely on witness statements from coworkers.

Effective interviews build rapport and stress that the goal is prevention, not blame, then use open-ended questions. Threats of discipline or yes/no questioning reduce candor, and skipping the interview loses first-hand facts.

A supervisor is being interviewed about a forklift near-miss. The investigator asks, "Did you see the forklift operator speeding?" The supervisor answers "No."

What would have been a better question to encourage useful information?
"Why didn't you stop the operator if they were speeding?"
"Tell me what you observed when the forklift entered the aisle."
"Did the forklift almost hit the pedestrian?"
