Loss control programs prevent and reduce losses at their source through hazard identification, controls, training, and claims management. Insurance and contracts only transfer or finance losses.
Which of the following is a key characteristic of an effective occupational health and safety program?
Assigning responsibility only to managers, supervisors, and customers
Assigning safety responsibilities to managers, supervisors, and employees at all levels
Assigning responsibility only to managers, employees, and customers
Assigning safety responsibilities only to supervisors, employees, and customers

Effective programs (OSHA Recommended Practices, ANSI Z10, ISO 45001) assign safety responsibility and accountability at every level, including managers, supervisors, and employees. Customers are not part of the internal responsibility structure.

Name two atmospheric tests that must be conducted if entering an
excavation broken sewer main in a trench

Sewage decomposition produces hydrogen sulfide (toxic, PEL ceiling 20 ppm) and methane (flammable, LEL 5%), along with oxygen deficiency, so OSHA 1926.651(g) atmospheric testing should include H2S and LEL/methane.

Workers are installing pipe in a 9-ft-deep trench in Type B soil with no protective system in place. The competent person has stepped away. What corrective action is required before work can continue?
Provide hard hats and high-visibility vests
Get workers out and install a protective system (sloping, shoring or shielding) before re-entry
Backfill the trench at the end of the shift
Place a ladder at one end of the trench
Trenches 5 ft or deeper require a protective system unless they are in stable rock (1926.652). PPE and a ladder do not protect against a cave-in.
How is the OSHA Totat Recordable Incident Rate (TRIR) calculated?
(Total OSHA Recordable incidents 200,000) / Total Hours Worked in the Year
(Total OSHA Recordable incidents x 100,000) / Total Hours Worked in the Year
(Total OSHA Recordable incidents 300,000) / Total Hours Worked in the Year
(Total OSHA Recordable incidents x 150,000) / Total Hours Worked in the Year
TRIR = (recordable cases x 200,000) / total hours worked; 200,000 represents 100 full-time workers x 40 hr/week x 50 weeks per year.

A facility spends $40,000 on a new machine guarding syste
year, the company saves $70,000 in reduced injuries, downtime, and insurance
costs. As a safety professional evaluating the financial impact, which
statement best reflects the ROI benefit of this improvement?
ROI = (Benefits minus Costs) divided by Costs, times 100%.
The investment was too costly because the equipment didn't eliminate all injuries
The investment id not impact safety, only business costs
The investment nerated a positive return because the savings exceeded the cost
The investment should only be evaluated on its regulatory compliance benefits
ROI = (70,000 - 40,000) / 40,000 x 100% = 75%, a positive return because savings exceeded cost. Eliminating every injury is not the measure of ROI.
What is the first step in developing a safety management system in the workplace per ANSI-

ANSI/ASSP Z10 (section 5) and ISO 45001 begin with management leadership and commitment, which provides the policy, resources, and authority needed before planning, risk assessment, and implementation.

Root Cause Identification
After a worker suffered a severe hand injury while clearing a jam in a conveyor system, the
investigation team used a 5 Whys technique to trace the cause back to a lack of proper
lockout/tagout procedures.
Which investigative process best describes this method?

The 5 Whys is a root cause analysis technique that repeatedly asks why to move from symptoms to underlying system causes (e.g., missing LOTO procedures). Event trees model forward consequences; change analysis compares to normal.

Following a chemical spill, the safety manager assembles a multidisciplinary team to
analyze deviations in valve operation, human error, and procedural gaps. The team uses a
structured worksheet to identify causes and corrective actions for People, Procedures,
Equipment, Environment, and Management Systems.
Which investigation technique is being applied?
Categorizing causes into branches such as People, Procedures, Equipment, Environment and Management Systems is the cause-and-effect (fishbone/Ishikawa) method.

After a steam line rupture, an investigator diagrams the sequence of events, identifying how
control valve failure, poor maintenance, and lack of alarm response combined to cause the
event. The analysis works backward from the incident through the system.
Which method is most likely being used?

Fault tree analysis works deductively backward from the top event through AND/OR combinations of contributing failures (valve failure, maintenance, alarm response). FMEA works forward from individual component failure modes.
Which color in the NFPA diamond represents fire.
In the NFPA 704 diamond, red is flammability, blue is health, yellow is instability/reactivity, and white is special hazards (e.g., W, OX, SA).

Site-Specific Safety Plan (SSSP) Development
A general contractor is preparing a Site-Specific Safety Plan for a new commercial build. The
safety professional is asked to define scope, site conditions, and subcontractor safety
responsibilities.
Which section of the SSSP should this information be included in?
Project scope, site conditions and subcontractor responsibilities belong in the project overview and responsibility-assignment section of a site-specific safety plan.

During a roofing project, a subcontractor's employee falls through an unguarded skylight.
The general contractor (GC) did not create the hazard but had authority over the site and
conducted weekly inspections.
Under OSHA's multi-employer policy, what role does the GC have?

The GC had general supervisory authority over the site and the ability to correct hazards, which makes it the controlling employer under OSHA's multi-employer citation policy, even though it did not create the hazard.
During a plant expansion, a RACI chart is developed for a confined space entry program. The site safety professional is marked "A" for approving the entry permit process. What does "A" mean?
Accountable - the one person who owns the outcome and signs off
In RACI, A = Accountable: one owner per task who approves the work. The doer is R (Responsible); advisors are C (Consulted).

A hospital is disposing of used radiological materials from its imaging department. The
waste is labeled as "decay-in-storage," and radiation levels are monitored until they fall to
background levels before disposal.
Which principle of radioactive waste management is being demonstrated?
Direct release to municipal waste without documentation
Controlled decay and verification prior to disposal
Mixing radioactive with regular biomedical waste to dilute exposure

Decay-in-storage (NRC 10 CFR 35.92) holds short-lived radionuclides until surveys show activity indistinguishable from background, then disposes of them with records. Dilution or undocumented release is prohibited.

A construction company changes its purchasing policy to require recycled concrete aggregate, energy-efficient lighting, and low-VOC materials on all projects. Which sustainability principle does this BEST represent?
Compliance with local code minimums only
Source reduction and sustainable material selection
Specifying recycled, efficient and low-toxicity inputs at procurement reduces impacts before they occur (green purchasing).

Aging Infrastructure and Environmental Impact
A city's wastewater treatment facility experiences frequent leaks due to corroded underground
piping, leading to surface contamination. The environmental manager proposes a phased
replacement plan with modern corrosion-resistant piping.
What is the most significant benefit of this approach?
It reduces the plant's staffing needs
It mitigates long-term environmental contamination and service disruptions
It eliminates the need for monitoring discharge permits
Replacing corroded infrastructure prevents leaks and releases, protecting soil and water and maintaining service reliability. It does not remove NPDES monitoring or EPA reporting obligations.

During a maintenance operation, an employee notices a small fire starting in a flammable
liquid storage area. Several fire extinguishers are nearby, including water (Class A), C02 (Class
BC), and dry chemical (Class ABC).
Which extinguisher Should be used to safely put out the fire?
C02 or Dry Chemical extinguisher (Class BC or ABC)
None — attempt to smother with rags or absorbent pads

Flammable liquid fires are Class B; CO2 (BC) or dry chemical (ABC) extinguishers smother or interrupt the reaction. Water can spread burning liquid, halon is phased out, and rags are unsafe (NFPA 10).

A welding contractor is assigned to repair handrails near a wooden platform. Sparks from
previous work were found to have scorched nearby materials. The site safety manager insists
on establishing a 35-foot radius fire watch and removing combustibles.
Which fire prevention principle is the manager applying?
Implementation of a hot work permit and fire watch
Training all workers in welding techniques
Limiting welding time to less than 10 minutes
NFPA 51B and OSHA 1910.252 require a hot work permit, removal or shielding of combustibles within 35 ft, and a fire watch during and after hot work. PASS is the extinguisher operating technique.
What should a forklift operator do when approaching an intersection?
Slow down and sound the horn
Check for hazards by leaning out of the cab
Get through as quickly as possible
OSHA 1910.178(n)(4) requires drivers to slow down and sound the horn at cross aisles and other locations where vision is obstructed. Leaning out of the cab exposes the operator to crushing.

Forklift modifications and additions that affect the vehicle's capacity or safe operation are
strictly prohibited unless the user first obtains:
An inspection by a competent person who documents the change.
An engineer's approval certified by a professional seal.
The certified driver's approval after a trial run.

OSHA 1910.178(a)(4) prohibits modifications and additions affecting capacity and safe operation without the manufacturer's prior written approval, after which capacity plates and labels must be updated.
A team must lift a 3,000-lb component with a 5-ton bridge crane. The only available wire rope sling has a visible cut in its outer strands. What is the safest course of action?
Remove the damaged sling from service and defer the lift until an inspected, compliant sling is available
Proceed but reduce crane speed to compensate
Have a qualified rigger certify the damaged sling for one-time use
Use the sling only if the load is under 50% of its rated capacity
1910.184 requires slings with damage such as cut strands to be removed from service immediately. Derating or "one-time use" is not permitted.

During an audit of a manufacturing facility, the auditor noted that the site's safety
management plan was missing a component related to worker participation. Which of the
following is a required component that should be added to meet regulatory and best practice
standards?
An automated software system for employee training
A procedure to involve employees in hazard identification and control measures
A mandatory wellness program offering biometric screening
A digital attendance tracking system for safety meetings

Worker participation in hazard identification and control is a required element of ISO 45001 (clause 5.4), ANSI Z10, and OSHA Recommended Practices. Software, wellness, and attendance tracking are optional tools.

A logistics company is implementing a new health and safety program. During review,
a consultant advises that one of the following is essential for regulatory compliance and
workforce engagement. What is the consultant MOST likely referring to?
A procedure for employees to report hazards without fear Of retaliation
A monthly newsletter summarizing productivity statistics
A wearable device pilot program to track worker movements
An optional suggestion box for safety ideas

A hazard reporting process free of retaliation is essential; OSH Act Section 11(c) protects employees who report hazards, and ISO 45001 requires removing barriers to participation. Optional suggestion boxes are weaker.

An example of effective training preparation is when an organization provides the trainer with
a document that systematically identifies the gaps in employees' current knowledge and skills
relative to job requirements before those gaps start creating real issues. What is the name of
this document or process?
Past test scores of the students

A training needs analysis systematically compares current knowledge and skills to job requirements to identify gaps before training is designed (ADDIE, ANSI/ASSP Z490.1). Curricula and past scores are inputs, not the gap analysis.

A four-step instruction protocol is effective in delivering important lessons to your
workers. The four steps are:
Prepare the worker for instruction, present the operation, have the worker perform the operation, and follow-up with the worker to confirm understanding and answer questions.
Provide manufacturers' instruction sheet(s), provide a computer based competency module, administer an examination, and rank workers based on their examination score.
Schedule training, deliver the information in person, conduct a written examination of 20 questions, and assign tast> to those who achieve an 80% or greater score.
Describe the job, provide a written list of the rules to be followed, identify disciplinary actions if the rules are not followed, and communicate the expected levels of productivity.

The four-step Job Instruction Training method (TWI): prepare the worker, present the operation, try out performance, and follow up. The other options emphasize rules, ranking, or testing rather than instruction.
Which method is the engineering control is demonstrated on a flat roof.
Workers are given anti slip footwear.
Guardrails used on the roof edge.

Guardrails are a passive engineering control that physically prevents falls without worker action (OSHA 1910.28, 1926.502(b)). Harnesses are PPE, safety monitors are administrative, and footwear is PPE.

During a machine guarding review, a safety professional observes employees reaching near
exposed pinch points to clear jams. The team suggests several corrective measures:
Install a light curtain that stops the machine when hands are detected near the danger zone.
Provide thicker gloves to reduce hand injuries.
Develop a new lockout/tagout (LOTO) training program.
Post warning labels near the pinch point. According to the ANSI/ASSP Zl O hierarchy of controls, ich option provides the most effective level of risk reduction?

A light curtain is an engineering safeguarding device that stops hazardous motion when the danger zone is entered, ranking above administrative measures (LOTO training, warning labels) and PPE (gloves) in the ANSI/ASSP Z10 hierarchy.

You are short 0.2 CEU for the recertification cycle. What should the safety profession do?
Ref: https://online.fliphtm15.com/pbcyp/eprz/#p= 10
Write BCSP and ask for an extension.
Add 0.4 CEOs and make it up later.
Write BCSP and ask for an exemption.

BCSP recertification rules provide for requesting an extension when a certificant cannot complete required points by the cycle end; rounding up or claiming unearned credit is misrepresentation, and exemptions are for limited situations. Note: Depends on current BCSP recertification policy; verify with BCSP.

A speaker says he has a CSP certification as a consultant. It is listed on his business card.
You check on the BCSP website and see he does not have any BCSP credentials. What is the
BEST way to proceed?
Confront him quietly in the hallway and ask him to explain.
Ask him in a meeting about his CSP designation.
Send an email to your management teams questioning his credentials.

The BCSP Code of Ethics expects certificants to report credential misuse to BCSP, which investigates and enforces use of its marks. Public confrontation or spreading accusations to management risks defamation and is not the proper channel.

Senior management asks the safety manager to sign a confined space entry permit before atmospheric testing is done, calling it "just a formality" so work can start on schedule. What is the MOST ethical and professionally responsible action?
Sign the permit and perform testing later
Let the supervisor sign on the manager's behalf
Document the request, refuse to sign until testing is completed, and escalate if pressured further
Give verbal approval and note the delay at the next safety meeting
The BCSP Code of Ethics puts protection of people first; a permit certifies conditions that have not been verified. Delegating or verbally approving is the same violation.
A 2,000-lb load is supported by a two-leg sling, and each leg makes a 45-degree angle with the horizontal. What force is exerted in each leg?
Each leg = (2,000/2) / sin 45 = 1,000 / 0.707 = 1,414 lb. 1,155 lb would be the answer at 60 degrees. As the angle from horizontal decreases, leg tension increases.
A two-piece block and tackle with 5 part of rope to lift a weight of 2,000 pounds requires how much force for lift (no friction)? lbs.?
With no friction, required force = load / parts of line supporting the load: 2,000 lb / 5 = 400 lb.

While guiding a suspended load, a worker stands directly beneath the toad to adjust its
position. What should the rigger or safety officer do immediately?
Instruct the worker to move quickly and reposition
Stop the lift and remove the worker from under the load
Continue the lift but warn the worker to be careful
Allow the lift if the worker is wearing a hard hat
OSHA 1926.1425 and ASME B30 prohibit workers under suspended loads; stop the lift and move the worker clear, guiding the load with taglines. A hard hat offers no protection from a falling load.
A HAZOP study encourages the use of----------- to help explore where the procedure could deviate from its intended function.
HAZOP applies guide words (No, More, Less, Reverse, As Well As, Part Of, Other Than) to process parameters at each node to identify deviations from design intent and their causes and consequences.

A system safety technique that selects an undesired event whose possibility or probability
is to determined and then requirements could occur is called?
Failure effect modes and effect analysis

Fault tree analysis starts with a selected undesired top event and deductively determines the combinations of failures and conditions (via AND/OR gates) that could produce it, allowing probability calculation. Boolean algebra is a tool used within FTA.

Before a non-routine lift of an awkward load onto a mezzanine, a supervisor fills out the JHA alone at his truck and says he will "just get the guys to sign it." What is the MOST appropriate immediate action for the safety professional?
Let the job proceed and observe the lift for a future JHA update
Report the supervisor to the project manager
Politely hold the start and gather the crew for a few minutes to review the lift and improve the JHA together
Hand the supervisor a generic JHA and ask him to copy it
A JHA is only effective when the workers doing the task help identify hazards. Fix it before work starts, constructively; reporting or generic forms do not.

A general contractor is evaluating the safety performance of subcontractors. Which of the
following would be the best combination of leading and lagging indicators?
Days without injury and safety posters displayed
Near-miss reports and OSHA inspection records
Lost-time injuries and toolbox talk sign-in sheets
Pre-task hazard analysis completed and number of recordable injuries

Pre-task hazard analyses completed is a leading (proactive activity) measure and recordable injuries is a lagging (outcome) measure, giving a balanced set. The other pairs mix weak, non-measurable, or same-type indicators.

A construction company has experienced a rise in near-miss incidents over the past
quarter, though no recordable injuries have occurred. The safety manager decides to start
tracking the number of completed pre-task hazard analyses (PTHAs), the frequency of
supervisor safety observations, and attendance at toolbox talks each week.
Which Of the following best describes the type Of safety performance measurement being
implemented?
Lagging indicators that evaluate past incidents and injuries
Predictive analytics that estimate total recordable incident rates (TRIR) based on prior data
Financial performance metrics that track the cost of safety incidents
Leading indicators that measure proactive actions taken to prevent incidents
PTHAs completed, supervisor observations and toolbox talk attendance measure proactive activities before incidents: leading indicators.

A severe weather warning is issued during a work shift, sirens are sounding in the
community, indicating a tornado may be approaching. What is the best course of action?
Instruct workers to finish their tasks and then seek shelter
Move workers to a designated storm shelter or interior safe zone
Allow employees to go outside and wait in their car
Wait until the tornado is visible before taking any action

When tornado warning sirens sound, the emergency action plan (OSHA 1910.38) requires immediate movement to designated shelters or interior rooms on the lowest floor away from windows. Vehicles and waiting to see the tornado are deadly.

During a night shift, a fire breaks out in a section of a warehouse. Several employees evacuate safely, but one forklift operator is unaccounted for. The plan identifies assembly points and alarm systems but has no accountability procedure. What element is missing from the emergency plan?
A system for accounting for all employees after evacuation
OSHA 1910.38(c) requires procedures to account for all employees after evacuation; without it, missing workers may not be identified for rescue.

A maintenance supervisor decides to replace a pump with a new model rated for higher
pressure output to "improve efficiency." The new pump is installed without reviewing the piping system design or updating the operating procedures. A week later, a flange gasket fails,
releasing hot process fluid.
Which step in the Management of Change process was most likely missed?
Reviewing and approving the change before installation
Notifying purchasing about the new equipment model

OSHA 1910.119(l) MOC requires technical basis, safety impacts, procedure updates, and authorization before a change is implemented. A higher-pressure pump installed without design review or approval bypassed this step.

A company merges two production departments to reduce costs. After the merger, safety
performance declines, and employees report confusion about responsibilities and
supervision. The MOC review focused only on equipment relocation, not personnel or
procedural impacts.
Which aspect of MOC was overlooked?
Organizational change impact on roles and communication
MOC covers organizational changes too (staffing, roles, supervision, communication), not just equipment. The review missed the people/organizational impacts.

A chemical plant substitutes a new raw material in a batch recipe. The engineer assumes it is compatible because it is "chemically similar" and skips the hazard review. At startup, excessive heat causes the reactor relief valve to lift. Which MOC requirement should have prevented this?
Inspecting the relief valve after installation
Reviewing safety data and performing a hazard evaluation of the change before implementation

MOC requires the technical basis and safety impact of a change, including chemical reactivity and compatibility, to be evaluated BEFORE the change is made. Everything else in the list happens after the hazard has been introduced.

A research hospital has six recordable injury cases and one days-away or restricted case for
a total of seven cases.
TCIR = Number of injuries or illness cases x 200,000 + Total number of hours worked
Assuming a total of 278,942 hours worked for the year, what is the total case incident rate
(TCIR) for this hospital?

A wire rope applies a steady force of 500 N to a cart, causing the cart to move in a straight
line and accelerate at a rate of 5 m/sA2.
Given the formula: Force = Mass x Accelerati
What is the cart's mass?
F = m x a, so m = F / a = 500 N / 5 m/s2 = 100 kg (about 220 lb).

Reliability data for a chemical transfer system show a 0.5 probability of pump seal failure and a 0.3 probability of pipe gasket leak over 1,000,000 hours. Assuming the events are independent, what is the probability that BOTH failures occur?
AND for independent events = P1 x P2 = 0.5 x 0.3 = 0.15. Trap: adding gives 0.8 (that is not even the correct OR, which is 0.65).

Your employees must go Into a 40 foot x 60 foot unused underground vault to Investigate a
rotten smell. There are stairs down to the this vault. The Four gas meter reads 0% hydrogen
sulfide, 0% carbon monoxide, 0% flammables, 14% oxygen. The carbon dioxide is 35,000 ppm per another meter.
What respirator would you recommend?
Powered air-purifying respirator with vapor cartridges.
Tight fitting full face respirator with vapor cartridges

14% O2 is below the 19.5% threshold and CO2 at 35,000 ppm approaches the 40,000-ppm IDLH, so OSHA 1910.134(d)(2) requires atmosphere-supplying respiratory protection such as SCBA. Air-purifying respirators cannot supply oxygen.

During an inspection at a metal fabrication shop, the safety professional observes
an employee wearing a half-mask respirator white grinding stainless steel. The worker
mentions they've been using the same cartridges for several weeks and notice a slight
metallic odor during use.
What should the safety professional do first?
Instruct the employee to tighten the facepiece straps to improve the seal
Replace the cartridges immediately and review the change-out schedule
Tell the worker to continue until the next scheduled fit test
Advise the worker to switch to a dust mask instead of a respirator

Odor or taste during use indicates breakthrough or leakage; OSHA 1910.134(d)(3)(iii) requires cartridge change-out schedules. Leave the area, replace cartridges, check the seal, and review the schedule; a dust mask gives less protection.

A new conveyor system is being installed in a distribution center. During design review, engineers propose adding emergency-stop pull cords but leaving several exposed pinch points near the rollers because "guards can be added later if injuries occur." Which Prevention through Design action is MOST appropriate?
Install signs warning employees to keep hands clear of the rollers
Provide gloves to protect workers if their hands get too close
Train workers to avoid pinch points during startup
Eliminate or enclose the pinch points with fixed guards before installation
PtD addresses hazards at the design stage rather than after injuries. Fixed guarding designed in now beats signs, training or PPE, which are lower in the hierarchy.

A company is automating a welding workstation. The project manager skips the hazard review during initial design to "save time" and plans to do it at commissioning. Engineers later find that the robot's reach envelope intersects the operator walkway. Which step was missed?
Early-stage hazard identification and risk assessment
PtD requires hazard identification and risk assessment at the conceptual/design stage, when changes are cheapest. A PSSR at commissioning is too late to redesign the layout cheaply.

A facility plans to reduce fall hazards on a mezzanine. Current options being discussed
include:
Installing warning-line tape along the edges
Training workers on fall awareness
Requiring harnesses and lanyards
Redesigning the mezzanine with built-in guardrails
Which option BEST aligns with PtD and the hierarchy of controls?
Redesign the mezzanine to include permanent guardrails
Issuing fall arrest systems to all workers
Training all workers annually on fall hazards

Prevention through Design (ANSI/ASSP Z590.3) builds permanent guardrails into the mezzanine, eliminating or engineering out the fall hazard. Harnesses (PPE), warning lines, and training rank lower in the hierarchy.

A chemical plant uses a flammable solvent in quantities above OSHA's threshold. During a
PHA meeting, the team identifies a scenario where a transfer pump could overheat and ignite
vapors if cooling water flow is interrupted. The facilitator documents the scenario but decides
no follow-up actions are needed.
What is the MOST appropriate next step nder PSM requirements?
No further action is needed since the hazard was identified
Perform annual refresher training on pump operation
Conduct a Management of Change (MOC) review for all pumps on site
Develop recommendations and assign corrective actions to reduce the identified risk

OSHA 1910.119(e)(5) requires the employer to promptly address PHA team findings and recommendations, document resolution, and assign actions with completion dates. Identifying a credible ignition scenario without action is noncompliant.

Operators at a blending unit rely on tribal knowledge because the written procedures were never updated after a recipe change. During startup an operator adds an ingredient too early, causing a runaway reaction that lifts the relief system. Which PSM element was MOST directly violated?
1910.119(f) requires written, current operating procedures, certified annually. An MOC failure contributed, but the most direct gap is outdated procedures.

Mechanical Integrity Scenario
A facility stores chlorine under pressure. During inspection, a technician finds corrosion on a
piping elbow but defers repair because production is behind schedule. A week later, the elbow
fails, causing a hazardous release.
Which PSM principle would have prevented this incident?
Using contractors trained in hazard communication
Implementing a behavioral safety observation program
Updating the Emergency Action Plan annually
Following the mechanical integrity program's inspection and repair requirements

OSHA 1910.119(j) mechanical integrity requires inspection, testing, and correction of equipment deficiencies before further use or in a safe and timely manner. Deferring repair of corroded chlorine piping for production violated this element.

During an inspection of a business occupancy, you find a storage room converted to an office. The occupant load rose from 4 to 12, but the only egress door from the room is 24 in. wide and no exits were added. Which NFPA 101 life-safety issue does this MOST clearly create?
Failure to install emergency lighting in rooms with more than 10 occupants
Excessive travel distance for a business occupancy
Lack of a posted occupant-load sign in the office
Insufficient means-of-egress capacity/width for the increased occupant load
A change of use that raises occupant load requires a re-check of egress capacity and door width. A 24-in. door is below the minimum clear width for a means-of-egress door.
In a new healthcare wing, contractors prop open smoke-barrier doors for long periods while moving equipment between patient sleeping units. Under NFPA 101, what is the GREATEST concern?
Door hardware will wear out prematurely
The facility may be cited for fire drill documentation
Employees may trip on staged equipment
The propped doors compromise smoke-compartment integrity, which defend-in-place protection depends on
Healthcare occupancies use a defend-in-place strategy that relies on smoke compartments. Doors must self-close, or be held open only by devices that release on alarm.

A banquet hall (assembly occupancy) hosts an event for 400 guests. During the pre-event
walkthrough, the safety officer notes that the automatic fire alarm system is temporarily offline for maintenance, and only manual pull stations remain functional. The event organizer insists the gathering can continue since "it's only for a few hours."
Which NFPA 101 requirement is most directly violated?
Assembly occupancies must have posted emergency escape maps
Fire alarm systems must be fully operational when the space is occupied
Events over 300 occupants require two trained crowd managers
Portable fire extinguishers must be upgraded to Class K for food service events

NFPA 101 requires fire protection systems such as alarms to be in service whenever a building is occupied; impairments require a fire watch or evacuation per NFPA 101 section 9.7.6. Continuing a 400-person event without the alarm violates this. Note: NFPA 101 allows impairment procedures (fire watch) rather than an absolute ban; key defensible.

l. Which index is MOST commonly used by industrial hygienists to assess and control
employee thermal stress?

ACGIH TLVs, NIOSH, and OSHA guidance use WBGT, combining natural wet bulb, globe, and dry bulb temperatures, to assess occupational heat stress. Indoor/outdoor formulas: 0.7NWB + 0.3GT or 0.7NWB + 0.2GT + 0.1DB.

A metal finishing shop uses a nickel-containing polishing compound. Workers complain of sinus irritation during buffing. No prior exposure data exists and ventilation effectiveness is unknown. What is the MOST appropriate first step in the exposure assessment?
Conduct full-shift dosimetry on all workers in the department
Rely on SDS information to estimate exposures without sampling
Assume exposures are below limits because symptoms are mild
Perform task-based personal air sampling on workers performing the buffing activity

With symptoms, no data, and unknown ventilation, the first step is task-based personal breathing-zone sampling of the buffing workers. Department-wide dosimetry is unfocused; SDS data alone cannot quantify exposure.

Which of the following is an essential ergonomic practice for maintaining a neutral seated
posture during work?
Sitting on a seat pan that extends past the knees for additional thigh support
Keeping the knees at approximately the same height as the hips, with feet flat or slightly forward
Sitting upright without lumbar support to encourage natural back alignment
Holding the elbows close to the torso with the forearms bent between 450 and 900

Neutral seated posture places knees about level with hips, feet flat or on a footrest, lumbar support, and elbows near 90-100 deg. A seat pan past the knees compresses the popliteal area and restricts circulation.
The position that places the least amount of stress on the body
The most difficult position for the body to hold
A safe position that protects only the back
The only position in which one can work
A neutral posture keeps joints aligned near the middle of their range of motion, minimizing muscle force, joint stress, and fatigue across the whole body, not just the back.

On an assembly line, workers repeatedly reach more than 20 in in front of their bodies to grab parts from a supply bin, and several report shoulder fatigue late in the shift. Which improvement would MOST effectively reduce the shoulder strain?
Increase job rotation so workers switch positions every two hours
Provide anti-fatigue mats to reduce discomfort while standing
Move the parts bin closer to the worker to reduce extended forward reaches
Require workers to stretch before starting their shift
Reducing the reach distance (moving the bin into the primary reach zone) removes the risk factor at its source. Rotation, mats and stretching do not change the reach.

A warehouse employee lifts 40-pound boxes from the floor to a conveyor at waist height,
completing the task more than 300 times per shift. The worker reports lower-back discomfort
by midday.
Which control best aligns with ergonomic principles to reduce the risk of injury?
Require the worker to lift the boxes more slowly
Provide a lifting belt for added lumbar protection
Train the worker to use "proper lifting techniques" when lifting from the floor
Raise the boxes off the floor using a pallet stand or lift table to reduce bending

Raising the pickup point eliminates floor-level bending and improves the NIOSH lifting equation's vertical multiplier, an engineering control. Lifting belts are not proven effective (NIOSH) and training alone is weak.
What are the three types of particle radiation?
Particulate (particle) radiation includes alpha particles, beta particles, and neutrons; X-rays, gamma, and UV are electromagnetic (photon) radiation.

A radiography crew performs weld inspections with a gamma source. A helper normally works 4 ft from the source but steps back to 12 ft during exposures. How does the radiation intensity at 12 ft compare with that at 4 ft?
Radiation intensity follows the inverse square law: I2/I1 = (d1/d2)^2 = (4/12)^2 = 1/9. Trap: 1/3 assumes intensity drops linearly with distance.

During a facility expansion, engineering proposes installing new automated palletizers. The
safety manager notes that no formal risk assessment or design review has been conducted.
According to ANSI Zl O, what should occur before installation?
Conduct a job hazard analysis after the equipment is operating for 30 days
Rely on the manufacturer's safety manual since it meets CE/UL requirements
Install the equipment immediately and review safety concerns during commissioning
Perform a documented design review and pre-installation risk assessment to identify hazards and required controls

ANSI/ASSP Z10 (design review and management of change) and Z590.3 require documented design reviews and risk assessment before new equipment is installed so controls are built in. Manufacturer certification does not cover site-specific hazards.

A chemical facility is reorganizing workflows and changing operator job duties.
Supervisors want to roll out the changes next week. The safety manager warns that
rushing the rollout could miss safety impacts. Under ANSI Zl O, what is the correct
safety professional action?
Approve the changes because workflow revisions are strictly an HR function
Delay the changes until all employees complete refresher PSM training
Conduct a Management of Change (MOC) analysis to evaluate risk impacts before implementing the changes
Implement changes first, then conduct incident trend analysis

ANSI/ASSP Z10 MOC applies to changes in organization, staffing, and job duties as well as equipment; evaluate the risk impacts before implementation. Organizational changes are not purely an HR matter.

After several near misses on a packaging line, management wants to issue PPE as the immediate solution. According to ANSI/ASSP Z10's hierarchy of controls, what should the safety professional recommend FIRST?
Provide upgraded PPE with higher ratings
Retrain operators on safe work practices
Evaluate and implement higher-level controls, such as elimination or engineering, before relying on PPE
Z10 ranks elimination, substitution, engineering, warnings and administrative controls above PPE. PPE can be interim but is not the first recommendation.

During an internal audit, you discover that several departments are performing risk
assessments using different formats and scoring methods. This inconsistency makes it
difficult to compare risks across the organization. According to ISO 45001, what should the
safety professional do FIRST?
Allow departments to keep their preferred method as long as they understand their own risks
Develop a standardized risk-assessment method and integrate it into the OHSMS
Require each department to train their workers on whichever risk-assessment tool they choose
Conduct a survey to determine which risk tool employees like best

ISO 45001 clause 6.1.2 requires the organization to establish a consistent process for hazard identification and risk assessment within the OHSMS, so a standardized method enables comparison and prioritization across departments.

A manufacturing facility plans to install a new automated packaging line. Engineering
wants to move forward immediately, but safety has not yet reviewed the design. Under
ISO 45001, which action BEST aligns with the standard?
Approve the installation and review safety issues after commissioning
Ask the vendor for assurances that equipment meets CE/UL requirements
Perform a Management of Change (MOC) review to identify new hazards and required controls
Allow installation but require employees to sign a hazard acknowledgement form

ISO 45001 clause 8.1.3 requires management of planned changes, including new equipment, to identify hazards and controls before implementation. Vendor CE/UL assurances and signed acknowledgement forms do not assess site risks.

After a serious near-miss involving a forklift and pedestrian, management asks how to
prevent recurrence. Under ISO 45001 's requirements for continual improvement, what is the
MOST appropriate next step?
Remind forklift operators to slow down and pedestrians to stay alert
Implement disciplinary action for anyone violating traffic rules
Conduct an incident investigation, identify root causes, and update controls and procedures
Increase the number of safety signs in pedestrian areas

ISO 45001 clause 10.2 requires investigating incidents and near misses, determining root causes, and implementing and reviewing corrective actions. Reminders, discipline, and signs do not address systemic causes.

A forklift operator nearly strikes a pedestrian after swerving erratically. During your
investigation, you learn the operator was observed with slurred speech, inconsistent reaction
times, and the smell of alcohol on their breath. The supervisor allowed him to continue working
because he "seemed fine earlier."
What is the company MOST liable for in this situation?
Failing to provide refresher forklift training
Not conducting a post-incident drug/alcohol test immediately
Allowing a known or suspected impaired employee to operate equipment
Not documenting daily pre-shift equipment inspections

Allowing a worker with observable signs of impairment to operate a forklift is the primary liability (OSHA General Duty Clause, negligent supervision). Missing training records or post-incident testing are secondary to the supervisor's failure to act.

During a morning toolbox talk, an employee appears extremely drowsy, has pinpoint pupils,
slow or shallow breathing, and repeatedly "nods off" despite attempts to stay awake.
Coworkers notice he is confused and unable to follow simple instructions.
Which condition does this MOST strongly indicate and require immediate response?
Heat exhaustion from working outdoors the previous day
Fentanyl or opioid-related impairment requiring emergency medical assistance
Stress-related fatigue that can be corrected with rest breaks

Pinpoint pupils, depressed breathing, and unresponsiveness are the classic opioid toxidrome (e.g., fentanyl). Call EMS immediately and administer naloxone if available; heat exhaustion and hypoglycemia do not cause pinpoint pupils.

A road construction crew has been working 12-hour night shifts for nine consecutive days. A worker falls asleep while using a plate compactor and nearly injures a coworker. Investigation reveals management ignored multiple fatigue complaints and denied requests for schedule rotation. What is the employer MOST at risk for?
Violating OSHA's hearing conservation program requirements
Increased workers' compensation claim costs due to predictable fatigue-related incidents
Failure to provide adequate PPE for night-shift operations
Violating EPA regulations related to nighttime noise pollution

Ignoring known fatigue complaints makes fatigue-related incidents foreseeable, increasing injury frequency and workers' compensation costs (and potential General Duty Clause exposure). The other options are unrelated regulatory areas. Note: General Duty Clause liability is also plausible but not offered; key defensible.

If workers must risk a bloodborne pathogen exposure, such as administering first aid,
which control measures must be in place?
Eye wash station and a deluge shower
Antiseptic hand soap and disposable paper towels
Chlorine-based bleach wipes and a surgical mask that covers the mouth and nose
Face shield, latex gloves, and a disposable apron

OSHA 1910.1030(d)(3) requires appropriate PPE such as gloves, face and eye protection, and gowns or aprons where blood exposure is anticipated. Eyewashes and soap support hygiene but are not barrier protection.
Which statement best describes the concept of workplace safety?
Completely eliminating all hazards from the work environment
Controlling identified hazards so they do not cause harm to workers, equipment, or the environment
Finishing tasks as quickly as possible, even if procedures are bypassed
Leaving safety enforcement solely up to management
Workplace safety means identifying hazards and controlling risk to acceptable levels so they do not harm people, property, or the environment; total hazard elimination is rarely feasible.
Which element was added to the traditional fire triangle to form the fire tetrahedron?

The tetrahedron adds the uninhibited chemical chain reaction to fuel, heat and oxygen; agents such as dry chemical and halon work by interrupting it. Dispersion and confinement belong to the dust pentagon.
A flash point of 70 °F indicates the liquid is classified under NFPA 30 as:
Class IB liquids have a flash point < 73 °F and a boiling point ≥ 100 °F, such as acetone or toluene.
Which NFPA standard governs the installation of automatic sprinkler systems?
NFPA 13 specifies design and installation of sprinkler systems; NFPA 25 covers inspection and maintenance.
The minimum distance that oxygen cylinders must be separated from fuel-gas cylinders in storage is:
Per OSHA 1910.253(b)(4)(iii), separation must be at least 20 ft or a 5-ft-high, half-hour-rated non-combustible barrier.
During hot work in a non-designated area, the fire watch must remain in place for at least:
NFPA 51B requires a 30-minute post-work fire watch to detect smoldering fires or heat transfer.
Which ICS component is responsible for developing the Incident Action Plan (IAP) and tracking resources?
Planning collects and evaluates information, tracks resource status, and prepares the IAP. Operations executes it; Logistics obtains resources.
Under OSHA 1910.38, an Emergency Action Plan (EAP) must include which of the following?
Procedures for reporting fires and other emergencies
OSHA 1910.38(c) requires procedures for reporting emergencies, evacuation routes, and accounting for employees.
Which suppression agent leaves no residue and is suitable for sensitive electrical equipment?
NFPA 2001 clean-agent systems use gaseous agents that extinguish fires without conductive residue or water damage.
A combustible dust explosion requires which two elements in addition to the fire tetrahedron (fuel, heat, oxygen, chain reaction)?
The dust explosion pentagon adds dispersion (a dust cloud) and confinement to fuel, ignition and oxygen. Fuel, ignition and oxygen are already part of the base elements.
In a Business Continuity Plan (BCP), the Recovery Time Objective (RTO) refers to:
Total time allowed before declaring a disaster
Maximum acceptable downtime for a critical process
Total time to restore all minor services
RTO defines the maximum time a function can be disrupted before unacceptable impact, guiding recovery priorities.
Which NFPA standard is considered the primary reference for comprehensive emergency management and business continuity programs?
NFPA 1600 establishes guidelines for preparedness, response, recovery, and continuity across all types of emergencies.
The Safety Officer in the Incident Command System (ICS):
Identifies hazards and ensures responder safety
The Safety Officer advises the Incident Commander on all matters related to responder and scene safety.
Which of the following describes the most effective engineering control for combustible dust hazards?
Local exhaust ventilation with explosion vents
NFPA 68 and 69 recommend dust collection and explosion venting as primary engineering controls for dust hazards.
An Emergency Action Plan (EAP) is required to include which element under OSHA 1910.38(c)?
Procedures to account for all employees after evacuation
Budget allocation for training and drills
Design details of fire alarm circuits
OSHA requires accounting for all employees after evacuation to ensure everyone is safe and accounted for.
What is the primary function of the Operations Section in the Incident Command System (ICS)?
The Operations Section implements field-level tactical operations in line with the Incident Action Plan.
A workplace stores both oxygen and acetylene cylinders in the same area. Which control ensures OSHA compliance?
Separation by at least 20 feet or a 5-foot fire barrier
Storage in the same ventilated cabinet
OSHA 1910.253(b)(4)(iii) mandates 20 feet of separation or a non combustible 5-foot barrier between oxidizers and fuel gases.
In a workplace violence prevention program, which element BEST demonstrates management commitment?
Installing CCTV cameras without any policy updates
A written zero-tolerance policy signed by top leadership and communicated to all employees
OSHA's program elements begin with management commitment and employee participation, shown by a visible, leadership-endorsed written policy backed by resources.
Which fire extinguisher type is suitable for use on energized electrical fires?
Class C extinguishers contain non- conductive agents like CO₂ or dry chemical to prevent electrical conduction hazards.
Which phase of emergency management focuses on actions taken after an incident to restore normal operations?
Recovery includes restoring operations, conducting investigations, and implementing corrective actions post-incident.
During a severe weather event, which of the following is the best protective action for employees in a tornado-prone facility?
Move to interior windowless rooms or shelter areas
Take cover under vehicles in the parking area
NFPA 1600 and FEMA guidelines recommend moving to interior, windowless shelters to protect against debris impact.
Which type of suppression system is most appropriate for a data center where water damage must be avoided?
Clean-agent systems (NFPA 2001) use gas to extinguish fires without leaving residue, ideal for sensitive electronics.
What is the recommended minimum air change rate for flammable liquid storage rooms according to NFPA 30 §9.5?
NFPA 30 requires mechanical ventilation providing at least six air changes per hour (ACH) to prevent vapor accumulation.
Which of the following is not part of the five core functions of the Incident Command System (ICS)?
ICS functions include Command, Operations, Planning, Logistics, and Finance/Administration - investigation occurs later during recovery.
Under OSHA 1910.106, what is the maximum quantity of flammable liquids permitted in a single approved storage cabinet?
OSHA 1910.106(d)(3)(ii)(a) limits Class I or II flammable liquids to 60 gallons per cabinet.
The Incident Commander’s first priority during an emergency should be to:
Ensure life safety and scene assessment
ICS protocol prioritizes life safety first, followed by incident stabilization and property conservation.
Which OSHA regulation requires employers to prepare and maintain written procedures for dealing with potential hazardous substance releases?
OSHA 1910.120 (HAZWOPER) mandates written emergency response plans for hazardous substance releases.
A combustible dust explosion often becomes catastrophic because of:
Secondary explosions from disturbed dust layers
Secondary explosions ignite disturbed surface dust, creating much larger pressure waves and destruction.
Which NFPA standard outlines guidance for active shooter or hostile event response programs?
NFPA 3000 establishes best- practice frameworks for planning and responding to active shooter or hostile events.
What is the MOST appropriate post-incident action following a workplace violence event?
Provide medical and psychological support, then investigate and review controls
Focus only on legal reporting requirements
OSHA guidance calls for immediate care, trauma counseling and debriefing, followed by investigation and corrective action to prevent recurrence.
In a chemical storage area, preventing static discharge during liquid transfer is achieved primarily by:
NFPA 77 requires grounding and bonding during transfer of Class I liquids to equalize potential and prevent ignition from static electricity.
Which NFPA standard specifies the inspection, testing, and maintenance requirements for water-based fire protection systems such as sprinklers?
NFPA 25 covers ITM of water-based systems; NFPA 13 covers sprinkler installation and design, NFPA 72 fire alarms, NFPA 70E electrical safety.
What is the minimum clearance required below sprinkler heads to ensure proper spray pattern and coverage?
NFPA 13 recommends maintaining an 18-inch clearance below sprinklers to prevent obstruction of discharge.
Which detection device is most appropriate in an electrical equipment room where dust may cause false smoke alarms?
Heat detectors are preferred in dusty or electrical rooms since they respond to temperature, not airborne particles.
The Finance/Administration Section in the Incident Command System (ICS) is responsible for:
Finance/Admin manages incident- related costs, contracts, and time records to ensure accountability and reimbursement.
Which of the following best defines a Continuity of Operations Plan (COOP)?
A plan to maintain essential functions during and after disruptions
A COOP ensures critical functions continue during emergencies through alternate sites, authority delegation, and vital records protection.
What is the most effective control to prevent ignition during welding near flammable materials?
Cover combustibles with flame-retardant blankets and obtain a hot-work permit
Store combustibles in metal cabinets only
NFPA 51B requires a hot-work permit and removal or shielding of combustibles to prevent ignition.
Under OSHA 1910.165, which system component ensures that fire alarms can alert employees even in noisy environments?
OSHA 1910.165(b)(3) mandates both audible and visual signals for employee alarms where ambient noise could mask sound.
Which activity occurs during the Preparedness phase of emergency management?
Preparedness includes training, drills, and planning activities performed before an emergency occurs.
What is the primary goal of post-incident after-action reviews?
Evaluate performance and identify lessons learned
After-action reviews assess response effectiveness, document lessons learned, and guide improvement of ERP and training.
Which element of a Business Continuity Plan (BCP) identifies critical processes and prioritizes their restoration?
A BIA evaluates time-sensitive operations and determines recovery priorities and resource needs for continuity planning.
Which of the following best describes the purpose of an Emergency Operations Center (EOC)?
To coordinate decision-making and communication during emergencies
To conduct regular training and fire drills
To record maintenance data for safety systems
The EOC serves as the command hub where leaders coordinate actions, resources, and information during emergencies.
According to NFPA 72, manual fire alarm pull stations should be located:
Near exit doors and paths of egress
NFPA 72 requires manual pull stations to be located near exits to ensure quick alarm activation during evacuation.
Which NFPA standard governs foam-water sprinkler systems used for flammable liquid fires?
NFPA 16 provides design and installation requirements for foam-water sprinkler and foam-water spray systems.
Which action should be taken first when a small chemical spill occurs that poses inhalation risk?
Attempt to neutralize the spill immediately
Evacuate the area and notify the emergency response team
Wait for air monitoring results before reacting
OSHA 1910.120 mandates immediate evacuation and notification for hazardous substance releases before attempting cleanup.
The Planning Section Chief in the ICS is primarily responsible for:
Collecting information and developing the Incident Action Plan (IAP)
The Planning Section Chief gathers incident data, evaluates progress, and prepares the next operational plan.
Which type of fire detection system is best for detecting fast-flaming hydrocarbon fires in refineries or fuel storage areas?
UV/IR detectors rapidly detect hydrocarbon flames through ultraviolet and infrared radiation, suitable for fuel environments (NFPA 72).
A Workplace Violence Prevention Program should include which of the following first steps?
Develop and communicate a written zero- tolerance policy
Conduct refresher training every five years
Contact law enforcement for every verbal threat
Program implementation starts with a written, management-endorsed zero- tolerance policy communicated to all employees.
Under OSHA 1910.157, portable fire extinguishers must be inspected visually at least:
OSHA requires monthly visual inspection and annual maintenance for all workplace fire extinguishers.
Which of the following best defines Mitigation within the emergency management cycle?
Steps taken before an incident to eliminate or reduce risk
Real-time actions to protect people and property
Activities to restore normal operations after an event
Efforts to maintain public communications during crises
Mitigation involves proactive measures (engineering, policies, and planning) to reduce potential impact before incidents occur.
Which NFPA code governs the design and maintenance of exhaust ventilation systems to control flammable vapors and dust?
NFPA 91 outlines design and performance requirements for exhaust ventilation systems that handle combustible vapors and dust.
Which of the following is a requirement under OSHA 1910.38 for maintaining an Emergency Action Plan (EAP)?
Review the plan after every drill regardless of results
Make the written plan available to employees for review
Submit the plan annually to OSHA for approval
Update the plan only when a fire occurs
OSHA 1910.38(e) requires that the written EAP be kept available to all employees for review and training.
A Mass Notification System (MNS) designed under NFPA 72 must include which of the following?
Visual and voice alerts for building occupants
NFPA 72 Chapter 24 requires MNS to include visual strobes, sirens, and clear voice instructions for effective communication.
Which NFPA standard specifically addresses biological event and pandemic preparedness within emergency management programs?
NFPA 1600 (Section 8.7) includes requirements for pandemic planning and biological hazard preparedness.
In pandemic response planning, which of the following administrative controls is most effective for minimizing person-to-person transmission?
Staggering shifts and promoting remote work
Administrative controls such as staggered shifts and remote work reduce crowding and direct exposure risks.
Which federal agency provides standardized ICS training courses such as ICS- 100 and ICS-200 for responders?
The Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) manages ICS training through the National Incident Management System (NIMS).
A bioterrorism response plan should include which of the following first actions when suspicious biological material is discovered?
Evacuate, isolate the area, and notify authorities
OSHA and CDC guidelines require isolation, evacuation, and immediate notification of law enforcement and public health agencies.
What is the primary goal of emergency drills and exercises under NFPA 1600?
Test, validate, and improve the emergency response plan
NFPA 1600 requires drills to assess readiness, identify weaknesses, and improve ERP effectiveness through continuous improvement.
Which of the following best defines Continuity of Operations (COOP) in emergency management?
Returning to normal production levels after recovery
Maintaining essential functions during and immediately after a disruption
COOP ensures that vital operations continue without interruption, even under emergency or disaster conditions.
During an emergency, which ICS function is responsible for obtaining and managing supplies, facilities, and equipment?
Logistics provides facilities, services and materials (food, fuel, communications, equipment). Finance/Admin tracks costs, Planning tracks resource status.
What is the MOST important step after conducting an emergency drill?
Repeat the same drill immediately until all employees pass
Send the drill results to OSHA for recordkeeping
Conduct an after-action review and document improvement areas
Dismiss employees early as a reward for participation
Drills exist to test and improve the plan; the after-action review captures weaknesses and assigns corrective actions. OSHA does not collect drill results.
According to NFPA 25, how often must sprinkler system waterflow alarms typically be tested?
NFPA 25 requires quarterly testing of waterflow alarm devices to ensure proper operation and system readiness.
Which statement correctly describes the role of the Liaison Officer in the Incident Command System (ICS)?
Ensures safe operations on the scene
Handles external coordination with assisting agencies
The Liaison Officer serves as the point of contact between the Incident Commander and outside organizations.
The Emergency Operations Center (EOC) should ideally be equipped with which feature to remain functional during a crisis?
Redundant systems ensure the EOC can operate continuously during emergencies, maintaining communication and coordination.
Which phase of the emergency management cycle focuses on analyzing potential hazards and reducing their probability or impact?
Mitigation aims to identify risks and reduce their likelihood or severity through design, planning, and preventive actions.
What is the first priority in the event of a fire emergency at a workplace?
The first action in any fire scenario is life safety - evacuate employees before suppression or documentation.
Which NFPA code provides standards for inspection, testing, and maintenance of fire alarms and signaling systems?
NFPA 72 governs design, installation, testing, and maintenance of fire alarm and emergency communication systems.
In the Incident Command System, which principle ensures that each individual reports to only one supervisor?
Unity of Command ensures clear communication and prevents conflicting orders by assigning one supervisor per responder.
Which document within a Business Continuity Plan (BCP) details time-critical functions and identifies alternate resources?
The BIA identifies essential functions, their downtime tolerance, and resources required for recovery and continuity.
What is the required inspection and maintenance frequency for portable fire extinguishers under OSHA 1910.157 and NFPA 10?
Monthly visual inspection and annual maintenance
OSHA 1910.157(e) requires monthly visual inspection and annual maintenance checks; hydrostatic testing occurs at longer intervals (5 or 12 years).
During emergency response operations, which ICS section is responsible for resource procurement and supply management?
The Logistics Section acquires, tracks, and distributes all resources needed for operations, such as food, fuel, and communications.
Which NFPA code provides guidelines for explosion venting used to protect enclosures containing combustible dust?
NFPA 68 specifies design methods for explosion venting systems that relieve pressure in enclosures containing combustible dust or vapors.
Under OSHA 1910.120 (HAZWOPER), which of the following personnel must receive annual refresher training?
Emergency responders dealing with hazardous substance releases
HAZWOPER requires annual 8- hour refresher training for all employees involved in hazardous substance emergency response.
Which of the following is the best indicator of an effective emergency drill program?
Reduction in evacuation time and improved response performance
Effective drills show measurable performance improvement such as reduced response time and better role execution.
The command structure of an Emergency Operations Center (EOC) should mirror which organizational model to ensure interoperability with national systems?
Occupational Safety and Health Review Commission model
FEMA and NFPA 1600 recommend using the ICS structure for EOC organization to align with the National Incident Management System (NIMS).
What is the main purpose of a post- incident debriefing?
To assign individual blame for response failures
To capture lessons learned and strengthen future response plans
Post-incident debriefings evaluate response performance, identify lessons learned, and guide future improvements.
During a flammable liquid spill, which control measure must be implemented first before cleanup?
Eliminate ignition sources and ventilate the area
Add absorbent material directly to the spill
Flush with water to dilute vapors
Eliminating ignition sources and ensuring ventilation prevent ignition of flammable vapors before cleanup (NFPA 30 / OSHA 1910.106).
A CO₂ suppression system is most appropriate for which type of area?
Electrical switchgear rooms without permanent occupants
NFPA 12 permits CO₂ use only in normally unoccupied, high-risk areas like transformer or generator rooms due to asphyxiation hazards.
Which activity represents a continuity (recovery) objective rather than an immediate response activity?
Restoring IT systems and production operations
Response protects life and stabilizes the incident; recovery and continuity restore critical systems and business functions after stabilization.
The primary function of an after-action report following an emergency is to:
Evaluate the effectiveness of the response and recommend improvements
After-action reports assess what worked, what failed, and outline corrective actions to enhance future preparedness.
According to NFPA 1600, which of the following elements must be integrated into the evaluation and improvement phase of emergency management?
NFPA 1600 requires organizations to incorporate corrective actions and continual improvement into their emergency management programs to maintain effectiveness.
Which regulation requires employers to review and update their Emergency Action Plan (EAP) whenever operations or assignments change?
OSHA 1910.38(f) mandates that the EAP be reviewed whenever employee responsibilities or workplace conditions change to keep plans current.
In an effective Emergency Communication Plan, redundancy is achieved by:
Using a single centralized PA system
Allowing verbal communication only through supervisors
Delaying mass alerts to prevent confusion
Redundancy ensures messages reach all personnel even if one system fails; NFPA 72 requires layered channels like voice, text, and strobes.
Which of the following best demonstrates a company’s safety culture during emergencies?
Waiting for supervisors to initiate all responses
Employees proactively following EAP procedures without delay
Contracting emergency actions to external agencies only
Keeping emergency plans confidential from staff
A strong safety culture is shown when workers take immediate, informed action according to training and procedures.
When conducting an EAP audit, which of the following should be verified first?
Employee familiarity with exit routes and assembly points
The total cost of drills conducted
The location of the HR office
The effectiveness of an EAP depends on employee awareness of evacuation routes and meeting areas, confirming functional readiness.
Which NFPA code requires emergency lighting and illuminated exit signs in buildings to support evacuation?
NFPA 101 (Life Safety Code) specifies design, placement, and maintenance of emergency lighting and exit signage for safe egress.
What is the primary advantage of using addressable fire detection systems instead of conventional ones?
Easier to install but less accurate
Identifies the exact detector or location in alarm
e Explanation: Addressable systems pinpoint the specific device in alarm, reducing response time and improving maintenance efficiency (NFPA 72).
The most critical document supporting recovery operations and continuity of business after a disaster is the:
A BCP outlines strategies, contacts, and recovery priorities to restore essential functions quickly after disruption (NFPA 1600).
During a drill evaluation, observers note confusion about who should contact external emergency responders. Which plan element MOST likely needs improvement?
Number and placement of fire extinguishers
The plan must assign clear roles, including who notifies outside responders; confusion here is a chain-of-command and communication gap, not a hardware issue.
Which of the following ensures continuous improvement of an organization’s emergency management system?
Corrective action tracking and follow-up after every drill or event
NFPA 1600 and ISO 22301 stress continual improvement through corrective- action tracking and regular program evaluation.
An Incident Command Post (ICP) should be established:
Inside the main plant control room
At a safe, easily accessible location near the incident site
In a remote administrative building only
Within the same room as hazardous materials
The ICP must be near enough for command visibility yet safe from hazards, ensuring effective coordination and communication (ICS guidelines).
Which of the following most accurately defines the scope of an Emergency Response Plan (ERP)?
List of fire extinguisher locations only
Procedures for all types of foreseeable emergencies within a facility
Actions limited to chemical spills only
OSHA 1910.38 and NFPA 1600 require that ERPs address all reasonably anticipated emergencies, not just single-hazard situations.
During an audit, you discover several employees unaware of their assembly point after evacuation. What immediate corrective action should be taken?
Conduct refresher EAP training and update posted maps
The evaluation phase focuses on measuring performance, documenting lessons learned, and implementing improvements (NFPA 1600).
If the facility’s primary communication network fails during an emergency, what should occur next?
Activate the redundant or backup communication channel
Wait for IT personnel to arrive
NFPA 72 and ICS guidelines require redundancy-switch immediately to backup radios, PA, or satellite systems to maintain command flow.
Which of the following is a key indicator of an effective training program for emergency preparedness?
Demonstrated competency and reduced error during drills
Number of slides presented in class
Performance-based results- competency, confidence, and quicker response times-show actual learning effectiveness.
What is the purpose of integrating an ERP with the site’s Occupational Health and Safety Management System (OHSMS)?
To ensure emergency actions align with hazard controls and responsibilities
Integration ensures consistency between daily hazard management and emergency response, supporting ISO 45001 and NFPA 1600 principles.
Which NFPA standard provides requirements for CO₂ fire-extinguishing systems?
NFPA 12 outlines design, installation, and safety provisions for carbon- dioxide fire-extinguishing systems.
A post-incident review finds that slow decision-making resulted from responders receiving orders from several supervisors. Which ICS principle was violated?
Unity of command means each responder reports to only one supervisor. Span of control (3-7, ideally 5) limits how many people one supervisor manages.
Which metric would best evaluate the effectiveness of emergency drills over time?
Reduction in average evacuation time and communication errors
Quantitative improvements-faster evacuations and fewer communication gaps- reflect true progress in preparedness.
Following a severe storm, a company activates its Business Continuity Plan (BCP). Which action should occur FIRST?
Restore the critical operations identified as essential in the Business Impact Analysis
BCP activation prioritizes restoring the time-critical functions ranked in the BIA; financial, insurance and review activities follow.
Which element of the PDCA cycle focuses on measuring performance and identifying improvement areas?
The Check stage measures and audits performance to verify that objectives are being achieved (ISO 45001 Clause 9).
A safety program objective states: “Reduce TRIR by 10 % within 12 months.” Which SMART component is missing?
The goal includes all SMART attributes-specific (TRIR), measurable (10 %), achievable/time-bound (12 months), and relevant (safety).
Which of the following best defines management leadership in an SH&E management system?
Allocating resources and modeling expected behaviors
Delegating all EHS duties to supervisors
Leadership provides direction, resources, and example-core to ISO 45001 Clause 5.1 and ANSI Z10 §3.1.
Which U.S. guideline explicitly integrates management leadership and worker participation as its two foundational pillars?
OSHA’s Recommended Practices for Safety and Health Programs emphasize leadership and participation as core elements.
A gap analysis reveals missing documentation for chemical-hazard training. Which PDCA phase should be initiated?
The Act stage corrects non- conformities and implements preventive actions for continual improvement.
During risk assessment, the team assigns “Severity = 5, Likelihood = 2.” The risk score is 10. What does this indicate?
Moderate risk-apply engineering or admin controls
A mid-range score triggers additional controls but not shutdown; exact thresholds depend on the site’s risk matrix.
Which of the following best describes a leading indicator?
Percent of corrective actions closed on time
Leading indicators are proactive and predictive; closure of actions prevents future incidents.
According to ISO 19011, which principle underpins all auditing?
The evidence-based approach is the rational method for reaching reliable, reproducible audit conclusions from verifiable evidence.
Which document demonstrates that identified risks are being managed and reviewed periodically?
The risk register records hazards, risk ratings, controls, responsible persons, and review dates.
Which clause of ISO 45001 directly addresses leadership and worker participation?
Clause 5 defines leadership, worker participation, roles, responsibilities, and authority-central to effective SHMS governance.
Which communication style best supports open safety reporting and collaborative problem-solving?
Assertive communication expresses needs clearly and respectfully, encouraging two-way discussion and trust.
Under a RACI chart, who is Accountable for the outcome of a safety program objective?
The safety committee consulted for input
The HR department informed of progress
Accountability rests with one individual who owns the result and signs off on completion; responsibility may be shared.
According to Herzberg's two-factor theory, which factor is a true motivator that increases job satisfaction?
Motivators are achievement, recognition, responsibility and growth. Pay, policy and conditions are hygiene factors that only prevent dissatisfaction.
In McGregor's Theory X and Theory Y, a supervisor who believes employees seek responsibility and are capable of self-direction follows:
Theory Y assumes workers are self-motivated, supporting participative management. Theory X assumes workers dislike work and need control.
Which step must occur first in an effective Management of Change (MoC) process?
Identify the proposed change and screen risk
MOC begins by identifying the proposed change and screening it for hazards/risk; authorization, training and closure come later.
During an internal audit, the auditor is assigned to evaluate her own department’s procedures. Which audit principle is being violated?
Auditors must be impartial and independent of the area audited to avoid conflict of interest (ISO 19011 § 5.3).
Which of the following is the most effective leading performance indicator?
Percentage of near-miss reports closed with action verification
Percentage of near-miss reports closed with verified action measures proactive hazard control and follow-through. The other options are lagging outcomes.
Which motivational approach aligns with Vroom's expectancy theory?
Reward behavior immediately after every safe act
Rely mainly on punishment for unsafe acts
Ensure employees believe their effort will lead to performance and a reward they value
Remove hygiene factors from the workplace
Expectancy theory: motivation = expectancy (effort leads to performance) x instrumentality (performance leads to reward) x valence (reward is valued).
A site implements a major equipment upgrade. Which MoC step ensures new hazards are communicated before start-up?
Conduct pre-startup risk assessment and employee briefing
Review only at the next audit
Pre-startup review and communication verify that new hazards are identified, controls validated, and workers informed.
Which of the following best demonstrates management accountability in a safety program?
Reviewing KPIs and personally closing overdue actions
Requesting monthly reports without follow- up
Signing the policy once per year
True accountability means leaders track and resolve issues, showing visible involvement in performance outcomes.
According to Fiedler’s Contingency Theory, effective leadership depends on:
Fit between leader’s style and situational factors
Ability to reward and punish performance
Degree of team size and composition
Fiedler proposed that leader effectiveness is contingent on task structure, leader-member relations, and position power.
Which leadership style emphasizes vision, inspiration, and individualized consideration?
Transformational leaders inspire, challenge assumptions, and motivate followers through personal engagement and shared vision.
A supervisor gives clear instructions for a new worker but allows experienced staff autonomy. This reflects:
Situational leadership adjusts direction and support based on follower readiness and competence.
Which leadership theory focuses on leader behaviors that remove obstacles and clarify paths to goal achievement?
Path-Goal leaders identify the goal, clarify steps, and provide support or reward to ensure success.
Which statement BEST differentiates transactional from transformational leadership?
Transactional focuses on compliance through rewards and penalties; transformational focuses on inspiration and shared vision
Transactional is people-oriented; transformational is task-driven
Both use identical approaches with different terminology
Transactional leaders manage by exchange (rewards/discipline); transformational leaders build commitment through vision, trust and individual consideration.
Which leadership approach best supports a generative safety culture where employees proactively solve safety issues?
Transformational and servant leadership create high engagement and trust, leading to a proactive (generative) culture.
A safety project manager creates a Work Breakdown Structure (WBS). Its main purpose is to:
Define and organize the deliverables into manageable work packages
The WBS decomposes scope into work packages so each can be scheduled, costed and assigned.
In project management, the Critical Path Method (CPM) is used to determine:
The number of employees needed per task
The longest sequence of dependent tasks, which sets the total project duration
Critical-path tasks have zero float; any delay to them delays the whole project.
During the Check phase of PDCA, the organization should:
“Check” corresponds to evaluation through monitoring, measurement, and internal audit results.
Which of the following actions represents the Act phase in PDCA?
Implementing corrective and preventive actions based on audit findings
