Compare the plant's total number of DART cases with the national number of DART cases
Compare the plant's DART rate with BLS data for the same NAICS industry code, establishment size and year
Compare the plant's DART rate with the all-industry national average
Compare the plant's DART rate with a competitor's TRIR

Valid benchmarking compares like with like: the same metric, normalized to hours (rate), for the same industry, size class and period. Raw counts, all-industry averages or different metrics distort the comparison.
A company with 12 plants compares lockout/tagout audit scores and practices among its own sites to identify the best-performing site's methods and spread them. This is an example of:
Comparing performance and practices among units within the same organization is internal benchmarking; data are easy to obtain and comparable, but the view is limited to company practice.
Following an audit, a safety manager writes an action plan to close 15 identified gaps. Which set of elements MUST the action plan contain to be effective?
A list of the gaps and the auditor's name
A description of each gap and a general statement that it will be fixed
Specific actions, a responsible person for each, target completion dates, required resources and a method to verify completion
The audit score and a comparison with last year's score

An action plan turns findings into accountable work: what will be done, by whom, by when, with what resources, and how completion/effectiveness will be verified. Lists without owners and dates rarely get closed.
A gap analysis identifies these deficiencies, but the budget will fund only one this quarter. Which should be addressed FIRST?
Missing fall protection at an unguarded 4.5 m (15 ft) mezzanine edge used daily
Training records stored in two different databases
Safety committee minutes not posted on time
Action plans are prioritized by risk (severity x likelihood). A daily exposure to a potentially fatal fall outranks administrative and documentation gaps.

An investigation finds that an operator's hand was caught while clearing jams on a conveyor because the task requires reaching into the nip point while the belt runs, and jams occur about 20 times per shift. Which corrective action is MOST effective?
Retrain all operators on the hazards of nip points
Discipline the operator for reaching into the conveyor
Redesign the infeed to reduce jams and install an interlocked guard that stops the belt when opened
Post a warning sign at the jam location

Corrective actions should follow the hierarchy of controls and address the root cause: reducing jams (elimination of the task) plus interlocked guarding (engineering) beats training, signs and discipline.
A site recorded 8 OSHA recordable cases in 400,000 hours: 3 involved days away from work, 2 involved restricted duty/job transfer, and 3 were medical treatment only. What is the DART rate?
DART counts only days-away plus restricted/transfer cases: (3 + 2) x 200,000 / 400,000 = 2.5. Trap: using all 8 cases gives the TRIR (4.0), and days-away only gives 1.5.
A plant's occupational health nurse keeps employee audiograms and respirator medical evaluations. Where should these records be maintained?
In a separate, confidential medical file with access limited to authorized persons
In each employee's personnel file so supervisors can review fitness for duty
In the supervisor's office for quick reference
In the training records database with the employee's course history
Employee medical records must be kept confidential and separate from general personnel files (ADA; 1910.1020 access rules). Supervisors may be told work restrictions, not diagnoses.
A $60,000 automated lift-assist system is expected to save $24,000 per year in injury and productivity costs. What is the simple payback period?
Payback = initial cost / annual savings = 60,000 / 24,000 = 2.5 years. Trap: 0.4 is the inverted ratio.
Purchasing is about to issue a request for proposals for new powered industrial trucks. What is the safety professional's MOST valuable role in the procurement process?
Write safety, ergonomic and training requirements into the specifications and help evaluate bids before selection
Inspect the trucks after delivery and reject unsafe units
Recommend the lowest-cost bid so savings can fund training
Leave procurement to purchasing and train operators after delivery
Safety is cheapest to build in at the specification stage (prevention through design). Post-delivery inspection is reactive and costly.

An experienced operator is seen bypassing a machine guard. The company has a progressive discipline policy that has been applied to others for the same violation. Which response is MOST consistent with effective discipline principles?
Wait and raise it at the annual performance review
Terminate the operator immediately to set an example
Overlook it because the operator is productive and experienced
Address it immediately, apply the policy as it was applied to others, focus on the behavior, and document it
The 'hot stove' rule: discipline should be immediate, consistent, impersonal and with prior warning. Inconsistency destroys credibility and legal defensibility.
While reviewing a RACI chart for a hot-work permit program, you find that three different managers are each marked "A" for permit approval. What is the BEST recommendation?
Leave it; more approvers provides more safety oversight
Assign a single Accountable person and reclassify the others as Responsible, Consulted or Informed
Discard the RACI chart and rely on job descriptions
Each task should have exactly one Accountable person; multiple A's create confusion where everyone assumes someone else approved.
Last year's 100 injuries were: lacerations 46, strains 30, contusions 12, burns 7, eye injuries 5. Using Pareto analysis, which categories should be targeted first?
Contusions, burns and eye injuries, because they are easiest to fix
Pareto (80/20) focuses on the vital few: lacerations and strains are 76% of injuries. Lacerations alone leave a large share untouched.
A fire risk assessment of a distribution warehouse produces four findings. Which should receive the HIGHEST priority?
Cardboard stored next to an office copier
A closed sprinkler control valve in an area with high-piled plastic commodities and forklift battery charging
One burned-out exit sign bulb in a well-lit corridor with a second marked exit
A fire extinguisher whose monthly inspection tag is one week overdue
An impaired sprinkler system over a high fuel load with an ignition source combines high likelihood and catastrophic severity; restore protection and use impairment procedures.
An EHS manager must rank hazardous materials risks across a facility's chemical inventory to prioritize controls and compliance work. Which approach is MOST appropriate?
Rank each chemical by hazard class, quantity relative to regulatory thresholds and likelihood of release, then monitor changes through inventory updates and MOC
Rank chemicals in the order of the SDS binder
Rank only the chemicals that have spilled in the past
Risk ranking combines hazard severity, quantity (e.g., PSM or EPCRA thresholds) and likelihood, and must be monitored as inventory changes. Spill history alone misses latent risks.
A ransomware attack encrypts the building automation and process control servers at a chemical plant during operations. According to the facility's emergency response plan, what should be done FIRST?
Pay the ransom quickly to restore operations
Restore the servers from backup while they remain connected to the network
Wait for the IT vendor to diagnose the problem before taking any action
Isolate affected systems from the network and activate the cyber incident response plan, placing processes in a safe state
Containment comes first: isolate infected systems to stop spread and move the process to a safe state. Restoring while still connected risks reinfection.
Employees report a strong odor of natural gas in an office building after nearby utility work. What is the BEST immediate action?
Turn on exhaust fans to ventilate the building
Locate the leak by checking appliances and connections
Evacuate the building without operating electrical switches, then call the gas utility and 911 from a safe location
Have employees stay at their desks while maintenance investigates
Utility gas leaks present an explosion hazard: evacuate, avoid ignition sources such as switches and phones, and report from a safe distance.
A receptionist receives a telephone bomb threat. According to a typical emergency response plan, what should the receptionist do?
Hang up immediately and continue working
Keep the caller talking, record details using a bomb threat checklist, and notify security and police per the plan
Personally search the building for suspicious packages
Announce over the public address system that there is a bomb in the building
Bomb threat procedures emphasize capturing caller details (checklist) and notifying authorities, who decide on search or evacuation; panic announcements and self-searches are inappropriate.
A company ships placarded quantities of hazardous materials by highway. Under 49 CFR 172 Subpart I, its written security plan must address which elements?
Personnel security, unauthorized access, and en route security
Fire extinguisher placement and sprinkler coverage
Driver hours-of-service logs and vehicle fuel economy
DOT security plans must include an assessment of transportation security risks and measures for personnel security, unauthorized access and en route security, plus security training.
Under DOT hazmat training rules (49 CFR 172.704), which training must ALL hazmat employees receive in addition to general awareness and function-specific training?

All hazmat employees need general awareness, function-specific, safety and security awareness training, with recurrent training at least every 3 years. In-depth security training applies when a security plan is required.
A worksite analysis of a 24-hour convenience store shows that most incidents occur late at night during robberies. Which control is MOST effective at reducing this risk?
Require employees to work faster during night shifts
Post a zero-tolerance policy in the break room
Limit cash on hand with a drop safe, keep windows clear for visibility, and provide bright lighting with posted signs
Provide annual training only for day-shift workers

Engineering and administrative controls that reduce the reward and raise visibility (drop safes, low cash, clear sight lines, lighting) are proven robbery deterrents. A policy alone does not deter outsiders.
A hazardous waste container storage area holds twenty 55-gallon drums of liquid waste. Under RCRA (40 CFR 264.175), what is the MINIMUM secondary containment capacity?
Containment must hold 10% of total volume or 100% of the largest container, whichever is greater: 10% x (20 x 55 = 1,100) = 110 gal, which exceeds 55 gal. Trap: using only the largest container.
A facility stores ammonium nitrate and other theft-attractive hazardous materials. Which measure BEST addresses hazardous materials security?
Store the materials near the loading dock for faster shipping
Restrict access to authorized personnel, conduct regular inventory reconciliation, and report unexplained losses
Rely on GHS labels to deter theft
Keep the storage area unlocked so emergency responders can enter
Hazmat security combines access control, inventory accountability and reporting of losses so diversion is prevented or detected quickly. Labels communicate hazards but do not secure them.
Employees clean up a spill of a listed hazardous solvent using absorbent pads. How should the used absorbent be managed?
In the regular trash once it has dried
By rinsing it in a floor drain and reusing the pads
As universal waste, since it came from a spill
As hazardous waste, properly containerized, labeled, and disposed of through a permitted facility
Spill cleanup materials contaminated with a listed hazardous waste carry that listing (contained-in principle) and must be managed as hazardous waste. Absorbents are not a universal waste category.
A manufacturer replaces single-use cardboard shipping boxes with durable plastic totes that suppliers return for refilling. Which principle does this represent?
Using the same item again for its original purpose without reprocessing is reuse. Recycling would break the material down to make new products.
A company finds that most of its environmental footprint comes from raw materials made by overseas suppliers. What is the BEST first step to improve supply chain sustainability?
Stop tracking supplier impacts because they are outside the company's control
Switch all suppliers immediately regardless of cost or quality
Establish a supplier code of conduct with sustainability criteria and assess suppliers against it
Publish a sustainability statement without supplier engagement
Setting clear expectations, then assessing and engaging suppliers, is the foundation of supply chain sustainability; ignoring or making unfounded claims (greenwashing) is weak.
The 'triple bottom line' approach to sustainability evaluates an organization's performance in which three areas?
The triple bottom line measures social (people), environmental (planet) and economic (profit) performance, a precursor to ESG reporting.
A plant collects scrap aluminum trimmings, sends them to be remelted, and buys back the resulting ingots for production. This is BEST described as:
The material is reprocessed (remelted) and returned to the same product system, which is closed-loop recycling, a circular economy practice. Reuse would involve no reprocessing.
Outdoors in direct sun, a heat stress survey records: natural wet bulb 25 C, globe 40 C, dry bulb 30 C. What is the WBGT? (Outdoor: WBGT = 0.7 NWB + 0.2 GT + 0.1 DB)
WBGT = 0.7(25) + 0.2(40) + 0.1(30) = 17.5 + 8 + 3 = 28.5 C. Trap: 29.5 C uses the indoor/no-solar-load formula (0.7 NWB + 0.3 GT).
A cohort study reports a relative risk of 1.4 for solvent exposure and liver disease, with a 95% confidence interval of 0.8 to 2.4. What is the BEST interpretation?
The association is not statistically significant at the 0.05 level because the interval includes 1.0
Solvent exposure is proven to cause a 40% increase in liver disease
Solvent exposure is protective against liver disease
Solvent exposure reduces liver disease risk by 40%
A 95% CI for a ratio that includes 1.0 (no effect) means the result is not statistically significant. Trap: reading the point estimate of 1.4 as proof of causation.
Foundry workers show a higher lung cancer rate than office workers, but the foundry workers also smoke at a much higher rate. In this study, smoking is BEST described as a:
A confounder is linked to both the exposure group and the outcome and can distort the apparent association. It must be controlled by stratification, matching or adjustment.
At the start of a year, 25 of a plant's 400 workers already have occupational dermatitis. During the year, 15 new cases occur. What is the annual incidence rate per 100 workers at risk?
Incidence = new cases / population at risk = 15/(400 - 25) = 15/375 = 4.0 per 100. Trap: 3.75 wrongly includes existing cases in the denominator; 10.0 counts all 40 cases (prevalence).

Area noise levels average 82 dBA (below the 85 dBA action level), yet several workers in a fiberglass boat lay-up area that uses styrene resin show standard threshold shifts. What is the MOST likely contributing factor?
Ototoxic styrene exposure acting together with noise
Ototoxins such as styrene, toluene, lead and carbon monoxide can damage hearing on their own and add to the effect of noise, causing hearing loss below noise limits.
Section 11 of an SDS states that a solvent caused malformations in the offspring of pregnant test animals but showed no germ-cell mutations. How is this solvent BEST classified?
A teratogen causes birth defects in a developing embryo or fetus. A mutagen alters genetic material (DNA), and a carcinogen causes cancer. Exposure control plans should address pregnant workers.
An industrial hygienist must measure a painter's 8-hour exposure to toluene vapor. Which sampling method is MOST appropriate?
Activated charcoal sorbent tube on a low-flow personal pump in the breathing zone
PVC filter with a cyclone pre-selector
Area grab sample taken at the room exhaust fan
Organic vapors such as toluene are collected on sorbent media (charcoal tube or passive badge) in the breathing zone. Filters collect particulates, and a cyclone is for respirable dust.

A NIOSH lifting analysis gives these multipliers: HM 0.625, VM 0.93, DM 0.91, AM 1.0, FM 0.88, CM 0.95. The load is 30 lb. What are the RWL and Lifting Index? (RWL = 51 lb x HM x VM x DM x AM x FM x CM)
RWL = 51 x 0.625 x 0.93 x 0.91 x 1.0 x 0.88 x 0.95 = 22.6 lb; LI = 30/22.6 = 1.33 (above 1.0, so the task needs redesign). Trap: dividing RWL by load gives 0.75.

A RCRA hazardous waste container storage area holds twenty 55-gallon drums. Under 40 CFR 264.175, secondary containment must hold 10% of the total volume or 100% of the largest container, whichever is greater. What minimum containment capacity is required?
Total = 20 x 55 = 1,100 gal; 10% = 110 gal; largest container = 55 gal. The greater value is 110 gal. Trap: 55 gal applies only the largest-container rule.

Under OSHA 1910.106, an approved flammable storage cabinet may hold no more than 60 gallons of Category 1, 2 or 3 flammable liquids. How many full 5-gallon safety cans of a Category 2 liquid may be stored in one cabinet?
60 gal / 5 gal per can = 12 cans. The 120-gal cabinet limit applies only to Category 4 (combustible) liquids, and no more than three cabinets are allowed per fire area.
An incident trend shows operators skipping a startup checklist step. The plant manager asks the CSP to schedule retraining for all operators. What should the CSP do FIRST?
Analyze whether the problem is caused by a lack of knowledge or skill, or by other factors such as time pressure, equipment design, or supervision
Schedule retraining for all operators immediately
Discipline the operators involved in the incidents
Purchase an online refresher course on startup procedures

A needs assessment first determines whether a performance gap is actually a training problem. If operators know the step but skip it, the fix is a management or design issue, and retraining will not work.
A training coordinator applies the Plan-Do-Check-Act cycle to a fall protection course. Comparing post-training field observation data against the course objectives occurs in which phase?
Check is measuring results against objectives. Act is the next step: standardizing what worked or revising the course based on what Check found.
Post-training audits show workers pass the lockout/tagout quiz but often skip the zero-energy verification step in the field. What is the BEST continuous improvement action?
Determine why the step is being skipped, revise the training to include hands-on verification practice and supervisor follow-up, then re-measure field performance
Repeat the same course for all employees
Remove the verification step from the procedure

Passing a knowledge test without transfer to the job signals a gap in practice or reinforcement. Improve the program based on root cause and verify with Level 3 observation. Repeating unchanged training is the trap.
Which event should MOST directly trigger a review and update of an existing training program?
A request for new classroom furniture
A change in the color scheme of the company logo
Introduction of new equipment or a process change under Management of Change
New equipment, processes, hazards, regulations, or incident findings change required competencies, so MOC should include training review. Z490.1 also calls for periodic program review.
In a continuous improvement model of training, results from the ADDIE Evaluate phase should be used primarily to:
Archive the course permanently once evaluation is complete
Rank trainers for compensation purposes only
Feed back into analysis and revise the design, materials, and delivery of the program
ADDIE is cyclic when used for continuous improvement: evaluation findings feed back into analysis and every other phase. Treating evaluation as the end point is the trap.
A CSP must verify that newly trained powered industrial truck operators are competent before they operate independently. Which evaluation method BEST meets this need?
A practical performance evaluation of each operator in the workplace by a qualified evaluator
A written quiz on forklift terminology

For skill-based tasks, competence is verified by demonstration; OSHA 1910.178(l) requires formal instruction, practical training, and evaluation of operator performance in the workplace. Attendance and quizzes do not prove skill.

A new safety technician is paired with an experienced CSP who observes the technician's field audits, asks guiding questions, and gives regular individualized feedback over several months. This method is BEST described as:
Coaching is ongoing one-on-one guidance and feedback on real work to develop performance. It is individualized and continuous, unlike a one-time class.
A plant relies on informal 'follow an experienced worker' on-the-job training. What is the PRIMARY weakness of this approach?
It is always more expensive than classroom training
It cannot occur at the actual workstation
Unsafe shortcuts and inconsistent practices may be passed on unless the training is structured with written procedures, checklists, and competency sign-off
Unstructured OJT transfers whatever the mentor does, including bad habits. Structured OJT uses standard procedures, qualified trainers, and documented evaluation.
A company plans to use only computer-based training (CBT) to qualify employees on a respirator fit and donning procedure. What is the PRIMARY limitation of this plan?
CBT cannot be updated once published
CBT cannot be accessed by remote workers
CBT alone cannot verify the psychomotor skill; a hands-on demonstration and fit test are still needed
CBT is efficient for knowledge content, but physical skills must be practiced and demonstrated; respirator use also requires fit testing under 1910.134.
